10240.label: Polar loop hotspots; S/T-rich disorder
10240.summary: Polar, small-residue–rich flexible regions and conserved polar loop residues. The feature marks Ser/Thr/Gly/His/Asn–enriched low‑complexity/disordered segments (notably the C-termini of bacteriophage tail fibers/spikes) and also singles out isolated, function-critical polar residues in loops (e.g., the selectivity‑filter threonine in K+ channels, the ABC transporter NBD Q‑loop/signature glutamine, and active‑site histidines adjacent to catalytic phosphoserines in sugar‑phosphate mutases). Overall it tracks hydrogen‑bonding/nucleophilic microenvironments in exposed loops and tails across diverse proteins.
10240.description:
Summary: Polar, small-residue–rich flexible regions and conserved polar loop residues. Overall it tracks hydrogen‑bonding/nucleophilic microenvironments in exposed loops and tails across diverse proteins.
Activation pattern: Bimodal: (i) long, contiguous activation blocks in late, disordered S/T/G/H‑rich regions (especially in phage structural proteins); (ii) sharp single‑residue peaks at polar residues in catalytic/ion‑binding/coupling loops of enzymes and channels. Additional shorter S/T‑rich clusters appear in cytosolic loops of multi‑pass membrane proteins and disordered tails of plant transcription factors; rare low‑intensity hits occur within ordered secondary structure (e.g., a beta‑strand in a SET domain).
Exemplars: - Bacteriophage tail fibers/spikes and capsid/connector proteins: strong activation on C‑terminal, disordered G/S/T/H‑rich receptor‑binding/carbohydrate‑interacting regions.
- Potassium channels: single conserved threonine in the TVGYG selectivity filter.
- ABC transporter nucleotide‑binding domains (ECF‑type): conserved glutamine in the Q‑loop/signature coupling region.
- Sugar‑phosphate mutase family (e.g., phosphomannomutase): histidine in the active‑site loop adjacent to the catalytic phosphoserine.
- Plant C2H2‑type zinc finger transcription factors and other plant regulators: disordered, low‑complexity S/T‑ (often Cys/His‑) rich C‑terminal segments.
- Multi‑pass membrane proteins (MS4A/CD20, TMEM176): short S/T‑ and charged‑residue clusters in cytosolic loops.
- Ribosomal large subunit proteins L3/L4: short Gly/Ser‑rich flexible loops.
- Intein‑containing proteins: S/T/C/H‑rich motifs around splice junctions.
- Viral tailspike depolymerases and carbohydrate‑active enzymes: S/T/H‑enriched loops in carbohydrate‑binding/catalytic regions.
- SET‑domain histone methyltransferases: occasional low‑amplitude peaks on small residues within a beta‑strand near the catalytic core.

13260.label: Phage tail fiber distal motifs
13260.summary: Structured β-strand/short-helix segments in phage tail fiber and baseplate proteins, with peaks centered on hydrophobic/aromatic residues (Y, V, A, L, M, P, K) within local secondary-structure elements of receptor-binding/distal fiber domains.
13260.description:
Summary: Structured β-strand/short-helix segments in phage tail fiber and baseplate proteins, with peaks centered on hydrophobic/aromatic residues (Y, V, A, L, M, P, K) within local secondary-structure elements of receptor-binding/distal fiber domains.
Activation pattern: Sharp residue-level peaks within short helices, turns, and β-strands of the distal/receptor-binding regions of tail fibers and baseplate wedges, often spanning 4-8 residues in a single structural element, with broader lower-level activation distributed across the same chain.
Exemplars:
- Bacteriophage T4 short tail fiber gp12: peaks in a helix-turn region (~residues 373-383) with context PLYASRIGTRY.
- Bacteriophage T4 long tail fiber gp37: peaks in a short helix (~844-849) with context PKLAVAYPSGV.
- Bacteriophage T4 baseplate wedge gp10: peaks in a short helix (~470-473) with context NPNNPVTYMGF.
- Bacteriophage lambda side tail fiber (stf/gp27): peaks in a homologous PKLAVAYPSGV motif (~residues 562-572).

15023.label: Active-site loop/turn scaffolds
15023.summary: Active-site loop/turn microenvironments that scaffold catalytic and metal-binding pockets. The feature recognizes short gly/pro-enriched loop/turns and adjoining helices/strands that shape enzyme cores; it often coincides with histidine-centered metal/proton-ligand settings (e.g., His–His/His–Tyr–His, heme/copper) when present but is not dependent on His, also marking analogous loop environments around non-His catalytic motifs. The same loop/turn signature recurs as repeated modules across long extracellular phage tail/fiber regions.
15023.description:
Summary: Active-site loop/turn microenvironments that scaffold catalytic and metal-binding pockets. The feature recognizes short gly/pro-enriched loop/turns and adjoining helices/strands that shape enzyme cores; it often coincides with histidine-centered metal/proton-ligand settings (e.g., His–His/His–Tyr–His, heme/copper) when present but is not dependent on His, also marking analogous loop environments around non-His catalytic motifs. The same loop/turn signature recurs as repeated modules across long extracellular phage tail/fiber regions.
Activation pattern: Predominantly regional activation on compact 20–60 aa segments within well-structured domains, with residue-level peaks in loops and immediately adjacent secondary structure; frequently mid-to-C-terminal and excluding signal peptides. In soluble enzymes it highlights loop/β–loop/α contexts near catalytic/metal-binding sites (sometimes including the ligand residue), in membrane oxidases it runs along the transmembrane helix hosting ligating residues, and in phage tail/fiber proteins it broadens over long, repetitive gly/pro-rich stretches.
Exemplars:
- Multicopper oxidase/tyrosinase: strong activation around copper-ligand segments and flanking loop→helix elements in the catalytic core.
- Cu/Zn superoxide dismutase: activation around the metal-binding loop/β elements adjacent to His ligands.
- Heme–copper oxidase subunit I (COX1): activation along transmembrane helices that house heme/copper ligands, emphasizing surrounding helical environment.
- Sortases (A/D): focused activation on the His-centered catalytic segment and neighboring structural elements, not the distant catalytic Cys alone.
- Cyclophilin-type PPIase: loop-rich segment within the PPIase domain adjacent to the active-site pocket.
- Ntn-hydrolase acylases (e.g., PvdQ, glutaryl‑7‑ACA acylase): helical/loop blocks that scaffold the catalytic core while avoiding the Ntn catalytic nucleophile.
- Gamma‑glutamylcyclotransferase/AIG2-like: extended β‑strand/loop blocks in the core fold adjacent to, but not on, the catalytic residue.
- 3‑methyladenine DNA glycosylase (AlkA-like): mixed helix/β/hairpin regions forming the DNA-binding groove scaffold with peaks in loop elements.
- Bacteriophage tail/baseplate/fiber/tube proteins: long, repetitive segments enriched in GG/PG/TG runs consistent with extracellular β‑solenoid/fiber scaffolds that reiterate the same loop/turn signature.

9652.label: Trimeric viral fiber appendages
9652.summary: Trimeric viral appendage architectures of receptor-binding fibers, tailspike depolymerases, and tail needles—dominated by beta-solenoid/beta-helix repeats and also including trimeric coiled-coil shafts/needles—with spillover to homologous viral spikes and bacterial trimeric autotransporter adhesins; often contiguous with a C-terminal intramolecular chaperone/autopeptidase segment.
9652.description:
Summary: Trimeric viral appendage architectures of receptor-binding fibers, tailspike depolymerases, and tail needles—dominated by beta-solenoid/beta-helix repeats and also including trimeric coiled-coil shafts/needles—with spillover to homologous viral spikes and bacterial trimeric autotransporter adhesins; often contiguous with a C-terminal intramolecular chaperone/autopeptidase segment.
Activation pattern: Extensive domain-level activation across long repetitive shafts/cores—beta-solenoid/tri-beta-spiral and trimeric coiled-coils—with pronounced local peaks on short Gly/Ser/Thr/Asn/Asp/Tyr-rich repeats; strong continuous coverage in long fibers/spikes and tail needles; occasional activation near/within adjacent intramolecular chaperone/autoprotease segments; outside viral appendages, only isolated single-residue peaks in generic coiled-coils.
Exemplars:
- Bacteriophage long tail fibers (T4-like gp37): activation along the distal beta-helix/shaft repeats and receptor-binding tip.
- Klebsiella/Enterobacterales phage capsule-depolymerase tailspikes: activation across the right-handed beta-helix catalytic/binding repeats and into the C-terminal intramolecular chaperone auto-cleaving domain.
- Phage endosialidase/hyaluronidase tailspikes: activation on the beta-solenoid CAZyme core that binds/cleaves capsular polysaccharides.
- Baseplate-associated receptor-binding proteins with beta-solenoid or mixed-fld RBDs: activation on the adhesion module contiguous with fiber attachment.
- Phage tail needle proteins (e.g., Salmonella phage P22 gp26): activation along the trimeric coiled-coil needle shaft.
- Non-bacteriophage viral fibers (e.g., adenovirus fiber shaft, reovirus sigma1): activation on the triple beta-spiral shaft repeats.
- Trimeric autotransporter adhesins (YadA/Hia family): lower-level activation on head beta-roll/solenoid repeats and proximal stalk transitions.
- Polysaccharide-degrading beta-helix enzymes (pectate-lyase-like folds): activation across the solenoid repeat core.
- Off-target/coincidental: outside viral appendages, only isolated single-residue peaks in unrelated coiled-coil helices.

5835.label: Folded catalytic core activation
5835.summary: Activation across the full mature catalytic chain of diverse enzymes, broadly tracking structured (folded) regions and depleted in disordered termini and signal peptides.
5835.description:
Summary: Activation across the full mature catalytic chain of diverse enzymes, broadly tracking structured (folded) regions and depleted in disordered termini and signal peptides.
Activation pattern: Near-uniform activation over almost the entire mature polypeptide once any disordered N-terminal extension or signal peptide is excluded; local residue-level peaks at a small number of hotspot positions within the folded core (often on beta-strands and adjacent loops), with reduced signal in disordered N-/C-terminal segments.
Exemplars: - DNA-3-methyladenine glycosylases: broad activation over the glycosylase chain with peaks in the C-terminal catalytic domain core.
- Aldose 1-epimerases / galactose mutarotases (incl. bifunctional gal10 mutarotase domain, maltose epimerase): broad activation over the mutarotase domain with a sharp hotspot on a conserved Y-L-P-V patch on a central beta-strand (around residues ~198-211).
- ATP synthase subunit a (F0 sector): a long transmembrane helix and adjacent cytoplasmic helix at the proton half-channel interface.
- Protein-L-isoaspartate O-methyltransferases (SAM/SAH-dependent): Rossmann-like core segment encompassing the SAH/SAM-binding site.
- Expansin/EG45-like proteins: beta-strand/coil patch across the EG45 domain surface implicated in polysaccharide binding.
- Carbonic anhydrases: Zn-binding core around the histidine triad and surrounding beta-sheet/loop framework.
- Cu/Zn superoxide dismutases and copper chaperones: metal-binding loops within the beta-sandwich core.
- Methionine aminopeptidases: metallo-catalytic core around the metal-binding motif and adjacent secondary structure.
- Ribosomal large-subunit proteins (uL2/uL3, organellar): conserved helical core segments that contact rRNA.
- Urease system proteins: Ni-active-site region in catalytic subunits and metal-handling segments in accessory factors.

13124.label: C-terminal capping/recognition segment
13124.summary: C-terminal, surface-exposed recognition/capping segments located in flexible loops, short helices, or edge β-strands that terminate domains. These segments often mediate partner recognition (protein, carbohydrate, substrate/metal) or include trafficking motifs in secreted/periplasmic proteins, and act as terminal capping/interaction loops in enzymes.
13124.description:
Summary: C-terminal, surface-exposed recognition/capping segments located in flexible loops, short helices, or edge β-strands that terminate domains. These segments often mediate partner recognition (protein, carbohydrate, substrate/metal) or include trafficking motifs in secreted/periplasmic proteins, and act as terminal capping/interaction loops in enzymes.
Activation pattern: Regional activation of contiguous blocks (tens of residues) that concentrate at or near the extreme C-terminus of a domain/protein; peaks tend to lie in coil/loop segments and can extend into adjacent short helices or edge β-strands. Frequently overlaps low-confidence or disordered tails but can also occur in well-structured terminal loops. Isolated peaks elsewhere are rare.
Exemplars: - Bacterial adhesins (e.g., invasin): activation spans the C-terminal integrin-binding D5 domain that mediates receptor interaction.
- Formylglycine-generating enzymes (ER luminal FGE-like): activation on the C-terminal segment containing Ca2+-binding residues and a disordered tail with an ER-retention motif.
- Ergothioneine biosynthesis enzyme EgtB (hercynylcysteine S-oxide synthase): strong activation at the extreme C-terminal loop/short helix of the synthase domain.
- Signal peptidase I (periplasmic serine peptidase): activation on the flexible, low-confidence C-terminal portion of the periplasmic domain, distal to the catalytic dyad.
- Ulilysin family metalloproteases: activation on a C-terminal loop (including a substrate-binding residue and a disulfide-linked segment) and adjacent terminal helix.
- Neurotrophins (e.g., BDNF): activation confined to the mature growth factor, strongest in the flexible C-terminal tail crucial for receptor engagement.

15659.label: Whole-chain activation with central peaks
15659.summary: Broad, near-whole-chain activation on small-to-medium subunit proteins, with strongest peaks landing on structured beta-strands and short helices in the central portion of the chain. The feature shows widespread coverage (typically the entire mature chain is active) rather than a sharp local signature, with secondary structure elements in the middle of the protein carrying the highest activation values.
15659.description:
Summary: Broad, near-whole-chain activation on small-to-medium subunit proteins, with strongest peaks landing on structured beta-strands and short helices in the central portion of the chain. The feature shows widespread coverage (typically the entire mature chain is active) rather than a sharp local signature, with secondary structure elements in the middle of the protein carrying the highest activation values.
Activation pattern: Diffuse domain-level activation spanning essentially the full chain, punctuated by stronger peaks within structured strand/helix elements in the central region; both N- and C-terminal portions are typically active, with little evidence of suppression over structured cores.
Exemplars: - Eukaryotic RNA polymerase alpha-like subunits (RPB3, RPAC1 from yeast, human, Arabidopsis, Dictyostelium, fission yeast, bovine): activation covers the entire chain, with top peaks on central beta-strands and short helices around the conserved fold (residues ~100-175).
- Bacteriophage T4 baseplate wedge protein gp8: broad activation across the chain with strongest peaks on N-terminal helices and strands.
- Plant RNA polymerase IV/V subunit 3B: full-length activation pattern with peaks on central structured elements.

15513.label: Catalytic/interface βαβ module
15513.summary: Compact mixed αβ submodule (a loop–short helix flanked by β strands; a βαβ unit) that forms the key functional surface of many domains—encompassing catalytic loops in enzymes or basic interaction patches used for nucleic‑acid/protein binding and assembly in regulatory/structural proteins.
15513.description:
Summary: Compact mixed αβ submodule (a loop–short helix flanked by β strands; a βαβ unit) that forms the key functional surface of many domains—encompassing catalytic loops in enzymes or basic interaction patches used for nucleic‑acid/protein binding and assembly in regulatory/structural proteins.
Activation pattern: Regional activation across a single contiguous block (~60–120 aa), usually in the N‑terminal to central part of the protein, with strongest signal on a short α‑helix and adjacent β‑strand(s); local peaks often coincide with catalytic/ligand‑binding residues or basic patches; predominantly within well‑structured regions but can taper into an adjoining disordered tail.
Exemplars: - Viral capsid/scaffolding serine proteases (assemblin): activation over the N‑terminal catalytic core around the histidine of the charge‑relay, spanning β–loop–helix elements.
- Mono‑ADP‑ribosyltransferase toxins (mART/ARTC): activation on the C‑terminal β‑strand/loop of the TR core bearing catalytic/NAD+‑binding residues (e.g., H‑Y‑E region).
- Plant NAC transcription factors: activation across the C‑terminal half of the NAC DNA‑binding domain and into the adjacent basic tail that mediates nucleic‑acid/protein interactions.
- CRISPR type III RAMP complex subunit Cmr6: activation at the C‑terminal loop–helix–β element of the structured core implicated in RNA/protein interfaces.
- General transcription factor IIF subunit 1: activation on a central structured αβ segment immediately N‑terminal to a disordered regulatory region (includes a phosphosite).
- Soluble guanylate cyclase α subunits: activation within the central PAS‑like αβ segment that mediates intra-/interdomain interactions.

3038.label: Extended structured domain surfaces
3038.summary: Extended, well-folded interaction surfaces typified by the phenylalanyl-tRNA synthetase β subunit core—covering its B5 editing domain and adjacent mid-protein structured regions—and, at lower activation, analogous long, structured, charged/hydrophobic domain surfaces in other large proteins; rare exceptions show single-residue emphasis on acidic metal-binding sites

Activation pattern: Predominantly domain-level activation as long, contiguous blocks in mid-to-C-terminal regions of large proteins; transmembrane helices and disordered tails are suppressed; occasional sharp, residue-level peaks at catalytic Mg2+-binding aspartates
Exemplars: - Phenylalanyl-tRNA synthetase β subunits (bacterial/archaeal/organellar): strong, broad activation centered on the B5 editing domain and surrounding mid-protein structured regions, with an additional moderate C-terminal FDX-ACB (anticodon-binding) block
- Flagellar M-ring assembly protein (FliF): high activation across the central, well-structured periplasmic ring-building domain; N-/C-terminal transmembranes and disordered regions inactive
- Ribonuclease E: a single sharp peak at the Mg2+-coordinating catalytic Asp within a β-strand
- Tudor-domain–associated chromatin/RNA regulators: moderate regional activation over the Tudor-containing or adjacent structured segments
- Peptidyl-prolyl isomerases (cyclophilins/PPIases): moderate activation spanning the cyclophilin-like β-barrel domain
- Other bacterial enzymes/scaffolds: low-to-moderate activation over central, well-folded domains; minimal signal on transmembranes and low-complexity tails

7819.label: Phage and viral structural proteins
7819.summary: This feature broadly tags whole proteins from viral and bacterial extracellular assemblies, with a strong bias for bacteriophage distal tail proteins, tail tips, baseplate hubs, and tail knobs, as well as viral capsid proteins. It also activates on some non-phage proteins such as paramyxovirus matrix proteins, dsRNA virus major capsid proteins, rotavirus outer capsid spike proteins, and certain plant ribosome-inactivating proteins.
7819.description:
Summary: This feature broadly tags whole proteins from viral and bacterial extracellular assemblies, with a strong bias for bacteriophage distal tail proteins, tail tips, baseplate hubs, and tail knobs, as well as viral capsid proteins. It also activates on some non-phage proteins such as paramyxovirus matrix proteins, dsRNA virus major capsid proteins, rotavirus outer capsid spike proteins, and certain plant ribosome-inactivating proteins.

Activation pattern: Largely chain-wide rather than focal: the feature activates across nearly all residues of these proteins, with peaks distributed across helices, strands, turns, and loops. Local maxima can fall on small/polar residues in G/S/T/N-rich contexts but also on hydrophobic and charged residues embedded in secondary-structure elements. Peaks frequently coincide with structured regions and inter-subunit interfaces of fibrous/assembling architectures (tail tubes, baseplate hubs, capsid shells, matrix layers).

Exemplars:
- Phage tip attachment/tail fiber (e.g., lambda gpJ): broad activation across the chain with peaks on both helical and strand elements of the tip region.
- Phage tail tip proteins (lambda gpL, N15 gpL): activation throughout the protein, including on Fe-S cluster-binding residues and helical segments critical for tail assembly.
- Phage baseplate hub and distal tail proteins (T5 pb3, T5 pb9): near-complete chain coverage with peaks in mixed strand/loop environments.
- Phage tail knob (phi29 gp9): broad activation with strongest peaks within C-terminal strands and helices of the knob.
- Viral matrix and capsid proteins (measles M, ScV-L-A major capsid, rotavirus VP4/VP8*): activation across the entire chain, with peaks on helices and strands of the assembled-layer regions.
- Plant ribosome-inactivating protein (sapovaccarin-S1): chain-wide activation with peaks distributed across the catalytic domain.

7070.label: Phage tail attachment segments
7070.summary: N-terminal assembly/attachment segments of tailed bacteriophage virion structural proteins—especially tail fibers/spikes and receptor‑binding depolymerases—plus related tail/baseplate/tail‑tube/needle components; these regions are typically low‑complexity and enriched in small/polar residues. Weaker cross‑activation occurs on non-phage viral capsid/scaffold segments and on bacterial N‑terminal helical domains that mimic this composition.
7070.description:
Summary: N-terminal assembly/attachment segments of tailed bacteriophage virion structural proteins—especially tail fibers/spikes and receptor‑binding depolymerases—plus related tail/baseplate/tail‑tube/needle components; these regions are typically low‑complexity and enriched in small/polar residues. Weaker cross‑activation occurs on non-phage viral capsid/scaffold segments and on bacterial N‑terminal helical domains that mimic this composition.
Activation pattern: Predominantly long, contiguous N‑terminal regional activation across roughly the first ~100 residues, with clustered peaks rather than isolated residues. Outside phage proteins, activation is weaker and may appear as short N‑terminal stretches or occasional single‑residue peaks.
Exemplars: - Phage tail fibers/long-tail fiber (gp37-like) proteins: strong activation across the N‑terminal baseplate/head‑attachment and oligomerization modules.
- Phage tailspike receptor‑binding depolymerases/glycosidases (e.g., Klebsiella capsule depolymerases): activation on the N‑terminal tail‑attachment segment.
- Other tail apparatus components (tail tube, baseplate, needle proteins): N‑terminal stretches activate.
- Non‑phage viral minor outer capsid/scaffold proteins: weaker activation on extended disordered regions outside structured/catalytic domains (e.g., outside a PPPDE domain).
- Mycobacterial PE‑PGRS family: activation confined to the N‑terminal PE helical domain.
- Bacterial flotillin-like scaffolds and RNA polymerase β″: only weak, local peaks at helix/strand transitions or single helical residues (likely incidental).

3509.label: C-terminal helix-to-IDR transition
3509.summary: Terminal helix-to-tail segments of small alpha-helical proteins—most prominently histone-fold proteins—where the feature marks the last α-helix of the compact fold and the adjoining low-complexity/disordered tail (often Lys/Arg-rich in histones) that mediates DNA/RNA binding or assembly interactions; the pattern generalizes to analogous C-terminal helix→IDR transitions in other small helical proteins.
3509.description:
Summary: Terminal helix-to-tail segments of small alpha-helical proteins—most prominently histone-fold proteins—where the feature marks the last α-helix of the compact fold and the adjoining low-complexity/disordered tail (often Lys/Arg-rich in histones) that mediates DNA/RNA binding or assembly interactions; the pattern generalizes to analogous C-terminal helix→IDR transitions in other small helical proteins.
Activation pattern: Regional, broad, and contiguous—often spanning nearly the full length of the small helical protein, with the strongest peaks concentrated at the C-terminal α-helix and adjacent low-complexity/disordered tail. Composition bias toward Lys/Arg and G/S/P/A in these tails; N-terminal basic tails of core histones also activate, generally at moderate levels.
Exemplars: - Core histones (H2A/H2B/H3; centromeric and testis-specific variants): peak activation on the C-terminal docking/α3 helix and Lys/Arg-rich tails, with additional activation on N-terminal basic tails.
- Kinetochore/repair histone-fold proteins (CENP-W/X/T; MHF1/2): activation on the C-terminal α-helix of the histone fold and the adjacent tail (e.g., strong C-terminal helix in MHF2).
- Histone-fold transcription factors (NF-Y subunits; NC2/DRAP1; TFIID/TAFs): activation on disordered terminal tails flanking the fold and occasionally overlapping the fold's terminal helix.
- Chromatin-associated small helical proteins (e.g., CAC 16 kDa subunit): activation across a C-terminal helical block and the following acidic disordered tail that modulates DNA binding.
- RNA polymerase small subunits (bacterial ω; archaeal Rpo4): activation across the C-terminal helical/coil segment that transitions into a disordered tail.
- Bacterial microcompartment/carboxysome shell proteins (BMC-H/EutM): activation on the C-terminal α-helix and flexible tail beyond the BMC domain.
- Ribosomal proteins (various): lower-level activation on basic terminal tails that contact rRNA.
- Archaeal and viral histones: strong activation on basic histone-like tails and terminal helices.

12804.label: Cysteine-rich LU/CRD domains
12804.summary: Small cysteine-rich, disulfide-bonded extracellular modules of the LU/uPAR three‑finger superfamily and closely related cysteine‑rich ECDs (e.g., toxin-like LU folds/CRDs), characterized by densely spaced cysteines interleaved with turn‑promoting residues; with occasional weak, off-target activation on short alpha‑helical segments in unrelated proteins.
12804.description:
Summary: Small cysteine-rich, disulfide-bonded extracellular modules of the LU/uPAR three‑finger superfamily and closely related cysteine‑rich ECDs (e.g., toxin-like LU folds/CRDs), characterized by densely spaced cysteines interleaved with turn‑promoting residues; with occasional weak, off-target activation on short alpha‑helical segments in unrelated proteins.
Activation pattern: Primarily domain-level activation across the mature extracellular cysteine‑rich domain (long, contiguous spans), excluding signal peptides and C‑terminal TM/GPI regions; secondarily, isolated residue-level peaks within short alpha‑helices in other folds.
Exemplars: Ly6/uPAR domain proteins (including three-finger toxin/LU-fold family): activation spans the extracellular LU domain, highlighting conserved disulfide-bonded cysteines and adjacent loops; TGF‑beta/BMP receptor cysteine‑rich repeats (CRDs): activation across the cysteine‑dense ECD modules; fungal hydrophobins: activation over the small secreted cysteine‑rich domain; ADF‑H/cofilin family: limited activation on the N‑terminal helix and adjacent residues of the ADF‑H domain; acyl‑CoA‑binding (ACB) proteins (e.g., Golgi ACBD3/GCP60): scattered peaks in an N‑terminal helical segment; globins: brief peak on a short helix within the globin fold; bacterial penicillin‑binding protein (PBP2): single‑residue peak within a periplasmic alpha‑helix.

6113.label: Proteolytic cleavage junctions and linkers
6113.summary: Proteolytic cleavage junctions—either intramolecular (autoproteolytic) or protease-mediated—and their immediately flanking hinge/linker segments at domain boundaries that partition large precursor or modular proteins into functional fragments, together with related ectodomain hinge/linker regions in single-pass membrane proteins. This prominently includes GPS/GAIN sites in adhesion GPCRs, FIIND (ZU5–UPA) autoprocessing in inflammasome adaptors, the Peptidase S59 cut that yields NUP98–NUP96, the C1/C2 cleavage boundary of cartilage intermediate layer proteins (CILP-1/CILP-2), ZU5-domain regions of netrin receptors and SH3BP4-like proteins, and protease-sensitive linkers in receptor ectodomains, secreted growth factors/enzymes, GPI-anchored ZP proteins, bacterial/viral secreted factors, and nuclear body proteins with caspase-cleavable low-complexity regions.

Summary: Proteolytic cleavage junctions—either intramolecular (autoproteolytic) or protease-mediated—and their immediately flanking hinge/linker segments at domain boundaries that partition large precursor or modular proteins into functional fragments, together with related ectodomain hinge/linker regions in single-pass membrane proteins. This prominently includes GPS/GAIN sites in adhesion GPCRs, FIIND (ZU5–UPA) autoprocessing in inflammasome adaptors, the Peptidase S59 cut that yields NUP98–NUP96, the C1/C2 cleavage boundary of cartilage intermediate layer proteins (CILP-1/CILP-2), ZU5-domain regions of netrin receptors and SH3BP4-like proteins, and protease-sensitive linkers in receptor ectodomains, secreted growth factors/enzymes, GPI-anchored ZP proteins, bacterial/viral secreted factors, and nuclear body proteins with caspase-cleavable low-complexity regions.
Activation pattern: Mixed—sharp residue-level peaks centered on the scissile bond or processing boundary with elevated activation across adjacent flexible linkers, tapering upon entry into the next structured domain; additionally, broad regional activation across ectodomains, flexible intracellular segments, or low-complexity regions that harbor protease sites (including caspase motifs), with weaker signal in transmembranes or repeat cores.
Exemplars:
- Adhesion GPCRs: maximal, localized signal at GPS/GAIN autoproteolytic junction (P1' Thr and neighbors).
- Inflammasome adaptors (CARD8/NLRP1): peak at FIIND ZU5–UPA autoprocessing site with elevated signal across UPA, loss in terminal CARD.
- Nucleoporins: rise through Peptidase S59 autoprotease with a peak at the NUP98–NUP96 cleavage boundary.
- Cartilage intermediate layer proteins (CILP-1/CILP-2): sharp peak at the C1/C2 cleavage boundary, with elevated activation across the C2 chain.
- Netrin receptors (UNC5 family): extended activation across cytosolic ZU5/Death-domain regions harboring protease sites.
- SH3BP4-like proteins: localized activation within the ZU5 domain.
- FAM171 family (FAM171A1/A2/B): broad activation across the extracellular ectodomain with strongest signal in a conserved hinge segment preceding the transmembrane helix.
- Secretin-like (class B) GPCRs: localized activation in N-terminal ectodomain hinge/linkers that are protease-sensitive.
- Secreted growth factors and ZP/GPI proteins (e.g., VEGF-C, uromodulin): peaks at propeptide/sheddase cleavage sites.
- Bacterial/viral secreted proteins and enzymes (e.g., GH101 hydrolases, SSLs): activation at propeptide removal or interdomain processing junctions.
- Nuclear body proteins (e.g., SP100/SP140 family): activation in low-complexity linkers enriched for caspase-cleavage motifs during regulated proteolysis.

10281.label: C-terminal noncatalytic accessory modules
10281.summary: C-terminal accessory/binding modules in multi-domain secreted enzymes and heme-binding cytochrome subunits; the feature marks non-catalytic regions in the C-terminal half of the protein and avoids the catalytic core of attached enzymes, spanning diverse secreted, membrane-associated, and soluble proteins.
10281.description:
Summary: C-terminal accessory/binding modules in multi-domain secreted enzymes and heme-binding cytochrome subunits; the feature marks non-catalytic regions in the C-terminal half of the protein and avoids the catalytic core of attached enzymes, spanning diverse secreted, membrane-associated, and soluble proteins.
Activation pattern: Regional activation over extended contiguous C-terminal segments; in carbohydrate-binding modules peaks concentrate on beta-strand elements with a conserved aromatic/hydrophobic core (W/F/M/I/V) within motifs such as "S(V/I)xWxD"; in cytochrome subunits peaks fall in extracellular/periplasmic chain regions distal to heme-binding residues.
Exemplars:
- Endo-1,4-beta-xylanase A/C (Paenibacillus, Thermotoga, Thermoanaerobacterium): peaks in C-terminal CBM-cenC domains on beta-strand residues within an aromatic-containing motif (e.g. SVxWxD, YSWSD).
- Cytochrome b558/566 subunit A (Sulfolobus acidocaldarius): activation distributed over the large extracellular domain with a C-terminal peak.
- Dimethylsulfide dehydrogenase / selenate reductase / chlorate reductase gamma subunits: peaks in a conserved C-terminal "ERDGLKxV" region of the heme-binding subunit.
- Cytochrome c-552 (Stutzerimonas stutzeri): peaks near the C-terminus distal to the heme-binding site.

10364.label: Secreted glycoprotein loop motifs
10364.summary: Signatures of secreted glycoprotein domains—typically within or immediately flanking beta-rich ligand/binding modules—and often within disulfide-bracketed regions of small cysteine-rich folds or adjacent glycosylated flexible loops; characteristic of ZP-domain glycoproteins, netrin-like (NTR) modules, fibrinogen-like domains, and some growth-factor folds involved in ECM interactions and secreted signaling.
10364.description:
Summary: Signatures of secreted glycoprotein domains—typically within or immediately flanking beta-rich ligand/binding modules—and often within disulfide-bracketed regions of small cysteine-rich folds or adjacent glycosylated flexible loops; characteristic of ZP-domain glycoproteins, netrin-like (NTR) modules, fibrinogen-like domains, and some growth-factor folds involved in ECM interactions and secreted signaling.
Activation pattern: Predominantly regional activation over compact secreted modules. Broad plateaus span whole NTR-type modules, with sharper residue-level peaks on loops bracketed by conserved cysteines/disulfides; in some ligands the feature extends over long, coil-rich, low-pLDDT, glycosylated segments adjoining a terminal Ig-like domain. Within compact domains (e.g., FGF, fibrinogen-like), activation narrows to one short loop—often including a disulfide or residues affecting secretion. Shorter, weaker hits can occur in extracellular loops of membrane proteins.
Exemplars: - ZP domain glycoproteins: strong regional signal in the C-terminal ZP-C subdomain between disulfide-bonded cysteines, including functionally critical loop residues.
- Tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases (TIMP): broad activation across the netrin-like (NTR) module of the mature inhibitor, peaking on a short loop bracketed by conserved disulfides (around the CSF/CGQ motif) and including residues that modulate metalloproteinase affinity.
- Angiopoietin/angiopoietin-like proteins: focused activation in a flexible loop of the fibrinogen-like domain containing a disulfide and secretion-critical residues.
- Fibroblast growth factors (FGFs): short, high-confidence peak on a structured surface loop within the FGF fold.
- EGF-family/neuregulin-like ligands with Ig-like modules (e.g., Vein): long activation over a coil-rich, N-glycosylated disordered stretch immediately preceding the Ig-like domain.

6038.label: β-sheet globular domain cores
6038.summary: Compact β‑sheet–dominated globular domain cores, most often from secretory‑pathway/extracellular proteins and frequently disulfide‑stabilized (cystatin, cystine‑knot and MRH lectin folds, RNase A–like), with spillover to intracellular β‑sheet–rich globular domains (e.g., NTF2‑like, WD40/β‑propeller, OB-/ribosomal cores) in cytosolic/mitochondrial proteins.
6038.description:
Summary: Compact β‑sheet–dominated globular domain cores, most often from secretory‑pathway/extracellular proteins and frequently disulfide‑stabilized (cystatin, cystine‑knot and MRH lectin folds, RNase A–like), with spillover to intracellular β‑sheet–rich globular domains (e.g., NTF2‑like, WD40/β‑propeller, OB-/ribosomal cores) in cytosolic/mitochondrial proteins.
Activation pattern: Domain‑level activation over long contiguous blocks (≈50–200 aa) corresponding to the folded core; peaks within β‑strands and around conserved cysteines in extracellular/lumenal contexts; avoids signal peptides, transmembrane segments, and low‑complexity tails; in type‑I membrane/lumenal factors, activation falls in mid‑sequence luminal domains; in cytosolic cases, activation centers on β‑sheet cores and can taper into adjacent disordered tails.
Exemplars:
- ER/Golgi glycan‑recognition/processing factors (OS‑9/XTP3‑B, mannose‑6‑phosphate receptor homology proteins, glucosidase II β, GNPTG): activation on the luminal MRH β‑sandwich lectin domain.
- Ribonuclease A superfamily: activation across the disulfide‑stabilized catalytic domain core.
- Cystatin/kininogen and cathelicidin pro‑regions (cathelin domain): activation over the cystatin‑like β‑sheet core.
- Cystine‑knot cytokines/growth factors (neurotrophins/Spätzle, DAN family BMP antagonists, IL‑17 family): activation on the cystine‑knot β‑sheet core.
- Antimicrobial/host‑defense peptide precursors (often defensin‑like): activation on the disulfide‑bonded β‑sheet region of the mature peptide/proregion.
- CD36/SNMP family receptors: activation restricted to the large extracellular ectodomain, including disulfide‑bonded and N‑glycosylated segments.
- mRNA export factor Mex67/TAP: activation on the C‑terminal portion of the NTF2‑like β‑sandwich domain, with reduced signal in adjacent disordered tail and no activation on LRR or TAP‑C regions.
- Intracellular β‑sheet scaffolds: WD40/β‑propeller proteins (e.g., RalGAPβ) and β‑rich ribosomal protein cores (e.g., mitochondrial mL45) show activation across their compact β‑sheet domains.

7192.label: Chromatin/DNA recognition domains
7192.summary: Chromatin/DNA-recognition segments of nuclear transcriptional regulators (and viral mimics), chiefly the cores of DNA-binding domains (ETS, IRF, HSF, BEN/SAND) and histone-mark reader bromodomains, sometimes extending into adjacent low-complexity regulatory tails used for cofactor/co-repressor recruitment
7192.description:
Summary: Chromatin/DNA-recognition segments of nuclear transcriptional regulators (and viral mimics), chiefly the cores of DNA-binding domains (ETS, IRF, HSF, BEN/SAND) and histone-mark reader bromodomains, sometimes extending into adjacent low-complexity regulatory tails used for cofactor/co-repressor recruitment
Activation pattern: Domain-level activation over long contiguous windows; strongest within structured cores (often the C-terminal half and helical subsegments) of these recognition domains, spanning multiple secondary-structure elements; frequently extends into immediately adjacent disordered/basic–acidic low-complexity tails; multiple activated regions per protein are common
Exemplars: - Bromodomain/BET–GTE proteins: C-terminal helices of the bromodomain and downstream segment
- BEN domain transcription factors: C-terminal helix of the BEN DNA-binding domain plus trailing tail
- ETS family transcription factors: C-terminal wing/β-sheet and helix of the ETS DNA-binding domain
- Heat shock factors: core of the HSF DNA-binding domain with a peak in a coil subsegment
- Viral interferon regulatory factors: C-terminal portion of the IRF tryptophan-pentad DNA-binding domain
- DEK chromatin proteins: a conserved central basic-hydrophobic motif (KKEEL/KKEDI…LEF) upstream of the DEK-C domain, with secondary activation across the DEK-C DNA-binding region
- Ski co-repressors: disordered repression/cofactor-binding regions in the C-terminus and a central low-complexity segment

7192.exemplar_protein_families:
- Bromodomain/BET–GTE proteins: C-terminal helices of the bromodomain and downstream segment
- BEN domain transcription factors: C-terminal helix of the BEN DNA-binding domain plus trailing tail
- ETS family transcription factors: C-terminal wing/β-sheet and helix of the ETS DNA-binding domain
- Heat shock factors: core of the HSF DNA-binding domain with a peak in a coil subsegment
- Viral interferon regulatory factors: C-terminal portion of the IRF tryptophan-pentad DNA-binding domain
- DEK chromatin proteins: a conserved central basic-hydrophobic motif (KKEEL/KKEDI…LEF) upstream of the DEK-C domain, with secondary activation across the DEK-C DNA-binding region
- Ski co-repressors: disordered repression/cofactor-binding regions in the C-terminus and a central low-complexity segment

1226.label: Short basic/aromatic interaction patches
1226.summary: Short basic/aromatic–enriched segments, typically at or just beyond catalytic domains and especially the retroelement integrase C‑terminal module (integrase CTD/GPY‑F region), that often occur as flexible coils or short helices and serve as DNA/chromatin- or partner‑interaction patches; the feature also recognizes analogous Trp‑rich motifs (e.g., PWWP‑like) in diverse proteins.
1226.description:
Summary: Short basic/aromatic–enriched segments, typically at or just beyond catalytic domains and especially the retroelement integrase C‑terminal module (integrase CTD/GPY‑F region), that often occur as flexible coils or short helices and serve as DNA/chromatin- or partner‑interaction patches; the feature also recognizes analogous Trp‑rich motifs (e.g., PWWP‑like) in diverse proteins.
Activation pattern: Domain‑scale, contiguous C‑terminal blocks in retroviral/retrotransposon Pol proteins mapping immediately C‑terminal to the integrase catalytic core (often low pLDDT, Lys/Arg and aromatic enriched, with GPY/GPF triplets); outside retroelements, shorter 10–20 aa windows or residue‑level peaks in flexible coils or short helices at termini or adjacent to catalytic elements; occasional single N‑terminal flexible segments.
Exemplars: - Retroviral/retrotransposon integrase within Pol polyproteins: strong domain‑level activation on the C‑terminal integrase DNA‑binding module (integrase CTD/GPY‑F region) immediately after the DDE catalytic core (Pro‑Pol polyproteins; endogenous retrovirus K integrase; gypsy integrase‑like proteins).
- PIF1‑family DNA helicases: short, unstructured basic/aromatic patch near the C‑terminus between secondary‑structure elements.
- Calpain‑like cysteine proteases: a localized short coil/helix immediately preceding the catalytic His within the peptidase C2 catalytic domain.
- NAD(P)H‑quinone oxidoreductase subunit O (NDH‑O): a short flexible N‑terminal segment comprising alternating short helices and coils.

16075.label: Charged β-edge cap motif
16075.summary: Short, charged β‑turn/β‑strand‑edge “cap” motif at the junction between a β‑strand and an adjacent loop (often a β–loop–β connector), especially in OB/S1‑like and related β‑sheet–rich domains; sequence preference for mixed acidic/basic residues with frequent Pro/Ser (e.g., E/D–x–R–P–L–S–[K/R]), used on exposed sheet edges that mediate nucleic‑acid or partner interactions.
16075.description:
Summary: Short, charged β‑turn/β‑strand‑edge “cap” motif at the junction between a β‑strand and an adjacent loop (often a β–loop–β connector), especially in OB/S1‑like and related β‑sheet–rich domains; sequence preference for mixed acidic/basic residues with frequent Pro/Ser (e.g., E/D–x–R–P–L–S–[K/R]), used on exposed sheet edges that mediate nucleic‑acid or partner interactions.
Activation pattern: Residue‑level peaks on short (∼7–12 aa) segments located at the end of a β‑strand, in a tight turn/loop connecting two β‑strands, or at coil→β transitions; usually one or a few localized peaks per protein; pLDDT high in strands and moderate/lower in the adjoining loop/turn.
Exemplars: - Translation initiation factor eIF1A (S1/OB‑like domain): turn linking adjacent β‑strands in the S1‑like core.
- Plant B3 DNA‑binding domain proteins: C‑terminal end of a β‑strand into the following loop within the B3 domain.
- SOSS/RMI complex OB‑fold subunits: short β‑strand/edge segment within the OB fold that contacts ssDNA.
- NAD‑dependent DNA ligases: flexible loop connecting two β‑strands within the DNA‑binding region.
- Proteasomal AAA+ ATPases: coil→β transition and a β–β connecting turn on the central β‑sheet.
- Ribosomal proteins (uS17/uS12, L14/L19, eS6): conserved charged β‑turn/strand‑edge motifs on exposed sheet edges (e.g., E–x–R–P–L–S–K in uS17).
- ssDNA/RNA‑binding proteins with OB/CSD or HIN domains (SSB, LIN28, PYHIN sensors): strand‑edge loops/turns that contact nucleic acids.
- GroES/Hsp10 and carboxysome shell vertex proteins: β‑hairpin/turn elements at oligomer interfaces exhibiting the same charged cap motif.

2289.label: Catalytic beta-strands and FN3
2289.summary: Beta-strand residues within structured domains of large secreted enzymes and accessory FN3/Ig-type modules; activation concentrates on short beta-strands of catalytic (β-propeller/β-barrel) folds and on FN3 domains appended to carbohydrate-active enzymes.
2289.description:
Summary: Beta-strand residues within structured domains of large secreted enzymes and accessory FN3/Ig-type modules; activation concentrates on short beta-strands of catalytic (β-propeller/β-barrel) folds and on FN3 domains appended to carbohydrate-active enzymes.
Activation pattern: Multiple discrete peaks distributed across several short beta-strands within a single structured domain, with high mean activation per strand; additional strong activation in FN3 modules when present; explicitly disordered/low-complexity regions are not activated.
Exemplars: - Secreted carbohydrate-active enzymes (rhamnogalacturonan lyases YesW/YesX, exo-β-1,2-glucooligosaccharide sophorohydrolase): activation on beta-strands of the catalytic β-propeller/β-barrel fold.
- Lysosomal glycoside hydrolases (alpha-L-iduronidase across human, mouse, dog, Drosophila): activation on C-terminal beta-strands of the accessory C-terminal domain, with overlap onto a long disulfide-bridged region.
- Multidomain bacterial amylopullulanase: strong activation across FN3 domains flanking the catalytic core.
- Bacterial peptidylarginine deiminase: activation on beta-strands of the C-terminal domain.
- Animal toxin precursors (latroinsectotoxin): activation in the N-terminal region near the first ankyrin repeat.

11087.label: Nucleic acid/mark recognition cores
11087.summary: Structured alpha/beta reader/binder surfaces that contact nucleic acids or chromatin modification marks—most strongly the cores of YTH/ASCH RNA-binding folds and BAH methyl-lysine readers—and analogous recognition/catalytic patches in DNA/RNA damage/processing factors (e.g., SRAP/HMCES, PriA, MazF); overall a nucleic-acid/mark-recognition motif enriched in aromatic and basic residues.
11087.description:
Summary: Structured alpha/beta reader/binder surfaces that contact nucleic acids or chromatin modification marks—most strongly the cores of YTH/ASCH RNA-binding folds and BAH methyl-lysine readers—and analogous recognition/catalytic patches in DNA/RNA damage/processing factors (e.g., SRAP/HMCES, PriA, MazF); overall a nucleic-acid/mark-recognition motif enriched in aromatic and basic residues.
Activation pattern: Primarily domain-level, contiguous activation across compact, well-ordered cores; residue-level peaks at aromatic-cage or catalytic beta-strand positions. Frequently near protein N-termini. Long continuous blocks in large eukaryotic chromatin/RNA regulators; shorter N-terminal patches in bacterial DNA/RNA enzymes and toxins.
Exemplars: - YTH m6A reader domain: strong activation over the RNA-binding core, including aromatic residues forming the m6A pocket.
- ASCH RNA-binding domain (EOLA1 family): activation over central beta-strand/helix elements of the structured RNA-binding core.
- BAH domains in CMT-type DNA methyltransferases and ORC1: activation across the N-terminal half of the BAH reader that engages methyl-lysine histone marks.
- SRAP (HMCES/YedK) abasic-site processing proteins: focused activation on the catalytic beta-strand region containing the acidic active-site residue.
- PriA replication restart helicase: activation on the N-terminal beta-sheet–rich subdomain preceding the helicase ATP-binding core, implicated in nucleic acid recognition.
- MazF family endoribonuclease toxins: N-terminal beta-strands and adjacent coil forming the RNA-binding/active-site framework are highlighted.
- ATP-sulfurylase (sulfate adenylyltransferase): activation on a structured N-terminal alpha/beta segment within the enzyme’s core.

10328.label: Hydrophobic surface β-strand/loop motifs
10328.summary: Short, surface-exposed β-strand/loop micro-motifs—often hydrophobic and frequently flanked by small/glycine residues—that shape active-site or protein/ligand-binding surfaces. The motif recurs across diverse secreted/periplasmic enzymes (notably β-lactamases and other hydrolases) and binding/scaffolding proteins, and can also appear as isolated hydrophobic β-strands in unrelated enzymes.
10328.description:
Summary: Short, surface-exposed β-strand/loop micro-motifs—often hydrophobic and frequently flanked by small/glycine residues—that shape active-site or protein/ligand-binding surfaces. The motif recurs across diverse secreted/periplasmic enzymes (notably β-lactamases and other hydrolases) and binding/scaffolding proteins, and can also appear as isolated hydrophobic β-strands in unrelated enzymes.
Activation pattern: Residue-level peaks confined to short segments (~6-20 aa; sometimes a single β-strand); multiple noncontiguous sites per protein; in many cases enriched for W/F/Y and Gly, but in others dominated by aliphatic Ala/Leu/Ile residues; typically on surface β-strands and adjoining loops that form binding pockets.
Exemplars: - Penicillin-binding proteins/transpeptidases and DD-carboxypeptidases: activation on short W/F/Y–G-rich loops/β-strands in the C-terminal transpeptidase domain that shape the peptidoglycan-binding pocket.
- β-Lactamases and β-lactam resistance sensors: activation on aromatic-glycine clusters (often WFG/WGW-type) in surface β-strands and neighboring loops that tune substrate specificity.
- Serpins (secreted serine protease inhibitors): activation on short aromatic/glycine-rich stretches within or adjacent to the reactive center loop that mediate protease binding and conformational switching.
- PsbP/OEE2 (thylakoid lumen): activation on exposed aromatic loop/strand segments implicated in docking to photosystem II.
- Other hydrolases (glycosidases, peptidases, metalloproteases): activation on short surface β-strands and adjoining loops that contribute to substrate positioning/entry.
- TRPM8 channel-associated factors and related M60-peptidase-containing proteins: paired hydrophobic β-strand segments (Ala/Ile/Leu-rich with adjacent Gly/Tyr) outside the catalytic domain.
- Glutamine amidotransferase/glutaminase domains: activation on glycine-rich oxyanion-hole/active-site loops with nearby aromatic residues around the catalytic cysteine.
- Biotin-protein ligase (BPL/LplA fold): a single, isolated N-terminal β-strand outside the catalytic domain is selected, illustrating the feature's focus on short surface β-strands.

11668.label: Structured beta-surface interaction patches
11668.summary: Structured interaction patches on ligand/partner-binding surfaces of diverse proteins—commonly beta-strand/loop–centered regions in beta-rich folds (CBMs, VHL beta-domain, Ig-/Siglec-like and jelly-roll modules) and ferredoxin-like modules, and analogous patches within the C-terminal sub-domain of secreted metallocarboxypeptidases; often positioned in mid-to-C-terminal portions and used for carbohydrate recognition or protein–protein docking; frequently found in secreted/surface-exposed proteins but also in intracellular complexes
11668.description:
Summary: Structured interaction patches on ligand/partner-binding surfaces of diverse proteins—commonly beta-strand/loop–centered regions in beta-rich folds (CBMs, VHL beta-domain, Ig-/Siglec-like and jelly-roll modules) and ferredoxin-like modules, and analogous patches within the C-terminal sub-domain of secreted metallocarboxypeptidases; often positioned in mid-to-C-terminal portions and used for carbohydrate recognition or protein–protein docking; frequently found in secreted/surface-exposed proteins but also in intracellular complexes
Activation pattern: Regional activation over a contiguous ~15–40 aa span with multiple peaks across neighboring beta-strands and loops (sometimes a short helix), concentrated in well-structured segments (pLDDT ≳60–80), with minimal signal in disordered termini or signal peptides
Exemplars:
- S-layer proteins: activation on beta-strand/coil interfaces mediating lattice contacts.
- VHL family: activation on the C-terminal portion of the beta-domain forming the HIF-binding face.
- AMPK/SNF1 beta subunits: activation within the KIS that docks the catalytic alpha subunit.
- CBM20/CBM48 modules and GH11 xylanases (and analogous patches in GH catalytic domains): activation across glycan-binding loops in beta-sandwich/jelly-roll or alpha/beta folds.
- SRR adhesins and fimbrial subunits: activation on Ig-/Siglec-like beta-sandwich domains mediating host adhesion.
- Metallocarboxypeptidases (e.g., CPN, CPE, CPM, CPZ, AEBP1): activation on a structured beta-strand-rich patch within the C-terminal sub-domain that follows the M14 catalytic domain.
- 2Fe-2S ferredoxin-like proteins and their cognate reductases (FNR systems): activation on segments adjacent to cofactor-binding loops that mediate partner docking.

10161.label: Diffuse intradomain activation
10161.summary: Broad regional activation across long internal stretches of large multidomain proteins, including CRISPR/anti-phage defense nucleic-acid–associated assemblies and large cytosolic regulatory/scaffolding proteins, as well as some soluble metabolic oxidoreductases. Activation often falls inside structured catalytic or NTPase domains rather than being restricted to terminal tails.
10161.description:
Summary: Broad regional activation across long internal stretches of large multidomain proteins, including CRISPR/anti-phage defense nucleic-acid–associated assemblies and large cytosolic regulatory/scaffolding proteins, as well as some soluble metabolic oxidoreductases. Activation often falls inside structured catalytic or NTPase domains rather than being restricted to terminal tails.
Activation pattern: Diffuse, high-coverage activation spanning hundreds of residues per protein, with strongest peaks distributed across α-helical and mixed α/β regions of large domains; not restricted to short catalytic motifs.
Exemplars: CRISPR Cas3 subtype I-F (HD Cas3-type domain), CRISPR Cmr2/Cas10 (helical regions), Druantia DruE helicase (helicase ATP-binding domain), Kinase D-interacting substrate Kidins220/ARMS (cytoplasmic loop within KAP NTPase domain), and soluble oxidoreductases such as nitrosuccinate synthase and oleate hydratase.

6849.label: Ser/Thr-rich disordered segments
6849.summary: Low-complexity and disordered segments, typically enriched in Ser/Thr and often Lys/Arg, including N-terminal signal/transit-like leaders and downstream propeptides, as well as internal disordered linkers, inserts, and basic/disordered tails of soluble proteins.
6849.description:
Summary: Low-complexity and disordered segments, typically enriched in Ser/Thr and often Lys/Arg, including N-terminal signal/transit-like leaders and downstream propeptides, as well as internal disordered linkers, inserts, and basic/disordered tails of soluble proteins.
Activation pattern: Regional activation often spans long continuous stretches with residue-level peaks within S/Thr-rich or basic runs; activation can begin at or near the initiator Met but also concentrates in internal disordered regions, domain "inserts," or mature peptide segments; strongest in low pLDDT, low-complexity segments and tapers within well-structured catalytic cores.
Exemplars:
- Secreted subtilisin-like proteases: activation over the signal peptide and peaking just after the cleavage site into the disordered propeptide.
- Apicomplexan mucin-like/repeat-rich surface antigens and adhesins: activation on S/Thr-rich, low-complexity N-termini following signal peptides.
- Viral envelope, capsid, and small regulatory proteins: activation on N-terminal signal peptides and/or basic, disordered N-terminal tails.
- Channels/transporters and small integral membrane proteins: activation on disordered S/Thr-rich N-terminal cytosolic or luminal tails, including signal anchors.
- Plastid-associated proteins (e.g., plastid RNA polymerase subunits in green algae): activation on low-complexity Ser/Thr- and/or Lys/Arg-rich extensions and internal disordered stretches.
- Methyltransferases and other enzymes with disordered N-terminal extensions or internal domain inserts: activation on low-complexity, basic/S/Thr-rich regions and "insert" subdomains.
- Cytosolic metabolic/regulatory and nucleic-acid enzymes: activation on short disordered terminal tails or internal low-complexity linkers.
- Neuropeptide and toxin precursors: activation on mature peptide segments and adjacent propeptide/leader regions.

4505.label: SH3 C-terminus and disordered linkers
4505.summary: Boundary regions of SH3-family modules and the immediately adjacent low-complexity/disordered segments in eukaryotic scaffold/signaling proteins (C-terminal edge of a canonical SH3 transitioning into a proline-rich linker/tail); in Gram-positive secreted/surface cell wall–associated proteins (peptidoglycan hydrolases, phage endolysins, and adhesins/invasins such as internalins) it corresponds to Gly/S/T-rich interdomain linkers and the termini of cell wall–binding repeat modules (e.g., SH3b, LysM, GW).
4505.description:
Summary: Boundary regions of SH3-family modules and the immediately adjacent low-complexity/disordered segments in eukaryotic scaffold/signaling proteins (C-terminal edge of a canonical SH3 transitioning into a proline-rich linker/tail); in Gram-positive secreted/surface cell wall–associated proteins (peptidoglycan hydrolases, phage endolysins, and adhesins/invasins such as internalins) it corresponds to Gly/S/T-rich interdomain linkers and the termini of cell wall–binding repeat modules (e.g., SH3b, LysM, GW).
Activation pattern: Regional activation in contiguous blocks that peak at the last β-strand(s)/C-terminus of an SH3 domain and extend into the following low-pLDDT disordered linker or tail; in Gram-positive proteins, strong activation across long low-complexity linkers between catalytic/adhesive domains and C-terminal cell wall–binding repeat arrays (SH3b/LysM/GW), often peaking at repeat boundaries/termini.
Exemplars:
- MAGUK/tight junction scaffolds: activation across the C-terminal half of the SH3 domain into the flexible linker; minor spillover to adjacent PDZ elements.
- NADPH oxidase organizers/activators (p47phox/p67phox/p40phox): activation at SH3 C-termini extending into disordered linkers/terminal regions.
- Peroxisomal import component PEX13: strong activation over the cytosolic SH3 C-terminus and trailing unstructured tail.
- RIM-binding proteins and other synaptic scaffolds: SH3 boundary regions and nearby proline-rich segments.
- Actin-cytoskeleton SH3-network adapters: SH3-proximal PRR/linker segments.
- Gram-positive cell wall proteins: peptidoglycan hydrolases and phage endolysins with SH3b/LysM repeats, and internalin-type adhesins with GW-repeat regions—activation on long low-complexity linkers and at repeat termini.

16129.label: Short hydrophobic junction motif
16129.summary: A short, hydrophobic secondary-structure junction motif: strand–loop and helix–coil boundary segments that cap or connect modular domains/repeats; in kinases, the conserved β3–αC ATP-binding unit. The feature marks β-sheet edge segments of β-sandwich and small β–α domains (FNIII, SH3, cadherin, RRM), the C-terminal ends of helical repeats (PPR, Sel1-like, ankyrin), and helix caps at membrane–loop junctions in multi-pass transporters, capturing short segments that pack domains/repeats or scaffold active sites.
16129.description:

- Cadherins: activation on a β-strand plus adjacent coil near the C-termini of extracellular cadherin repeats.
- Helical repeat proteins: activation at repeat C-termini and linkers in PPR, Sel1-like, and ankyrin repeats (e.g., IκB family).
- Multi-pass transporters/permeases: activation at transmembrane helix caps and adjacent loop/helix junctions.
- RNA-binding factors with RRMs (e.g., U2AF65): activation on β-sheet edge strands and flanking loops within RRM domains.
- Multi-domain scaffolds with SH3 and FNIII modules (e.g., RIM-binding proteins): activation on short β-strands with flanking loops within SH3 and FNIII domains.

8901.label: Extracellular non-catalytic motif activation
8901.summary: Regional activation within large secreted/periplasmic and membrane-associated enzymes and adhesins, typically firing on internal segments of structured catalytic or extracellular domains while sparing catalytic active sites and metal-binding residues.
8901.description:
Summary: Regional activation within large secreted/periplasmic and membrane-associated enzymes and adhesins, typically firing on internal segments of structured catalytic or extracellular domains while sparing catalytic active sites and metal-binding residues.
Activation pattern: Broad regional activation spanning many residues across the protein, with the strongest peaks clustering on short stretches of conserved sequence within structured domains; consistently avoids annotated catalytic and metal-binding residues, and frequently spares annotated disordered/low-complexity tails and linkers.
Exemplars:
- Glycoside hydrolases (cellulases/exoglucanases/endoglucanases): activation centered on a conserved internal motif within the catalytic domain (e.g. the "WETIP/WETVP" stretch in CelS, Exoglucanase-2, and Endoglucanase A), within β-strand-containing regions of the GH fold.
- Fungal β-glucosidases/glucosylceramidases: activation on an internal segment of the catalytic domain (e.g. an "HGVW" stretch), away from active-site nucleophiles.
- Type IV pilus adhesins (PilY1 family): regional activation in the structured N-terminal portion of the chain, with peaks near aromatic-rich stretches but not within the annotated disordered tails.
- Bacterial extracellular lipases: activation on an internal acidic/basic-rich disordered region between structured blocks of the enzyme.
- Periplasmic/outer-membrane lysophospholipases: regional activation on an internal segment within the mature chain, distinct from lipidation and active-site residues.

11044.label: Short acidic loop/turn motif
11044.summary: Short, solvent-exposed loop/turn acidic micro-motif: a short linear segment (≈10–30 aa) centered on a compact acidic/polar turn (Asp/Glu ± Thr/Asn), frequently but not invariably accompanied by a nearby aromatic residue (Tyr/Phe/Trp), and typically embedded in a Gly/Pro‑rich, mixed‑charge context (GP/PP, GxP, interspersed E/D and K/R). This generic loop/turn element recurs at interface/assembly or regulatory patches across unrelated proteins.
11044.description:
Summary: Short, solvent-exposed loop/turn acidic micro-motif: a short linear segment (≈10–30 aa) centered on a compact acidic/polar turn (Asp/Glu ± Thr/Asn), frequently but not invariably accompanied by a nearby aromatic residue (Tyr/Phe/Trp), and typically embedded in a Gly/Pro‑rich, mixed‑charge context (GP/PP, GxP, interspersed E/D and K/R). This generic loop/turn element recurs at interface/assembly or regulatory patches across unrelated proteins.

Activation pattern: - Single, contiguous 10–30 aa windows with residue‑level peaks at or immediately around a compact acidic (Asp/Glu ± Thr) turn; an adjacent aromatic is common but not required; often bracketed by Pro/Gly.
- Positional context varies by family: mid‑domain patches in many transcription factors and enzymes; stereotyped mid‑protein windows (~165–205) in geminiviral CP/NSP; near the extreme C‑terminus in LOX/LOXL; short internal blocks in some propeptides.
- Tends to prefer conserved loop/turn segments within structured regions or short regulatory inserts, rather than long low‑complexity stretches.

Exemplars: - Fungal Velvet complex regulators (VosA/VeA/VelB/VelC): a single patch within the Velvet domain enriched for Fhe adjacent to Asp/Glu and nearby Gly/Pro (e.g., F–G–K–D/E–H core).
- Vertebrate p53 family (p53/p63/p73): conserved mid‑chain loop in the DNA‑binding region bearing an aromatic–Asp/Thr pair.
- Lysyl oxidase family (LOX/LOXL): C‑terminal Cys–Tyr–Asp/Thr micro‑motif in the mature enzyme.
- Plant geminiviral capsid and nuclear shuttle proteins: short mid‑protein loops (~165–205) with mixed charge and GP motifs, frequently containing an aromatic with nearby Asp/Thr.
- Grainyhead/CP2 transcription factors (GRHL/LSF/CP2/UBP1): a compact conserved aromatic–Asp/Thr motif.
- Myelin regulatory factor (MYRF): central Pro/Thr‑rich stretch with a compact acidic turn; an aromatic may be absent.
- Signal peptidase complex subunit 3 (SPCS3): short mixed basic/acidic loop (≈110–130) matching the acidic/GP turn signature without requiring an aromatic.
- ER translocation/co‑chaperones (ERdj2/SEC63): gly/ala‑rich loops with a small/acidic residue, optionally near an aromatic anchor.
- Yeast arrestin‑like adaptors (ART/ROD/Ldb/Gid): Lys/Gly/Asp‑rich loop patches often containing an aromatic–acidic pair.
- Secreted/lysosomal and insect defense proteins (e.g., Hdd11‑like): compact Cys/Gly/Glu–Pro loops with nearby aromatics.
- Deuterolysin metalloproteases (neutral protease 2): a very short propeptide block (≈97–105) featuring a compact acidic stretch with nearby Tyr/Phe and Pro/Thr residues.
- Actinobacterial C‑glycoside deglycosidase β subunits: an acidic core immediately preceding a conserved aromatic pair or short cluster (commonly WF or WWF) within a single activated window.
- Mycobacterial porins and other structural proteins: GNGPG and related GP‑rich loop turns that match the same short loop/turn signature (aromatic often reduced or absent but the GP‑turn context preserved).

11554.label: Nucleic-acid binding and assembly tracks
11554.summary: Extended, compositionally biased (glycine- and charge-rich, Pro-frequent) surface/loop segments that form nucleic‑acid–binding tracks and protein–protein assembly interfaces in large macromolecular complexes—most prominently the crRNA‑binding ridges of CRISPR RAMP/Cascade subunits, but also analogous interfaces in RNA/DNA‑processing enzymes, polymerase/ribosome subunits, clamps, viral capsids, and certain protein-only scaffolds
11554.description:
Summary: Extended, compositionally biased (glycine- and charge-rich, Pro-frequent) surface/loop segments that form nucleic‑acid–binding tracks and protein–protein assembly interfaces in large macromolecular complexes—most prominently the crRNA‑binding ridges of CRISPR RAMP/Cascade subunits, but also analogous interfaces in RNA/DNA‑processing enzymes, polymerase/ribosome subunits, clamps, viral capsids, and certain protein-only scaffolds
Activation pattern: Regional activation over long, contiguous stretches spanning mixed secondary structure; peaks often center on coils/loops that adjoin helices/strands and can extend into low‑confidence/disordered tails; not confined to catalytic residues but to the continuous binding/assembly surface
Exemplars:
- CRISPR Type I/III RAMP/Cascade subunits (Cas5/Cas6/Cas7; Csm/Cmr): activation along the gly/charged loops and ridges that bind the crRNA backbone within Cascade/Csm/Cmr assemblies
- RNA adenosine deaminases (ADAR/ADAT; tRNA A37 deaminases): activation within the C‑terminal deaminase catalytic domain on loops that cradle the RNA substrate (e.g., the A‑to‑I “editase” region)
- RecBCD/Exonuclease V–like nucleases: activation on a contiguous, non–metal‑binding segment near the nuclease core consistent with a DNA‑contacting/assembly surface
- Large ribosomal subunit proteins (eL20/uL16): activation on rRNA‑contacting beta‑strands/turns within the ribosome
- RNA polymerase alpha/Rpo3 (bacterial, archaeal, plastid/mitochondrial): activation on basic/acidic surface patches used for nucleic‑acid engagement and subunit assembly
- tRNA pseudouridine synthases: activation on substrate‑recognition loops that position tRNA for modification
- KEOPS complex subunits (Kae1/Bud32/Pcc1 etc.): activation on tRNA‑binding and intersubunit assembly interfaces
- DNA sliding clamps and checkpoint clamps (β clamp/PCNA/9‑1‑1): activation on DNA‑facing basic patches and flexible loops that mediate partner binding
- Viral capsid/scaffolding proteins: activation on basic, gly/pro‑rich genome‑binding stretches and assembly scaffolds
- Polycomb/RING‑type E3 ubiquitin ligase components and plant VQ‑motif proteins: activation on low‑complexity charged/Pro‑rich segments that scaffold chromatin‑associated or transcriptional assemblies
- Cell‑cycle checkpoint proteins (e.g., MAD2/MCC components): activation on flexible, charged loops mediating partner capture and conformational switching
- Autophagy initiation complex components (e.g., ATG101/ATG13): activation on low‑complexity acidic/basic segments used for protein‑only scaffold assembly

213.label: RGG/GP-rich low-complexity IDRs
213.summary: An Arg/Gly/Pro-rich, mixed-charge low-complexity signature of eukaryotic nuclear and RNA granule–associated proteins—classically RGG/GAR- and related GP/PG-containing intrinsically disordered tracts used for RNA binding, RNP assembly, and granule scaffolding—with activation that can extend to nearby compact RNA-binding modules (e.g., RRM, RanBP2-type zinc finger) embedded in or flanked by such low-complexity context; also observed in non-RNA-binding disordered nuclear regulators (e.g., cancer/testis antigens).
213.description:
Summary: An Arg/Gly/Pro-rich, mixed-charge low-complexity signature of eukaryotic nuclear and RNA granule–associated proteins—classically RGG/GAR- and related GP/PG-containing intrinsically disordered tracts used for RNA binding, RNP assembly, and granule scaffolding—with activation that can extend to nearby compact RNA-binding modules (e.g., RRM, RanBP2-type zinc finger) embedded in or flanked by such low-complexity context; also observed in non-RNA-binding disordered nuclear regulators (e.g., cancer/testis antigens).
Activation pattern:
- Predominantly long, continuous activation over intrinsically disordered, low-pLDDT regions (often terminal tails), enriched for glycine with interspersed Pro and variable charge (often Arg/Lys but not required; RGG/GAR common but not obligatory).
- Local maxima at RG/RGG and GP/PG patterns; basic clusters (e.g., NLS-like patches) frequently included; mixed-charge acidic/basic segments can also activate.
- Suppressed in well-ordered globular domains, except moderate–strong activation in certain RNA-binding folds (RRM, RanBP2-type ZnF) and at domain–IDR junctions; prion-like Q-rich IDRs lacking Gly/Pro/RG are generally not targeted.
- Peaks often start near termini and/or at structured-to-disordered transition helices.
Exemplars:
- Poly(A)-binding protein–interacting scaffold (PBP1): strong, sustained activation across a long, disordered low-complexity C-terminal region; structured N-terminus largely inactive.
- LSm complex subunit (Lsm4): highest activation at the Sm-domain C-terminus and into the short helix that transitions to the disordered tail; remainder of the tail weak.
- UAP56-interacting factor (RNA export/splicing cofactor): low in structured N-terminus; high across a disordered, polar C-terminal region.
- Stem–loop binding protein (histone RNA hairpin-binding/SLBP): deactivated in the central ordered RNA-binding domain; maximal in the low-complexity C-terminal tail; moderate across N-terminal disordered/NLS-containing region.
- FET family RNA-binding protein (EWS): strong activation on the RRM and the RanBP2-type zinc finger (with peaks at Gly/Pro) and moderate over a C-terminal basic/NLS segment; low over the repetitive N-terminal low-complexity prion-like region.
- BEX adaptor proteins (brain-expressed X-linked): broad activation across low-complexity regions with basic/acidic bias, peaking near RG-rich/basic patches linked to nuclear localization; reduced over histidine/metal-binding clusters.
- Also consistent with LSM14/Scd6 (RGG-bearing granule proteins), RNAPIII small subunit C31 (basic/low-complexity tails), eIF4B (IDR- and RRM-junction activation), and Aly/REF/THOC4 (disordered mixed-charge regions).

2428.label: Short amphipathic interface elements
2428.summary: A conserved internal segment of small TRAPP-fold subunits, marking a beta-strand–containing core region used for complex assembly. The feature also extends to a broader set of short helical/strand interaction elements (coiled-coils, basic DNA/RNA-binding helices, BTB/H-NOX helices, signal/transit peptide flanks) across diverse proteins.
2428.description:
Summary: A conserved internal segment of small TRAPP-fold subunits, marking a beta-strand–containing core region used for complex assembly. The feature also extends to a broader set of short helical/strand interaction elements (coiled-coils, basic DNA/RNA-binding helices, BTB/H-NOX helices, signal/transit peptide flanks) across diverse proteins.
Activation pattern: Regional activation of a single contiguous window, typically centered around residues ~85-110 of small (~150-200 aa) subunits, peaking on a beta-strand flanked by short helices; charged residues adjacent to a hydrophobic core often carry the strongest activation; usually one activation window per protein.
Exemplars: - TRAPP complex subunits (TRAPPC3/BET3, TRAPPC5, TRAPPC6A/B, TRAPPC31): activation on an internal beta-strand region within the longin-like fold that mediates multisubunit assembly.
- Defensin-like peptide precursors and venom/antimicrobial toxins: activation on the N-terminal signal peptide and adjacent low-structured region around the cleavage site.
- Chloroplast/mitochondrial proteins: activation on Arg-rich amphipathic transit peptides at the extreme N-terminus.
- Soluble guanylate cyclase subunits (alpha/beta, invertebrate gcy): activation within the N-terminal H-NOX helical region that seeds dimerization/ligand sensing.
- BTB/POZ/KCTD family proteins: activation on the N-terminal BTB helical core used for oligomerization.
- Plant bHLH transcription factors: activation on the basic DNA-binding helix and adjacent HLH helix.
- Small bacterial antitoxins and transcriptional regulators: activation on the N-terminal HTH DNA-binding helix.
- Ribosomal proteins, initiation factors, RNase P/MRP subunits, helicases: activation on short basic/amphipathic helices or helical extensions that contact RNA and partner proteins.
- Alba-family nucleic-acid–binding proteins: activation on the N-terminal helix that interfaces with nucleic acids.
- tRNA modification/queuosine-thiolation components: activation on short N-terminal amphipathic helices used for partner/RNA engagement.
- Bacterial/archaeal cell division and nucleoid occlusion factors: activation on coiled-coil/dimerization helices near the N-terminus.

7453.label: N-terminal assembly leader
7453.summary: N-terminal/leader segments of bacteriophage and related bacterial assembly proteins, capturing the very start of the polypeptide where it forms the first short helix and the adjacent β-strand used for subunit assembly and chaperone interaction.
7453.description:
Summary: N-terminal/leader segments of bacteriophage and related bacterial assembly proteins, capturing the very start of the polypeptide where it forms the first short helix and the adjacent β-strand used for subunit assembly and chaperone interaction.
Activation pattern: Strong regional activation that typically starts at Met-1 and runs contiguously across the first 20–60 residues, peaking over the initial α-helix and tapering across the first β-strand; abrupt drop thereafter with little/no signal in the structured core. Activation tolerates N-terminal processing (Met excision, Nt-acetylation).
Exemplars: - Tailed bacteriophage tail tube/tip/terminator and baseplate proteins: activation on N-terminal leaders implicated in morphogenesis and assembly.
- Type VI secretion system Hcp/VgrG spike proteins: activation on the N-terminal strand of the spike/tube core.
- dsDNA virus capsid assembly proteins and head maturation proteases: activation on N-terminal propeptides/flexible regions that are targets of maturation proteolysis.
- Bacterial surface/secretion machinery (fimbrial/pilin systems and secretins): activation on leaders/linkers adjacent to targeting/assembly regions.
- Gasdermin family (eukaryotic and bacterial): activation around the disordered, acidic linker harboring the protease cleavage site separating N‑ and C‑terminal domains.
- DNA primase/primase‑like proteins (archaea/viruses/eukaryotes): activation on N-terminal tails used as flexible interaction regions.
- Phage single‑stranded DNA‑binding proteins: activation on terminal tails that mediate partner recruitment.
- Phage endolysins/peptidoglycan hydrolases: activation on N-terminal segments adjacent to catalytic/processing regions.
- SecB‑like chaperone (Rv1957): activation strictly confined to the first ~35 residues, peaking over the initial helix and decaying across the first strand, with no signal in the remaining structured core.

3749.summary: Feature for ZU5 domains and long mature segments of large secreted/cell-surface bacterial enzymes; activation centers on the conserved β-strand region near the N-terminal portion of ZU5 domains in eukaryotic ZU5-containing proteins (PIDD, MCC, SH3BP4, UNC-5 family) and on internal mature-chain segments of large secreted bacterial carbohydrate-active enzymes and surface-anchored hydrolases after signal peptide cleavage.

Activation pattern: Regional activation across tens to hundreds of residues; in ZU5-containing proteins, the strongest peaks fall within the ZU5 domain (commonly around a conserved DS/GG motif near its N-terminus); in large secreted bacterial enzymes, activation covers broad mature-chain segments while signal peptides and C-terminal LPXTG/sortase propeptides are not activated.
Exemplars:
- PIDD1 (human, mouse): peak within ZU5 domain 1 near residue ~325–335.
- SH3BP4 / MCC / related ZU5-containing scaffolds: peak within the single ZU5 domain at an analogous position.
- UNC-5 netrin receptor: activation across the cytoplasmic region with peak within the ZU5 domain.
- Surface-anchored bacterial hydrolases with LPXTG anchors (e.g., YfkN, fructan beta-fructosidase): broad activation through the mature chain; signal peptide and sortase-removed propeptide not activated.
- Large secreted carbohydrate-active enzymes (e.g., xylanase A, amylopullulanase): activation in interdomain mature-chain segments.
