5321.label: N-terminal domain-start leader regions
5321.summary: N-terminal leader/capping segments at the start of a protein or of a new domain, including pre-/pro-peptides, signal-anchor transmembrane helices with their flanking helices, and the first β/α elements that initiate the structured core; the feature emphasizes positional “domain/start-of-mature-chain” regions rather than catalytic metal-binding cores.
5321.description:
Summary: N-terminal leader/capping segments at the start of a protein or of a new domain, including pre-/pro-peptides, signal-anchor transmembrane helices with their flanking helices, and the first β/α elements that initiate the structured core; the feature emphasizes positional “domain/start-of-mature-chain” regions rather than catalytic metal-binding cores.
Activation pattern: Regional activation over a contiguous block (typically ~25–70 residues) at chain or internal domain starts; local peaks on the first β-strand or α-helix and adjacent stretches; sometimes spans a single-pass TM signal anchor with flanking amphipathic helices; activation drops off in the downstream catalytic/structured core. Can occur in disordered pre/pro-sequences or in well-structured leading elements.
Exemplars: - Acireductone dioxygenase family: strong activation across the N-terminal ~60 aa that precede the metal-binding core.
- Alpha-carbonic anhydrase proteins (including viral CA-like): activation on the N-terminal portion of the CA domain after any signal peptide, not on the zinc-binding core.
- Mitochondrial OXA1L insertase: activation centered on the sole transmembrane signal-anchor helix and its flanking helices at the start of the intermembrane domain.
- Small heat shock proteins (sHSPs): activation on the flexible N-terminal arm preceding the alpha-crystallin domain.
- Secreted lipid transfer/transfer protein precursors: strongest activation on the propeptide immediately after the signal peptide; mature domain has little to none.
- RNA polymerase small subunits: activation restricted to the first 30–40 residues forming the initial β/α elements.
- Lytic polysaccharide monooxygenases (chitin-binding type-4): activation at the start of the mature catalytic domain beginning at the copper-binding histidine and the adjacent initial strand/helix.

14887.label: Start of mature domain
14887.summary: Start-of-mature-domain segments, often the post‑signal‑peptide stretch or the first folded subdomain following an N‑terminal region: windows that frequently form the first helix or β‑strand of the mature domain, sometimes preceded by disordered low‑complexity tails enriched in small/polar residues (P/G/S/T/A). These regions mark the onset of a structured domain rather than catalytic cores, and often carry localization/export or assembly cues (e.g., secretion signals, transit/NLS motifs).

Activation tolerates both disordered, low‑complexity stretches and hydrophobic structured elements, and falls off in downstream catalytic/core domains and in C‑terminal regions.
Exemplars: - Type II restriction endonucleases: N‑terminal helical subdomain (e.g., residues ~5–70) preceding the catalytic Mg2+-binding core.
- Plant cell wall hydrolases (endo‑β‑1,4‑glucanases/xyloglucanases): post‑signal‑peptide N‑terminus spanning the first β‑strand/helix of the mature enzyme, not the catalytic glutamates.
- Viral capsid/coat proteins: early N-terminal segment including disordered tail and the first β‑strands of the jelly‑roll; structured capsid core not activated.
- Staphylococcal γ‑hemolysin and related pore‑forming toxins: N‑terminus of the mature secreted subunit immediately after the signal peptide, covering initial β‑sheet elements.
- ADP‑ribosyl cyclases/ectoenzymes: peak immediately after the signal peptide marking the start of the ectodomain; core catalytic residues not activated.
- Gram‑negative type III/IV effectors: extreme N‑terminal secretion/translocation signals enriched in small/polar residues and di‑glycine motifs.
- Gasdermins (bacterial/fungal): N‑terminal pore‑forming segments preceding the inhibitory C‑terminal domain.
- Glycolipid transfer proteins and other secreted/trafficking factors: N‑terminal segment that initiates the lipid‑binding/interaction domain.
- Large Gram-positive cell‑surface adhesins (e.g., antigen I/II family): activation centered on the first folded helical subdomain of the mature ectodomain rather than the extreme N‑terminus.

2191.label: N-terminal domain core detector
2191.summary: N-terminal “first-domain core” detector: the feature marks the initial structured block of the first globular domain after any leader segment, typically the opening α-helix and the N-terminal half of the ensuing core (often β-rich such as jelly-roll/lectin/C2-like), while de-emphasizing signal peptides, transmembranes, long disordered leaders, and frequently turning off at embedded catalytic/metal-binding motifs.
2191.description:
Summary: N-terminal “first-domain core” detector: the feature marks the initial structured block of the first globular domain after any leader segment, typically the opening α-helix and the N-terminal half of the ensuing core (often β-rich such as jelly-roll/lectin/C2-like), while de-emphasizing signal peptides, transmembranes, long disordered leaders, and frequently turning off at embedded catalytic/metal-binding motifs.
Activation pattern: Domain-level, contiguous segments biased to the N-terminus; often starts on the first α-helix and extends across early core strands/loops, with residue-level preference for small/polar/charged residues (Gly/Ser/Thr, Glu/Asp/Lys/Arg) and some aromatics. Typically off on signal peptides and transmembrane helices; may appear internally when a leader precedes the first folded domain. Frequently tapers or drops over conserved acidic/histidine motifs and other catalytic signatures.
Exemplars: - ER luminal lectins (OS-9/MRH family): activation on the helix preceding the MRH fold and the N-terminal half of the MRH core, including early carbohydrate-interacting residues, but not the later MRH conserved sites.
- Plant-pathogen Nep1-like cytolysins (NLPs): strong activation over the central β-sandwich core just after the disordered leader, peaking on the early helix/adjacent strands and turning off at the conserved undecapeptide and GHRHDWE motifs.
- Receptor-transporting proteins (RTP family): activation confined to the cytosolic N-terminal amphipathic helix and adjacent residues; absent from the downstream Zn-finger region and C-terminal transmembrane segment.
- Viral structural proteins (capsid/coat; bacteriophage tail/tube/fiber): highlights the N-terminal helix and early strands of the jelly-roll/β-solenoid-like core that nucleate assembly.
- Ciliary basal body proteins (B9/MKS1/tectonic-like): marks the N-terminal block of the B9/C2-like β-sandwich domain.
- Actin-binding ADF/cofilin/twinfilin/drebrin family: engages the N-terminal helix and the first β-strand region of the ADF-H fold that initiates the domain core.

8575.label: Conserved beta-sandwich Trp anchor
8575.summary: Conserved aromatic anchor (Trp, occasionally Phe/Tyr) in β-strands of extracellular β–strand–rich domains—especially FN3/Ig-like β-sandwiches, but also present in other β-strand repeat/beta-sandwich folds (e.g., SPRY/B30.2, LRR, and carbohydrate-binding β-sandwich modules)—prevalent in single-pass receptor ectodomains and related proteins.
8575.description:
Summary: Conserved aromatic anchor (Trp, occasionally Phe/Tyr) in β-strands of extracellular β–strand–rich domains—especially FN3/Ig-like β-sandwiches, but also present in other β-strand repeat/beta-sandwich folds (e.g., SPRY/B30.2, LRR, and carbohydrate-binding β-sandwich modules)—prevalent in single-pass receptor ectodomains and related proteins.
Activation pattern: Residue-level peaks centered on a tryptophan within an antiparallel β-strand of a β-sandwich (FN3/Ig/SPRY/CBM) or within the consensus β-strands of LRR repeats; often one peak per module, repeating across multi-domain ectodomains; absent from signal peptides, transmembranes, and cytosolic tails.
Exemplars: - Class I/II cytokine receptors (interleukin/interferon): strong peaks on W (sometimes F) in β-strands of FN3 ectodomains, often across successive repeats.
- LRIG family LRR–Ig single-pass receptors: dominant W peak in FN3/Ig-like β-strands, with weaker activation in adjacent modules.
- LRR-only ectodomain proteins (e.g., vasorin/slit-like): peaks on W in the β-strands of LRR repeats.
- FN3-containing regulatory/scaffold proteins (e.g., ATF7IP/ATF7IP2): localized W peak within an FN3 β-strand.
- TRIM/Midline E3 ligases with C-terminal SPRY/β-sandwich: single sharp W peak in a core β-strand.
- Secreted bacterial/phage proteins with FN3-/CBM-/β-sandwich modules: peaks on W within core β-strands.

8779.label: Conserved strand-loop edge motifs
8779.summary: Short conserved strand–loop micro-motifs typically enriched in Pro/aromatic/polar residues (e.g., H-(F/Y)-(T/S)-P or NDPNG-like signatures), located at junctions between secondary-structure elements. These segments frequently sit immediately adjacent to catalytic or ligand-binding loops in enzymes (prototypically the GH32/68 region neighboring the catalytic Asp and substrate-binding Trp), and analogous strand/loop edge motifs in other folds (e.g., beta-propellers) or just before transmembrane helices.

Activation pattern: Residue-level peaks confined to short (5–20 aa) segments, usually at a beta-strand/coil or helix/coil junction; peaks lie immediately adjacent to catalytic/ligand-binding sites or conserved sequence signatures (DP/NG, WD/YD) and can occur in flexible, lower-pLDDT regions adjoining structured elements.
Exemplars: - Fructosidases/levansucrases (GH32/68): strong activation on the short conserved loop just upstream of the substrate-binding region and catalytic Asp, spanning an aromatic–Pro–polar segment adjacent to the NDPNG/W motif.
- Cellulases (e.g., GH48 cellobiohydrolase): activation on the loop/strand segment harboring substrate-binding residues and adjacent catalytic Glu.
- Glucoamylases: activation across early strand–coil transitions within the catalytic domain, consistent with a conserved loop motif even when not individually annotated.
- Quinoprotein (PQQ) dehydrogenases: peak at a strand-to-coil boundary adjacent to the PQQ-binding site, centered on aromatic/glycine residues next to an acidic ligand-contact.
- Alpha-mannosidase I (type II membrane luminal enzyme): activation in flexible luminal loops preceding N-glycosylation sequons (N-X-S/T), consistent with conserved loop motifs at strand/coil boundaries near modification/binding sites.
- Cytochrome b (bc1 complex b subunit): activation on the N-terminal helix/coil segment immediately before the first transmembrane helix, at a conserved junction enriched in Pro/acidic/aromatic residues.
- Dynein intermediate chain/WD-repeat proteins: activation on a beta-strand/coil segment at the edge of or adjacent to the WD-propeller region, consistent with aromatic–acidic (WD/YD-like) strand-end motifs.

13803.label: Short exposed binding loops
13803.summary: Short, solvent-exposed loop/turn positions at domain surfaces that link secondary-structure elements or cap domain termini; these residues often form recognition/binding loops across diverse folds (e.g., SH3, blue-copper beta-sandwich, ribosomal proteins, helicase C-termini) rather than a specific sequence motif.
13803.description:

Activation pattern: Predominantly residue-level peaks concentrated in very short coil/loop segments (often low-to-moderate confidence), sometimes with weak flanking activation; occasional minor secondary peaks in adjacent strand/helix; no strong amino-acid bias and variable counts per protein.
Exemplars: PIF1-family 5′–3′ DNA helicases — surface loop residue with additional weak C-terminal activation near the DNA-binding region; SH3-domain signaling adaptors/scaffolds (e.g., MAGUKs, tight-junction ZO proteins, melanoma-derived growth regulatory protein) — hydrophobic loop residue within the SH3 barrel together with conserved Gly-rich loop peaks across the tandem PDZ domains; ribosomal protein uL24 (bacterial/organellar/archaeal) — hotspot in a flexible loop between the N-terminal helix and the beta-sheet; phytocyanin/early nodulin-like blue copper proteins — loop Trp (40–55) and loop Gly (80–100) flanking the copper-binding face; microtubule plus-end CAP-Gly/CLIP proteins — exposed binding loop of the CAP-Gly domain; additional represented classes (ARF transcription factors, YAK1-like kinases, MBT chromatin readers, RING-type E3 ligases, cobalamin-binding/transporters, secretion/export components) — single residues in surface loops adjacent to their binding or catalytic sites.

10731.label: Short motifs in structured/disordered regions
10731.summary: Feature highlights short, focused sequence motifs in a mixed set of contexts that include both compositionally biased disordered tails/linkers and structured segments embedded in larger multidomain proteins.
10731.description:
Summary: Feature highlights short, focused sequence motifs in a mixed set of contexts that include both compositionally biased disordered tails/linkers and structured segments embedded in larger multidomain proteins.
Activation pattern: Often sharp local peaks spanning ~5-10 contiguous residues, sometimes coinciding with short α-helical or β-strand elements within structured domains, and in other cases distributed over basic/proline-rich disordered stretches.
Exemplars:
- Cullin-7 (E3 ligase scaffold): strong, focused activation within the CPH domain on a short helix (~residues 360-376).
- 5'-3' exoribonuclease 1 (XRN1) across yeast, mouse, and human: peaks in a conserved central region around residue ~1090-1160.
- Plant U-box E3 ubiquitin ligases (PUB62/PUB63): activation on basic/polar segments in the C-terminal portion of the protein outside the U-box domain.
- Chloroplastic NDH subunit S: broad activation across a long Lys/Pro-rich disordered region, including basic-and-acidic and Pro-rich low-complexity stretches.

13024.label: SH3-like beta-loop motif
13024.summary: Beta-loop motif signature: the feature recognizes short loop/turn elements adjacent to β-strands that form ligand-binding surfaces in SH3-like domains and in analogous modular domains, uniting canonical eukaryotic SH3 domains with bacterial cell-wall–binding repeats (SH3b, LysM, and related peptidoglycan-binding modules) in Gram-positive hydrolases and phage endolysins, and a minor cohort of similar loops in other signaling proteins.

Activation pattern:
- Regional activation within short loop/turns near β-strands.
- Eukaryotes: short, localized peaks in SH3 loops/turns and in analogous surface loops of other signaling/scaffold domains (kinase accessory regions, MAGUKs, ankyrin/other repeats), often centered on a Tyr–Asp–[aromatic] or Tyr–Asp motif with nearby Gly; silent in unrelated regions (TPR, PB1, kinase catalytic core, long disordered segments).
- Bacteria/phages: extended, contiguous activation across C-terminal cell-wall–binding repeat arrays (SH3b, LysM, or related PG-binding repeats) of cell-envelope enzymes and endolysins; sequences enriched for small/polar/basic residues with recurring short patterns and aromatics; stronger magnitudes than eukaryotic matches.
- Plants (NDH/redox proteins): short activated surface loops bearing the same Tyr–Asp/aromatic-enriched motif.
Exemplars:
- SH3-containing adaptors/scaffolds (e.g., Intersectin, CRK/NCK, Beta-PIX) and PEX13: activation on SH3-domain loop/turns.
- NADPH oxidase subunits (p67phox, p40phox): activation confined to SH3 loops; absent from PB1, PX, TPR, and disordered regions.
- Nonreceptor tyrosine kinases without SH3 (e.g., TNK1): short activated loop in noncatalytic regions bearing the Tyr–Asp/aromatic motif.
- MAGUK scaffolds (e.g., PALS1): activation in the SH3 module loop.
- Gram-positive peptidoglycan hydrolases and phage endolysins (e.g., Bacillus LytG): extended activation across SH3b/LysM or related PG-binding repeat arrays.

1326.label: Buried hydrophobic core packing
1326.summary: Residue-level detector of buried hydrophobic side‑chain packing in well‑ordered secondary‑structure elements (primarily alpha‑helices but also beta‑strands) that form the structural cores of globular domains; broadly distributed across proteins (with enrichment in helical small‑GTPase regulatory domains such as RhoGAP) and not tied to a specific catalytic chemistry.

Activation pattern: Discrete, sparse residue-level peaks (most often Leu, Val, Phe, and sometimes Cys) repeated across multiple sites within structured domains; strongest in high‑confidence regions (high pLDDT), largely absent from disordered tails; peaks can appear adjacent to active or ligand‑binding motifs but reflect local packing rather than a specific active site; multiple peaks per protein, often in mid/late sequence positions of large multidomain proteins.
Exemplars: Rho family GTPase-activating proteins (RhoGAP domain): multiple peaks on Cys/Leu residues across separate alpha‑helices within the GAP fold; Metacaspases (cysteine-protease–like): aliphatic/aromatic residues across the alpha/beta catalytic core with a minor peak near the catalytic His; Kinesin motors and CH-domain cytoskeletal regulators: Leu/Val peaks in CH-domain helices and within motor-domain helices/sheets, with occasional signal in a structured loop near the ATP‑binding site; Fibroblast growth factors (FGF, beta‑trefoil): sparse peaks on Leu/Val within beta‑strands and adjacent coil segments of the trefoil core.

1587.label: Beta-edge interaction loops
1587.summary: Exposed β-sheet edge/β-hairpin loop segments within β‑rich domains (β‑sandwich/jellyroll/ferredoxin‑like folds) that form interaction patches for adhesion or ligand binding. The segments are short β‑strands flanked by turns/loops, enriched in turn‑favoring residues (G, P, T) and often containing aromatics (Y/F/W); they occur in both secreted structural proteins and intracellular scaffolds across taxa.

Exemplars: - Gram-negative fimbrial adhesin (Yersinia pH 6 antigen): activation on a C‑terminal loop linking two β‑strands of the adhesin’s β‑sheet, consistent with an interaction/adhesive patch.
- Type III CRISPR RAMP subunit Cmr6: activation on the C‑terminal β‑strand plus adjacent coils of a ferredoxin‑like β‑sheet surface.
- Fungal Velvet regulator (VelC): activation within the Velvet β‑sandwich over short β‑strands and connecting loops likely at a dimer/interface surface.
- Ephrin-B3 receptor‑binding domain: activation on a flexible loop between β‑strands in the extracellular jellyroll that contacts Eph receptors.
- p53 DNA‑binding core: activation on a β‑strand/loop segment (including Zn‑binding cysteines) that forms part of the nucleic‑acid/protein interaction surface.

2014.label: Disordered N-terminal assembly/export tail
2014.summary: Short, intrinsically disordered N-terminal pre-domain segments (MoRF-like assembly/export tails) of virion structural and bacterial extracellular/appendage proteins, typically the first 10–30 residues immediately after the initiator methionine or the signal peptide cleavage site; compositionally enriched for alternating hydrophobic and charged/polar residues and marking the boundary before the first stable secondary-structure element.

Summary: Short, intrinsically disordered N-terminal pre-domain segments (MoRF-like assembly/export tails) of virion structural and bacterial extracellular/appendage proteins, typically the first 10–30 residues immediately after the initiator methionine or the signal peptide cleavage site; compositionally enriched for alternating hydrophobic and charged/polar residues and marking the boundary before the first stable secondary-structure element.
Activation pattern: Strong regional activation as a contiguous block at the extreme N-terminus, peaking in the first few residues and dropping to baseline at the start of the first helix/strand; occasionally additional weaker activation at distal low-structure segments near intramolecular chaperone/autocleavage regions in very large fiber/spike proteins.
Exemplars: - Bacteriophage tail spike/fiber proteins: activation on the disordered N-terminal segment that initiates the mature chain and precedes the structured domains.
- Phage tail tube and tail sheath proteins: activation confined to short unstructured N-terminal tails that precede the highly structured cores.
- Phage baseplate proteins: activation on the N-terminal coil region that ends where the first helix begins.
- Capsid decoration proteins: activation on polar, intrinsically disordered N-termini.
- Flagellar hook-associated protein 2 (HAP2/FlgL family): activation on the unstructured N-terminal export/assembly signal.
- Type III secretion translocon pore (SctB/YopB/IpaB family): activation on the N-terminal secretion signal required for export (deletions abolish secretion).
- Autotransporter adhesin/protease (Peptidase S6 passenger): activation at the start of the mature passenger domain immediately following the signal peptide, including a short, low-confidence strand.

3390.label: Trp-rich polymer-binding modules
3390.summary: Tryptophan-rich substrate-binding surfaces of secreted polymer-degrading and adhesive proteins—principally carbohydrate-binding modules (CBM18/14/5/12, LysM/CBM50; hevein-like lectins) and analogous W/G/T/P-rich regions in bacteriophage tailspikes/fibers and other extracellular depolymerases (e.g., poly(3-hydroxybutyrate) depolymerases)—characterized by recurrent WG/WT motifs and aromatic stacking residues.

Exemplars:
- Chitinases (GH18/GH19) with CBMs (CBM5/12/14/18): activation on chitin-binding modules and adjacent W-rich segments.
- Plant/fungal chitin-binding lectins (hevein-like, peritrophins) and LysM effectors: activation across hevein/CBM18 or LysM repeats in secreted precursors.
- Cellulases, xylanases, and mannanases with CBMs (e.g., CBM1/2/3/4/6/10): activation on Trp-rich carbohydrate-binding modules.
- Bacteriophage tailspike/tail fiber polysaccharide-depolymerases: activation along beta-helix carbohydrate-binding/depolymerase tracts enriched in WG/WT motifs.
- Non-carbohydrate depolymerases such as PHB depolymerases: activation over W-rich polymer-binding/accessory domains.
- Minor cross-activation: intracellular W-motif modules (WW/CW/PWWP) and WGR/GRF-like nucleic-acid–binding repeats where WG/WxG motifs recur (e.g., ZGRF1).

3703.label: Organelle mature domain activator
3703.summary: Mature, structured domains of organelle-targeted precursor proteins (predominantly plant chloroplast and mitochondrial), with strong preference for conserved functional cores (DNA/RNA‑binding motifs, catalytic folds, and transmembrane helices) and avoidance of N‑terminal transit peptides and extended low‑complexity tails.
3703.description:
Summary: Mature, structured domains of organelle-targeted precursor proteins (predominantly plant chloroplast and mitochondrial), with strong preference for conserved functional cores (DNA/RNA‑binding motifs, catalytic folds, and transmembrane helices) and avoidance of N‑terminal transit peptides and extended low‑complexity tails.
Activation pattern: - Domain-level: Off across N-terminal chloroplast/mitochondrial transit peptides and other low-complexity segments; turns on within the mature protein.
- Regional: In soluble proteins, broad activation over conserved domains with peaks at hallmark functional motifs (e.g., polymerase core-binding segments, helix–turn–helix DNA-binding, P‑loop/switch regions, SAM-dependent catalytic loops). In membrane proteins, sustained activation across transmembrane helices and immediately flanking residues (often strongest at or just inside TM boundaries).
- Residue-level: Internal residues favored; peaks frequently occur on basic (Lys/Arg) positions within nucleic-acid–binding/catalytic motifs and on hydrophobic residues within TM spans; family-specific positional clusters are common, with most proteins showing a few sharp peaks and a minority displaying dense activated stretches.
Exemplars: - Chloroplast RNA polymerase sigma factors (Sig family): activation across the C‑terminal sigma region, highlighting the polymerase core‑binding segment and DNA‑binding H‑T‑H; silent on the N‑terminal transit peptide.
- Chloroplast mechanosensitive ion channels (MSL family): high signal through the membrane-embedded core (TM helices and adjacent residues), minimal on the transit peptide and long disordered C‑terminal tail.
- Mitochondrial rRNA methyltransferases and ribosome assembly factors: activation on the conserved catalytic fold/RNA‑binding surfaces of the mature enzyme; not on organelle presequences.
- ERA-family organellar GTPases: activation on the P‑loop NTP‑binding fold (Walker A/B and switch regions) within the mature domain.
- Organelle transporters and lipid/cofactor biosynthesis enzymes: activation within TM segments for transporters and within conserved catalytic cores for enzymes.
- Chloroplast RNA processing/splicing and nucleoid-associated proteins: activation on nucleic‑acid–binding modules within the mature region (e.g., HTH/helical bundles), with transit peptides de-emphasized.

4021.label: Extracellular glycan recognition modules
4021.summary: Surface/exposed recognition and carbohydrate-binding modules, plus a recurring C-terminal acidic motif: the feature marks proteins that present disulfide-stabilized cysteine-rich repeats (EGF, LDLR class A, CCP/Sushi, TSR, PSI/SEMA) and β-sheet carbohydrate-binding modules (CBMs and β-helix/β-sandwich tips), encompassing ECM glycoproteins/receptors, complement/MAC components, secreted metalloproteases/regulators, bacterial adhesins/CAZymes, phage tail fibers/baseplate components involved in host or glycan recognition, and a recurring acidic C-terminal segment in chloroplastic RuBisCO activase.

Activation pattern: Primarily domain-level activation across repeated extracellular/exposed modules with residue-level peaks on aromatic/hydrophobic residues (V/L/I/W/Y) in β-strand contexts that create glycan-binding/adhesive surfaces, and additionally on disulfide-bonded cysteines in some modules; in very large secreted proteins, multiple domains light up along the sequence; occasionally broad regional activation on acidic/threonine-rich, O-glycosylated segments of extracellular matrix proteins.
Exemplars: • Complement/MAC pathway components and regulators: activation on CCP/Sushi and EGF/TSR clusters mediating protein–protein recognition and assembly
• ADAMTS metalloproteases and TIMP-like inhibitors: activation on thrombospondin type-1 repeats and adjacent cysteine-rich ancillary domains
• ECM glycoproteins and guidance receptors (thrombospondins, spondins, semaphorins/plexins, netrin receptors, LDLR-family): activation on EGF, LDLR class A, TSR, PSI/SEMA cysteine-rich repeats
• Adhesion GPCRs and other secreted receptors: activation across disulfide-rich N-terminal modules that mediate ligand/ECM binding
• Bacteriophage tail spikes/tail fibers/baseplate proteins: activation on β-helix/β-sandwich carbohydrate-binding tips enriched in W/Y/F/L/V used for host glycan recognition, with additional peaks on disulfide cysteines in baseplate wedge components
• Bacterial CAZymes (glycosidases/lyases) with CBMs: activation on β-strand catalytic-region motifs and aromatic/hydrophobic subsites that stack with sugars
• Gram-positive surface adhesins (LPXTG-anchored MSCRAMMs): activation on Ig-like/lectin-like binding domains and glycan-binding patches
• Lectins and glycan-targeting domains (e.g., C-type lectins, CBM families): activation on Ca2+- and disulfide-stabilized folds and aromatic carbohydrate-contact residues
• Chloroplastic RuBisCO activase: activation on a conserved C-terminal acidic/disordered tail
• Dictyostelium extracellular matrix proteins: widespread activation on acidic/Thr-rich, heavily O-glycosylated segments involved in matrix adhesion

4025.label: Extracellular Cys–Trp disulfide-loop motif
4025.summary: Extracellular Cys–Trp (CW/CGW) disulfide‑loop signature common to secreted and single‑pass cell‑surface proteins and small cystine‑rich peptides; the feature highlights cysteine- and aromatic‑enriched ectodomain motifs used in adhesion, receptor–ligand/contact interfaces, and immune‑evasion coats (e.g., VSGs, semaphorins/plexins, integrins, RTKs, viral envelope glycoproteins)

- Semaphorin and plexin receptors: peaks at conserved CW/CGW sites in Sema/PSI ectodomains.
- Viral envelope/spike glycoproteins: activation on disulfide‑stabilized surface loops containing Cys–Trp and nearby aromatics.
- Integrin beta subunits: activation within extracellular PSI/I‑EGF repeats at CW/CGW motifs.
- Receptor tyrosine kinases and related single‑pass receptors: peaks on extracellular cysteine‑rich segments bearing CGW/CW signatures.
- Disulfide‑rich secreted peptides (toxins, cyclotides, defensins‑like): localized peaks where Trp neighbors disulfide‑bonded cysteines.
- Kinetoplastid hexose transporters: activation in extracellular loops containing the conserved C…W motif.
- Adhesion/glycocalyx components (e.g., mucins/proteoglycan core proteins): activation on cysteine/aromatic‑rich ectodomain motifs.

4272.label: Aromatic hydrophobic core tracts
4272.summary: Hydrophobic/aromatic-rich, well-ordered segments within soluble, folded domains that form packed cores and adjacent interaction patches (β-strand clusters or amphipathic α-helices), sometimes coinciding with ligand/protein-binding surfaces but not specific to any single fold; occurrence is enriched in certain domains (e.g., YTH and La/HTH RNA-binding domains, calponin-homology actin-binding domains, PP2A activator PTPA, and small GTPase regulator folds) but is not ubiquitous across all family members or orthologs.
4272.description:
Summary: Hydrophobic/aromatic-rich, well-ordered segments within soluble, folded domains that form packed cores and adjacent interaction patches (β-strand clusters or amphipathic α-helices), sometimes coinciding with ligand/protein-binding surfaces but not specific to any single fold; occurrence is enriched in certain domains (e.g., YTH and La/HTH RNA-binding domains, calponin-homology actin-binding domains, PP2A activator PTPA, and small GTPase regulator folds) but is not ubiquitous across all family members or orthologs.

Activation pattern: Regional activation in contiguous 15–40 aa blocks confined to high-confidence structured regions; spans runs of β-strands plus short connecting loops or a single long α-helix; peaks typically on L/I/V/F/W within hydrophobic runs with occasional acidic residues. A necessary discriminator is the presence of a Trp- or Phe-containing hydrophobic tract (≥1 W/F and multiple L/I/V/F within the block); proteins lacking this tract—even within the same fold—show no activation. Disordered regions are not activated; large multidomain proteins may show multiple, widely separated activated blocks when such tracts are present.

Exemplars: 
- YTH RNA-binding domain: activation across a triad of β-strands near the m6A-binding pocket when a W/F-rich hydrophobic tract is present; many YTH proteins without this tract show no activation.
- La/HTH (La-type) RNA-binding domain in LARP proteins: activation on a hydrophobic β-strand-to-helix segment containing a Trp/Phe-rich run; absence of this run yields no activation in other LARPs.
- Calponin-homology (CH) actin-binding domain: activation on a core amphipathic α-helix when it contains the requisite hydrophobic/aromatic pattern; CH-containing or other actin/cytoskeletal proteins lacking the motif are not activated.
- PP2A activator PTPA: activation on a long core α-helix only in subsets of orthologs bearing the hydrophobic/aromatic tract; others show no activation.
- Small GTPase regulator folds (e.g., VPS9/Rab5 GEFs, RasGAP/IQGAP-like): activation on hydrophobic interface patches when the tract is present; many paralogs/orthologs lack activation.

4817.label: Extracellular beta-sandwich domains
4817.summary: Beta-strand signatures of extracellular beta-sandwich domains—principally immunoglobulin-like (C2/I-set) and fibronectin type III modules—and related accessory beta-sandwich folds (e.g., CBMs, jelly-roll, cupredoxin-like) appended to secreted, surface, or capsid proteins, marked by short aromatic/charged residue clusters
4817.description:
Summary: Beta-strand signatures of extracellular beta-sandwich domains—principally immunoglobulin-like (C2/I-set) and fibronectin type III modules—and related accessory beta-sandwich folds (e.g., CBMs, jelly-roll, cupredoxin-like) appended to secreted, surface, or capsid proteins, marked by short aromatic/charged residue clusters
Activation pattern: Residue-level peaks in short 3–7 residue segments confined to beta-strands; repeated across successive Ig/FN3 repeats. 4965.label: Regulatory all-alpha helical cores
4965.summary: Alpha-helical bundle/repeat cores within regulatory domains of eukaryotic proteins—leucine‑rich, hydrophobic all‑alpha segments that form ligand‑binding, dimerization, and partner‑interaction surfaces (and sometimes catalytic cores), often in the C‑terminal regions of signaling, transcription, and scaffold proteins.
4965.description:
Summary: Alpha-helical bundle/repeat cores within regulatory domains of eukaryotic proteins—leucine‑rich, hydrophobic all‑alpha segments that form ligand‑binding, dimerization, and partner‑interaction surfaces (and sometimes catalytic cores), often in the C‑terminal regions of signaling, transcription, and scaffold proteins.
Activation pattern: Long, contiguous domain-level activation across well-folded helical regions (tens to hundreds of residues), with peaks on helices and short connecting loops; little to no activation in disordered segments or non-helical modules; frequently biased toward C‑terminal halves and can occur in multiple helical blocks per protein.
Exemplars: RhoGAP regulators: activation within a helical subregion of the RhoGAP catalytic domain (C-terminal portion in Bem3). RGS proteins: activation across the C-terminal half of the all‑alpha RGS domain (RGS9). Nuclear receptors: strong activation over the helical ligand‑binding domain while sparing the DNA‑binding domain (ecdysone receptor). Translation scaffolds (eIF4G): activation on MIF4G and MI/W2 HEAT-like helical modules, but not on disordered N‑termini. HECT E3 ubiquitin ligases: activation across the C‑terminal HECT domain including the catalytic region. AP‑2 family transcription factors: activation on the C‑terminal helix‑span‑helix dimerization domain. MOB kinase activator-like adaptors: activation on a compact helical core region that includes metal‑binding histidines.

5059.label: Focal activation on structured segments
5059.summary: Feature highlights short structured segments within large multi-domain proteins, including ankyrin repeats in spider latrotoxins and discrete secondary-structure elements (helices/strands) in large viral capsid/enzyme proteins.
5059.description:
Summary: Feature highlights short structured segments within large multi-domain proteins, including ankyrin repeats in spider latrotoxins and discrete secondary-structure elements (helices/strands) in large viral capsid/enzyme proteins.
Activation pattern: Focal peaks concentrated within a single repeat or secondary-structure element rather than spanning long disordered tracts; peaks land on residues such as N, Y, L, K, G, W, F across the targeted segment.
Exemplars:
- Spider latrotoxins (delta-latroinsectotoxin, alpha-latrotoxin): activation concentrated within the first ankyrin repeat or upstream contiguous segment, not on the cleaved C-terminal propeptide.
- Reovirus outer capsid protein lambda-2: activation over defined helices and strands in the N-terminal portion of the protein.

5127.label: Nucleic acid beta-strand hotspots
5127.summary: Short β-strand–centered hotspots within nucleic-acid–related modules, prominently the BAH reader domain of histone-associated factors, with additional analogous short β-strand/loop patches in nucleic-acid binding and processing enzymes.
5127.description:
Summary: Short β-strand–centered hotspots within nucleic-acid–related modules, prominently the BAH reader domain of histone-associated factors, with additional analogous short β-strand/loop patches in nucleic-acid binding and processing enzymes.
Activation pattern: Residue-level peaks in short 10–30 aa stretches, often multiple per protein; peaks align to β-strands and adjacent loops within these modules, with occasional weaker signals elsewhere in the same fold. Peak residues are typically aliphatic/hydrophobic positions (G/I/L/V/T) on the strand rather than a fixed sequence motif.
Exemplars:
- BAH domains of SNT2-family chromatin factors (S. cerevisiae SNT2; S. pombe Lid2C component Snt2): strong peaks on a β-strand within the BAH module.
- Cryptic loci regulator Clr2: peaks on annotated β-strands of a putative reader fold.
- 5'-3' exoribonuclease XRN1 (human, mouse, S. pombe): conserved hotspots on short β-strand/loop segments in the C-terminal half of the enzyme.
- DExH-box RNA helicases (e.g., Arabidopsis DExH11/SKI2 homolog): short β-strand patches outside the core helicase ATP-binding region.
- Other large chromatin/scaffold factors (e.g., BAZ1B): localized hotspots in short β-strand/loop segments.

5755.label: Surface-exposed ligand-binding regions
5755.summary: Surface-exposed receptor/substrate recognition regions of extracellular proteins, with a primary focus on glycan-binding/depolymerizing receptor-binding domains of bacteriophage tail spikes/fibers, and analogous exposed loops or binding patches in viral capsids, Gram-negative autotransporter adhesins, and secreted carbohydrate-active enzymes.
5755.description:
Summary: Surface-exposed receptor/substrate recognition regions of extracellular proteins, with a primary focus on glycan-binding/depolymerizing receptor-binding domains of bacteriophage tail spikes/fibers, and analogous exposed loops or binding patches in viral capsids, Gram-negative autotransporter adhesins, and secreted carbohydrate-active enzymes.
Activation pattern: Regional activation across long, solvent-exposed loops or beta-strand–rich tracts; frequent residue-level peaks on Ser/Thr/Gly and acidic residues; often concentrated in N-terminal passenger/adhesin regions of virion/OM adhesins. The feature tends to avoid catalytic motifs and intramolecular chaperone (peptidase S74) segments, and prefers flexible/disordered loops (low pLDDT) or non-catalytic substrate-binding patches.
Exemplars: - Bacteriophage tail spike/fiber receptor-binding proteins and capsule depolymerases (Enterobacteriaceae phages, e.g., Klebsiella K-type depolymerases): activation on central receptor-binding segments that form polysaccharide-contacting surfaces; not in the C-terminal intramolecular chaperone (S74) or mapped catalytic residues.
- Distal long tail fiber gp37 homologs: activation along receptor-contacting stretches that engage LPS/O-antigen.
- Trimeric autotransporter adhesins (YadA/BtaE-like): activation on exposed loops within the N-terminal passenger domain; minimal in the C-terminal beta-barrel translocator.
- Eukaryotic virus capsid proteins (adenovirus hexon): activation on hypervariable, surface-exposed loops.
- Secreted carbohydrate-active enzymes (glycoside hydrolases, polysaccharide lyases, cutinase-like esterases): activation on non-catalytic substrate-binding clefts/patches (e.g., cutinase substrate-binding region), not on catalytic triads or signal peptides.
- Rare intracellular proteins show isolated single-residue peaks, likely incidental rather than functional.

6332.label: Extracatalytic beta-sheet regional activation
6332.summary: Regional activation over extended beta-strand/coil architectures (beta-hairpins and beta-solenoids) occurring as long contiguous segments, typically outside catalytic cores; prototypical in phage tailspike/depolymerase beta-helix repeats and also present as non-catalytic insertions/linkers in diverse NTP-binding enzymes and translation factors.
6332.description:
Summary: Regional activation over extended beta-strand/coil architectures (beta-hairpins and beta-solenoids) occurring as long contiguous segments, typically outside catalytic cores; prototypical in phage tailspike/depolymerase beta-helix repeats and also present as non-catalytic insertions/linkers in diverse NTP-binding enzymes and translation factors.
Activation pattern: Regional activation over tens of residues in continuous stretches; strongest over beta-strands and hairpins within beta-sheet/solenoid regions or in flexible linker regions; usually away from P-loop/GTPase active sites and other catalytic motifs, frequently at N- or C-terminal accessory regions or domain insertions.
Exemplars: - Bacteriophage tailspike/depolymerases (capsule serotype–specific glycan depolymerases): activation across the parallel beta-helix/beta-solenoid repeat cores.
- Phage structural proteins (tail tips, baseplates, capsid components): long beta-strand/coil segments.
- AAA+ peroxisomal ATPases (PEX1/PEX6): extended N-terminal regions and flexible linkers; not the AAA+ P-loop core.
- Translation factors (IF2/eIF2 gamma, SelB, EF-like GTPases): C-terminal beta-sheet regions outside the tr-type GTPase domain.
- Polynucleotide 5'-hydroxyl-kinase/Clp1/Grc3/NOL9: C-terminal beta-strand/coil blocks away from the NTP-binding catalytic residues.
- Replicative DNA polymerases/helicases (often intein-bearing): beta-hairpin insertions and beta-strand/coil regions outside the catalytic center.
- ATP synthase F1 alpha/beta subunits: extended beta-strand segments in beta-sheet-rich regions rather than catalytic loops.
- Coilin and other Ser/Thr-rich nuclear proteins: long segments consistent with flexible linkers/regions prone to beta-prone/disordered behavior.

7411.label: Short surface-exposed interfacial motifs
7411.summary: Short surface-exposed segments on multi-domain and secreted/cell-surface proteins, including a conserved Pro/Asp/Ser-rich interfacial motif in subtilisin-family serine protease precursors and basic/aromatic patches in C2-domain membrane dockers and extracellular precursors.
7411.description:
Summary: Short surface-exposed segments on multi-domain and secreted/cell-surface proteins, including a conserved Pro/Asp/Ser-rich interfacial motif in subtilisin-family serine protease precursors and basic/aromatic patches in C2-domain membrane dockers and extracellular precursors.
Activation pattern:
- Residue-level peaks confined to short (≈5–15 aa) segments, often a single discrete patch per large multi-domain protein
- Localized to exposed loops and secondary-structure transitions (beta-to-coil) with lower structural confidence/flexibility
- In C2 contexts, maps to calcium/lipid-binding loops and/or polybasic faces that contact acidic phospholipids
- Frequently lies outside catalytic peptidase, HECT, or ABC transporter cores, though occasional overlap with metal-coordinating residues is observed
- Can occur near N-termini or scattered internally as separate interface-targeting micro-motifs
Exemplars:
- C2-domain membrane dockers (NEDD4-family/HECW E3 ubiquitin ligases, aex-1-like proteins): activates within the C2 domain on lipid-binding loop/polybasic faces
- Subtilisin-family serine protease/ABC transporter precursors (Dictyostelium tagA/B/C/D): a conserved internal "TDPP[A/S]GS" motif, separate from the peptidase S8 catalytic core and the transmembrane/ABC modules
- Secreted/cell-surface precursors (Delta-like ligands, treponemal membrane antigen): picks short N-proximal or surface-helix segments, often containing dibasic clusters or basic-aromatic character, implicated in interfacial association
- Membrane trafficking and phosphoinositide-pathway enzymes: highlights short polybasic–hydrophobic segments that recruit to anionic phospholipids, separate from catalytic residues
- Gram-positive cell-surface/secreted systems (e.g., teichoic acid poly(glycerol phosphate) polymerase; cellulosomal/carbohydrate-active modules): activates on aromatic/hydrophobic loop segments at beta-to-coil junctions that contact membranes or anionic polysaccharides

7734.label: Autoproteolysis and protease-sensitive linkers
7734.summary: Proteolytic-maturation and junctional protease-sensitive modules: structured segments that mediate or flank cis-autoproteolysis or regulated limited proteolysis that splits or remodels proteins—most prominently the GAIN/GPS site of adhesion GPCRs, ZU5/UPA (FIIND-like) regulatory modules, and the nucleoporin peptidase S59 autoprotease—with analogous cleavage‑proximal regions in secreted/luminal precursors and protease-sensitive interdomain linkers in cytosolic junctional MAGUK scaffolds (e.g., PDZ–SH3–GUK).
7734.description:
Summary: Proteolytic-maturation and junctional protease-sensitive modules: structured segments that mediate or flank cis-autoproteolysis or regulated limited proteolysis that splits or remodels proteins—most prominently the GAIN/GPS site of adhesion GPCRs, ZU5/UPA (FIIND-like) regulatory modules, and the nucleoporin peptidase S59 autoprotease—with analogous cleavage‑proximal regions in secreted/luminal precursors and protease-sensitive interdomain linkers in cytosolic junctional MAGUK scaffolds (e.g., PDZ–SH3–GUK).
Activation pattern: Primarily long regional activation (tens to >100 aa) concentrated within autoproteolytic/processing domains or immediately adjacent segments; sharp residue-level peaks on short β-strands or helices that harbor or flank the scissile bond; often multiple activated windows per protein; strongest in extracellular/luminal N-termini and in cytosolic FIIND-like modules, and also present in MAGUK PDZ–SH3–GUK supramodular linkers; sequences enriched for Cys and aromatic residues, with nearby His/Gly and occasional Ser/Thr/Pro-rich tracts.
Exemplars: - Adhesion GPCRs: Activation across the GAIN-B/GPS region, peaking on the GPS β-strand and spanning the autoproteolytic cleavage site; signal drops at the start of the Stachel peptide.
- UNC5 netrin receptors (dependence receptors): Strong signal within the cytosolic ZU5 domain overlapping NF-κB partner-binding residues, consistent with recognition of ZU5/UPA (FIIND-like) regulatory/autoprocessing modules; low at catalytic residues of adjacent peptidase elements.
- Nuclear pore nucleoporins (Nup98–Nup96/Nup145 system): Activation confined to the peptidase S59 autoprotease region responsible for self-cleavage that generates the two nucleoporins.
- Zona pellucida/ECM glycoproteins: Activation on cysteine- and aromatic-rich extracellular segments near proprotein convertase cleavage regions that enable maturation/polymerization.
- Inflammasome regulators (e.g., NLRP1/CARD8/PIDD1): Signal on the central FIIND (ZU5–UPA) domain that undergoes autoproteolysis.
- Tight junction MAGUKs (e.g., ZO-1/2/3): Activation on PDZ–SH3–GUK supramodular linkers known to be protease-sensitive during junction remodeling.

9634.label: Viral capsid structural proteins
9634.summary: Viral structural proteins, predominantly capsid/coat proteins from a broad range of viral families (dsRNA reoviruses, ssDNA parvoviruses, papillomaviruses, caliciviruses, ssRNA picobirnaviruses, and ssDNA bacteriophages). Activation is broadly distributed across the folded capsid domain rather than localized to a single short motif.
9634.description:
Summary: Viral structural proteins, predominantly capsid/coat proteins from a broad range of viral families (dsRNA reoviruses, ssDNA parvoviruses, papillomaviruses, caliciviruses, ssRNA picobirnaviruses, and ssDNA bacteriophages). Activation is broadly distributed across the folded capsid domain rather than localized to a single short motif.
Activation pattern: Broad regional activation covering most of the protein chain (often 80-100% of residues active), with the strongest peaks falling inside the structured capsid core on annotated helix, strand, and turn elements. Disordered N-terminal tails and low-complexity stretches, when present, tend to show weaker activation than the structured interior.
Exemplars:
- Reoviridae inner capsid proteins (e.g., reovirus lambda-1, aquareovirus VP3): strong activation across the central structured capsid domains.
- Bacteriophage capsid proteins (e.g., phiX174 capsid protein F): activation concentrated in the folded shell region rather than on terminal arms.
- Parvovirus VP1 proteins (Aleutian mink disease parvovirus, parvovirus LuIII, hamster parvovirus H1): activation across the VP1 core, with disordered N-terminal tails showing comparatively lower activation.
- Papillomavirus L1 major capsid proteins (HPV31, HPV58): activation across L1 core β-strand/helix elements.
- Calicivirus capsid proteins (feline calicivirus VP1): activation across the mature capsid region.
- Picobirnavirus capsid protein: activation across the structured capsid chain.

9903.label: Extended assembly interface regions
9903.summary: Extended assembly-interface regions of large multimeric machines (rings/pores/tubes), typically long and often N‑terminal stretches that scaffold or gate the complex—covering pore‑lining helices/strands, clip/stem interfaces, glycine‑rich assembly switches, and disordered linkers—rather than catalytic cores.
9903.description:
Summary: Extended assembly-interface regions of large multimeric machines (rings/pores/tubes), typically long and often N‑terminal stretches that scaffold or gate the complex—covering pore‑lining helices/strands, clip/stem interfaces, glycine‑rich assembly switches, and disordered linkers—rather than catalytic cores.
Activation pattern: Regional activation across tens to hundreds of residues with a bias toward N‑termini; local peaks at helix↔strand transitions, glycine‑rich loops (e.g., Walker A), and membrane‑embedded helices or beta‑strands that form or gate pores; minimal activation outside these assembly/gating segments.
Exemplars: - Phage portal proteins: strong activation on the N‑terminal clip/stem region that docks to the capsid and forms the DNA translocation/gating interface (peak across a helix→strand transition).
- Dynamin-like large GTPases: activation on the Walker A (G1) phosphate‑binding loop within the dynamin GTPase domain, a nucleotide‑controlled assembly switch (minor signal on G2; little on G3–G5).
- Mechanosensitive channels (e.g., YbiO/MscM family): activation on long transmembrane alpha‑helices forming the pore and gating bundle.
- Outer membrane usher proteins (pilus ushers): activation across a beta‑strand–rich segment of the N‑terminal/periplasmic assembly platform that recruits chaperone–subunit complexes.
- Cohesin/condensin kleisin subunits (e.g., Rec8): activation on an extended, low‑pLDDT disordered linker that tethers SMC heads and mediates complex assembly.

10592.label: Edge coil-to-beta transitions
10592.summary: Short coil-to-beta transition motif at edge beta-strands of beta-rich domains, including small beta-barrels (e.g., SH3, OB, Tudor/MBT) and beta-sandwich readers (e.g., BAH), and also peripheral edge beta-strands within larger alpha/beta enzymes or scaffolds (e.g., kinesin motor cores, RNase II S1/KH accessories).
10592.description:
Summary: Short coil-to-beta transition motif at edge beta-strands of beta-rich domains, including small beta-barrels (e.g., SH3, OB, Tudor/MBT) and beta-sandwich readers (e.g., BAH), and also peripheral edge beta-strands within larger alpha/beta enzymes or scaffolds (e.g., kinesin motor cores, RNase II S1/KH accessories).
Activation pattern: Highly localized peaks in 6–20 aa coil→beta transitions at conserved edge strands; often one peak per repeat; strongest at domain boundaries or peripheral edge strands; generally avoids active-site loops even within catalytic domains; minimal signal in long disordered regions or purely helical repeats.
Exemplars:
- Tudor/MBT readers: repeating peaks at the N-terminal edge strand of each repeat; no activation in OTU catalytic cores.
- Retroviral integrase: strong peak at the end of the catalytic core entering the SH3-like CTD; minor peaks in other short coil/beta segments.
- Plant ARFs: short, well-structured beta-strand peaks in the central region; absent from B3 and PB1.
- Chromatin regulators with BAH domains (e.g., CMT1, PBRM1): peaks on BAH edge strands; no signal in helical bromodomains.
- Ubiquitin pathway proteins: peaks on beta-sandwich or small beta-barrel accessory modules (e.g., CAP-Gly in CYLD) rather than in RING/USP catalytic cores; E3s like MIB2 show peaks in short beta-strands of accessory regions.
- Nucleic acid/metabolic enzymes: RNase II family and P-loop NTPase motors (e.g., KIF2C) show peripheral edge-strand peaks away from active-site motifs.

10881.label: Bacterial extracellular surface segments
10881.summary: Surface-accessible segments of secreted/extracellular and outer-membrane bacterial proteins, including both flexible disordered loops/tails and exposed structured loop/turn regions, while sparing catalytic residues, cofactor-binding motifs, and signal peptides.
10881.description:
Summary: Surface-accessible segments of secreted/extracellular and outer-membrane bacterial proteins, including both flexible disordered loops/tails and exposed structured loop/turn regions, while sparing catalytic residues, cofactor-binding motifs, and signal peptides.
Activation pattern: Regional activation forming multiple patches per protein, often centered on loops, turns, or short surface elements (sometimes within disordered regions, sometimes adjacent to or within structured strands/turns); minimal activation in signal peptides and at active/cofactor-binding sites.
Exemplars:
- Outer-membrane c-type cytochromes (OmcS, OmcB): activation across extended surface segments; absent at CXXCH heme-binding motifs.
- Subtilisin-family extracellular proteases (Aeromonas ASP, microbial serine proteinase): activation in surface loops within the Peptidase S8 domain, including segments bracketed by a disulfide bond, while charge-relay catalytic residues remain silent.
- Type IV pilus biogenesis factors PilY1 homologs: activation on disordered/polar loop regions of the extracellular passenger; Ca2+-binding residues silent.
- Autotransporter IgA1 protease and minor fimbrium subunit Mfa5: activation on exposed loop segments of the passenger/adhesin domains.

11088.label: N-terminal assembly/attachment segment
11088.summary: N-terminal segments of phage structural/assembly proteins that precede and delimit the first folded domain; in many proteins these regions function as assembly/attachment segments that mediate interaction with partner structural proteins (e.g., baseplate hubs, fiber adapters), as well as export/targeting signals (e.g., signal peptides) in some secreted proteins, with analogous N-terminal segments in other proteins also triggering activation.
11088.description:
Summary: N-terminal segments of phage structural/assembly proteins that precede and delimit the first folded domain; in many proteins these regions function as assembly/attachment segments that mediate interaction with partner structural proteins (e.g., baseplate hubs, fiber adapters), as well as export/targeting signals (e.g., signal peptides) in some secreted proteins, with analogous N-terminal segments in other proteins also triggering activation.
Activation pattern: Regional activation concentrated in a contiguous block at the extreme N-terminus (often ~10–40 residues but variable, sometimes much longer), frequently overlapping a short N-terminal alpha-helix or coiled-coil leader and sometimes extending into the adjacent assembly region; activation typically drops at the boundary with the first well-structured catalytic/receptor-binding domain. In large multidomain tail spikes/depolymerases, additional internal or C-terminal linkers can also activate.
Exemplars: - Bacteriophage baseplate wedge proteins: activation on a short N-terminal helical/leader segment involved in baseplate assembly.
- Bacteriophage side tail fiber proteins and gp38 receptor-recognizing proteins: activation on the N-terminal segment containing residues that mediate attachment to the fiber/baseplate adapter.
- Phage capsular depolymerases/tail spikes: activation confined to the short N-terminal attachment region immediately upstream of the catalytic domain, with deactivation at the catalytic domain start.
- Gram-negative autotransporter adhesins: activation within the N-terminal Sec-type signal peptide.
- Plant AT-hook transcription factors: activation on a compositionally biased, disordered N-terminal tail preceding the AT-hook and downstream folded domains.

12275.label: Extracellular Cys-rich ectodomains
12275.summary: Extracellular/cell-surface secretome signature: the feature recognizes ectodomains of secreted or surface-presented proteins, especially cysteine-rich, disulfide-stabilized peptides and repeats (e.g., toxins, EGF/disintegrin/adhesion modules, lectins), C-terminal regions surrounding GPI-anchor attachment sites, and also short exofacial loops of multi-pass membrane proteins when these loops are cysteine- and/or glycan-rich; it captures appended extracellular carbohydrate-binding modules of secreted CAZymes

Activation pattern: Primarily regional/domain-level activation over long, contiguous stretches of extracellular sequence (often at protein termini), with residue-level peaks near Cys clusters and adjacent residues (aromatics/Pro/Ser/Thr); frequently highest around the GPI omega site and drops within cleaved C-terminal propeptides; can cover complete mature secreted peptide chains or selectively highlight appended extracellular modules (e.g., CBMs) rather than catalytic cores; additionally, can mark short exofacial loops (not necessarily at termini) in multi-pass transporters when they contain Cys–Cys/Cys-x(n)–Cys or NXS/T glycosylation motifs
Exemplars: Trypanosome variant surface glycoproteins (VSGs) – strong activation across the disordered C-terminal GPI-anchor region, peaking at the omega site and disappearing in the cleaved propeptide; Ciliate mating pheromones – activation across the mature secreted cystine-rich peptide with peaks at N-terminal aromatic residues and reduced signal on disulfide-bonded cysteines; Secreted carbohydrate-active enzymes – activation on C-terminal CBM10 carbohydrate-binding modules and adjacent helices, not on the catalytic cores; Disulfide-rich venom peptides and Kunitz/other protease inhibitors – extended activation across the mature, disulfide-stabilized chains; Viral envelope/entry glycoproteins – activation on cysteine-rich ectodomain loops; EGF-like/disintegrin/adhesion modules and lectins – activation on cysteine-constrained extracellular repeats/domains; SLC/GLUT-family transporters – activation on short extracellular loops bearing conserved disulfide-bonded cysteines and glycosylation sites

12467.label: Subunit assembly interface belts
12467.summary: Subunit-assembly interface segments of extracellular/virion macromolecular structures—especially bacteriophage structural proteins and their bacterial analogs—capturing the N-/C‑terminal polymerization modules and beta/alpha interface patches that build capsids/coats, contractile tails/sheaths (and Type VI sheaths), portals/baseplates/adapters, tail fibers/fimbrial adhesins, and S‑layer lattices.

12486.label: Extracellular disulfide-bonded repeats
12486.summary: Detector of disulfide‑bonded cysteine‑rich modules in secreted/extracellular proteins, activating on the conserved Cys frameworks and β‑strand/turn cores of small extracellular repeats such as VWF C/chordin modules, EGF‑like repeats, thrombospondin type‑1 repeats (TSR), CCP/Sushi (complement control) repeats, SRCR domains, and cysteine‑rich serine protease inhibitor folds (Kunitz/Kazal/WAP/antistasin), including viral mimics of these modules

Summary: Detector of disulfide‑bonded cysteine‑rich modules in secreted/extracellular proteins, activating on the conserved Cys frameworks and β‑strand/turn cores of small extracellular repeats such as VWF C/chordin modules, EGF‑like repeats, thrombospondin type‑1 repeats (TSR), CCP/Sushi (complement control) repeats, SRCR domains, and cysteine‑rich serine protease inhibitor folds (Kunitz/Kazal/WAP/antistasin), including viral mimics of these modules

12856.label: EGF C2–C3 loop motif
12856.summary: Disulfide-braced loops of extracellular cysteine-rich modules, most prominently the C2–C3 loop of EGF-like domains that carries the O-fucosylation site and (in cbEGF modules) Ca2+-binding determinants; peaks center on the third conserved cysteine and nearby S/T, Asp/Asn, Gly/Pro, or His residues; repeated across tandem EGF repeats, with similar signal also occurring in other compact disulfide-rich scaffolds (e.g., Kunitz/Kazal, TIL, cyclotides) and occasional weaker matches in CCP/Sushi modules and in disulfide-bonded beta-sandwich domains (e.g., Ig-like, CUB)

- Selectins and LDL receptor family members: dominant peaks within EGF-like domains, plus weaker periodic hits in successive CCP/Sushi repeats
- EGF-repeat–containing secreted regulators (e.g., WIF1, cbEGF-bearing developmental modulators): localized activation at the N-terminal end of cbEGF modules including paired cysteines and nearby His/Asp residues
- Small cysteine-rich toxins and protease inhibitors (e.g., cyclotides, Kunitz/Kazal/TIL inhibitors): activation on short disulfide-braced loops centered on conserved cysteines
- Ig-superfamily/FNIII adhesion proteins and CUB-domain proteases: occasional activation adjacent to the conserved disulfide within Ig-like or CUB domains

14110.label: Proteolytic maturation domain hotspots
14110.summary: Proteolytic processing hotspots in large secreted/extracellular or virion-associated proteins and select intracellular scaffolds—long, structured segments that undergo or neighbor maturation cleavages into separate chains. This includes autoprotease modules (e.g., GAIN/GPS in adhesion GPCRs, FIIND in NLRP1, Peptidase S59 in Nup98/116, ZU5 autoproteolytic domains in UNC5/ankyrin/PIDD-family scaffolds) and non-enzymatic processing sites (convertase/caspase/metalloprotease/furin cleavages) in adhesion/scaffold receptors and ECM modules.

- Adhesion GPCRs: activation across GAIN-B immediately N-terminal to GPS autoproteolysis, tapering at the cleavage edge.
- Nucleoporins: strong signal on the Peptidase S59/NRM autoprotease core in Nup98/116 and on adjacent/derived structured regions in related nucleoporins (e.g., Nup96).
- NLRP family: FIIND autoproteolysis segments highlighted (e.g., NLRP1).
- ZU5-containing scaffolds and receptors (UNC5, SH3BP4, MACC1, PIDD1): contiguous hotspots spanning the ZU5 autoproteolytic domain.
- ECM modules (Frizzled-like, ZP proteins, CILP-family): hotspots near documented convertase/metalloprotease/caspase processing regions or within mature cleavage-derived chains.

- Phage baseplate/fiber/tail-spike proteins: autochaperone/autoproteolytic maturation segments within assembly modules highlighted.

14134.label: Ser/Thr-rich regulatory IDRs
14134.summary: Long, low-complexity intrinsically disordered regulatory segments of eukaryotic signaling proteins—especially fungal serine/threonine kinases and MAPK-pathway components—enriched in Ser/Thr/Pro (often Q/N) and populated with phosphosites and short linear motifs—most often at N-termini, but also sometimes central or C-terminal—adjacent to or flanking folded catalytic/signaling domains.

Activation pattern: Regional activation across these IDRs (from termini or interdomain linkers), with sub-peaks over Ser/Thr-rich tracts and SLiMs; near-zero activation within downstream or neighboring folded domains; segment length ranges from tens to hundreds of residues and is independent of local secondary-structure predictions.
Exemplars: - MAPKK of the HOG pathway (Pbs2): activation on the long disordered regulatory/scaffold region; no activation on the kinase domain
- Wee1 family checkpoint kinase: broad activation across the N-terminal IDR; inactive on the catalytic domain
- Haspin/ALK1 kinase: activation on the N-terminal IDR containing KEN/D-box degrons; absent in the kinase domain
- AGC kinases (Ypk3): activation confined to the disordered region preceding the AGC kinase core
- NDR/LATS family kinase (Cbk1/Sid2): strong activation across low-complexity regulatory segments; none on the kinase and AGC-tail domains
- CaMKK/CaMK-related kinases: activation on short N-terminal IDRs or variable linker segments; none on the kinase core
- Two-component response regulators (e.g., SskA/Ssk1): activation on long disordered regulatory segments flanking the structured receiver domain
- DYRK-family kinases (Pom1/MBK): high activation across long N-terminal or flanking IDRs; none on the kinase domain
- Nitrogen permease regulator kinase (Npr1): activation across an S/Thr-rich disordered regulatory region; inactive on the kinase domain

14441.label: Solvent exposed assembly segments
14441.summary: Solvent-exposed assembly segments of bacterial and bacteriophage surface/structural proteins (flagellins, phage tail sheath, baseplate wedge), with activation concentrated on outer-domain helical and adjacent strand regions that contribute to oligomeric assembly surfaces.
14441.description:
Summary: Solvent-exposed assembly segments of bacterial and bacteriophage surface/structural proteins (flagellins, phage tail sheath, baseplate wedge), with activation concentrated on outer-domain helical and adjacent strand regions that contribute to oligomeric assembly surfaces.
Activation pattern: Regional activation over contiguous outer-domain blocks, with the strongest signal on alpha-helical segments and secondary activation on flanking beta-strands within the same structural module; sparser, residue-level peaks appear in compositionally similar exposed segments of unrelated proteins.
Exemplars:
- Bacterial flagellins (Pseudomonas, Vibrio spp.): consistent activation in the outer D2/D3 region around an EELATYINGQ-like segment that lies on the solvent-exposed surface of the filament
- Bacteriophage tail sheath protein (phage Mu gp39/L): strong activation on a surface helix and adjacent strands in the assembly core
- Bacteriophage baseplate wedge protein (T4 gp11): activation on a surface helix flanked by strands in the wedge body
- Bacteriophage structural proteins more broadly (tailspikes/fibers/baseplates/capsids): activation across exposed assembly segments of the virion shell
- Non-bacteriophage viral capsid/outer-capsid proteins: activation along exposed lattice segments
- Bacterial S-layer proteins: activation over contiguous lattice segments
- Autotransporter passenger domains: activation along extracellular scaffold repeats
- Apicomplexan AMA1 ectodomain: moderate, shorter activation in disulfide-stabilized extracellular loops/sheets
- CRISPR Cas13a: weaker regional activation in an acidic, predicted helical linker between HEPN-like domains
- RqcH (Rqc2/NFACT-N): isolated peak on a beta-strand near the tRNA-binding surface
- XRCC4-like factor: sparse activation on residues within a solvent-exposed helix of the coiled-coil assembly region

14938.label: Small/polar beta-strand repeats
14938.summary: Small/polar beta‑strand repeat architecture: the feature recognizes low‑hydrophobicity, G/S/T/A‑rich beta‑strand ladders that typify beta‑rich repeat domains (parallel beta‑helix/beta‑solenoid and beta‑propeller) in phage tailspikes/depolymerases and other secreted carbohydrate‑active enzymes and viral structural proteins; it also fires on G/S/T/A‑rich low‑complexity/beta‑adjacent segments in large enzymes (including viral replicative proteins), with pronounced peaks at intein C‑terminal splice junctions when present.
14938.description:
Summary: Small/polar beta‑strand repeat architecture: the feature recognizes low‑hydrophobicity, G/S/T/A‑rich beta‑strand ladders that typify beta‑rich repeat domains (parallel beta‑helix/beta‑solenoid and beta‑propeller) in phage tailspikes/depolymerases and other secreted carbohydrate‑active enzymes and viral structural proteins; it also fires on G/S/T/A‑rich low‑complexity/beta‑adjacent segments in large enzymes (including viral replicative proteins), with pronounced peaks at intein C‑terminal splice junctions when present.
Activation pattern: Primarily long, domain‑scale activation across contiguous beta‑rich repeat segments (often tens to hundreds of residues; sometimes in multiple blocks per protein); with localized peaks at processing/assembly boundaries and other G/S/T/A‑rich low‑complexity segments, notably the intein C‑terminal splice junction when present.
Exemplars: - Bacteriophage tailspike and depolymerase enzymes: strong activation across the right‑handed beta‑helix core that mediates polysaccharide binding/degradation; may extend into adjacent self‑processing/autochaperone regions.
- Secreted carbohydrate‑active enzymes: activation across pectate/alginate/rhamnogalacturonan lyase beta‑helix domains and in some glycosidases with beta‑propeller architectures.
- Viral tail/capsid/baseplate structural proteins: activation along beta‑rich/repetitive regions (beta‑solenoid fibers/shafts or beta‑propeller‑like patches) within virion assemblies.
- Replicative/housekeeping proteins (with or without inteins; e.g., replication factor C small subunit, DNA/RNA polymerases, EF‑2): activation on G/S/T/A‑rich segments; sharp, localized peaks at intein C‑terminal splice junctions when present.
- ATP synthase and V‑ATPase subunits: localized activation on gly/ser‑rich beta/loop segments; intein insertions, where present, sharpen the junctional peak.
- Cell shape–determining protein MreC: activation within the elongated periplasmic beta‑rich region consistent with solenoid‑like repeats.
- Calpain family proteases: activation on small/polar, repetitive segments (e.g., low‑complexity linker/autolysis regions) adjacent to the protease core.

15164.label: C2 beta-sandwich loop junctions
15164.summary: Short loop/strand junction motifs in C2 β-sandwich domains and related β-sandwich modules, marking exposed loops commonly used for membrane/ligand and Ca2+ interaction in eukaryotic trafficking proteins, lipid kinases, and receptors, with additional hits in some bacterial/eukaryotic secreted multidomain enzymes.
15164.description:
Summary: Short loop/strand junction motifs in C2 β-sandwich domains and related β-sandwich modules, marking exposed loops commonly used for membrane/ligand and Ca2+ interaction in eukaryotic trafficking proteins, lipid kinases, and receptors, with additional hits in some bacterial/eukaryotic secreted multidomain enzymes.
Activation pattern: Regional, with multiple separated 8–15-residue clusters primarily within annotated C2 domains; strongest at coil→β transitions and strand termini, frequently overlapping Ca2+-binding loops. Similar junctions can also be marked in other β-sandwich domains. Residue-level peaks span polar, acidic, and hydrophobic residues (S/T/D, V/L/N, occasional P/Y/F/C), with recurring local motifs around the activation peak. Typically appears in the C-terminal half of long cytosolic proteins (e.g., lipid kinases) or in extracellular regions of receptor-like proteins; minimal/absent in kinase catalytic cores, transmembrane helices, extended coiled-coils, and most low-complexity/disordered tracts. Occasional weaker-to-moderate hits occur at similar loop/strand junctions outside primary C2 domains.
Exemplars: PI3K lipid kinases with PI3K-type/C-terminal C2 domains: short, discrete activations within each C2 module; catalytic core and helical regions are silent. Pore-forming proteins (e.g., Perforin-1): peaks fall directly on the Ca2+-binding loop of the C2 domain. C2 domain–containing signaling proteins (e.g., RGS-7-like): a sharp loop/strand-junction segment inside the C2 domain dominates, with long disordered regions and the RGS domain silent. Discoidin domain receptors (RTKs with extracellular F5/8 type C repeats): two short coil→β segments within discoidin/F5/8C domains are marked; no signal in the transmembrane or cytoplasmic kinase domain. Rare bacterial secreted glycan-processing enzymes (e.g., PNGase F): activation localizes to β-sandwich accessory modules or analogous loop/strand junctions; catalytic cores are largely silent.

15988.label: Structural small-polar patches
15988.summary: The feature fires on short Ala/Gly/Thr/Asp-rich segments in beta-strand and loop regions of phage capsule depolymerases, phage capsid proteins, and membrane-anchored acyltransferases. It marks small-polar patches in the structural body of these proteins rather than any specific catalytic site.
15988.description:
Summary: The feature fires on short Ala/Gly/Thr/Asp-rich segments in beta-strand and loop regions of phage capsule depolymerases, phage capsid proteins, and membrane-anchored acyltransferases. It marks small-polar patches in the structural body of these proteins rather than any specific catalytic site.
Activation pattern: Regional activation on short-to-moderate segments enriched in small/polar residues (A, G, T, S, D), typically located in the N-terminal to middle regions of the proteins. Activation can produce multiple separated peaks per protein and occurs both in cytosolic regions and in domains involved in substrate/host-component interaction.
Exemplars:
- Klebsiella phage capsule depolymerases / tail spikes (K1, K2, K47, K63 specificities): activation on small/polar segments within the host capsule-interaction region.
- Phage major capsid proteins (e.g., Salmonella phage P22 gp5): activation on beta-strand segments within the assembly-relevant I domain.
- Yeast membrane acyltransferases (e.g., S. cerevisiae GPAT1 and GPAT2, S. pombe C1718.04): activation on short patches within the cytoplasmic domain.
- Phage tail-associated structural proteins: activation on small/polar patches in the structural body.

504.label: ICA-adjacent trimeric beta-solenoid
504.summary: Trimeric beta-solenoid/beta-helix “fiber body” segments of extracellular/virion adhesins and depolymerases—particularly the long, G/T/S/N/D‑rich receptor‑binding or polysaccharide‑degrading regions of bacteriophage tail fibers/tail spikes and related viral/bacterial fibers—typically lying immediately N‑terminal to, and sharply excluding, the intramolecular chaperone/autoprocessing Peptidase S74 (ICA) domain; the same ICA‑adjacent region in eukaryotic MYRF also activates.
504.description:
Summary: Trimeric beta-solenoid/beta-helix “fiber body” segments of extracellular/virion adhesins and depolymerases—particularly the long, G/T/S/N/D‑rich receptor‑binding or polysaccharide‑degrading regions of bacteriophage tail fibers/tail spikes and related viral/bacterial fibers—typically lying immediately N‑terminal to, and sharply excluding, the intramolecular chaperone/autoprocessing Peptidase S74 (ICA) domain; the same ICA‑adjacent region in eukaryotic MYRF also activates.
Activation pattern: Predominantly domain‑scale activation over hundreds of residues in beta‑strand/coil–rich, low‑pLDDT monomeric regions with many sharp local peaks (often at Gly/Thr/Ser/Asn/Asp); strong drop at the ICA/S74 cleavage site and little/no signal in helical assembly domains or the S74 chaperone itself. In unrelated intracellular proteins, only isolated, low‑magnitude residue peaks appear.
Exemplars: - Phage long tail fibers (gp37‑like): extensive activation across the mature distal fiber beta‑solenoid; no activation in the C‑terminal Peptidase S74 chaperone after the autolytic cleavage site.
- Phage tail fiber S proteins: strong activation over the C‑terminal beta‑strand–rich receptor‑binding region; N‑terminal helical/assembly regions largely inactive.
- Phage tail spikes/capsule depolymerases (e.g., Klebsiella depolymerases): activation over the trimeric beta‑helix enzymatic body implicated in polysaccharide recognition/hydrolysis, tapering near the downstream ICA/S74 domain.
- Non‑tailed viral receptor‑binding fibers/spikes (e.g., adenovirus/reovirus‑type fibers): activation on the trimeric beta‑solenoid shaft/head segments.
- Bacterial trimeric autotransporter adhesins (TAAs): sparse activation within the surface‑exposed passenger domain; no activation in the C‑terminal translocator beta‑barrel.
- Eukaryotic MYRF family: a contiguous activated stretch immediately N‑terminal to the Peptidase S74/ICA domain.
- Off‑target single‑site hits: occasional isolated peaks in unrelated cytosolic or membrane proteins (e.g., a Gly in Rho’s ATP‑binding loop, a Tyr in a coiled‑coil of UTP14A, or residues around a GPCR TM helix) without domain‑level coherence.
