576.label: Spike/adhesin assembly modules
576.summary: Extracellular "spike/adhesin" assembly and maturation modules and analogous cytosolic coiled-coil scaffolds: long terminal segments mediating oligomerization (frequently trimerization), self/host-mediated proteolytic processing (where present), and receptor/fusion or complex-assembly functions in surface-exposed proteins and certain cytosolic scaffolds (e.g., WASH complex); includes intramolecular chaperone/autoprotease (Peptidase S74/ICA) or analogous autochaperone/oligomerization regions and adjacent receptor-binding/fusion or assembly tails.
576.description:
Summary: Extracellular "spike/adhesin" assembly and maturation modules and analogous cytosolic coiled-coil scaffolds: long terminal segments mediating oligomerization (frequently trimerization), self/host-mediated proteolytic processing (where present), and receptor/fusion or complex-assembly functions in surface-exposed proteins and certain cytosolic scaffolds (e.g., WASH complex); includes intramolecular chaperone/autoprotease (Peptidase S74/ICA) or analogous autochaperone/oligomerization regions and adjacent receptor-binding/fusion or assembly tails.
Activation pattern: Domain-level activation across long, contiguous terminal stretches (ectodomains or coiled-coil/low-complexity assembly regions), frequently spanning proteolytic cleavage sites when present; captures both structured autochaperone/beta-solenoid-like modules and neighboring flexible, low-cysteine, repeat-rich segments enriched in G/S/T/N and small hydrophobics.
Exemplars:
- Bacteriophage tailspike/tail fiber and capsule depolymerases: activation over the C-terminal intramolecular chaperone/autoprotease (Peptidase S74/ICA) domain, precisely beginning at the autoproteolytic scissile bond and covering the chaperone chain.
- Viral class I envelope glycoproteins (e.g., retroviral Env): activation confined to the extracellular ectodomain, spanning the SU/TM cleavage site, fusion peptide, and immunosuppressive region, and stopping before the transmembrane helix.
- Type VI secretion spikes (VgrG): activation on the variable, disordered C-terminal tail beyond the conserved spike core, consistent with receptor/effector-attachment extensions.
- Gram-negative trimeric autotransporter adhesins (YadA-like, Type Vc) and related Type V autotransporters: activation on the passenger's C-terminal autochaperone/oligomerization region and adjacent repeat-rich stalk/head elements that assemble on the cell surface.
- Eukaryotic extracellular matrix and pattern-recognition proteins (collectins/ficolins with fibrinogen-like domains; C1q/TNF-like; pentraxins; collagens/tenascins): activation within secreted oligomerization/recognition modules (collagen-like and C1q/FG domains) that drive higher-order assembly.
- Myelin regulatory factor (MYRF) and homologs: activation on the C-terminal ICA/S74-like intramolecular chaperone/autoprotease that trimerizes and self-cleaves to release the functional N-terminal fragment, extending across the adjacent coiled-coil and downstream membrane-proximal segments.
- Phage baseplate/needle and tail proteins (e.g., gp26, gp9, gp10): activation on terminal coiled-coil or assembly-interface segments mediating oligomerization and contact with neighboring subunits.
- Mycobacterial PE/PE_PGRS and other cell-envelope adhesins: activation across glycine/serine-rich, low-cysteine repetitive extracellular stretches associated with surface adhesion and immune interaction.
- Cytosolic coiled-coil scaffolds in membrane-proximal complexes (e.g., WASH complex subunits such as CCDC53/WASHC3): activation on coiled-coil and low-complexity terminal regions mediating oligomerization and complex assembly.

1297.label: Viral fiber/spike beta repeats
1297.summary: Extracellular repetitive beta-rich segments used to build viral/bacterial fibers and receptor-binding or polysaccharide-degrading domains, plus occasional other extracellular repeat scaffolds (e.g., collagen-like G–X–Y tracts); recognized as long arrays of short G/T/S/N/D/E- or G–X–Y–type repeats with low cysteine/aromatic content.
1297.description:
Summary: Extracellular repetitive beta-rich segments used to build viral/bacterial fibers and receptor-binding or polysaccharide-degrading domains, plus occasional other extracellular repeat scaffolds (e.g., collagen-like G–X–Y tracts); recognized as long arrays of short G/T/S/N/D/E- or G–X–Y–type repeats with low cysteine/aromatic content.
Activation pattern: Regional/domain-level activation across long contiguous repeat/beta-structured blocks, with peaks landing on beta-strand and turn elements within these arrays; activation can occur at N-terminal, internal, or C-terminal positions of the fiber/spike depending on the protein.
Exemplars:
- Bacteriophage tail fibers: long fiber proteins with beta-repeat/beta-strand arrays (e.g., T2 gp37, T5 pb1, lambda stf, T4 gp12).
- Bacteriophage tail spikes: beta-rich domains with glycan-binding/depolymerase activity (e.g., epsilon15 gp20, Klebsiella K5-2 depolymerase).
- Phage spike/receptor-binding proteins with beta-strand-rich domains (e.g., PRD1 P5, Bordetella BPP-1 MTD).
- Fibritin-like trimeric collar/foldon-associated beta-structured regions.
- Non-bacteriophage viral fibers (e.g., adenovirus): shaft beta-spiral repeat regions.
- Phage baseplate/adapter components with gly/ser/asn-rich beta-repeat segments (e.g., wedge proteins).
- Occasional off-targets: extracellular collagen-like proteins with G–X–Y triple-helix repeats; rare inner-membrane apolipoprotein N-acyltransferases with short low-complexity loops.

2145.label: Domain-boundary capping motifs
2145.summary: Short capping segments at the N-termini of disulfide-rich extracellular domains (especially von Willebrand factor type D modules) and at interdomain hinges; recurs at edges of intracellular enzyme and nuclear/chromatin domains (e.g., RNA polymerases, SET methyltransferases) and other globular domains.
2145.description:
Summary: Short capping segments at the N-termini of disulfide-rich extracellular domains (especially von Willebrand factor type D modules) and at interdomain hinges; recurs at edges of intracellular enzyme and nuclear/chromatin domains (e.g., RNA polymerases, SET methyltransferases) and other globular domains.
Activation pattern: Residue-level peaks in short windows (~10-25 aa) at domain starts and in interdomain linkers; multiple peaks per protein; consistently adjacent to conserved disulfide-bonded cysteines at VWFD N-termini, with peak residues commonly including C-V-L/I-D and G/P/aromatic-containing motifs; typically in predicted coils/IDRs.
Exemplars: Vitellogenins: sharp peak at the N-terminus of a von Willebrand factor type D domain next to a disulfide-forming Cys; Mucins/von Willebrand factor-like polymerization modules: peaks at the starts of VWFD repeats; Secretory phospholipase A2 receptor and CTLD family 13 receptors: peaks at the N-edge of FN2 and in linkers flanking CTLD modules; Extracellular proteases/inhibitors and CCP/EGF/Kunitz repeat proteins: activation at boundaries around these disulfide-rich modules; Carbonic anhydrases and CA-like matrix proteins: short acidic/aromatic Gly/Pro loops at domain edges; RNA polymerases and ribosomal proteins: short acidic/Gly-Pro-aromatic loops at internal domain boundaries; Nuclear/chromatin proteins (e.g., SET methyltransferases): peaks at hinges flanking SET/SANT/chromo-like modules.

2968.label: Flexible C-terminal enzyme tails
2968.summary: C-terminal auxiliary extensions adjacent to catalytic cores—typically flexible, helix/coil-rich segments enriched in basic and aromatic residues and glycine—that cap or immediately follow enzyme redox/aromatic-metabolism domains. The feature preferentially marks these mid-to-C-terminal tails or domain-edge/linker regions rather than the cofactor-binding core, most commonly in flavin/quinone-linked oxidoreductases and related enzymes (also seen in PAL-type lyases).

Activation pattern: Regional activation across sizeable mid-to-C-terminal windows (tens to >100 residues), usually peaking at the last helices or very end of the catalytic domain and extending into the C-terminal tail/linker; consistently lower predicted structural confidence than the catalytic core; mixed alpha-helices and short coils; generally outside annotated FAD/NAD(P) binding motifs but may include substrate-binding helices.
Exemplars: - Sulfide:quinone reductase: strong activation on the low-confidence C-terminal tail distal to the catalytic core
- Demethylphylloquinone reductase (phylloquinone/quinone reductase): activation on a C-terminal helical segment outside FAD/NADP-binding sites
- FAD-dependent halogenase (brominase): activation on a flexible C-terminal helix/coil region
- Phenylalanine ammonia-lyase: activation across the C-terminal helical subdomain, with strongest signal in the terminal helix bundle that includes substrate-binding helices
- Geranylgeranyl diphosphate reductase (isoprenoid redox enzyme): activation confined to a disordered/helix-rich C-terminal tail
- MICAL family monooxygenase: activation at the C-terminal edge of the monooxygenase domain and into the linker preceding the next domain

3107.label: CTLD/Link hydrophobic ligand patch
3107.summary: Conserved hydrophobic ligand‑interaction patch in extracellular adhesion modules—predominantly the C‑type lectin‑like domain (CTLD) and, by functional analogy, Link modules—centered on a short loop/strand flanked by helix/β that frequently contains an aromatic–Gly–Leu motif (e.g., W‑x‑G‑L). This surface segment forms part of the glycan or receptor‑binding face used by immune lectins, venom snaclecs, eggshell lectins, hyaluronan‑binding proteins, and some bacterial adhesins.
3107.description:
Summary: Conserved hydrophobic ligand‑interaction patch in extracellular adhesion modules—predominantly the C‑type lectin‑like domain (CTLD) and, by functional analogy, Link modules—centered on a short loop/strand flanked by helix/β that frequently contains an aromatic–Gly–Leu motif (e.g., W‑x‑G‑L). This surface segment forms part of the glycan or receptor‑binding face used by immune lectins, venom snaclecs, eggshell lectins, hyaluronan‑binding proteins, and some bacterial adhesins.
Activation pattern: Regional activation within an extracellular recognition domain: contiguous 20–40 aa stretches inside CTLD or Link modules with sharp residue‑level peaks (often at Leu within a W‑x‑G‑L–like patch), spanning coil/short β and adjacent helix/β elements; repeated occurrences across proteins with multiple CTLD repeats; minimal activation in cytosolic or transmembrane regions; typically not centered on the Ca2+‑ligating residues of CTLDs.
Exemplars: - Immune C-type lectin receptors (e.g., CD209/DC‑SIGN): contiguous segment within the CTLD with a peak in a coil on the ligand‑binding face, distinct from the Ca2+‑binding residues.
- Killer cell lectin‑like receptors (KLR family): mixed β/α region in the CTLD centered on a hydrophobic W‑x‑G‑L–like patch.
- CLEC2D: helix–loop–β region within the CTLD with a strong peak at L in the loop adjacent to an N‑glycosylation site.
- Snake venom C‑type lectin‑like toxins (snaclecs): flexible loop immediately followed by an α‑helix in the CTLD; peak on the loop Leu within the hydrophobic patch.
- Eggshell lectin (ovocleidin‑17): short β‑strand plus surrounding coil in the CTLD with a Leu‑centered peak.
- Hyaluronan link‑module proteins (TSG‑6): HA‑binding stretch in the Link domain (including the H‑L‑A motif) and nearby residues that also mediate heparin binding.
- Bacterial adhesins (Yersinia invasin): integrin‑binding loop in the C‑terminal adhesin domain near a disulfide; coil flanked by short helices marks the peak.
- Generic CTLD‑containing extracellular proteins: central β/coil patch within the CTLD (e.g., CTLD‑containing protein 87) showing the characteristic hydrophobic/Trp‑Gly‑Leu enrichment.

4369.label: Beta-solenoid spikes and FG repeats
4369.summary: Low-complexity, small-hydrophobic/phenylalanine–enriched stretches that adopt extended β/coil conformations used to build elongated spikes/fibers and multivalent interaction regions—especially β-solenoid/β-spiral receptor-binding/depolymerase modules of trimeric spikes and phenylalanine-rich FG-repeat segments of nucleoporins. While primarily capturing phage/bacterial spikes and FG nucleoporins, only some eukaryotic viral attachment fibers show strong activation.
4369.description:
Summary: Low-complexity, small-hydrophobic/phenylalanine–enriched stretches that adopt extended β/coil conformations used to build elongated spikes/fibers and multivalent interaction regions—especially β-solenoid/β-spiral receptor-binding/depolymerase modules of trimeric spikes and phenylalanine-rich FG-repeat segments of nucleoporins. While primarily capturing phage/bacterial spikes and FG nucleoporins, only some eukaryotic viral attachment fibers show strong activation.

Activation pattern: Broad regional activation across long repeat-rich β/coil segments (often in C-terminal halves) with many sites per large protein; strong on residues G/A/S/T/V/I/L and on Phe within FG motifs; little activation on well-packed α-helical/coiled-coil regions; peaks frequently coincide with low-pLDDT, flexible segments that become structured upon trimerization/assembly or multivalent binding; activation is reduced on highly ordered triple β-spiral shafts (e.g., many adenovirus fibers).

Exemplars:
- Phage tail spikes/fibers/baseplates: high activation on β-solenoid/β-rich receptor-binding/depolymerase domains
- Capsule-depolymerase tail spikes (Klebsiella/E. coli): glycan-binding/-degrading right-handed β-helix repeats
- Type VI secretion system VgrG spikes: β-prism/β-helix tip regions of the trimeric puncturing spike
- Trimeric autotransporter adhesins and giant outer-membrane adhesins: β-rich head/adhesin repeats (not the α-helical stalk or translocator barrel)
- Eukaryotic viral attachment fibers: some (e.g., reovirus σ1, certain coronavirus S1 subregions) show activation in β-rich/low-complexity regions; adenovirus fibers often show weak activation limited to flexible loops rather than the ordered triple β-spiral shaft
- Nuclear pore complex nucleoporins: FG/FXFG/GLFG phenylalanine-rich repeat tracts
- MYRF family: activation on N-terminal β-rich repeat segments upstream of the membrane anchor
- Bacterial S-layer/large surface proteins: repetitive β-domains and low-complexity adhesin regions

5261.label: Terminal disulfide beta-strand
5261.summary: Short, structured beta-strand segments at or near domain termini in extracellular proteins/domains—most prominently the conserved C-terminal strand of C-type lectin-like domains (CTLD)—often bearing closely spaced, disulfide-forming cysteines and flanked by aromatic/basic residues; analogous terminal strands in other adhesin/receptor-binding ectodomains and in compact disulfide-rich secreted toxins/antimicrobial peptides also trigger.
5261.description:
Summary: Short, structured beta-strand segments at or near domain termini in extracellular proteins/domains—most prominently the conserved C-terminal strand of C-type lectin-like domains (CTLD)—often bearing closely spaced, disulfide-forming cysteines and flanked by aromatic/basic residues; analogous terminal strands in other adhesin/receptor-binding ectodomains and in compact disulfide-rich secreted toxins/antimicrobial peptides also trigger.
Activation pattern: Residue-level peaks on 8–20 aa stretches at ectodomain or domain termini; highest on cysteines within a beta-strand (often terminal) and immediate neighbors; repeats once per CTLD module in multi-CTLD proteins; occasionally extends just beyond the annotated CTLD into a short structured island; also marks the terminal beta-strand at the ends of viral/bacteriophage receptor-binding fibers and short strands within disulfide-rich peptide toxins.
Exemplars:
- Selectins: activation at the CTLD C-terminus at the CTLD–EGF boundary, mapping to a short beta-strand.
- NK/killer cell lectin-like receptors: activation on the CTLD terminal beta-strand, peaking on paired cysteines implicated in disulfides.
- Invertebrate C-type lectins (e.g., echinoidin): activation confined to the CTLD C-terminal beta-strand.
- Echinoderm spicule matrix CTLD proteins: activation on a short beta-strand immediately C-terminal to the CTLD within an otherwise disordered tail.
- Bacteriophage long-tail fiber proteins: activation on the extreme C-terminal beta-strand of the fiber tip/knob domain.
- Cysteine-rich peptide toxins (e.g., sea anemone sodium-channel toxins): activation on a short beta-strand around paired cysteines, typically near a terminus.

5656.label: Polar catalytic microenvironments
5656.summary: Polar, enzyme-active/binding microenvironments—most prominently the small/polar‑rich grooves of phage tailspike/receptor‑binding fibers and capsule depolymerase beta‑solenoids, but more generally the immediate catalytic neighborhoods on enzymes (e.g., residues flanking a peroxidatic Cys or a membrane‑embedded catalytic His).
5656.description:
Summary: Polar, enzyme-active/binding microenvironments—most prominently the small/polar‑rich grooves of phage tailspike/receptor‑binding fibers and capsule depolymerase beta‑solenoids, but more generally the immediate catalytic neighborhoods on enzymes (e.g., residues flanking a peroxidatic Cys or a membrane‑embedded catalytic His).
Activation pattern: Typically broad, domain‑level activation spanning long, gly/Ser/Thr/Asn/Asp‑rich solenoid regions in phage fibers/depolymerases; in non‑phage enzymes the signal collapses to sparse, residue‑level peaks at or adjacent to essential catalytic residues (often within a helix or TM helix), with little/no signal in unrelated domains of the same protein.
Exemplars: - Phage tailspike and capsule depolymerases (pectate‑lyase–like right‑handed beta‑helix glycanases; many K‑antigen–specific): strong, extended activation over the glycan‑binding/catalytic solenoid (often encompassing regions annotated with intramolecular chaperone/autoprotease).
- Phage receptor‑binding fibers and filamentous phage minor coat attachment proteins: activation along host‑binding/attachment regions enriched in small/polar residues.
- Mitochondrial protoheme IX farnesyltransferase (COX10, membrane prenyltransferase): a single sharp peak at the essential membrane‑embedded catalytic histidine within a TM helix.
- Hybrid peroxiredoxin 5 (thioredoxin‑like peroxidase): sparse activation on the catalytic helix flanking the peroxidatic cysteine within the thioredoxin domain, with no signal in the C‑terminal glutaredoxin domain.

5749.label: Aromatic-flanked Gly/Pro NIDO loops
5749.summary: Gly/Pro-rich loop/turn segments flanked by aromatic residues (Tyr/Trp/Phe) in extracellular regions of secreted multi-domain precursors, with strongest activation in NIDO (nidogen) domains and the surrounding N-terminal extracellular segments
5749.description:
Summary: Gly/Pro-rich loop/turn segments flanked by aromatic residues (Tyr/Trp/Phe) in extracellular regions of secreted multi-domain precursors, with strongest activation in NIDO (nidogen) domains and the surrounding N-terminal extracellular segments
Activation pattern: Regional activation that concentrates on a single ~140–170 aa NIDO domain or an adjacent extracellular module, but can tile broadly across the extracellular portion of large precursors, producing long stretches of continuous activation across hundreds of residues
Exemplars: - Nidogens/entactins (vertebrate and invertebrate): strong activation centered on the NIDO domain and the N-terminal extracellular segment of the precursor
- Mesh/SUSD2-like adhesion precursors with NIDO/AMOP/VWFD/Sushi architecture: dominant activation on the NIDO domain, with weaker tiling across AMOP and VWFD modules
- Plexin domain-containing proteins (PLXDC1/PLXDC2): broad activation across the extracellular plexin-like region
- Dendrite extension defective protein 1 and related precursors with tandem NIDO domains: activation distributed across both NIDO modules

6526.label: C-terminal IDLSxG calcium-cap motif
6526.summary: A short conserved C-terminal motif in secreted/extracellular bacterial metalloproteases and alginate-modifying enzymes, centered on an "IDLS-x-G" / "DLS-LG-" pattern in the C-terminal calcium-binding cap region that lies just downstream of RTX/hemolysin-type repeat tracts.
6526.description:
Summary: A short conserved C-terminal motif in secreted/extracellular bacterial metalloproteases and alginate-modifying enzymes, centered on an "IDLS-x-G" / "DLS-LG-" pattern in the C-terminal calcium-binding cap region that lies just downstream of RTX/hemolysin-type repeat tracts.
Activation pattern: Focal activation on a short (~4-6 residue) conserved motif near the C-terminus, often overlapping β-strands/turns/helices adjacent to Ca2+-binding residues. The motif can recur a few times in proteins with multiple C-terminal cap-like regions (e.g., long AlgE-family epimerases), but activation is not spread across the upstream RTX or β-helix repeats themselves, nor at catalytic Zn-binding active sites.
Exemplars:
- Bacterial serralysin-family RTX metalloproteases (Serratia, Pseudomonas, Photorhabdus, Proteus, Dickeya, Erwinia): activation on the "IDLS-x-G" motif within the C-terminal Ca2+-binding cap, downstream of the hemolysin-type repeats and away from the Zn2+ active site.
- Mannuronan C5-epimerases (AlgE4, AlgE7) and related CAZy enzymes: activation on the same C-terminal "DLS-LG-" motif, recurring across tandem C-terminal modules in multi-domain AlgE proteins.
- Bacteriophage tailspike/baseplate depolymerases: activation over beta-helix cores.
- Type V autotransporter adhesins and other extracellular repeats: activation on extended acidic beta-solenoid stretches.
- Chitinases and beta-glucanases: activation in acidic linkers/CBM-adjacent low-complexity regions, not the catalytic core.
- Bacterial sialidases (e.g., NanA) and pentraxins/pilins: activation in exposed acidic patches or low-complexity tails.
- Oomycete CRN effectors: activation on short Asp-rich patches at DWL domain starts (e.g., ISDDHD).

6809.label: Extracytoplasmic trimeric coiled-coil stalks
6809.summary: Fibrous stalk/shaft segments of extracellular and virion attachment machinery—primarily trimeric coiled‑coils and repeat‑rich, low‑complexity linkers that project or connect receptor‑binding/catalytic heads (e.g., phage tail fibers/spikes/tip proteins, trimeric autotransporter adhesins, S-layer–associated OM proteins, flagellar hook-associated proteins); these regions are often enriched in small polar residues and predicted with lower structural confidence.

Summary: Fibrous stalk/shaft segments of extracellular and virion attachment machinery—primarily trimeric coiled‑coils and repeat‑rich, low‑complexity linkers that project or connect receptor‑binding/catalytic heads (e.g., phage tail fibers/spikes/tip proteins, trimeric autotransporter adhesins, S-layer–associated OM proteins, flagellar hook-associated proteins); these regions are often enriched in small polar residues and predicted with lower structural confidence.
Activation pattern: Predominantly broad regional/domain-level activation over long contiguous stretches spanning alpha-helical coiled-coils and flexible/disordered tail segments; activation typically covers the mature fiber/stalk chain and excludes appended chaperone, catalytic, or translocator domains; rare off-target isolated peaks occur in generic helices.
Exemplars: Bacteriophage tail fiber/tailspike proteins: broad activation across the elongated fibrous body of the mature chain, often extending across both N-terminal connector and middle shaft segments; Klebsiella phage capsule depolymerases: activation on low-confidence helical/linker and trimerization-stalk regions rather than the catalytic beta-helix; Phage tip attachment protein J: broad activation across the C-terminal, low-confidence LamB-binding tail following an FN3 domain; Trimeric autotransporter adhesins (e.g., Neisseria NadA-like): sustained activation across the coiled-coil stalk, absent in the signal peptide and beta-barrel translocator; Outer-membrane SlpA/S-layer–associated proteins: activation within the periplasmic alpha-helical segment between the SLH domain and C-terminal beta-barrel; Flagellar hook-associated proteins: activation at the N-terminal end of the coiled-coil shaft; Rare off-target: a single residue peak in a cytosolic IF-3 helix.

6811.label: Fibrillar adhesin stalk regions
6811.summary: Broad activation within mature phage tail fiber and tailspike/capsule-depolymerase proteins, as well as in viral capsid attachment fibers; the feature targets the body of these long fibrillar/surface-exposed proteins while systematically avoiding the C-terminal intramolecular chaperone (peptidase S74) domain that is cleaved off during maturation.
6811.description:
Summary: Broad activation within mature phage tail fiber and tailspike/capsule-depolymerase proteins, as well as in viral capsid attachment fibers; the feature targets the body of these long fibrillar/surface-exposed proteins while systematically avoiding the C-terminal intramolecular chaperone (peptidase S74) domain that is cleaved off during maturation.

Activation pattern: Regional activation distributed across hundreds of residues of the mature fiber/tailspike chain, with the strongest peaks typically falling in early-to-middle portions of the protein (often in the first ~250-300 residues, sometimes including the immediate N-terminus). Activation drops sharply at the boundary of the intramolecular chaperone/peptidase S74 domain and is essentially absent in that C-terminal region. Peak residue contexts are biased toward small polar residues (Ser/Thr/Asn) mixed with Gly/Ala and hydrophobic residues, in regions of low to moderate predicted structure.

Exemplars:
- Phage side tail fibers and capsule-depolymerase tailspikes (T5 pb1, T4 gp12, T7 gp17, Klebsiella phage depolymerases, K1F endo-N-sialidase): broad activation across the mature tailspike chain, with sharp cutoff at the peptidase S74 intramolecular chaperone domain.
- Reovirus and other eukaryotic virus attachment fibers (e.g., Avian reovirus Sigma-C): activation on the N-terminal capsid-anchoring tail region rather than the distal receptor-binding head.
- Trimeric autotransporter adhesins (e.g., Neisseria NhhA): activation across the Sec signal peptide/N-terminus immediately before the passenger domain.
- Collectins/C1q-like collagenous lectins (e.g., surfactant protein A): activation spanning the signal peptide cleavage junction and N-terminal disulfide-forming region before the collagen-like stalk.
- Type VI secretion effectors with N-terminal PAAR modules and C-terminal mART (ADP-ribosyltransferase) toxins: activation in the short flexible linker between the PAAR targeting tip and the catalytic core.

7212.label: Extracellular appendage stalks and boundaries
7212.summary: A signal for long surface-exposed stalk/shaft and domain-boundary segments of extracellular receptor-binding appendages—such as phage fibers/tailspikes/baseplate linkers and Gram-negative autotransporter adhesin passenger domains—that connect or present binding/enzymatic heads (often glycan-directed).
7212.description:
Summary: A signal for long surface-exposed stalk/shaft and domain-boundary segments of extracellular receptor-binding appendages—such as phage fibers/tailspikes/baseplate linkers and Gram-negative autotransporter adhesin passenger domains—that connect or present binding/enzymatic heads (often glycan-directed).
Activation pattern: Predominantly domain- or long regional activation across extended passenger/fiber/shaft segments, including coiled-coil stalks and helical/coil tracts, with local peaks at transitions between subdomains; little to no signal in signal peptides, transmembrane barrels, or compact catalytic cores.
Exemplars: - Autotransporter adhesins (Type V): high activation across the surface-exposed passenger domain, including coiled-coil stalk segments; absent from the signal peptide and C-terminal translocator barrel.
- Phage capsule depolymerases/tailspike enzymes: activation on helical/linker and terminal segments flanking the enzymatic core.
- Phage baseplate wedge/appendage proteins: signal on helical/strand stalk regions of the appendage.
- Bulb-type mannose-binding lectins: activation at the C-terminal ends of lectin domains and into the adjoining disordered tails.

7284.label: Gly/aromatic strand-coil transition motifs
7284.summary: Short Gly/aromatic-enriched secondary-structure transition segments—typically the coil linking β-strands (β-hairpin/β-arch or edge-strand loops) or the boundary of an α-helix—often surface-exposed and sometimes disordered, with recurrence on conserved family-specific motifs in certain enzyme groups.
7284.description:
Summary: Short Gly/aromatic-enriched secondary-structure transition segments—typically the coil linking β-strands (β-hairpin/β-arch or edge-strand loops) or the boundary of an α-helix—often surface-exposed and sometimes disordered, with recurrence on conserved family-specific motifs in certain enzyme groups.
Activation pattern: Regional activation with sharp residue-level peaks over 10–20 aa segments; maxima frequently occur on Gly or aromatic residues (Y/F/W), and can also center on conserved sequence motifs shared by homologs. Activations commonly span the end of a β-strand or α-helix into the adjacent coil and sometimes into the next β-strand; occurs across diverse proteins, often in periplasmic/extracellular or other surface regions, with occasional multiple segments per protein.
Exemplars: - FKBP-type peptidyl-prolyl isomerases: loop within the FKBP domain starting on a β-strand and peaking in a flexible Gly-centered coil.
- YidC membrane insertase: N-terminal periplasmic β–loop–β segment with a peak on a Tyr-containing strand; secondary weaker site on another β-strand.
- Flagellar L-ring protein: short disordered coil immediately preceding a β-strand.
- Alkaline phosphatase: C-terminus of an α-helix continuing into the following loop (peak at Arg) in the periplasmic enzyme.
- Gamma-glutamylamine cyclotransferase: coil → short helix → loop into the start of a β-strand adjacent to the substrate-binding region.
- Proton-gated ligand-gated ion channel (pLGIC): extracellular/periplasmic coil between two β-strands (P/G-rich) with additional weaker peaks on neighboring β-strands.
- Peptidoglycan amidase (AmpD): short α-helix with flanking coils (peak at Trp) within the catalytic domain but away from the active site.
- Woronin body major protein: β–coil–β segment with moderate flexibility, peaking across the loop/second strand.
- Urea amidolyase / allophanate hydrolase: conserved internal "WQLEK"-centered segment.
- Urease β subunit: conserved "GSHFHFF" motif region peaking on the aromatic His/Phe stretch.

7433.label: Extracellular coiled-coil stalks
7433.summary: Non-transmembrane elongated oligomeric “stalk/shaft” segments that connect baseplates/barrels to distal receptor-binding or enzymatic head domains in extracellular and virion-associated proteins (phage tail fibers/spikes/depolymerases, trimeric autotransporter adhesins, S-layer/surface fibers), typically low-complexity and enriched in Ser/Thr/Ala; most are α-helical coiled-coils but some are fibrous β-repeat stalks (e.g., triple β-spirals).
7433.description:
Summary: Non-transmembrane elongated oligomeric “stalk/shaft” segments that connect baseplates/barrels to distal receptor-binding or enzymatic head domains in extracellular and virion-associated proteins (phage tail fibers/spikes/depolymerases, trimeric autotransporter adhesins, S-layer/surface fibers), typically low-complexity and enriched in Ser/Thr/Ala; most are α-helical coiled-coils but some are fibrous β-repeat stalks (e.g., triple β-spirals).
Activation pattern: Regional activation across long, contiguous stalk repeats (heptad coiled-coils and, when present, fibrous β-spiral shafts), with residue-level peaks on polar S/T/N/Q/E positions within helices and adjacent loops. De-emphasized/absent on compact β-rich domains (β-solenoids, β-barrels), intramolecular chaperone/catalytic head regions, signal peptides, and transmembrane segments.
Exemplars:
- Bacteriophage tail fibers/tailspikes and capsule depolymerases: strong activation on the N-terminal trimerization/baseplate-binding stalks; weak or none over the C-terminal β-solenoid depolymerase and intramolecular chaperone.
- Structural phage baseplate/needle/head-fiber proteins: activation on elongated oligomeric arms/shafts used for assembly and projection.
- Trimeric autotransporter adhesins (SadA/YadA-like): activation on passenger-domain coiled-coil stalks and proximal periplasmic helices; absent in the C-terminal β-barrel translocator and the signal peptide.
- Bacterial/archaeal S-layer and other outer-surface proteins: activation on long non-transmembrane coiled-coil or other fibrous stalk segments; off in signal peptides and membrane anchors.
- Eukaryotic viral receptor-binding fibers/spikes: activation on helical stalks or fibrous β-spiral shafts.
- Mycobacterial PE/PPE/PE-PGRS: variable but generally weaker-to-moderate activation on S/T/A-rich low-complexity helical/coil stretches.

7594.label: Transmembrane metal-transport residues
7594.summary: Transmembrane helices of ZIP/IRT-family divalent metal transporters: the feature marks hydrophobic and small residues that line TM helices forming the metal permeation pathway, with occasional peaks on histidines at known metal-coordination positions.
7594.description:
Summary: Transmembrane helices of ZIP/IRT-family divalent metal transporters: the feature marks hydrophobic and small residues that line TM helices forming the metal permeation pathway, with occasional peaks on histidines at known metal-coordination positions.
Activation pattern: Residue-level peaks on isolated positions within well-structured TM helices; strongly enriched in transmembrane segments of metal importers; peaks predominantly fall on hydrophobic residues (Leu, Ile, Val, Phe) and Gly within the TM bundle, with occasional histidine hits at coordination sites; minimal activation in disordered regions.
Exemplars: - ZIP/SLC39 zinc importers (ZIP1, ZIP2, ZIP10, plant OsZIP/AtZIP): discrete TM peaks on pocket-lining hydrophobic/glycine residues within the permeation bundle, occasionally on Zn-coordinating histidines.
- Fe2+ transporters (IRT1, IRT2, OsIRT1): TM-helix peaks along the metal-translocation pathway, including a histidine within the C-terminal TM helix in some orthologs.
- CDF/ZnT and other cation transporters: discrete TM peaks including histidines and neighboring residues that line metal-binding/transport sites; little activation in disordered tails.
- Rhomboid intramembrane serine proteases: residues at/near the Ser–His catalytic dyad inside TM helices.
- M14 carboxypeptidases (zinc metalloproteases): residues adjacent to Zn2+-binding histidines and the catalytic glutamate within the peptidase domain.
- 5′-nucleotidases: Zn2+-binding aspartates and a transition-state–stabilizing histidine in the catalytic site.
- HD-domain dNTPases (e.g., SAMHD1): the metal-binding histidine of the HD motif and nearby residues influencing catalysis/oligomerization.

7744.label: C-terminal beta-solenoid repeats
7744.summary: Short hydrophobic-residue peaks within β-strand repeats of extracellular β-solenoid/fiber architectures used for receptor binding and polysaccharide depolymerization, with strongest activation across the C-terminal receptor-binding/enzymatic domains of phage tailspikes/fibers; weak matches also occur in compositionally similar disordered repeat linkers
7744.description:
Summary: Short hydrophobic-residue peaks within β-strand repeats of extracellular β-solenoid/fiber architectures used for receptor binding and polysaccharide depolymerization, with strongest activation across the C-terminal receptor-binding/enzymatic domains of phage tailspikes/fibers; weak matches also occur in compositionally similar disordered repeat linkers
Activation pattern: Primarily long, periodic runs of 3–4-residue peaks across C-terminal β-solenoid/receptor-binding regions of large virion/surface proteins; strongest within β-strands of the repeat shaft; additional clusters in disordered, Gly/Ser-rich C-terminal extensions; occasional isolated single-residue peaks in unrelated structured elements
Exemplars: - Bacteriophage tailspikes and tail fibers (capsule depolymerases, endosialidases): dense activation across C-terminal right-handed β-helix receptor-binding/enzymatic domains
- Type V autotransporter adhesins (e.g., SadA): repeated peaks at each β-solenoid turn linking passenger-domain β-strands
- Type VI secretion system spikes (VgrG): clusters in flexible/distal C-terminal extensions consistent with β-solenoid-like or effector/receptor-binding regions
- Non-bacteriophage virion fibers: activation along β-spiral/β-solenoid shaft repeats
- MYRF-like intramolecular chaperone/autoprotease proteins: residues immediately N-terminal to the self-cleavage site
- FG-nucleoporins: residues preceding LFG/GFG motifs within disordered FG-repeat linkers
- Flagellar cap proteins (FliD/HAP2): isolated peak within a β-strand
- FtsK DNA translocase: rare single-residue hit in an α-helix

7756.label: Glycine-rich extracellular attachment regions
7756.summary: Glycine‑rich, low‑complexity segments (often G/P/S/T‑rich, including collagen‑like Gly‑X‑Y repeats) and adjacent regions in extracellular attachment/receptor‑binding proteins—most prominently phage tail fibers/tail spikes and bacterial trimeric autotransporter adhesins—and in secreted trimeric eukaryotic ECM/C1q/TNF‑related proteins.
7756.description:
Summary: Glycine‑rich, low‑complexity segments (often G/P/S/T‑rich, including collagen‑like Gly‑X‑Y repeats) and adjacent regions in extracellular attachment/receptor‑binding proteins—most prominently phage tail fibers/tail spikes and bacterial trimeric autotransporter adhesins—and in secreted trimeric eukaryotic ECM/C1q/TNF‑related proteins.
Activation pattern: Regional activation over long, continuous stretches, frequently peaking on glycine runs or G‑rich motifs but also extending across mixed-composition segments and into adjacent structured elements (short helices and strands) near domain junctions linking shafts and heads; broadly distributed across the chain rather than confined to disordered tails.
Exemplars: - Phage tail fibers/tail spikes and baseplate receptor-recognition components: activation across N‑terminal G‑rich motifs and internal segments, with peaks that can occur in both flexible loops and short structured elements.
- Klebsiella phage capsule depolymerase tail spikes: inactive catalytic beta‑helix flanked by active N‑ and C‑terminal disordered tails.
- Reovirus and other viral attachment fibers (e.g., Sigma‑C): disordered turns/linkers connecting the helical shaft to the head and in terminal tails.
- Phage spike proteins with collagen-like regions: strong on glycine‑rich collagen‑like segments and G‑runs at domain boundaries.
- Trimeric autotransporter adhesins (TAAs, e.g., SadA): repetitive low‑complexity loops within the passenger domain and at the passenger–translocator junction.
- TNF ligand family (e.g., TRAIL): flexible linker immediately preceding the TNF homology domain, including alternatively spliced/disordered segments.
- Mycobacterial PE/PGRS proteins: glycine‑rich low‑complexity repeat regions.
- Vertebrate ECM and C1q/TNF‑related proteins: collagen‑like Gly‑X‑Y stalks and other G‑rich extracellular segments in secreted, trimeric assemblies.

7915.label: SET/PR AdoMet-binding fold
7915.summary: Conserved SET/PR-domain catalytic core that frames the SAM/AdoMet-binding pocket—centered on the I‑SET/AWS β‑strand–loop–β‑strand unit and adjacent SET/post‑SET elements—with enrichment for aromatic–glycine motifs (YxG, DWG/NWG) and nearby Cys/His residues; a fold-level signal common to SET-family methyltransferases (histone and non-histone) and PRDMs, independent of specific substrate or catalytic activity, with occasional weaker activation in unrelated enzymes that present convergent β‑strand–loop–β aromatic–glycine/Cys‑His patches (e.g., dUTPase, SRAP/YedK-like).

Summary: Conserved SET/PR-domain catalytic core that frames the SAM/AdoMet-binding pocket—centered on the I‑SET/AWS β‑strand–loop–β‑strand unit and adjacent SET/post‑SET elements—with enrichment for aromatic–glycine motifs (YxG, DWG/NWG) and nearby Cys/His residues; a fold-level signal common to SET-family methyltransferases (histone and non-histone) and PRDMs, independent of specific substrate or catalytic activity, with occasional weaker activation in unrelated enzymes that present convergent β‑strand–loop–β aromatic–glycine/Cys‑His patches (e.g., dUTPase, SRAP/YedK-like).

Activation pattern: Regional activation typically confined to the SET/PR domain as a 30–80 aa block: strongest in the N‑terminal half of the SET core or the immediately N‑terminal AWS/I‑SET segment that shapes the SAM pocket; frequently a weaker secondary block near the C‑terminal/post‑SET edge. Peaks coincide with annotated AdoMet-binding residues and the β‑strand–loop–β active‑site architecture; outside this region, activation is minimal, except for occasional low-scoring patches in non‑SET proteins that mimic the same β‑loop‑β motif.

Exemplars:
- PRDM family (e.g., PRDM14): activation across the PR/SET-like core (often two subclusters) despite low/absent catalytic activity.
- SET-domain KMT (nematode SET‑17–like): activation within the N‑terminal half of the SET domain.
- KMT5C/SUV4‑20 (H4K20 methyltransferase): activation over the SAM-binding loop within the SET domain containing key AdoMet-contact residues.
- ATXR5 (plant H3K27 mono‑methyltransferase): activation spans SET residues annotated for AdoMet binding within the catalytic core.
- SETD7-like SET-domain KMT: primary activation in the N‑half of the SET fold overlapping annotated SAM-binding residues.
- SETD5 (pseudo‑SET): activation marks the SET-fold substructure (N‑terminal core plus weaker C‑terminal edge) despite likely inactivity.
- SMYD family: two peaks within the SET domain (N‑terminal core and C‑terminal edge) in well‑structured β‑strand/coil segments.
- Small eukaryotic SET-domain KMT: activation overlaps residues where mutations reduce or abolish activity (N‑terminal core and near C‑terminus).
- SETD3 (actin histidine N‑methyltransferase): activation covers the N‑terminal SET core with AdoMet-binding residues and a secondary peak near catalysis/actin‑binding determinants.
- Non‑SET enzymes (e.g., dUTPase): show low‑level activation on local β‑strand–loop–β aromatic–glycine/Cys‑His patches.

8521.label: Extracellular ectodomains and IDRs
8521.summary: Long, solvent‑exposed non‑transmembrane regions, with a strong preference for extracellular/lumenal ectodomains of secretory‑pathway proteins—especially viral envelope/fusion glycoproteins and eukaryotic cell‑surface fusogens/receptors—often enriched for N‑glycosylation sites and disulfide bonds and containing flexible loop/beta‑rich segments; the feature generally excludes signal peptides and transmembrane helices and also generalizes to long intrinsically disordered regions in non‑secreted proteins.
8521.description:
Summary: Long, solvent‑exposed non‑transmembrane regions, with a strong preference for extracellular/lumenal ectodomains of secretory‑pathway proteins—especially viral envelope/fusion glycoproteins and eukaryotic cell‑surface fusogens/receptors—often enriched for N‑glycosylation sites and disulfide bonds and containing flexible loop/beta‑rich segments; the feature generally excludes signal peptides and transmembrane helices and also generalizes to long intrinsically disordered regions in non‑secreted proteins.
Activation pattern: Domain‑level activation across ectodomains: high immediately after the signal peptide and persisting through the virion‑surface/extracellular region, then dropping sharply over transmembrane helices; Residue‑/regional‑level peaks on fusion loops, disulfide‑bonded cysteines, and N‑glycosylation neighborhoods; Suppressed on signal peptides, heptad‑repeat/transmembrane helices, and well‑structured cytosolic domains; Occasional low/moderate activation in short cytoplasmic tails adjacent to the membrane; Often coincident with regions of low predicted structure confidence or intrinsic disorder, though activation can span both flexible and more ordered parts of the ectodomain; In non‑secreted proteins, activation tracks long central intrinsically disordered segments.
Exemplars: - Bunyavirales Gn/Gc envelope glycoproteins: strong, continuous activation over the lumenal Gn and class II Gc ectodomains with peaks at fusion loops; depleted on signal peptides and transmembranes.
- Coronavirus Spike: high across the S1 subunit (NTD and RBD) up to the S1/S2 cleavage; reduced across S2 heptad repeats and absent in the C‑terminal transmembrane region.
- Paramyxovirus Fusion (F) proteins: activation focused on the F1 ectodomain, covering coiled‑coil/loop regions and residues involved in disulfides and N‑glycosylation; drops in the transmembrane helix with occasional reactivation in the short cytoplasmic tail.
- Viral envelope glycoproteins (e.g., rhabdovirus/orthomyxovirus HE/HEF): broad activation across virion‑surface ectodomains; off over signal peptides, transmembranes, and intravirion/cytosolic regions.
- Fusexins/cell‑cell fusogens (AFF‑1; HAP2/GCS1 family): strong activation across the large extracellular domain; suppressed on the signal peptide and single‑pass transmembrane helix.
- Interleukin‑17 receptor family: localized activation within a flexible segment of the extracellular domain (including an N‑glycosylation site); absent in the transmembrane helix and cytosolic SEFIR domain.
- Large secreted glycoproteins (vitellogenins): activation across secreted regions consistent with glycosylated, disulfide‑rich extracellular domains.
- Nuclear structural proteins (sister chromatid cohesion protein 4): broad activation over the long central intrinsically disordered region, with low activation in more structured terminal segments.

8982.label: Conserved anchors in repeats
8982.summary: Detector of conserved positions within tandem-repeat grammars: (a) small cysteine-centered modules (EGF-like, Ca2+-binding EGF, LDLR class A/LA, TB/8‑Cys, antistasin-like) and (b) long low-complexity repeat tracts (e.g., FG-, S/T/P/G/Y-, or E/Q-rich repeats), and also C2H2 zinc-finger arrays. It highlights canonical positions in cysteine-rich modules near the C-terminal conserved Cys, as well as periodic anchor residues within low-complexity repeat blocks.
8982.description:
Summary: Detector of conserved positions within tandem-repeat grammars: (a) small cysteine-centered modules (EGF-like, Ca2+-binding EGF, LDLR class A/LA, TB/8‑Cys, antistasin-like) and (b) long low-complexity repeat tracts (e.g., FG-, S/T/P/G/Y-, or E/Q-rich repeats), and also C2H2 zinc-finger arrays. It highlights canonical positions in cysteine-rich modules near the C-terminal conserved Cys, as well as periodic anchor residues within low-complexity repeat blocks.

Activation pattern: Residue-level periodic peaks recurring once per repeat unit; strong signal within disulfide/metal-stabilized modules and within repetitive low-complexity tracts; minimal in nonrepetitive linkers, transmembrane segments, cytosolic tails lacking repeats, and generic PTM motifs. Peaks often fall on: (i) a position two residues N-terminal to the last conserved Cys of a Ca2+-binding EGF-like module (commonly S/A/T/R/D/K in a G/D-x-x-C-x-D context), (ii) select helix residues (T/S and basic) in C2H2 fingers, and (iii) repeated anchors within low-complexity blocks (e.g., FG in nucleoporins; Tyr/Pro/Ser or Glu/Gln anchors in extensins/glue/involucrin; repeated peptide motifs in neuropeptide precursors).

Exemplars:
- Latent TGF-β binding proteins and Notch-pathway receptors/ligands: arrays of Ca2+-binding EGF-like and TB/8‑Cys domains; disordered nonrepetitive linkers are weak.
- LDL receptor family: repeated peaks in LA and EGF-like modules; β‑propeller, transmembrane, and nonrepetitive cytosolic tails are inactive.
- C2H2 zinc-finger transcription factors: periodic peaks within each finger.
- Low-complexity repeat extracellular proteins: plant extensins (Pro/Ser/Tyr-rich), invertebrate salivary glue proteins, and keratinocyte envelope proteins (involucrin; Glu/Gln-rich) show long-run periodic activation within repeat blocks.
- FG-repeat nucleoporins (e.g., NUP98): peaks track the FG-based repeats.
- Secreted protease inhibitors with small cysteine-rich repeats (e.g., antistasin-like): activation on conserved positions within those repeats.
- Neuropeptide precursors: activation over repeated peptide-motif blocks within secreted precursors.

9159.label: Extracellular beta-solenoid repeats
9159.summary: Extracellular beta‑strand solenoids—most prominently the right‑handed parallel beta‑helix (beta‑solenoid) and related beta‑strand–rich repeat modules found in secreted/surface or virion spike/fiber domains (autotransporter passenger regions, phage tail spikes/fibers, polysaccharide lyases/epimerases, ice‑binding beta‑solenoids, and beta‑strand modules of receptor extracellular domains)
9159.description:
Summary: Extracellular beta‑strand solenoids—most prominently the right‑handed parallel beta‑helix (beta‑solenoid) and related beta‑strand–rich repeat modules found in secreted/surface or virion spike/fiber domains (autotransporter passenger regions, phage tail spikes/fibers, polysaccharide lyases/epimerases, ice‑binding beta‑solenoids, and beta‑strand modules of receptor extracellular domains)
Activation pattern: Residue‑level peaks that repeat periodically along long domains; peaks concentrate on hydrophobic/small residues within beta‑strands (and occasional Asn), spanning extended extracellular/passenger/spike segments. Activation is largely absent from signal peptides, transmembrane helices, cytosolic regions, and autotransporter translocator beta‑barrels. The signal can appear in both high‑confidence beta‑strand regions and low‑confidence “coil” predictions typical of repeat‑rich solenoids.
Exemplars: - Bacteriophage long tail fibers/spikes: distributed single‑residue peaks across gp37 consistent with repetitive beta‑solenoid elements in distal tail fibers.
- Autotransporter passengers: IgA protease passenger shows strongly periodic peaks on beta‑strands; Bordetella autotransporter adhesin BtaE and Chlamydia Pmp passengers are similarly highlighted; no activation in the C‑terminal translocator barrels.
- Type VI secretion VgrG spikes: peaks in the C‑terminal spike segment preceding the effector, consistent with beta‑strand–rich spike architecture.
- Fungal/yeast adhesins (GPI‑anchored): AWP1 shows peaks confined to the structured N‑terminal beta‑strand region, absent from low‑complexity C‑terminal repeats.
- Polysaccharide lyases: Pectate lyase A (PL1) activations fall on beta‑strands of the canonical right‑handed parallel beta‑helix core.
- Mannuronan C5‑epimerase AlgE: strongly periodic peaks aligned with PbH1 beta‑helix repeats along the solenoid.
- Ice‑binding proteins: peaks distributed over beta‑strands of the beta‑solenoid core rather than specific binding motifs.
- Receptor tyrosine kinases (EGFR family): activation confined to the extracellular domain on beta‑strand modules; absent from TM and kinase domains.

9338.label: Surface loops with cysteine hotspots
9338.summary: Surface-exposed, low‑helix, low‑complexity loop/repeat segments of extracellular attachment proteins (viral fibers, trimeric autotransporter adhesin passengers) with a bias for small/polar residues, with sharp localized peaks on cysteine‑centered motifs (disulfide or catalytic) and occasional single-residue hits in structured enzymes.
9338.description:
Summary: Surface-exposed, low‑helix, low‑complexity loop/repeat segments of extracellular attachment proteins (viral fibers, trimeric autotransporter adhesin passengers) with a bias for small/polar residues, with sharp localized peaks on cysteine‑centered motifs (disulfide or catalytic) and occasional single-residue hits in structured enzymes.
Activation pattern: Primarily long regional activation across flexible passenger/fiber regions; strongly reduced in stable alpha‑helical coiled‑coils and compact cores; superimposed residue‑level hotspots at Gly/Pro and especially at functionally important Cys (disulfide or catalytic); sporadic isolated peaks in unrelated, well‑structured domains.
Exemplars: - Adenovirus fiber proteins: activation over the disordered N‑terminal pre‑shaft and scattered Gly/Pro within shaft repeats; not in the globular head.
- Phage fibritin (viral fiber): activation at the non‑helical C‑terminal tip and loop segments; absent from the central coiled‑coil shaft.
- Trimeric autotransporter adhesins (e.g., NhhA): broad activation across the surface‑exposed passenger domain; not in the signal peptide or beta‑barrel translocator.
- Collagens (VWFC propeptide modules): localized peaks on cysteine within cystine‑rich loops.
- Antistasin‑like serine protease inhibitors: activation on the reactive loop and adjacent disulfide‑bonded cysteines.
- Cysteine proteases (calpains): single‑residue peak at the catalytic cysteine.
- Kinesin motor proteins: occasional isolated residue within the motor domain.
- Pyruvate dehydrogenase E2 components: isolated peak at a beta‑turn residue in an otherwise structured region.

9839.label: Beta-repeat register hotspots
9839.summary: Register-specific beta-strand positions within repetitive beta-rich fiber domains (beta-solenoids/beta-spirals) typical of extracellular/virion attachment and polysaccharide-depolymerase modules; in compact beta-domains the signal collapses to a single conserved anchor residue at the same register (e.g., the signature Trp in kringle), and it can also mark analogous short beta-strand segments in other beta-folds.
9839.description:
Summary: Register-specific beta-strand positions within repetitive beta-rich fiber domains (beta-solenoids/beta-spirals) typical of extracellular/virion attachment and polysaccharide-depolymerase modules; in compact beta-domains the signal collapses to a single conserved anchor residue at the same register (e.g., the signature Trp in kringle), and it can also mark analogous short beta-strand segments in other beta-folds.
Activation pattern: Widely distributed, punctate residue-level peaks across long extracellular passenger/fiber regions; enrichment for small/polar residues (G/S/T) in short runs within ordered beta repeats; relative avoidance of transmembrane segments; in repeat modules often one specific position per repeat activates; occasionally a single sharp peak on a short beta-strand within non-extracellular beta-folds.
Exemplars: - Trimeric autotransporter adhesins: multiple short hotspots across the surface-exposed passenger domain (repeat/head units), with little to no signal in the C-terminal outer-membrane beta-barrel.
- Phage tail fibers/receptor-binding proteins and polysaccharide-depolymerases: distributed activation over beta-solenoid/carbohydrate-active repeat regions that form virion-exposed fibers.
- Viral attachment fibers (e.g., adenoviral fiber shafts/heads): activation along beta-spiral/fiber repeats.
- Kringle domains (apolipoprotein/plasminogen family): a single conserved tryptophan at a fixed register within each kringle repeat is marked, with silence elsewhere (including protease-like domains).
- Myelin regulatory factor family (NDT80-like transcription factors): isolated peak(s) in the central portion of the protein outside the transmembrane and lumenal segments.
- Extracellular matrix modules with collagen-like/C1q or glycine-rich repeats: extended, fiber-like beta-associated repeats show distributed activation.

10835.label: His/Cys coordination/catalytic motifs; disordered tails
10835.summary: Two recurrent activation modes — (1) Cys/His Zn-coordination clusters in zinc-finger folds (FYVE/RING/CH-type), and (2) short disordered, polar/acidic low-complexity tail segments. Also flags histidine-centered coordination/catalytic micro-motifs such as heme-axial His pairs in cytochrome b5 folds and "histidine box" motifs in membrane desaturases.
10835.description:
Summary: Two recurrent activation modes — (1) Cys/His Zn-coordination clusters in zinc-finger folds (FYVE/RING/CH-type), and (2) short disordered, polar/acidic low-complexity tail segments. Also flags histidine-centered coordination/catalytic micro-motifs such as heme-axial His pairs in cytochrome b5 folds and "histidine box" motifs in membrane desaturases.
Activation pattern: Motif-sized, contiguous windows (≈8–30 aa) with residue-level peaks at His/Cys in Zn-binding regions, or at polar/acidic residues (D/E/N/P/S/G) in disordered low-complexity stretches. Can expand to cover a compact coordination/binding domain while remaining silent on adjacent non-coordination domains.
Exemplars:
- UPF1/NAM7 helicases: activation across the N-terminal Upf1 CH-rich domain, peaking on the C3H and CC/SHH/C Zn-ligation clusters.
- Cytochrome b5/b5-reductase: strong domain-level activation across the heme-binding fold, peaking at the two axial histidines.
- FYVE-domain and other Zn-fingers (RING, CH-type): activation on the Cys/His Zn-ligation clusters.
- Fatty acid desaturases: activation on conserved histidine boxes (HxxxH/HxxHH) that coordinate di-iron.
- Ubiquitin-system enzymes (E3/E4 ligases, deubiquitinases): activation on RING Zn-sites or catalytic Cys/His-containing loops.
- Amidotransferases (e.g., GFAT, asparagine synthetase): activation around the glutaminase-domain catalytic Cys/His loop.
- Exodeoxyribonuclease VII small subunit: activation on the disordered, acidic/polar C-terminal tail (compositionally biased basic/acidic and polar residue stretches).
- Membrane enzymes such as LspA and fungal chitin synthases: activation on short His/charged loop motifs near TM/catalytic regions.

11116.label: Beta-rich receptor-binding head
11116.summary: Beta-rich globular “head” domains—most often C-terminal—used for extracellular/virion attachment and ligand (including receptor or glycan) recognition, prominently including the jelly-roll beta-sandwich folds of gC1q/TNF homology domains and viral fiber/knob or coat heads; the feature highlights the beta-strands and adjoining loops that make the binding surface. While predominant on extracellular modules, it can also mark structurally similar beta-rich trimeric enzymes via analogous strand/loop patches at subunit interfaces.
11116.description:
Summary: Beta-rich globular “head” domains—most often C-terminal—used for extracellular/virion attachment and ligand (including receptor or glycan) recognition, prominently including the jelly-roll beta-sandwich folds of gC1q/TNF homology domains and viral fiber/knob or coat heads; the feature highlights the beta-strands and adjoining loops that make the binding surface. While predominant on extracellular modules, it can also mark structurally similar beta-rich trimeric enzymes via analogous strand/loop patches at subunit interfaces.
Activation pattern: Domain-/regional-level activation as long contiguous blocks (typically 20–100 aa), usually concentrated in C-terminal globular heads; strong signal on beta-strands and adjacent loops with hydrophobic/aromatic enrichment; minimal signal on signal peptides, transmembranes, and collagen-like repeats; occasionally a shorter localized beta-strand patch within related beta-sandwich modules and trimeric all-beta enzymes.
Exemplars:
- Phage tail tip/fiber attachment proteins: activation on the C-terminal receptor-binding head
- Phage capsule depolymerase/tailspike enzymes: activation on the C-terminal polysaccharide-binding head (beta-rich receptor-binding module)
- TNF ligand superfamily: activation on the extracellular TNF homology domain (jelly-roll beta-sandwich)
- C1q/TNF-related (CTRP) and gC1q-domain ECM proteins: activation on the C-terminal gC1q globular domain
- Collagen triple-helix repeat–containing ECM proteins: activation on the non-collagenous C-terminal globular (C1q-like/NC1) domain
- Viral fiber/attachment and capsid/coat proteins (e.g., norovirus VP1 P-domain): activation on the globular head/knob or jelly-roll capsid surface
- Subtilase/kexin proprotein convertases: activation on the P/Homo B beta-sandwich insert domain
- Plant virus movement proteins: activation on a localized beta-strand patch within a beta-sheet region
- Trimeric all-beta enzymes (e.g., viral dUTPase): activation on conserved beta-strand/loop patches at subunit interfaces

11196.label: Surface-exposed strand-edge residues
11196.summary: Surface-exposed or flexible loop/turn and strand-edge residues in extracellular/cell-surface modules (often beta-rich and frequently large; e.g., autotransporter passengers/β-helices, phage tail fibers/spikes, lectins/CBMs, ice-binding modules, fungal adhesins, and receptor ectodomains) that scaffold ligand-recognition and processing sites. The same pattern also occurs in small metal-binding proteins (metallothioneins) and in flexible linkers adjacent to processing/cleavage sites in intracellular regulators. These positions typically flank—rather than constitute—sugar/ice/Ca2+/metal-binding motifs or N-glycosylation/cleavage sites, and frequently fall on hydrophobic/aromatic strand residues (F, Y, L, V, I) interspersed with small/polar residues (G, N, T, S), with relative avoidance of Cys.

11471.label: Small residue-rich low-complexity tracts
11471.summary: Segments enriched in small/polar residues (G/S/T/A; also tolerating Cys-rich arrays) within repeat-like or compositionally biased tracts, typically located in the mid-to-C-terminal regions of long viral/bacterial spike, fiber, and tail proteins, as well as eukaryotic low-complexity modules (e.g., nucleoporins, keratin-associated repeats; also consistent with cysteine-rich metallothioneins). Activation occurs both in flexible linker-like stretches and within short beta-strand elements embedded in receptor-binding/spike domains.

Activation pattern: - Broad regional activation across mid-to-C-terminal portions of very long phage tail/spike/fiber proteins, with strong residue-level peaks within short beta-strand segments and adjacent turns
- Patchy, repeated peaks within low-complexity arrays (e.g., selects Gly in FG repeats; terminal positions of 5-aa repeats) and dense clusters of small residues
- Rare residue-level peaks at Gly–Gly motifs marking beta-strand termini/turns
Exemplars: - Bacteriophage tail needle/spike/fiber proteins: strong activation over C-terminal regions including short beta-strand elements; reduced activation in central trimeric coiled-coil cores
- Type VI secretion system VgrG spikes: continuous activation across large C-terminal intrinsically disordered tails
- Nucleoporins (e.g., FG-repeat proteins): activation throughout FG-repeat–rich IDRs, preferring Gly over the aromatic partner; absent in structured Ran-binding domains
- Keratin-associated repeat proteins: sparse, motif-position–specific activation within N-terminal 5-aa tandem repeat tracts; none in non-repetitive C-termini
- Myelin gene regulatory factor-like proteins: a localized C-terminal low-confidence coil-rich stretch at a domain boundary shows activation
- Non-ribosomal peptide synthetases: isolated residue-level activation on a GG dipeptide at a beta-strand to coil transition

11942.label: Polar beta-loop adhesion sites
11942.summary: Surface-exposed ligand/attachment interfaces on beta-rich extracellular proteins—especially receptor-binding heads of phage/viral fibers and globular TNF/C1q- and Ly6/three-finger–type scaffolds—marked by clusters of small/polar residues (Ser/Thr/Gly) on loops and edge beta-strands; frequently located at C-terminal receptor-binding regions in spikes and generally used for adhesion to proteins, glycans, or surfaces (e.g., ice, cell walls).

Summary: Surface-exposed ligand/attachment interfaces on beta-rich extracellular proteins—especially receptor-binding heads of phage/viral fibers and globular TNF/C1q- and Ly6/three-finger–type scaffolds—marked by clusters of small/polar residues (Ser/Thr/Gly) on loops and edge beta-strands; frequently located at C-terminal receptor-binding regions in spikes and generally used for adhesion to proteins, glycans, or surfaces (e.g., ice, cell walls).
Activation pattern: Regional activation on solvent-exposed loops and adjacent edge beta-strands within extracellular binding domains; multiple residue-level peaks concentrated in Ser/Thr/Gly-rich patches; in phage tail spikes often a long, contiguous band across the C-terminal receptor-binding head and sometimes into flexible/disordered tail tips.
Exemplars: - Phage tail spikes/fibers and capsule depolymerases: strong, extended activation over C-terminal receptor-binding heads and flexible tail tips; secondary peaks on internal loops that line carbohydrate-binding grooves of beta-solenoids.
- C1q/TNF superfamily cytokines: focused activation on the globular C1q head or TNF homology domain at receptor-binding epitopes (e.g., CD70 loop/edge strand adjacent to a receptor-critical residue).
- Three-finger toxin/Ly6/uPAR proteins: localized activation on the inter-strand loops of the beta-sheet scaffold that contact targets.
- Viral capsid/attachment proteins: activation on outer loops and edge strands of jelly-roll/beta-sandwich heads that engage host receptors.
- Lectins and rhamnose-binding lectins: activation on glycan-binding faces composed of polar loop/strand patches.
- Antifreeze/ice-binding proteins: activation on Thr/Ser-lined ice-binding surfaces.
- Fungal hydrophobins: activation on exposed loops of the small beta-sheet scaffold mediating surface adhesion.
- Secreted proteases (metallo-, cysteine proteases, convertases): activation on solvent-exposed substrate-binding loops adjacent to catalytic regions.

14133.label: TFIIB-family conserved linker peak
14133.summary: TFIIB-family general transcription factors and their relatives (TFIIB, BRF2, plant-specific PBRP/PTF2), labeled across most of the chain with the strongest activation in the conserved region between the N-terminal TFIIB-type zinc finger and the first cyclin-fold repeat.
14133.description:
Summary: TFIIB-family general transcription factors and their relatives (TFIIB, BRF2, plant-specific PBRP/PTF2), labeled across most of the chain with the strongest activation in the conserved region between the N-terminal TFIIB-type zinc finger and the first cyclin-fold repeat.
Activation pattern: Broad, near-chain-wide activation with a pronounced peak in a short structured segment (~50–110 residues from the N-terminus) located between the TFIIB-type Zn finger and the first cyclin repeat; the cyclin-fold repeats also activate strongly. Metal-binding residues of the Zn finger are comparatively depressed relative to the peak.
Exemplars:
- Yeast TFIIB (P29055): top activation in a short helix/strand cluster (~residues 95–115) immediately preceding the first cyclin repeat; high signal throughout both cyclin repeats; lower over the Zn-binding residues.
- Drosophila TFIIB (Q9NHP7): peaks at residues ~62–73 between the Zn finger and cyclin repeats; broad activation across both repeats.
- Vertebrate BRF2 (Q4R318, A4QNR3, Q66IW8, A8KBY2): consistent peak near residues 50–60 just C-terminal to the TFIIB-type Zn finger; strong signal across cyclin repeat 1 and 2.
- Plant-specific TFIIB-related proteins (O23215 PBRP1, Q9LIA6 PBRP2, O81787 PTF2): broad activation across the chain with peaks in the linker region downstream of the TFIIB-type Zn finger.

14198.label: Coiled-coil hinge interruptions
14198.summary: Flexible coil/loop interruptions and hinge/linker segments embedded within long fibrous stalks—most commonly coiled-coil tethers of oligomeric scaffolds and surface projections—often positioned just upstream of or between structured domains/interaction modules; sequences are S/T/A- and charged-residue–rich and cysteine-poor, and occur across bacteria, viruses, and eukaryotes (adhesins, phage fibers, centrosomal/golgi tethers, nuclear-envelope SUN tethers).
14198.description:
Summary: Flexible coil/loop interruptions and hinge/linker segments embedded within long fibrous stalks—most commonly coiled-coil tethers of oligomeric scaffolds and surface projections—often positioned just upstream of or between structured domains/interaction modules; sequences are S/T/A- and charged-residue–rich and cysteine-poor, and occur across bacteria, viruses, and eukaryotes (adhesins, phage fibers, centrosomal/golgi tethers, nuclear-envelope SUN tethers).
Activation pattern: Regional activation over extended stretches with pronounced residue-level peaks in low-pLDDT coil/loop segments that break or flank predicted coiled-coils; weaker spillover into adjacent helices; frequently localized immediately before globular domains or within annotated partner-binding regions.
Exemplars: - Trimeric autotransporter adhesins (e.g., Neisseria NadA-like): activation on loop/hinge segments within the coiled-coil stalk connecting helical heptads.
- Bacteriophage tail fiber proteins: activation across flexible, coil-rich regions of the fiber shaft with low structural confidence.
- Centrosomal coiled-coil scaffolds (CEP/CCDC-type tethers): activation at short unstructured coil breaks interrupting very long coiled-coils.
- Nuclear-envelope SUN-domain tethers (SUN1/SUN2): activation in the luminal coiled-coil segment immediately N-terminal to the SUN domain, overlapping regions sufficient for KASH/nesprin interaction.

14472.label: Conserved glycine beta-sheet site
14472.summary: Glycine-centered single-residue activations occurring in conserved sequence contexts, found in compact beta-sheet folds such as disulfide-stabilized secreted domains (chemokines, Kunitz/Kazal/WAP) and beta-rich chromatin modules (e.g., MBD), as well as in some short conserved glycine sites within otherwise disordered plant stress proteins—indicating the feature tracks a conserved glycine in a particular sequence environment rather than a specific function.
14472.description:
Summary: Glycine-centered single-residue activations occurring in conserved sequence contexts, found in compact beta-sheet folds such as disulfide-stabilized secreted domains (chemokines, Kunitz/Kazal/WAP) and beta-rich chromatin modules (e.g., MBD), as well as in some short conserved glycine sites within otherwise disordered plant stress proteins—indicating the feature tracks a conserved glycine in a particular sequence environment rather than a specific function.
Activation pattern: Predominantly residue-level peaks (typically a single site per protein); maxima land on glycine. In small secreted proteins, peaks are within the first ~100 residues (chemokines ~60–90; Kunitz/Kazal/WAP ~40–70). In larger multi-domain/nuclear proteins, peaks occur within structured beta-sheet modules (e.g., MBD).
Exemplars: - Chemokines (CC, CXC, XC, CX3C): activation on a conserved small residue (often glycine) in the beta-sheet core/helix junction region (~60–90 in prepro numbering).
- Kunitz-type serine protease inhibitors (including venom Kunitz peptides): activation on the glycine/small residue within the reactive loop/beta-hairpin between beta-strands (~40–70).
- Kazal and WAP domains: activation on a small residue in a beta-hairpin of the disulfide-stabilized fold.
- Extracellular matrix/secreted modulators: analogous glycine-centered strand/turn sites within beta-rich secreted domains.
- Methyl-CpG-binding proteins (e.g., MeCP2, MBD4, BAZ2A): activation on a single glycine embedded in the MBD, with little/no signal elsewhere.
- Histone methyltransferases and other chromatin regulators: isolated peaks on small residues within structured beta-sheet elements of catalytic/regulatory modules.
- Plant late embryogenesis abundant (LEA) proteins: a single glycine peak within a conserved short motif (e.g., PDPxTGYY).
- Broadly across organelle proteins and bacterial enzymes: sporadic single-site activations on glycine, consistent with a general conserved-glycine signal across taxa.

15619.label: Extracellular receptor-binding heads
15619.summary: Extracellular receptor‑binding modules and their adjoining Ser/Thr/Gly/Asp/Asn‑rich linkers, typically in repetitive small/polar–rich architectures; commonly beta‑helix/beta‑roll/lectin‑like heads of phage/TAAs/CBMs, but also including certain eukaryotic ECM/signaling scaffolds (e.g., collagen triple helix, cystine‑knot/Ig‑like ligands).
15619.description:
Summary: Extracellular receptor‑binding modules and their adjoining Ser/Thr/Gly/Asp/Asn‑rich linkers, typically in repetitive small/polar–rich architectures; commonly beta‑helix/beta‑roll/lectin‑like heads of phage/TAAs/CBMs, but also including certain eukaryotic ECM/signaling scaffolds (e.g., collagen triple helix, cystine‑knot/Ig‑like ligands).
Activation pattern: Long, contiguous regional activation that usually begins in a low‑complexity linker and peaks across the onset and early strands/loops of the binding domain; often at high residue indices (distal/C‑terminal heads), with patchier signal across later repeats and a secondary rise on terminal tails; little/no signal on N‑terminal assembly/catalytic scaffolds; occasional weak, sparse hits in intracellular proteins reflect short low‑complexity segments.
Exemplars:
- Bacteriophage tailspikes/tail fibers (T4/T‑even‑like): strong activation on C‑terminal receptor‑binding/depolymerase heads with beta‑helix (pectin‑lyase–like) repeats and the preceding flexible linker
- Capsule/glycan‑degrading enzymes (e.g., pectate/alginate lyases, sialidases with CBMs): activation on beta‑solenoid catalytic/CBM regions and Ser/Thr‑rich inter‑domain linkers
- Gram‑negative trimeric autotransporter adhesins (YadA/Hia/SadA): activation across the repetitive small/polar‑rich YadA‑head beta‑roll and the adjacent stalk/linker segments
- Secreted lectins/carbohydrate‑binding modules (discoidin/F5/8C, ricin B‑like): activation in the linker and the N‑terminal half of the lectin‑like domain
- Viral attachment/capsid receptor‑binding heads (e.g., fiber knobs/spikes): activation on distal beta‑rich head domains that contact host receptors
- Eukaryotic ECM/signaling ligands (e.g., collagen I chains, Spaetzle/cystine‑knot cytokines, neurexophilins): activation on secreted low‑complexity linkers and the onset of their receptor‑binding scaffolds

15700.label: Disulfide-clamped glycan-binding beta-strand
15700.summary: Conserved Gly/Cys-flanked β-strand–loop motifs in extracellular recognition or substrate-binding modules of secreted proteins—prominently the N-terminal disulfide-anchored β-strand of fungal GH54 alpha-L-arabinofuranosidase B catalytic domains, and the fibrinogen C-terminal (FReD) lectin domain of intelectins—associated with glycan/ligand recognition.
15700.description:
Summary: Conserved Gly/Cys-flanked β-strand–loop motifs in extracellular recognition or substrate-binding modules of secreted proteins—prominently the N-terminal disulfide-anchored β-strand of fungal GH54 alpha-L-arabinofuranosidase B catalytic domains, and the fibrinogen C-terminal (FReD) lectin domain of intelectins—associated with glycan/ligand recognition.

Activation pattern: Domain- to regional-level activation within compact extracellular recognition domains, typically as contiguous patches; strong residue-level peaks on a short β-strand bracketed by a disulfide bond, with the highest signal on hydrophobic/Ala residues in a "GGxPCxAA" or "DGLYxL"-type context, and enrichment for nearby Gly/Ser/Thr and Cys in β-strand/loop regions; activation extends across the catalytic/recognition domain but largely spares the C-terminal accessory (e.g. ABD) module.

Exemplars:
- Fungal alpha-L-arabinofuranosidase B (GH54) from Aspergillus, Penicillium, Trichoderma: activation on the N-terminal disulfide-anchored β-strand of the catalytic domain.
- Intelectins (human ITLN-1, rainbow trout intelectin): activation on the fibrinogen C-terminal (FReD) lectin domain, centered on the disulfide-clamped β-strand near the glycan-binding face.

16057.label: C-terminal capsid interfacial strands
16057.summary: C-terminal structural segments of phage capsid and tail proteins—predominantly the C-terminal β-strands/turns of HK97-like major capsid proteins (and analogous C-terminal regions of capsid vertex, tail tubular, and tail fiber proteins) that participate in subunit packing and intersubunit contacts in self-assembling viral particles
16057.description:
Summary: C-terminal structural segments of phage capsid and tail proteins—predominantly the C-terminal β-strands/turns of HK97-like major capsid proteins (and analogous C-terminal regions of capsid vertex, tail tubular, and tail fiber proteins) that participate in subunit packing and intersubunit contacts in self-assembling viral particles
Activation pattern: Regional, distributed activation (typically 20–30% of residues active) concentrated in the C-terminal portion of the protein, with the strongest peaks landing on C-terminal β-strands and adjacent turns rather than isolated single positions
Exemplars:
- HK97-like bacteriophage major capsid proteins (e.g., SPP1 gp13, T4 gp23, KVP40 gp23, P22 gp5, T7 gp10A, T3 gp10B): activation peaks on the C-terminal β-strand region of the mature capsid protein.
- Capsid vertex/pentameric capsid proteins (e.g., T4 gp24): activation on C-terminal β-strand and adjacent turns.
- Phage tail tubular proteins (e.g., Klebsiella phage KP34/KP32 TTPA): activation at the extreme C-terminal segment.
- Tail fiber/receptor-binding proteins (e.g., T4 gp12): activation on C-terminal β-sandwich strands involved in host-contact regions.
- Encapsulin shell proteins: activation on the E-loop and hinge loops that drive T=1/T=3 shell assembly.
- Jelly-roll (icosahedral) viral capsid proteins (RNA/DNA viruses): activation on interfacial CD/EF/GH loops mediating quasi-equivalent contacts.
- Phage baseplate/connector proteins: activation on intersubunit loops at hub/base interfaces.
- Capsid scaffolding proteins and capsid maturation proteases: activation on flexible scaffolding/propeptide segments involved in procapsid assembly/maturation.
- Ribosomal proteins (bacterial/archaeal/mitochondrial): activation on extended basic loops/β-hairpins that insert into rRNA.
- CRISPR RAMP/Cas proteins: activation on RNA-binding loops/hairpins of ferredoxin-like domains within multi-subunit RNPs.
- DNA repair glycosylases: activation on β-hairpin "wedge" loops used for base flipping/DNA engagement.
- Urease accessory UreF/UreEF: activation on flexible loop regions implicated in assembly/activation scaffolding.
- Secreted lectin-like and angiopoietin-like proteins: activation on Ca2+-binding/fibrinogen-like domain loops that mediate ligand/protein contacts.
