3436.label: N-terminal mixed-charge tails
3436.summary: Extended, compositionally biased intrinsically disordered regions—preferentially at protein N-termini—enriched in mixed charged (Lys/Arg and Asp/Glu) and polar/serine residues, used as flexible interaction tails in RNA/nuclear assemblies but found broadly across eukaryotic and some viral proteins.
3436.description:
Summary: Extended, compositionally biased intrinsically disordered regions—preferentially at protein N-termini—enriched in mixed charged (Lys/Arg and Asp/Glu) and polar/serine residues, used as flexible interaction tails in RNA/nuclear assemblies but found broadly across eukaryotic and some viral proteins.
Activation pattern: Long regional activation over low-pLDDT, low-complexity stretches, usually starting near the N-terminus and continuing through charged/polar disordered tracts; activation can also extend through downstream regions of the chain; often selects specific IDRs (charged/polar-rich) with particularly strong signal in N-terminal disordered tails; occasional local peaks within polar- or repeat-biased segments.
Exemplars: - RNA polymerase III subunit RPC4/C53: strong activation over the N-terminal disordered tail; no activation on a downstream disordered patch.
- Kinetochore CENP-C/MIF2: activation focused on the acidic/polar, low-complexity N-terminal IDR; structured C-terminus inactive.
- Nucleoporin NUP96: activation across a mid-protein disordered, polar-biased segment overlapping LC/FG-like tracts.
- PAF1 (RNA Pol II-associated factor): selective activation on the N-terminal low-complexity IDR; ignores a separate C-terminal disordered region.
- Rab3 GTPase-activating protein catalytic subunit: broad activation across a large N-terminal low-pLDDT region; structured C-terminus not activated.
- G-patch RNA-binding proteins (e.g., GPATCH1, TOUGH/TGH, GPKOW, TFIP11/STIP1 homologs): strong activation on charged/polar disordered tails N-terminal to and surrounding the G-patch domain.
- RNase P/MRP core subunits (POP/RPP proteins): activation on basic/acidic, glycine-rich disordered tails mediating RNA contacts.
- Viral RNA-directed RNA polymerases: activation on long N-terminal low-complexity segments preceding the conserved polymerase core.
- FG-nucleoporins and other nuclear pore components: activation on FG/polar low-complexity repeats.
- Jupiter microtubule-associated proteins: activation on gly/ser/acidic-rich disordered repeats.
- GPI-anchor biosynthesis factors (PIG family): activation on cytosolic low-complexity regions/tails.

14986.label: Extended assembly interface regions
14986.summary: Extended, compositionally biased segments that mediate assembly or anchoring—often helical or coiled-coil but sometimes including β-strand-rich oligomerization interfaces—located in terminal or accessory regions (basic or acidic low-complexity runs, or Leu/Ile/Val/Phe-rich stretches), rather than in compact catalytic cores.
14986.description:
Summary: Extended, compositionally biased segments that mediate assembly or anchoring—often helical or coiled-coil but sometimes including β-strand-rich oligomerization interfaces—located in terminal or accessory regions (basic or acidic low-complexity runs, or Leu/Ile/Val/Phe-rich stretches), rather than in compact catalytic cores.
Activation pattern: Long contiguous regional activation (tens to >100 residues) centered on assembly-relevant blocks; strongest over predicted coiled-coils, heptad-repeat or accessory helices and sometimes over adjoining β-strand/turn elements that form oligomerization interfaces. Frequently concentrated at C-terminal extensions or auxiliary subdomains; typically absent from small folded motifs and enzymatic cores (e.g., FAD-binding loops, WH2). Compositionally favors charged low-complexity (Lys/Arg- or Glu/Asp-biased, S/T/P-rich) or hydrophobic Leu/Ile/Val/Phe-rich segments (e.g., TM regions).
Exemplars: - Viral major capsid and portal proteins: activation on C-terminal assembly/oligomerization regions used in capsid/portal contacts.
- Retroviral envelope glycoproteins: activation on heptad-repeat coiled-coils (HR1/HR2) and often their transmembrane helix segments.
- WAVE/SCAR complex subunits: strong activation on the central basic coiled-coil region linking regulatory modules; absent on the small WH2 fold.
- Flavin-dependent halogenases/monooxygenases: activation on C-terminal helical accessory/dimerization "lid" regions, not the FAD-binding catalytic core.
- E2F/DP transcription factors and RNA biogenesis/regulatory complexes: activation on low-complexity, charge-biased coiled-coil/interaction regions rather than DNA-binding cores.
- Autophagy protein 9 homologs: activation on hydrophobic helix bundles/transmembrane segments that support membrane assembly.
- Encapsulins and other large scaffold/assembly subunits: activation on extended C-terminal regions driving shell/complex assembly.
- BREX/PglX-type adenine methyltransferases, hydrolases/acylases, and CAZymes: activation on long helical tails/linkers or coiled-coil regions implicated in oligomerization or partner binding.

6185.label: Lipovitellin and capsid jellyroll scaffold
6185.summary: Feature marks the large lipid-binding lipovitellin core of vitellogenin precursors and structurally analogous beta-barrel/jellyroll folds in viral capsid proteins, firing broadly across the mid-region beta-strand/helix scaffold of these assembly domains.
6185.description:
Summary: Feature marks the large lipid-binding lipovitellin core of vitellogenin precursors and structurally analogous beta-barrel/jellyroll folds in viral capsid proteins, firing broadly across the mid-region beta-strand/helix scaffold of these assembly domains.
Activation pattern: Long, contiguous regional activation spanning the mid-region structured core (beta-strands and short helices) of large secreted/assembled proteins; peaks land on ordered secondary structure rather than on flanking disordered or low-complexity tails.
Exemplars:
- Vitellogenins (yolk precursors): broad activation across the lipovitellin chain in the central portion of the precursor, concentrated on the beta-sheet/helix scaffold of the lipid-binding cavity; flanking phosvitin and disordered tails are largely inactive.
- Viral structural proteins (e.g., phiX174 capsid F): broad activation across the jellyroll beta-barrel and connecting helices of the capsid fold.
- Viral RNA polymerases: activation on structured mid-to-C-terminal segments mediating assembly or nucleic-acid interactions.
- Anaphase-promoting complex scaffolds (e.g., APC1/PCI-family components): activation on C-terminal segments outside the repeat/core domains.
- Ciliary intraflagellar transport and vesicle-trafficking scaffolds/adaptors: activation on extended regions that serve as interaction hubs.
- Bacterial soluble metallopeptidases (e.g., leucine aminopeptidase A): rare single-residue peak on a helix near the catalytic/metal-binding region.
6185.activation_pattern: Long, contiguous regional activation spanning the mid-region structured core (beta-strands and short helices) of large secreted/assembled proteins; peaks land on ordered secondary structure rather than on flanking disordered or low-complexity tails.
6185.exemplar_protein_families:
- Vitellogenins (yolk precursors): broad activation across the lipovitellin chain in the central portion of the precursor, concentrated on the beta-sheet/helix scaffold of the lipid-binding cavity; flanking phosvitin and disordered tails are largely inactive.
- Viral structural proteins (e.g., phiX174 capsid F): broad activation across the jellyroll beta-barrel and connecting helices of the capsid fold.
- Viral RNA polymerases: activation on structured mid-to-C-terminal segments mediating assembly or nucleic-acid interactions.
- Anaphase-promoting complex scaffolds (e.g., APC1/PCI-family components): activation on C-terminal segments outside the repeat/core domains.
- Ciliary intraflagellar transport and vesicle-trafficking scaffolds/adaptors: activation on extended regions that serve as interaction hubs.
- Bacterial soluble metallopeptidases (e.g., leucine aminopeptidase A): rare single-residue peak on a helix near the catalytic/metal-binding region.

8794.label: Polymerase thumb-palm clamp
8794.summary: C-terminal polymerase-core module (thumb subdomain plus adjacent C-terminal palm) that forms the nucleic acid–binding clamp in nucleic acid polymerases across types (DNA- and RNA-dependent polymerases, reverse transcriptases including telomerase, T7-like single-subunit RNAPs, and archaeal PolD), with occasional cross-reactivity in unrelated C-terminal helical regions.
8794.description:
Summary: C-terminal polymerase-core module (thumb subdomain plus adjacent C-terminal palm) that forms the nucleic acid–binding clamp in nucleic acid polymerases across types (DNA- and RNA-dependent polymerases, reverse transcriptases including telomerase, T7-like single-subunit RNAPs, and archaeal PolD), with occasional cross-reactivity in unrelated C-terminal helical regions.
Activation pattern: Long, contiguous regional activation within catalytic subunits, typically in the C-terminal half of the polymerase domain (helical thumb bundle and adjoining palm strands), sometimes extending just beyond the annotated domain boundary; peaks often flank but do not center on the catalytic acidic motifs; clean mapping to polymerase modules within viral polyproteins; occasional moderate activation in C-terminal helical or disordered segments of non-polymerase proteins (including P-loop NTPases and primase-like nucleotidyltransferases).
Exemplars:
- RNA-directed RNA polymerases (viral RdRp): activation across the C-terminal thumb helical bundle and adjacent palm region, downstream of the catalytic Asp motifs.
- Reverse transcriptases (including telomerase catalytic subunit): activation on the RT domain’s C-terminal thumb and adjoining palm that contact primer–template.
- Replicative B-family DNA polymerases (eukaryotic Pol α/δ/ζ and viral B-family polymerases with proofreading): activation in the C-terminal polymerase core (not the N-terminal exonuclease domain).
- Mitochondrial DNA polymerase γ (family A): activation in the polymerase domain’s thumb/palm region.
- Single-subunit T7-like DNA-dependent RNA polymerases: activation in the C-terminal polymerase lobe that grips the nucleic acid substrate.
- Archaeal DNA polymerase D (DP2 large subunit): activation over the polymerase core lobe analogous to the thumb/palm clamp.
- Bacterial LigD polymerase domain (Pol X family): primary activation in the C-terminal part of the Pol domain, with weaker secondary activation in the adjacent ligase module.
- Outliers: MutL homologs (e.g., MLH3, PMS2), kinetochore proteins (e.g., Mis15/CENP-L), and translation elongation factors (e.g., EF-2) can show moderate activation in their C-terminal helical domains; viral primases may show weak activation.

9477.label: C-terminal interaction/targeting platforms
9477.summary: Long, contiguous C‑terminal modules that act as interaction/assembly or targeting platforms, most often formed by repeat‑scaffold folds (WD40 beta‑propellers; TPR/HEAT/ankyrin/kelch alpha‑solenoids) but also including extended helical/transmembrane bundles in secretion/transport systems and regulatory disordered tails appended to enzymatic cores (e.g., viral SF3 helicases)
9477.description:
Summary: Long, contiguous C‑terminal modules that act as interaction/assembly or targeting platforms, most often formed by repeat‑scaffold folds (WD40 beta‑propellers; TPR/HEAT/ankyrin/kelch alpha‑solenoids) but also including extended helical/transmembrane bundles in secretion/transport systems and regulatory disordered tails appended to enzymatic cores (e.g., viral SF3 helicases)
Activation pattern: Domain‑level activation over 100–300 aa contiguous blocks, typically concentrated near the C‑terminus; coverage spans full secondary‑structure arrays (beta‑propeller blades, helix repeats, or multi‑pass TM clusters) and can extend into adjacent flexible/disordered tails; minimal activation elsewhere in the protein
Exemplars: - WD40 scaffold subunits (e.g., SAGA TAF5): activation across the C‑terminal WD‑repeat beta‑propeller
- Peroxisomal targeting signal receptors (PEX5 TPR domain, PEX7 WD40): activation across the C‑terminal repeat domains that bind cargo
- Nuclear pore/coatomer and related scaffold proteins (HEAT/TPR repeats): activation along contiguous repeat arrays, often in the C‑terminal half
- Papillomavirus and related SF3 helicases (e.g., E1): activation in the C‑terminal regulatory tail adjacent to the helicase core, with minor signal in nearby helices/loops
- Bacterial inner‑membrane permeases/transporters: activation across long multi‑pass transmembrane blocks, frequently in C‑terminal segments
- Accessory Sec and Type VII/ESX secretion components: activation on long coiled‑coil/helical regions and C‑terminal membrane anchors
- Two‑component sensor histidine kinases and sigma factors: activation on C‑terminal signaling/interaction modules (HisKA/HATPase or helix‑turn‑helix regions)

82.label: Right-hand polymerase catalytic core
82.summary: Conserved catalytic core of nucleic‑acid polymerases—most strongly the right‑hand polymerase domain (palm/fingers) of A- and B‑family DNA polymerases, single‑subunit RNA polymerases (T7/RpoT lineage), and viral RNA‑dependent RNA polymerases—with secondary activation on structurally related, nucleic‑acid–processing enzyme cores
82.description:
Summary: Conserved catalytic core of nucleic‑acid polymerases—most strongly the right‑hand polymerase domain (palm/fingers) of A- and B‑family DNA polymerases, single‑subunit RNA polymerases (T7/RpoT lineage), and viral RNA‑dependent RNA polymerases—with secondary activation on structurally related, nucleic‑acid–processing enzyme cores
Activation pattern: Domain-level, long contiguous stretches within the main enzymatic core; typically mid‑to‑C‑terminal in DNA polymerases and within the initiation/palm segment of single‑subunit RNAPs/RdRPs. Activation is broad around (but not limited to) conserved acidic motifs (e.g., DxD/GDD) and glycine-rich elements, highlighting the structured catalytic scaffold rather than only the catalytic residues.
Exemplars: - B-family DNA polymerases (eukaryotic Pol delta, archaeal PolB): wide activation across the PolB catalytic domain immediately downstream of essential acidic residues, covering helices/strands that form the polymerase core.
- A-family DNA polymerases (Pol gamma, Pol I/phage-like): strong activation spanning the Klenow-like palm/fingers polymerase region; proteins bearing 3′–5′ exonuclease domains appear, but activation concentrates on the polymerase module.
- Single-subunit RNA polymerases (T7-like; plant/algal organellar RpoT): activation over the structured N-terminal/initiation–palm region, not restricted to the catalytic Asp.
- Viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerases (e.g., mononegavirus L proteins): a contiguous window within the RdRp catalytic domain near motifs A–C.
- Organelle-targeted polymerases (mitochondrial/chloroplastic replicases): strong domain-level activation across their polymerase cores, consistent with the right-hand architecture.
- RNA modification enzymes (PUS7L/TRUD pseudouridine synthase family): broad activation over the C-terminal catalytic TRUD domain despite not peaking on the nucleophile Asp, reflecting spillover to nucleic-acid–processing enzyme cores.

2208.label: Beta-rich active-site cradle
2208.summary: Active-site cradle of extracellular carbohydrate-active enzymes: a beta-rich segment within the catalytic domain forming the polysaccharide-processing cleft, often flanked by aromatic/glycine-rich motifs.
2208.description:
Summary: Active-site cradle of extracellular carbohydrate-active enzymes: a beta-rich segment within the catalytic domain forming the polysaccharide-processing cleft, often flanked by aromatic/glycine-rich motifs.
Activation pattern: Regional activation over a long, contiguous stretch within the catalytic domain (beta-strands with connecting loops/short helices), with the strongest residue-level peaks falling on conserved aromatic/proline-containing motifs adjacent to the catalytic center rather than on the catalytic residues themselves; distal substrate-binding residues outside the catalytic core show little or no activation.
Exemplars:
- GH81 endo-1,3-beta-glucanases: peaks on a conserved YFP/FPxxR aromatic motif within the (alpha/beta)6 barrel subdomain that hosts the catalytic site.
- GH16 endo-1,3(4)-beta-glucanases: activation centered on the beta-strand carrying the E–E catalytic pair within the GH16 jelly-roll core.
- GH16 beta-porphyranases: strong activation around the catalytic E–E pair on the core beta-strand, extending into the adjacent loop/short helix; distant binding residues are not highlighted.
- Alpha-L-arabinofuranosidases: broad activation across the beta-strand–rich core segment that constitutes the active-site wall of the catalytic domain.
- Polysaccharide lyases (e.g., ulvan/alginate/heparin lyases): sustained activation across beta-strands of the catalytic core, with peaks on a conserved aromatic-rich strand near the catalytic acid/base residues.
- Levansucrase (GH68 fructansucrase): sustained activation across the C-terminal catalytic region with peaks near the catalytic acid/base residues.
- Pectate lyases (e.g., PL1/PL3): activation along the parallel beta-helix groove near the catalytic loop.
- AA9 LPMOs: activation on the beta-sandwich face forming the substrate surface near the His-brace copper site and adjacent aromatic platform.

1477.label: RT/RdRp palm catalytic core
1477.summary: Conserved polymerase palm-domain catalytic core of right-hand nucleic-acid polymerases, with broad coverage of the reverse transcriptase / RdRp module; also weakly recognizing homologous palm domains of some DNA-dependent DNA polymerases.
1477.description:
Summary: Conserved polymerase palm-domain catalytic core of right-hand nucleic-acid polymerases, with broad coverage of the reverse transcriptase / RdRp module; also weakly recognizing homologous palm domains of some DNA-dependent DNA polymerases.
Activation pattern: Regional activation across long contiguous segments of the polymerase core, spanning the palm and surrounding RT/RdRp subdomain; in viral polyproteins, localized to the C-terminal RdRp module rather than upstream protease/helicase regions.
Exemplars: - Telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT, eukaryotes): broad activation across the RT core.
- Coronavirus RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (nsp12, positive-sense RNA viruses): activation over the palm domain encompassing motifs A–C.
- Plant mitochondrial group II intron maturase (MatR/MatK-like RT): activation on the RT-like region.
- Mononegavirales L polymerase (negative-sense RNA viruses): activation within the RdRp catalytic core/palm region.
- Retroviral Pol reverse transcriptases (e.g., HIV/MLV): activation on the RT palm.
- Hepadnavirus polymerase (HBV Pol, RT/RNase H): activation at the RT palm.
- Bacterial retron reverse transcriptases: activation over the RT palm domain.
- DNA-dependent DNA polymerases (A/B families; phage/archaea/eukaryotes): weaker activation on the homologous palm region.

16368.label: Structural hydrophobic alpha-helices
16368.summary: Extended, hydrophobic α-helical segments (often amphipathic and Lys/Arg-biased) that serve as transmembrane helices or helical scaffold subdomains across proteins (membrane proteins and helix-rich soluble enzymes), indicating a structural (helix-rich) rather than catalytic motif
16368.description:
Summary: Extended, hydrophobic α-helical segments (often amphipathic and Lys/Arg-biased) that serve as transmembrane helices or helical scaffold subdomains across proteins (membrane proteins and helix-rich soluble enzymes), indicating a structural (helix-rich) rather than catalytic motif
Activation pattern: Regional activation over long, continuous α-helical stretches; frequently begins at the N-terminus; in multi-pass membrane proteins aligns with transmembrane helices; in small soluble enzymes can span most of the chain; generally avoids catalytic residues
Exemplars:
- 4′-phosphopantetheinyl transferases / holo-ACP synthases: strong coverage across the compact helical core, spanning much of the enzyme length
- Lipid-linked sugar phosphate transferases and related multi-pass glycosyl/phosphotransferases: activation on hydrophobic transmembrane helices
- Isoprenoid/carotenoid pathway enzymes: in soluble terpene cyclases, activation on N-terminal amphipathic helices and internal helical scaffolds; in membrane prenyltransferases/synthases, activation on membrane-embedded helices
- CRISPR-associated Cas2 endoribonucleases: activation on the helix-rich N-terminal segment of the small dimeric fold
- 3′–5′ exonucleases and exosome-related nucleases/helicases: activation concentrated on extended N-terminal helical regions rather than metal-binding/catalytic motifs
- Viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerases and bacterial reverse transcriptases: activation on hydrophobic/basic N-terminal helices implicated in membrane association or oligomerization
- Multi-pass ion channels (e.g., TMEM175/TMEM175-like): activation on hydrophobic transmembrane helices
- M13 zinc metalloprotease (peptidase M13): activation confined to a long α-helical subdomain (e.g., ~residues 242–333) away from Zn-binding and catalytic residues

5884.label: Polymerase palm pre-motif C helix
5884.summary: Conserved pre-motif C helix in the palm subdomain of viral-like polymerases (reverse transcriptases, RNA-dependent RNA polymerases, and telomerase): a loop-to-helix segment immediately N-terminal to the catalytic motif C (GDD/YMDD/TDD) that supports the active site without including the catalytic Asp residues.
5884.description:
Summary: Conserved pre-motif C helix in the palm subdomain of viral-like polymerases (reverse transcriptases, RNA-dependent RNA polymerases, and telomerase): a loop-to-helix segment immediately N-terminal to the catalytic motif C (GDD/YMDD/TDD) that supports the active site without including the catalytic Asp residues.
Activation pattern: Regional activation within the mid-to-C-terminal polymerase catalytic core, typically a 20–60 aa stretch with strongest peaks at a loop-to-alpha-helix just upstream of motif C; occasional secondary peaks on adjacent palm helices near motifs A/B. Some off-target activation can also occur outside polymerase contexts.
Exemplars: - Retroviral reverse transcriptases (e.g., Gag-Pol RT alpha/beta): strong signal on the helix preceding the YMDD region, near but not including the catalytic D residues; minimal signal in protease/integrase/RNase H.
- Endogenous retrovirus RT (ERV-K Pol): high activation on a long alpha-helix within the RT core, with weaker secondary activation on another RT helix.
- Hepadnavirus polymerase (HBV RT): a focused region immediately upstream of the YMDD motif within the RT domain; no activation in terminal protein or spacer.
- Retrotransposon reverse transcriptases (e.g., LINE/LTR such as Jockey): two RT-core segments activated, with the main peak on a coil-to-helix that maps to the palm just before motif C.
- Telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT): dominant activation in the C-terminal RT domain on the pre-motif C coil-to-helix segment; weaker signal earlier in the RT core; does not overlap Mg2+-binding residues.
- Plant virus RdRp (NIb/Pro-Pol): broad activation within the C-terminal RdRp catalytic domain, peaking on the palm helix near motif C.
- dsRNA and other viral RdRp: C-terminal catalytic-domain helices around motifs A–C show strong activation, consistent with palm pre-motif C architecture; similar pattern in probable RdRp with limited annotation.

13862.label: Pre-catalytic N-terminal accessory regions
13862.summary: N-terminal accessory beta-strand–rich subdomains and adjacent acidic, glycine-rich linkers that precede catalytic cores in CAZymes and related hydrolases/phosphodiesterases; often (but not exclusively) secreted/lumenal. These regions aid substrate recognition/scaffolding or domain tethering and may include metal-stabilizing sites; catalytic residues themselves are excluded.

Summary: N-terminal accessory beta-strand–rich subdomains and adjacent acidic, glycine-rich linkers that precede catalytic cores in CAZymes and related hydrolases/phosphodiesterases; often (but not exclusively) secreted/lumenal. Activation pattern: Domain-level, long contiguous activation starting near the N-terminus (immediately after signal peptides when present), strongest over beta-sandwich/CBM-like accessory subdomains and/or flexible/disordered linkers leading into the catalytic domain. Minimal activation on catalytic barrels/active-site residues and on distal CBMs.
Exemplars: - Retaining alpha-galactosidases (GH36/27-like): activation on N-terminal beta-sandwich adjacent to Ca2+-binding; catalytic Asp/Glu in the C-terminal core inactive.
- Endo-1,3-beta-glucanases (GH81): activation across N-terminal beta-sandwich and adjacent alpha/beta subdomain; inactive on the catalytic (alpha/beta)6 barrel.
- 4-alpha-glucanotransferases (GH77-type): activation confined to the N-terminal beta-strand–rich region preceding the catalytic core.
- Alpha-glucan/levan/amylo-synthase/transferases with CBM repeats: activation on post–signal peptide acidic/disordered N-terminal stretch linking to the core; catalytic residues and terminal CBMs inactive.
- GDPD/GDE-family phosphodiesterases: activation over N-terminal accessory/CBM20 segments where present or over low-complexity/linker regions proximal to the catalytic domain in cytosolic forms lacking annotated CBMs.

10309.label: Extended non-propeller core regions
10309.summary: A broadly-firing feature that marks long, contiguous regions of medium-to-large proteins, covering ordered helix/strand cores together with adjacent charged/low-complexity stretches in nucleic-acid/peptide-processing enzymes and scaffolding proteins; the feature avoids compact β-propeller WD domains.
10309.description:
Summary: A broadly-firing feature that marks long, contiguous regions of medium-to-large proteins, covering ordered helix/strand cores together with adjacent charged/low-complexity stretches in nucleic-acid/peptide-processing enzymes and scaffolding proteins; the feature avoids compact β-propeller WD domains.
Activation pattern: Domain- to regional-level activation over long, contiguous windows, with peaks frequently landing on hydrophobic ordered β-strand and α-helix segments while also extending across flanking charged/disordered regions. It is typically off in compact β-propeller regions and largely silent over WD-repeat arrays and transmembrane helices.
Exemplars:
- Ufm1-specific proteases (UfSP/UfSP2): broad activation across the catalytic domain with peaks on conserved β-strand and α-helix elements; active-site residues themselves are not the peak.
- Dynein intermediate chains (axonemal DNAI3, cytoplasmic dynein 2 WDR60): strong activation over the central adaptor/light-chain-binding region and adjacent charged segments; WD β-propeller repeats are silent.
- Anaphase-promoting complex (APC1) and other large transcription/cell-cycle scaffolds (Mediator, TFIIIC): long helix-rich α-solenoid segments in the central core.
- Viral RNA-directed RNA polymerases: aspartate-rich palm segments (DxD/GDD motifs) within extended acidic windows.
- HECT-type E3 ubiquitin ligases and ubiquitin-like proteases/deubiquitinases: catalytic domain cores together with flanking linkers.
- RNase III (Drosha/Dicer) and CRISPR–Cas nucleases: acidic, metal-binding active-site loops and surrounding stretches.
- Poly(ADP-ribose) glycohydrolases (PARG): acidic active-site/adjoining segments in macrodomains.
- Bacterial toxins (e.g., VasX): long ordered segments containing Trp/Phe-rich hydrophobic motifs within the mature toxin chain.

- Ufm1-specific proteases (UfSP/UfSP2): broad activation across the catalytic domain with peaks on conserved β-strand and α-helix elements; active-site residues themselves are not the peak.
- Dynein intermediate chains (axonemal DNAI3, cytoplasmic dynein 2 WDR60): strong activation over the central adaptor/light-chain-binding region and adjacent charged segments; WD β-propeller repeats are silent.
- Anaphase-promoting complex (APC1) and other large transcription/cell-cycle scaffolds (Mediator, TFIIIC): long helix-rich α-solenoid segments in the central core.

2934.label: PI-PLC Y-box activation
2934.summary: PI-PLC catalytic-core feature with broad activation across phosphoinositide-specific phospholipase C (PLC) enzymes, peaking inside the catalytic PI-PLC Y-box and extending strongly over adjacent intrinsically disordered linkers that contain polybasic (Lys/Arg-rich) and poly-acidic (Asp/Glu-rich) low-complexity tracts implicated in membrane/PIP association.

Summary: PI-PLC catalytic-core feature with broad activation across phosphoinositide-specific phospholipase C (PLC) enzymes, peaking inside the catalytic PI-PLC Y-box and extending strongly over adjacent intrinsically disordered linkers that contain polybasic (Lys/Arg-rich) and poly-acidic (Asp/Glu-rich) low-complexity tracts implicated in membrane/PIP association.
Activation pattern: Whole-protein activation in PLCs with maximum activation concentrated within the PI-PLC Y-box catalytic domain; strong secondary activation over disordered linkers immediately N-terminal to the Y-box that harbor runs of Lys/Arg and Asp/Glu compositional bias; lower but still substantial activation across the PI-PLC X-box and flanking EF-hand/C2 regions.
Exemplars:
- Mammalian PLC-zeta (mouse, human, pig, chicken): peak activation at the start of the PI-PLC Y-box, immediately downstream of the polybasic KKK/RKRK cluster (nuclear translocation signal) and an acidic-residue stretch in the X–Y linker.
- Plant PI-PLCs (Arabidopsis PLC2/PLC4/PLC5/PLC6): peaks within the PI-PLC Y-box with very strong activation across the upstream disordered X–Y linker containing acidic and basic+acidic low-complexity tracts.
- Mammalian PLC-delta and PLC-beta (human PLCD3, bovine PLCB4): peaks at the N-terminal edge of the PI-PLC Y-box with strong signal over the preceding disordered linker bearing acidic compositional bias.

8859.label: Catalytic cleft recognition loops
8859.summary: Functional cleft and adjacent loop/helix regions within the main domain that mediate ligand binding or catalysis, with a bias for acidic (Asp/Glu) and glycine-rich segments and frequent aromatic residues (e.g., Trp) used for substrate recognition; in multidomain secreted enzymes this corresponds to the mature catalytic domain, while in nucleic-acid–binding proteins it highlights the DNA/RNA-recognition elements at the edge or start of the DNA-binding domain.

Activation pattern: Domain-level, long contiguous activation over the mature catalytic domain in large secreted enzymes (often the C-terminal half), typically excluding N-terminal signal/propeptide segments, and including catalytic carboxylates and substrate-binding aromatics; shorter regional patches in smaller cytosolic proteins, frequently low-pLDDT loops or compact helix–strand–helix clusters adjacent to the active or binding site.

- Heat shock factor transcription factors: activation on the N-terminal, low-structure segment overlapping the beginning of the DNA-binding domain, consistent with DNA-recognition/regulatory elements.
- BolA-like proteins: activation across the C-terminal helix–strand–helix cluster that forms part of the DNA-binding surface.

13946.label: N-terminal accessory domains
13946.summary: Noncatalytic N‑terminal accessory/assembly modules of large enzymes—domains and linkers that mediate RNA/protein binding, oligomerization, targeting, or regulation—while avoiding the catalytic cores (polymerase, kinase/phosphatase, ligase, glycosyltransferase active sites). These segments can be helical bundles/coiled‑coils, β‑rich N‑terminal folds, or low‑complexity, phosphorylation‑rich linkers.
13946.description:
Summary: Noncatalytic N‑terminal accessory/assembly modules of large enzymes—domains and linkers that mediate RNA/protein binding, oligomerization, targeting, or regulation—while avoiding the catalytic cores (polymerase, kinase/phosphatase, ligase, glycosyltransferase active sites). These segments can be helical bundles/coiled‑coils, β‑rich N‑terminal folds, or low‑complexity, phosphorylation‑rich linkers.
Activation pattern: Domain-level: strong, contiguous activation across long N‑terminal regions, often starting at the initiator methionine, then dropping sharply at the boundary to the catalytic domain; typically repressed within conserved catalytic cores. Regional: tolerant of both structured N‑terminal folds and intrinsically disordered, acidic/proline‑rich regulatory segments; frequently highlights pre‑catalytic helical regions and oligomerization/interaction patches. Residue-level: peaks on known interaction motifs (e.g., TERT TFLY/QFP/CP) and β/α elements within N‑terminal domains; near‑zero on catalytic motifs (e.g., RT metal‑binding aspartates, kinase G‑loop/catalytic/activation loops).
Exemplars: - Telomerase/reverse transcriptases: high on N‑terminal RNA‑interaction/oligomerization domains (TEN and TRBD; motifs TFLY/QFP/CP and proline‑rich linker), off across the RT catalytic core.
- Viral RNA‑dependent RNA polymerases: preference for N‑terminal accessory/assembly regions that flank the polymerase core, with little to no signal on the conserved palm/fingers catalytic motifs.
- Phosphatidylinositol kinases (PI4K/PI3K‑like): activation on the PIK N‑terminal helical region and long acidic/polar disordered segments enriched in phosphosites; off throughout the PI3K/PI4K catalytic domain.
- Phosphoinositide phosphatases (Sac1/synaptojanin/myotubularin): signal on N‑terminal targeting/interaction modules (e.g., PH/GRAM, coiled‑coils, proline‑rich SH3‑binding regions), reduced in the catalytic phosphatase domains.
- HECT‑type E3 ubiquitin ligases: activation on N‑terminal C2/WW substrate‑/membrane‑binding regions and low‑complexity linkers; minimal on the C‑terminal HECT catalytic domain.
- NRPS‑independent siderophore biosynthesis ligases: strong on the structured N‑terminal accessory β/α domain, fading across the downstream catalytic body.
- Plant glycosyltransferases/cell‑wall enzymes: enrichment on N‑terminal cytosolic tails/stem and transmembrane‑proximal regulatory regions, with weak signal over the luminal catalytic domain.

14375.label: Interdomain gating hinges
14375.summary: Flexible boundary elements—short helix/strand/coil segments at interdomain or processing junctions that couple or gate catalytic modules; common in nucleic-acid enzymes but not restricted to them.
14375.description:
Summary: Flexible boundary elements—short helix/strand/coil segments at interdomain or processing junctions that couple or gate catalytic modules; common in nucleic-acid enzymes but not restricted to them.
Activation pattern: Regional activation over internal, contiguous 20–40 aa stretches with residue-level peaks; typically centered at transitions between domains or immediately adjacent to active regions/cleavage sites; mixed coil/strand/short helix architecture; generally avoids the catalytic residue itself.
Exemplars: - Phage terminase large subunits: strong activation on the ATPase–nuclease interdomain linker/hinge.
- CRISPR-Cas12 endonucleases: activation at the WED (wedge/OBD) – RuvC-I domain boundary, on short strand/helix elements that bracket the nuclease entry.
- Argonaute proteins: activation at the Mid–PIWI junction and in the L2 linker that gates/positions the guide–target duplex.
- mRNA capping enzymes (guanylyltransferases): activation in the loop/short helix immediately N-terminal to the active-site lysine ("lid" preceding the GTase active center).
- SAP-domain chromatin/DNA-binding proteins: activation on the N-terminal SAP helix, a short basic DNA-binding microdomain.
- DNA ligases: activation at the N-terminal domain–adenylation domain boundary within the flexible clamp/connector segment.
- UvrC excinucleases: activation in non-annotated helical/coil segments in the C-terminal half consistent with DNA-binding/hinge elements between nuclease modules.
- Aspartic protease zymogens (e.g., gastricsin): activation across the propeptide–mature chain cleavage region, a flexible processing junction acting as an access "plug/lid."

2925.label: Internal PDHRPK-like motif
2925.summary: A short, conserved sequence motif found within the structured body of several eukaryotic enzymes, centered on a proline/aspartate–histidine/glycine–arginine/lysine–proline pattern (e.g. PDHRPK, PGxLK), located internally rather than on terminal extensions.
2925.description:
Summary: A short, conserved sequence motif found within the structured body of several eukaryotic enzymes, centered on a proline/aspartate–histidine/glycine–arginine/lysine–proline pattern (e.g. PDHRPK, PGxLK), located internally rather than on terminal extensions.
Activation pattern: Tight, localized activation over a ~5–10 residue window in a single internal position of the catalytic chain; the surrounding 20+ residues are not co-activated and annotated disordered/charged-bias regions in the same proteins are not engaged.
Exemplars:
- Mitochondrial medium-chain acyl-CoA ligases (ACSF2 orthologs): activation on an internal Pro-Gly/Lys-containing segment (~residues 195–205) within the AMP-binding catalytic chain.
- tRNA-queuosine alpha-mannosyltransferases (QTMAN orthologs across vertebrates): activation on the PDHRPK(D/N) motif (~residues 145–150) within the glycosyltransferase domain.
- Histidine protein methyltransferase 1 (HPM1, S. pombe): activation on an internal segment of the catalytic chain around residues 192–200.

13797.label: ββα-Me/HNH nuclease catalytic core
13797.summary: ββα-Me/HNH-type nuclease active-site subdomain: a histidine- and Lys/Arg-enriched ββ–α core and its immediately adjacent cationic segment that bind/divalently coordinate nucleic acids for endonucleolytic cleavage; the feature also weakly recognizes structurally similar β–α–β/ββ–α ligand/metal-binding patches in other phosphate/nucleotide-processing enzymes

Activation pattern: Regional activation over a contiguous subdomain (often ~80–130 aa) centered on the ββ–α core; strong plateaus across the two β-strands and following α-helix with spillover into flanking loops/helices; silent on signal peptides and noncatalytic/distal domains; in non-nucleases only a narrow, low-amplitude band coincident with a cofactor/metal-binding β–α–β element
Exemplars: - Secreted/periplasmic nonspecific endonucleases (e.g., EndA/staphylococcal/Serratia-like nucleases): high activation on the N‑terminal ββ–α catalytic core of the mature enzyme, none on the signal peptide and little on distal regions
- CRISPR-associated nucleases (Cas9): activation on the HNH domain responsible for one-strand DNA cleavage
- Mitochondrial endonucleases (e.g., Endonuclease G): activation across the HNH/ββα‑Me nuclease module
- Bacterial toxin DNases/interbacterial competition factors (colicin-like HNH DNases, Type VI effectors): strong activation over the HNH DNase fold
- RNase T2 family: weaker activation around the His-containing catalytic region
- Other phosphate/nucleotide-related enzymes (inorganic pyrophosphatases, NAD(P)+ glycohydrolase toxins, carbonic anhydrases): modest cross-activation on histidine-rich metal/cofactor-binding β–α–β-like patches
- Folate-dependent formyltransferase (GAR transformylase): low, localized activation on the folate-binding β–α–β segment near the ligand-binding residues

14704.label: Interfacial aromatic-proline helix kinks
14704.summary: Short, motif-level signal for alpha-helix interfacial/capping segments enriched in aromatics and prolines, often with nearby acidic residues. It fires on (i) aromatic/proline-containing helical segments of type I terpene cyclases/prenyltransferases (WxxP/FxP/YxP type kink motifs), and (ii) transmembrane-helix starts/ends and signal-anchor regions at membrane boundaries, often containing interfacial aromatics and WxxP/WWP helix-kink motifs.

- Respiratory electron transport components (membrane subunits): activation at TM boundary segments.
- DNA repair nucleases/deaminases: activation on short acidic micro-motifs near catalytic metal-binding helices or at N-terminal helical segments.

15285.label: Hydrophobic structural core segments
15285.summary: Long, hydrophobic, well-ordered secondary-structure blocks that form the structural core and pocket-lining surfaces of folded domains—most often extended beta-sheet regions and, in some cases, a single helix—across enzymes that bind/process hydrophobic small molecules (oxygenases/dioxygenases, porphyrin/heme enzymes, terpene enzymes) and structured extracellular glycosyltransferase domains; generally excludes transmembrane segments and disordered tails.

- Multicopper oxidases and oxygen carriers: beta-sandwich core near copper sites highlighted.
- Terpene synthases/cyclases: hydrophobic helical core that shapes the terpene-binding cavity activates.
- Porphyrin/heme biosynthesis and handling proteins: core strands/helix segments near tetrapyrrole-binding regions activate.
- Viral envelope glycoprotein M: structured non-transmembrane segments (luminal loops/short helices) show activation while TM helices remain low.

9939.label: Polymerase palm Mg2+-chelating scaffold

- DNA-directed RNA polymerase β′ (RpoC/RPB1): strong block around the Mg2+-coordinating Asp triad (DFDGD), with peaks on neighboring helix/loop residues
- RNA-dependent RNA polymerases and single-subunit/phage RNAPs: palm-domain region surrounding the canonical GDD/HDD catalytic motif
- Helicases and other NTPases: residues near the Walker-B acidic motif and adjacent helices of the RecA-like core (weaker, shorter hits)
- Nucleases/CRISPR and topoisomerases: flanks of metal-dependent acidic motifs (HNH, RuvC, DDE) involved in phosphodiester cleavage
- GTP cyclohydrolase II (RibBA): single residue in a β-sheet immediately adjacent to a GTP-binding site
- Glutamyl‑tRNA reductase (HemA): clustered residues in a C‑terminal α-helix adjoining the catalytic core
- Glycoside hydrolases/glycosyl phosphorylases: isolated His/Asp/Glu within a catalytic helix near the active machinery
- Na+/H+ antiporter NhaA: short transmembrane segment near acidic ion-binding residues (brief activations)
- Tail spike peptidase S74/intramolecular chaperone: single residue near the autolytic cleavage site
- Alpha‑2‑macroglobulin/complement: scattered weak hits in secondary-structure elements (likely peripheral to the core concept)

14772.label: C-terminal catalytic core detector
14772.summary: Domain-level detector for long, ordered catalytic/regulatory cores in large eukaryotic signaling and trafficking proteins, most often their C‑terminal functional domains (e.g., HECT catalytic cores, cullin C‑terminal WHB/Rbx-binding regions, Ras/RapGAP-like folds, PIWI/RNase III/RdRP cores), and, in multipass membrane proteins, analogous long structured non-membrane loops
14772.description:
Summary: Domain-level detector for long, ordered catalytic/regulatory cores in large eukaryotic signaling and trafficking proteins, most often their C‑terminal functional domains (e.g., HECT catalytic cores, cullin C‑terminal WHB/Rbx-binding regions, Ras/RapGAP-like folds, PIWI/RNase III/RdRP cores), and, in multipass membrane proteins, analogous long structured non-membrane loops
Activation pattern: Domain-level activation over long contiguous stretches; frequently concentrated toward the C-terminus of multidomain proteins with C-terminal catalytic cores; low signal in transmembrane segments and disordered/low-complexity regions; in multipass membrane proteins, confined to long extracellular/lumenal loops between helices
Exemplars: - HECT-type E3 ubiquitin ligases: activation on the C-terminal HECT catalytic lobe containing the catalytic cysteine
- Cullin scaffold proteins and APC2 (CRL machinery): activation on the C-terminal cullin-homology/WHB region that binds the RING subunit/E2
- Sec1/Munc18 (SM) syntaxin-binding proteins: activation across the folded SM helical core that engages SNAREs
- Small GTPase regulators (Ras/Rap/Rab/Ral): activation on Ras/RapGAP-like catalytic domains and related noncatalytic GAP-like effectors (e.g., IQGAP); GEF catalytic modules when present
- Plexin cytoplasmic domains: activation on the split Ras/RapGAP-like catalytic region
- RNA interference/silencing machinery: Argonaute PIWI RNase H–like domain; Dicer C-terminal RNase III domains; RNA-dependent RNA polymerase catalytic core
- Vesicle transport/fusion components beyond SM: activation on long folded helical subdomains that scaffold coat/SNARE interactions
- Nucleic acid metabolism/repair proteins: activation on nuclease/polymerase RNase H–like or related catalytic cores
- Transmembrane channel-like proteins (e.g., TMC family): activation restricted to a long extracellular loop between adjacent transmembrane helices

4122.label: Flexible noncatalytic accessory domains
4122.summary: Non-catalytic, substrate/partner-engaging modules appended to enzymatic cores, with a strong preference for the C‑terminal TruD/PUA tRNA‑binding domain in pseudouridine synthases; more generally, the feature highlights flexible terminal/accessory regions (including disordered/coiled-coil segments and, in membrane enzymes, transmembrane helices/loops) that position or stabilize the active site, while avoiding the catalytic carboxylates themselves.
4122.description:
Summary: Non-catalytic, substrate/partner-engaging modules appended to enzymatic cores, with a strong preference for the C‑terminal TruD/PUA tRNA‑binding domain in pseudouridine synthases; more generally, the feature highlights flexible terminal/accessory regions (including disordered/coiled-coil segments and, in membrane enzymes, transmembrane helices/loops) that position or stabilize the active site, while avoiding the catalytic carboxylates themselves.
Activation pattern: Domain-level activation across the TruD/PUA-like C‑terminal domain; broad regional activation on low‑pLDDT, terminal/disordered or coiled‑coil segments; in membrane proteins, contiguous activation along TM helices and adjacent loops, especially flanking catalytic motifs; consistent suppression at catalytic Asp residues.
Exemplars: - TruD/Pus7 family tRNA pseudouridine synthases: strong, continuous activation over the C‑terminal TruD/PUA RNA‑binding domain; low around the catalytic Asp in the N‑terminal catalytic core.
- Pus10 tRNA pseudouridine synthase: activation on the N‑terminal coiled‑coil/disordered segment and a central non‑catalytic region; absent across the C‑terminal catalytic domain and at the catalytic Asp.
- TruA-family tRNA pseudouridine(38/39) synthase: activation confined to the N‑terminal non‑catalytic region; no activation at the catalytic region or catalytic Asp.
- Soluble enzyme with a well‑structured catalytic core: activation concentrated in disordered N‑ and C‑terminal tails; no activation at the nucleophilic active site.
- Signal peptide peptidase‑like aspartyl protease: activation along transmembrane helices and loops flanking the GxGD catalytic dyad and across the C‑terminal tail (including the PAL motif), while the catalytic Asp residues themselves are not activated.

2220.label: BED-transposase core activation
2220.summary: A feature that fires broadly across the central body of BED-domain zinc-finger / transposase-derived proteins and related fungal proteins containing BED-type zinc fingers. Activation covers an extended internal region downstream of the BED zinc finger, in the transposase/HAT-like core, and does not coincide with the BED zinc-finger DNA-binding module itself or with disordered/low-complexity flanking regions.
2220.description:
Summary: A feature that fires broadly across the central body of BED-domain zinc-finger / transposase-derived proteins and related fungal proteins containing BED-type zinc fingers. Activation covers an extended internal region downstream of the BED zinc finger, in the transposase/HAT-like core, and does not coincide with the BED zinc-finger DNA-binding module itself or with disordered/low-complexity flanking regions.

Activation pattern: Regional, contiguous activation spanning a large fraction of the protein (often 20-40% of residues), centered on the mid-protein transposase-like region. Peaks land on ordered segments enriched in aromatic and hydrophobic residues (W, F, Y, I, V), within recurrent motifs such as "TRWNS…", "WISTFY", and similar. Annotated low-complexity, acidic, and disordered regions are typically silent, as are the BED zinc-finger and its Zn-binding residues. In proteins with a single transmembrane helix adjoining the core, the TM segment can also be active.

Exemplars:
- BED/THAP/transposase-derived zinc-finger proteins (ZBED3, ZBED6, ZBED39, DAYSLEEPER, RICESLEEPER 1/4, Hobo transposase): contiguous activation across the central transposase-like region, downstream of the BED zinc finger.
- Fungal BED-ZF-containing regulators (Vid22, Vid11 in yeast): activation across the mid-to-C-terminal body of the protein, including the single transmembrane helix where present.
- Other large eukaryotic zinc-finger proteins (e.g. ZNF618): activation in an internal segment outside the annotated zinc fingers and disordered regions.

5873.label: CRISPR effector core activation
5873.summary: Structured catalytic-core segments within CRISPR-associated effector proteins, with particularly strong activation inside the HNH Cas9-type nuclease domain of Cas9 orthologs and the analogous structured cores of type I CRISPR subunits (Cas8/CasA).
5873.description:
Summary: Structured catalytic-core segments within CRISPR-associated effector proteins, with particularly strong activation inside the HNH Cas9-type nuclease domain of Cas9 orthologs and the analogous structured cores of type I CRISPR subunits (Cas8/CasA).
Activation pattern: Regional activation spanning tens of residues within an annotated functional domain; peaks fall in α-helices and adjacent β-strands of the structured core, while active-site and metal-coordinating residues themselves are largely avoided. Activation tolerates both helix and strand secondary structure.
Exemplars:
- CRISPR-associated endonuclease Cas9 (multiple orthologs including SpCas9, SaCas9, St-Cas9, Listeria, S. mutans, Neisseria): peaks concentrate inside the HNH Cas9-type domain, especially in a conserved helix near the C-terminal end of the HNH module (e.g., the KFD(N/Y)LTKAE-containing helix).
- CRISPR system Cascade subunit CasA/Cse1 (E. coli): activation over a structured β-strand/α-helix segment in the central body of the subunit.
- CRISPR-associated protein Cas8b (Haloferax) and Cas8a1/Csx13 (Myxococcus): activation across a structured internal segment of the Cas8 subunit.
- Across other overrepresented classes (E3 RING ligases, PIKfyve/FAB1 kinases, chromatin/Polycomb regulators, plant TFs DOF/SPL, RNA Pol III RPC5, RPAP2/RTR1, POT1, NarH, Rieske-type monooxygenases): activation typically maps to segments connecting or adjacent to functional domains.

8082.label: C-terminal helical scaffolds
8082.summary: Extended, C-terminal/distal alpha-helical “rod” segments (coiled-coils/alpha‑solenoids and juxtamembrane helices) and their helix–loop junctions, used for oligomerization/assembly or membrane-associated scaffolding rather than catalytic/DNA-binding cores; typically L/E/K/S/T-biased, long, and common in large eukaryotic scaffold/trafficking proteins but also seen in bacterial cytoskeletal systems.
8082.description:
Summary: Extended, C-terminal/distal alpha-helical “rod” segments (coiled-coils/alpha‑solenoids and juxtamembrane helices) and their helix–loop junctions, used for oligomerization/assembly or membrane-associated scaffolding rather than catalytic/DNA-binding cores; typically L/E/K/S/T-biased, long, and common in large eukaryotic scaffold/trafficking proteins but also seen in bacterial cytoskeletal systems.
Activation pattern: Broad regional activation over long contiguous helical runs (tens to hundreds of residues), usually in C-terminal halves; wide peaks centered on alpha helices with additional emphasis at helix–loop and helix–transmembrane boundaries; little activation on compact catalytic sites or Zn-finger DNA-binding domains.
Exemplars: - BED/THAP/Buster-like zinc-finger proteins: strong activation on long C-terminal helical tails (putative coiled-coil/dimerization regions), not on the N-terminal BED/THAP DNA-binding domain (cluster 1).
- Formins: activation within the C-terminal portion of the FH2 helical dimerization domain that mediates actin assembly (cluster 3).
- P4-ATPase lipid flippases: activation across a C-terminal transmembrane helix pair and the short cytosolic loop between them (juxtamembrane helical junction) (cluster 10).
- TMEM16/Anoctamin channel/scramblase family: activation on the cytosolic helix transitioning into a transmembrane segment (cluster 6).
- Vacuolar multi-pass membrane proteins (e.g., Hfl1): activation at loop–TM boundaries with spillover into adjacent helices (cluster 5).
- Cyclic nucleotide phosphodiesterases: activation on the terminal helix at the end of the catalytic PDEase domain, away from active/metal-binding residues (cluster 8).
- TubZ (tubulin-like plasmid partition): activation on a distal helix→coil segment just upstream of the disordered C-terminal tail involved in binding (cluster 9).

6004.label: Heme-proximal and jellyroll β-strands
6004.summary: Short, structured β-strand windows in heme-handling enzymes and viral capsid/hexon β-jellyroll proteins; the feature marks specific ~7-15 residue strand segments, often adjacent to cofactor- or interface-relevant residues, rather than long disordered or membrane-spanning stretches.
6004.description:
Summary: Short, structured β-strand windows in heme-handling enzymes and viral capsid/hexon β-jellyroll proteins; the feature marks specific ~7-15 residue strand segments, often adjacent to cofactor- or interface-relevant residues, rather than long disordered or membrane-spanning stretches.
Activation pattern: Sharp, localized peaks concentrated on individual β-strands and the immediately flanking helices/turns within the folded catalytic or capsid core; broader low-level activation across the surrounding domain, with signal peptides and N-terminal propeptides not activated.
Exemplars:
- Dye-decolorizing (DyP-type) peroxidases / deferrochelatases: peak activation on a conserved β-strand near the proximal heme-binding histidine (e.g., the RRGYSY-containing strand), with flanking helices and strands also lit up; signal peptides are not activated.
- Viral major capsid / hexon proteins (adenovirus hexons, PBCV-1 MCP, ASFV p72): peak activation on conserved β-strands within the jellyroll fold (e.g., the MWRIPFSSNF strand in adenovirus hexons; strand 579-593 in ASFV p72), with broader moderate activation across the surrounding β-barrel.

2512.label: Substrate pocket caps and interfaces
2512.summary: Substrate-recognition/cap regions that form aromatic- and gly/pro-loop–enriched pockets for small-molecule ligands, most prominently the C‑terminal substrate-binding domains of FAD-dependent oxidoreductases, plus analogous substrate-lining regions in other enzyme classes (non-flavin oxygenases/dioxygenases, glycoside hydrolases, aminoacyl‑tRNA ligases); also includes hydrophobic/aromatic interface caps of electron‑transfer accessory subunits in multi-subunit redox complexes that abut catalytic or quinone-binding sites; distinct from canonical cofactor/catalytic cores.
2512.description:
Summary: Substrate-recognition/cap regions that form aromatic- and gly/pro-loop–enriched pockets for small-molecule ligands, most prominently the C‑terminal substrate-binding domains of FAD-dependent oxidoreductases, plus analogous substrate-lining regions in other enzyme classes (non-flavin oxygenases/dioxygenases, glycoside hydrolases, aminoacyl‑tRNA ligases); also includes hydrophobic/aromatic interface caps of electron‑transfer accessory subunits in multi-subunit redox complexes that abut catalytic or quinone-binding sites; distinct from canonical cofactor/catalytic cores.

Activation pattern: Domain-level activation over long, contiguous mid-to-C‑terminal segments corresponding to structured substrate-binding/cap or interface regions; depleted on the exact cofactor-binding motifs (e.g., Rossmann glyglygly, metal‑ligating Cys motifs, ATP‑grasp cores) but often includes adjacent pocket-lining or interface loops.

Exemplars:
- Cytokinin dehydrogenase and other GMC/VAO/BBE-like FAD oxidases: activation on C-terminal substrate-recognition/cap domains; not on Rossmann-like FAD cores.
- Carotenoid cleavage and Rieske/non-heme iron oxygenases: activation on substrate-binding regions adjacent to the catalytic center.
- Glycoside hydrolases (e.g., beta-glucosidase/N-acetylglucosaminidase): activation at aromatic sugar-binding subsites (TIM-barrel mouth or C-terminal beta-sandwich/cap).
- Aminoacyl‑tRNA synthetases (e.g., GluRS): activation on the C-terminal anticodon/substrate-recognition lobe, not the catalytic Rossmann-like core.
- ATP-dependent ligases of glutathione biosynthesis (GshAB): activation on substrate-binding lobes shaping the glutathione-forming pocket, distal from the ATP-binding core.
- Glycolate oxidase/dehydrogenase complex: activation on the 2Fe–2S electron‑transfer subunit (GlcE-like) at the hydrophobic/aromatic interface cap adjacent to the FAD catalytic subunit, excluding the metal‑binding Cys motif.

3290.label: C-terminal helix-loop lids
3290.summary: C-terminal helix–loop subdomains that flank or include functional centers (active sites, ion/selectivity motifs, or nucleic‑acid/partner interfaces) at domain boundaries, often acting as lids/gates or interaction surfaces; these segments are typically enriched in charged/polar residues with frequent glycines.
3290.description:
Summary: C-terminal helix–loop subdomains that flank or include functional centers (active sites, ion/selectivity motifs, or nucleic‑acid/partner interfaces) at domain boundaries, often acting as lids/gates or interaction surfaces; these segments are typically enriched in charged/polar residues with frequent glycines.
Activation pattern: Regional activation: long, contiguous blocks predominantly in mid-to-C‑terminal regions, usually spanning a helix plus adjacent loop/strand. Peaks concentrate at helix termini, catalytic nucleophiles, or immediately upstream of selectivity/metal-binding motifs; activation can extend into acidic C‑terminal tails.
Exemplars: - Bacteriophage portal proteins: C‑terminal helical clip and acidic tail critical for DNA packaging, with a peak overlapping a mutationally sensitive site and activation along the preceding long helix.
- CRISPR-associated Cas1 endonucleases: C‑terminal helical lobe adjacent to the Mn2+ site, covering two helices and an intervening loop that frame the active center.
- HECT-type E3 ubiquitin ligases: C‑lobe segment around the catalytic cysteine within the HECT domain (active-site loop/coil with glycine peak) where ubiquitin transfer occurs.
- Pelota/DOM34 ribosome-rescue factors: discrete, structured C‑terminal patch (beta–helix–beta/helix motif) at the end of the domain.
- Catalases: C‑terminal coil/turn leading into a short helix; peak just before the helix that shapes the access channel/oligomeric interface.
- CorA Mg2+ transporters: C‑terminal end of the first transmembrane helix and short periplasmic loop immediately upstream of the GMN selectivity filter.
- Flavin-dependent thymidylate synthase (ThyX): C‑terminal helix/loop tail following the core domain, capping the dUMP/FAD-binding region and contributing to the multimer interface.

8326.label: Catalytic active-site cores
8326.summary: Catalytic-core regions of NAD+-utilizing enzymes and certain nuclease toxin payloads—including eukaryotic ADP-ribosyl cyclase / cyclic ADP-ribose hydrolases (CD38/BST1 family) and the C-terminal DNase payloads of contact-dependent inhibition (CdiA) polymorphic toxins—with focus on β-strands and helices flanking the active site and on toxicity/specificity-determining loops.
8326.description:
Summary: Catalytic-core regions of NAD+-utilizing enzymes and certain nuclease toxin payloads—including eukaryotic ADP-ribosyl cyclase / cyclic ADP-ribose hydrolases (CD38/BST1 family) and the C-terminal DNase payloads of contact-dependent inhibition (CdiA) polymorphic toxins—with focus on β-strands and helices flanking the active site and on toxicity/specificity-determining loops.
Activation pattern: Broad domain-level activation across the catalytic domain, with the strongest residue-level peaks falling on β-strands and short helices immediately adjacent to active-site residues, NAD+-binding residues, or specificity/toxicity-determining loops. Peak residues are commonly hydrophobic/polar core positions (V, M, L, H, T, K) within these secondary-structure elements. In modular toxins, N-terminal delivery/scaffold regions show weak activation while the C-terminal catalytic payload carries the strongest signal.
Exemplars:
- ADP-ribosyl cyclase / cyclic ADP-ribose hydrolases (CD38, BST1; vertebrate and Aplysia homologs): activation concentrated on β-strands and helices around the catalytic Glu/Cys and NAD+-binding residues.
- CdiA polymorphic toxin DNases (contact-dependent inhibition systems): activation restricted to the C-terminal DNase domain, peaking within toxicity-determining loops whose mutation abolishes nuclease activity and immunity binding.
- ADP-ribosyltransferase toxins (diphtheria/cholera/C3/ExoS-like): activation at NAD+-binding pockets and H–Y–E/R–S–E catalytic motifs and surrounding loops.
- Rhs polymorphic toxins: activation restricted to variable C-terminal toxin payloads (e.g., HNH/HHH nuclease, ADP-ribosyltransferase, protease payloads), not the RHS shell.
- Bacteriocins/colicins: activation on C-terminal DNase/RNase/tRNase domains.
- Peptidoglycan hydrolases and phage lytic transglycosylases: activation at catalytic glutamate/DxE motifs and glycan-binding loops.
- Cysteine and metalloprotease effectors: activation around catalytic Cys/His dyads or HExxH motifs and adjacent substrate-binding strands.
- Type III secretion effectors modulating host signaling (ExoU-like patatin phospholipases, SopB-like PI phosphatases, GAP/GEF-like modules, NEL-type E3 ligases): activation in catalytic pockets/loops.
- Viral capsid/nucleoproteins subset: activation over basic/polar nucleic-acid-binding surfaces.

- ADP-ribosyl cyclase / cyclic ADP-ribose hydrolases (CD38, BST1; vertebrate and Aplysia homologs): activation concentrated on β-strands and helices around the catalytic Glu/Cys and NAD+-binding residues.
- CdiA polymorphic toxin DNases (contact-dependent inhibition systems): activation restricted to the C-terminal DNase domain, peaking within toxicity-determining loops whose mutation abolishes nuclease activity and immunity binding.
- ADP-ribosyltransferase toxins (diphtheria/cholera/C3/ExoS-like): activation at NAD+-binding pockets and H–Y–E/R–S–E catalytic motifs and surrounding loops.
- Rhs polymorphic toxins: activation restricted to variable C-terminal toxin payloads (e.g., HNH/HHH nuclease, ADP-ribosyltransferase, protease payloads), not the RHS shell.
- Bacteriocins/colicins: activation on C-terminal DNase/RNase/tRNase domains.
- Peptidoglycan hydrolases and phage lytic transglycosylases: activation at catalytic glutamate/DxE motifs and glycan-binding loops.
- Cysteine and metalloprotease effectors: activation around catalytic Cys/His dyads or HExxH motifs and adjacent substrate-binding strands.

530.label: Tandem repeat and linker detector
530.summary: Detector of long tandem-repeat architectures and their stereotyped inter-repeat linkers in very large proteins. The feature turns on over arrays of repeated modules (e.g., C2H2 fingers, CCP/Sushi domains, cohesins, RTX/hemolysin repeats, PbH1 beta-helix blocks) and commonly their short, glycine/acidic/polar linkers, emphasizing the secondary-structure cores within each unit and the canonical linker motifs that connect them, while de-emphasizing unrelated domains, metal-binding cysteines, and transmembrane/cytosolic tails.
530.description:
Summary: Detector of long tandem-repeat architectures and their stereotyped inter-repeat linkers in very large proteins. The feature turns on over arrays of repeated modules (e.g., C2H2 fingers, CCP/Sushi domains, cohesins, RTX/hemolysin repeats, PbH1 beta-helix blocks) and commonly their short, glycine/acidic/polar linkers, emphasizing the secondary-structure cores within each unit and the canonical linker motifs that connect them, while de-emphasizing unrelated domains, metal-binding cysteines, and transmembrane/cytosolic tails.
Activation pattern: - Domain-level: Silent in nonrepeat modules (e.g., KRAB, CBM3, signal peptides, transmembranes), then near-continuous activation across long repeat arrays; often drops after the final repeat. Peaks frequently occur at or just before repeat boundaries.
- Residue-level: Preference for positions forming repeat cores (recognition helices or beta-strands; often hydrophobic/aromatic) and hallmark linker motifs enriched in S/T/E/G/K/P (e.g., TGEKP/Y between C2H2 fingers; GGXGXD in RTX). Metal-binding/disulfide cysteines (Zn-coordinating Cys/His; CCP disulfides) are consistently downweighted.
- Regional: Disordered, compositionally biased tracts are highlighted when they serve as repeat/linker belts within the array, but generic low-complexity segments outside such architectures can be suppressed.
Exemplars: - C2H2 zinc-finger transcription factors: strong activation across each finger’s recognition helix and the TGEKP/Y inter-finger linkers; low on Zn-coordinating Cys/His; KRAB N-termini inactive.
- Complement control protein (Sushi/CCP) domain arrays in complement receptors: high on hydrophobic beta-strands within CCP modules; low on disulfide cysteines; transmembrane helix and cytosolic tail off.
- RTX/hemolysin-type calcium-binding repeat proteins (e.g., FrpC, alginate epimerases): periodic peaks at GGXGXD and conserved hydrophobic/S/T positions within each RTX unit; activation falls after the last repeat.
- Cellulosomal scaffoldins: cohesive activation across cohesin domain arrays and their boundary linkers; N-terminal CBM domains largely inactive.
- Right-handed beta-helix (PbH1) repeat enzymes (alginate C5-epimerases): strong, contiguous signal across PbH1 blocks and associated hemolysin-type repeats; polar disordered linkers between repeats also elevated.
- Secreted mucin-like glycoproteins: accentuation of long S/T/N-rich, low-complexity disordered regions and their edges that function as linker belts.
- Telomere-associated nuclear megaprotiens: preference for hydrophobic secondary-structure blocks (repeat-like modules), with suppression over isolated low-complexity tracts.

15215.label: Disordered terminal tails
15215.summary: Disordered terminal/linker segments — especially N-terminal tails — that act as flexible interaction modules common in viral structural/nucleoproteins and in nucleic-acid–related enzymes and bacterial toxin/effectors; occasionally extends to compact terminal patches even when locally structured.
15215.description:
Summary: Disordered terminal/linker segments — especially N-terminal tails — that act as flexible interaction modules common in viral structural/nucleoproteins and in nucleic-acid–related enzymes and bacterial toxin/effectors; occasionally extends to compact terminal patches even when locally structured.
Activation pattern: Predominantly regional activation over long continuous stretches with low predicted structure quality, most often at the N-terminus and sometimes the C-terminus; minimal activation in well-folded catalytic cores, with rare activation of compact terminal segments.
Exemplars: - Phage minor capsid proteins: strong activation on the short, disordered N-terminal tail/propeptide immediately after the initiator Met.
- Phage peptidoglycan hydrolases/autolysins: activation on the disordered N-terminal segment and on additional low-confidence terminal regions, with no activation across the structured catalytic core.
- Rhabdovirus nucleoproteins: a focused peak on the basic N-terminal tail (e.g., around K18) within the flexible N-core region.
- CRISPR-Cas13a endoribonucleases: activation on disordered insertions and the C-terminal tail within/adjacent to HEPN-like domains; the structured central body is inactive.
- LXG family polymorphic toxins: activation at the extreme C-terminus outside the N-terminal LXG targeting domain, marking a terminal patch within the toxic effector region (even when locally structured).

3354.label: Noncatalytic assembly scaffolds
3354.summary: Extended non-catalytic scaffold regions that mediate assembly and binding in large macromolecular machines—typically alpha-helical (coiled-coil/alpha-solenoid) but also including basic low-complexity RNA/DNA-binding segments—especially in viral structural/packaging and other secreted/virulence proteins; these provide interaction surfaces rather than catalytic active sites.

Activation pattern: Broad regional activation across long, contiguous helical or basic low-complexity regions (hundreds to thousands of residues), with many activated positions and occasional peaks over nucleic-acid– or partner-binding patches; minimal activation at catalytic motifs (e.g., HEPN active sites in Cas13a).
Exemplars: - CRISPR-Cas13a endoribonucleases: strong activation on Helical-1/Helical-2/linker scaffold and crRNA-binding segments; low on HEPN catalytic residues
- Negative-sense RNA virus nucleoproteins: activation on basic, alpha-helical oligomerization arms and RNA-binding grooves that scaffold nucleocapsids
- Reoviridae core/outer capsid proteins: activation on extended helical bundles/coiled-coils for capsid assembly/stabilization
- Adenovirus packaging/vertex proteins: activation on helical assembly/packaging stalks and coiled-coil interfaces
- Herpesviridae terminase/portal proteins: activation on long helical barrel/coiled-coil scaffolds for DNA translocation portals
- Herpesvirus mRNA export regulators (ICP27/UL54 homologs): activation on basic, low-complexity RNA-binding/export segments and dimerization regions
- Apicomplexan invasion/secretory proteins: activation on secreted helical repeats/coiled-coil stalks mediating host interaction and complex assembly
- Bacterial type III secretion effectors and GEF mimics: activation on all-helical bundle scaffolds forming host-binding/activation interfaces
- Eukaryotic ER oxidoreductase ERO1: activation on non-catalytic helical scaffolding surrounding the FAD/disulfide catalytic core

7758.label: Phosphoinositide kinase/PX phosphate sensor
7758.summary: Phosphate-handling architecture centered on phosphoinositide signaling: the feature primarily recognizes the kinase-like catalytic cores of PI3/PI4 lipid kinases (and other ATP-dependent protein/inositol phosphate kinases), with hotspots around glycine-rich phosphate-binding loops and adjacent β/α elements; it also activates on phosphoinositide headgroup–binding modules (e.g., PX domains) and, more weakly, on other phosphate-binding pockets or basic, glycine-rich structured patches that mimic these surfaces (including some spore coat/invasin and cytoskeletal segments).
7758.description:
Summary: Phosphate-handling architecture centered on phosphoinositide signaling: the feature primarily recognizes the kinase-like catalytic cores of PI3/PI4 lipid kinases (and other ATP-dependent protein/inositol phosphate kinases), with hotspots around glycine-rich phosphate-binding loops and adjacent β/α elements; it also activates on phosphoinositide headgroup–binding modules (e.g., PX domains) and, more weakly, on other phosphate-binding pockets or basic, glycine-rich structured patches that mimic these surfaces (including some spore coat/invasin and cytoskeletal segments).
Activation pattern: Mixed: (1) long, contiguous activation blocks across the C-terminal catalytic lobes of lipid/protein/inositol phosphate kinases, often encompassing the glycine-rich loop and catalytic motifs; (2) short domain-segment activation at phosphoinositide-binding β/loop elements (PX domain N-termini) or ATP/phosphate-coordinating regions in adenylate/ligase folds; (3) sparse, weak residue-level peaks in other phosphate-binding pockets (phosphatases) or in structured, charged helices/strands that resemble phosphate-interacting surfaces (e.g., actin-binding CH helices, fungal CotH N-terminal domains).
Exemplars: - Phosphoinositide 3-/4-kinases (e.g., Vps34/PIK3C3, PI4KA/PI4KB/STT4 classes): long activation across the C-terminal catalytic domain, including the glycine-rich phosphate-binding loop and adjacent β-strands/α-helices.
- Secreted kinase family pseudokinase (FAM20A): strong activation over the N-lobe/catalytic-like core despite loss of activity, tracking the kinase-fold phosphate/ATP-binding architecture.
- Inositol phosphate kinases (e.g., IPMK/IP6K families): activation over the ATP/phosphate-binding catalytic core.
- Phox homology (PX) domain proteins (sorting nexins): activation at the N-terminal portion of the PX domain (β/loop region) that engages PI3P headgroups.
- ATP-dependent carboxylate–amine ligases/adenylate-forming enzymes (siderophore biosynthesis): mid-domain activation over the ATP/phosphate-binding subdomain.
- Protein tyrosine phosphatases: weak, focal activation within the phosphate-binding/catalytic pocket.
- Actin-binding calponin-homology (CH1) domains: isolated hotspot within the actin-binding helix that presents a basic/structured patch similar to phosphate-interacting surfaces.
- Fungal CotH spore coat/invasin proteins: extended activation over the structured N-terminal domain enriched in charged/polar residues, consistent with an anion-interacting surface that mimics the physicochemical signature of phosphate-binding regions.

16320.label: SPRY/pseudokinase PPI, acidic IDRs
16320.summary: Eukaryotic beta-rich interaction modules — particularly B30.2/SPRY domains and the beta-rich N-lobe scaffolds of pseudokinase domains — used as nonenzymatic PPI interfaces in chromatin, signaling, and RNA-binding proteins; and, in some cases, adjacent acidic/Ser/Thr-rich regulatory intrinsically disordered segments (including CaM-binding regions).

Summary: Eukaryotic beta-rich interaction modules — particularly B30.2/SPRY domains and the beta-rich N-lobe scaffolds of pseudokinase domains — used as nonenzymatic PPI interfaces in chromatin, signaling, and RNA-binding proteins; and, in some cases, adjacent acidic/Ser/Thr-rich regulatory intrinsically disordered segments (including CaM-binding regions).
Activation pattern: Domain-level, long contiguous activation across structured beta-rich folds with local peaks on strands and strand-flanking loops; and/or long bands within low-complexity acidic/polar regulatory regions flanking catalytic cores (e.g., kinase/phosphatase tails, CaM-binding segments). Signal frequently extends into adjacent N-lobe strands of (pseudo)kinase domains and into neighboring linkers. Occurs in N- or C-termini depending on architecture; broadly eukaryotic, rare in prokaryotes.

- ASH2/BRE2/ash-2 COMPASS components: activation across the B30.2/SPRY domain, with peaks on internal beta-strands.
- PEAK1/PRAG1 pseudokinases: activation across the pseudokinase N-lobe beta-sheet and adjacent homodimerization helix.
- hnRNP U-like 2 (SAF-A2): strong activation across the B30.2/SPRY domain.
- eEF2K: activation on Ca2+/calmodulin-binding regulatory segment and adjacent acidic IDR, not on the alpha-kinase core.
- CDC25 phosphatases: activation on the N-terminal regulatory low-complexity region rather than the catalytic phosphatase domain.

307.label: PI3K-like kinase catalytic core
307.summary: ATP-dependent kinase catalytic cores of phosphoinositide-metabolizing enzymes and PI3K-like protein kinases—i.e., PI3K/PI4K/PIPK families and PIKKs—recognized via the kinase-domain fold; with spillover to other nucleotide-dependent kinases, some phosphoinositide phosphatases, and rare non-kinase nucleotide-dependent transferases (e.g., glycosyl-/xylosyl-phosphotransferases, EC 2.7.8).

Activation pattern: Domain-level activation across long, contiguous stretches of the catalytic core, typically in the mid-to-C-terminal region of large enzymes; broadly covers the PI3K/PI4K catalytic domain including G-loop, activation loop, and C-lobe, with the strongest peaks concentrated near the C-terminal end of the catalytic domain; frequently marks the C-terminal kinase halves of class II PI3Ks and the extreme C-termini of PIKKs.
Exemplars:
- PI3K catalytic subunits (class I/II/III lipid kinases): activation over the PI3K catalytic core, peaking near its C-terminal end
- PI4-kinases (type III α/β and type II Golgi/ER enzymes): activation on the central-to-C-terminal kinase domain
- Phosphatidylinositol phosphate kinases (PIP5K/PIP4K): activation on the PIPK catalytic domain around the ATP-binding region (DLKDR-containing core)
- PI3K-related protein kinases (PIKKs: ATM/ATR/DNA-PK/mTOR/SMG1): activation on the extreme C-terminal PI3K-like Ser/Thr kinase domain
- Inositol phosphate kinases (e.g., IPMK, IP6K, PPIP5K): activation across their nucleotide-binding catalytic cores
- Eukaryotic Ser/Thr protein kinases, including atypical/secretory types (e.g., AGC/CaMK, haspin, alpha-kinases, Fam20): activation around the glycine-rich/ATP-binding region and catalytic motifs
- Phosphoinositide phosphatases (SAC1, synaptojanin/INPP5-type, PTEN-like): cross-activation across the phosphatase catalytic core due to shared inositol phosphate–binding architecture
- Rare non-kinase nucleotide-dependent transferases (e.g., xylosylphosphotransferase, EC 2.7.8.32): weak activation over the nucleotide-binding/phosphotransfer core
