2031.label: Conserved structured core detector
2031.summary: Detector of conserved, structured core domains in eukaryotic proteins—typically catalytic or DNA-binding cores—often in large signaling/regulatory proteins but also in metabolic enzymes; bias toward the onset and central portion of the globular core that may follow low-complexity or targeting-peptide regions.
2031.description:
Summary: Detector of conserved, structured core domains in eukaryotic proteins—typically catalytic or DNA-binding cores—often in large signaling/regulatory proteins but also in metabolic enzymes; bias toward the onset and central portion of the globular core that may follow low-complexity or targeting-peptide regions.
Activation pattern: Domain-level activation over long, contiguous, well-structured segments; typically rises at the transition from low-pLDDT/disordered or signal/targeting peptides into the core domain, stays high through the early-to-mid subdomain, and can taper in distal subregions; minimal activation in extended low-complexity flanks; occasional residue-level peaks at catalytic/ligand-coordinating residues.
Exemplars:
- Cyclic nucleotide phosphodiesterases (PDEs): activation on the N-terminal helical subdomain at the start of the PDEase catalytic core, with little signal over the distal metal-binding site.
- JmjC histone demethylases: strong activation across the JmjC catalytic core (double-stranded β-helix), including the Fe(II)/2-oxoglutarate-binding H/D/H triad.
- HECT-type E3 ubiquitin ligases: sustained activation across the HECT catalytic domain, including the active-site catalytic cysteine.
- Myotubularin/MTMR lipid phosphatases: activation concentrated in the N-terminal half of the PTP-like catalytic domain, reduced in the C-terminal regulatory/interaction subregion.
- GRAS/SCL/SHR/SCR transcription factors: activation within the GRAS domain, especially the LRI and VHIID subregions, absent from the long disordered N termini and later subregions (LRII/PFYRE/SAW).
- Phosphoinositide kinases (PI3Ks/PI4Ks): activation across the conserved kinase catalytic core following regulatory repeats.
- Other structured enzyme cores (e.g., terpene synthases, acyltransferases): activation across the main catalytic fold, often following short transit peptides or low-complexity N termini.

5596.description:
Summary: Conserved ATP-binding subdomain of kinase catalytic cores across diverse folds (protein kinase-like, PI3/4K-like, alpha-kinase, ABC1/COQ8, PIPK, Fam20/four-jointed, and some small-molecule kinases), centered on the N-terminal ATP-binding subdomain and adjacent N-lobe surface; typically excludes the C-terminal catalytic/activation segments.
Activation pattern: Regional activation over long contiguous stretches (≈100–300 aa) within the ATP-binding subdomain (often the N-terminal half) of the catalytic domain; peaks on a conserved N-lobe helix preceding the catalytic loop, with additional substantial signal on the glycine-rich/P-loop or fold-specific phosphate-binding segment and nearby Lys/basic region; in lipid kinases, also highlights basic membrane-interaction inserts; little signal in disordered flanks and in catalytic carboxylate/activation loops, though in some bacterial/small-molecule kinases it can extend into the catalytic Asp/Glu region.
Exemplars:
- Class III PI3K (Vps34): strong signal on the N-terminal part of the catalytic domain including a conserved N-lobe helix and the glycine-rich loop region; absent from catalytic and activation loops.
- Type II PI4K: broad activation across the N-lobe including substrate-binding residues and a membrane-interacting helix; weak in the C-terminal half of the domain.
- RIO atypical kinase: activation over the early kinase-domain N-lobe including the ATP-binding Lys; not over the C-lobe catalytic Asp region.
- Alpha-kinase (myosin heavy chain kinase): peak on an N-lobe helix preceding/adjacent to the ATP site; little signal at the annotated ATP-binding residues.
- Type I/II phosphatidylinositol phosphate kinases (PIP5K/PIP4K): activation on the N-terminal segment of the catalytic core including ATP/substrate-binding and basic inserts; weak in the distal half.
- Inositol hexakisphosphate kinase (IP6K): activation across the ATP-binding lid and adjacent core; minimal at distal catalytic residues.
- Secreted Golgi-lumenal protein kinases (four-jointed/Fam20-like): activation over ATP-lid/basic surface; weak at C-terminal catalytic segments.
- Bacterial isocitrate dehydrogenase kinase/phosphatase (AceK): activation spans the central catalytic core, including the ATP-binding site and extending to the active-site Asp.
- Ribokinase-like methylthioribose kinase: activation across the central ATP-binding core and can reach the catalytic Asp.
- Bacterial Ser/Thr protein kinase (ePK-like): broad N-lobe signal covering ATP-binding elements; minimal over the C-lobe catalytic Asp/activation loop.

738.label: Right-hand polymerase catalytic core
738.summary: Conserved catalytic core of "right-hand" nucleic acid polymerases, unifying RNA-dependent RNA polymerases and reverse transcriptases (including telomerase, retroviral/retrotransposon/LINE-1 and retron RTs) together with single-subunit T7-like/organellar RNA polymerases.
738.description:
Summary: Conserved catalytic core of "right-hand" nucleic acid polymerases, unifying RNA-dependent RNA polymerases and reverse transcriptases (including telomerase, retroviral/retrotransposon/LINE-1 and retron RTs) together with single-subunit T7-like/organellar RNA polymerases.
Activation pattern: Domain-level, long contiguous activation across the central/C-terminal RT/polymerase catalytic core, with sharp residue-level peaks at a conserved basic "RFxPK"/T-motif element within the palm/fingers region upstream of the acidic catalytic motifs.
Exemplars: - Viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerases from +ssRNA/−ssRNA/dsRNA viruses: broad activation across the RdRp catalytic core.
- Telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT): activation across the RT catalytic core, peaking at a conserved RFxPK palm/fingers motif.
- Retroviral and retrotransposon reverse transcriptases, including LINE-1 ORF2p and bacterial retron RTs: activation across the RT palm.
- Single-subunit RNA polymerases (T7-like bacteriophage RNAP) and organellar RNAPs (mitochondrial/plastid): activation within the central polymerase core.
- Plant group II intron maturase/MatR-like proteins: activation on the embedded RT-like domain.
- Minor cross-activation: RNase III–family nucleases (Dicer/Drosha) at their two-metal-ion active sites, weaker than in polymerases.

3261.label: Polymerase C-terminal extension
3261.summary: C-terminal, non-catalytic extensions of nucleic-acid polymerases—especially viral RdRps, reverse transcriptases, and single-subunit (phage/organellar-type) RNAPs—covering segments downstream of the polymerase catalytic core that mediate RNA binding and/or partner interaction (frequently including NLS motifs), and which in viral polyproteins can extend into the adjacent RNA-binding capsid region.
3261.description:
Summary: C-terminal, non-catalytic extensions of nucleic-acid polymerases—especially viral RdRps, reverse transcriptases, and single-subunit (phage/organellar-type) RNAPs—covering segments downstream of the polymerase catalytic core that mediate RNA binding and/or partner interaction (frequently including NLS motifs), and which in viral polyproteins can extend into the adjacent RNA-binding capsid region.
Activation pattern: Regional activation: long, dense stretches focused immediately C-terminal to the polymerase catalytic core, spanning both helical/structured elements and adjacent low-complexity/disordered tails; minimal activation within catalytic motifs; occasional weak, isolated peaks in other transcription factors (cross-reactivity).
Exemplars: - Negative-strand RNA virus L proteins (mononegavirales RdRp): strong activation across the C-terminal regulatory/interaction region that includes an NLS, not in the RdRp core.
- Positive-strand RNA virus replicases (e.g., plant virus RdRp/replicase 2a): activation on the C-terminal tail beyond the catalytic domain.
- Potyvirus polyprotein around the NIb→capsid junction: peak over the disordered segment preceding cleavage and continuing through the disordered, RNA-binding capsid protein.
- Large viral RNA replication proteins: continuous activation across the C-terminal tail after the annotated RdRp catalytic domain.
- Telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT): activation on the C-terminal extension (CTE) following the reverse transcriptase domain.
- Single-subunit DNA-dependent RNA polymerases (phage-type/organellar RNAPs): activation on the ~C-terminal 100 aa tail outside the active site.
- Sigma-70 factors (bacterial RNAP initiation factors): only a weak, isolated helical residue peak (rare cross-reactivity).

5056.label: Viral RdRp region marker
5056.summary: Viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) module within replicase proteins—marking the RdRp chain and immediately adjacent flanking regions across diverse RNA viruses (dsRNA, +ssRNA, −ssRNA). The signal broadly tracks the polymerase-bearing segment of polyproteins or standalone RdRps, with recurrent local suppression at the invariant catalytic Asp residues; non‑polymerase replication enzymes (e.g., capping/MTase, protease) show little activation.
5056.description:
Summary: Viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) module within replicase proteins—marking the RdRp chain and immediately adjacent flanking regions across diverse RNA viruses (dsRNA, +ssRNA, −ssRNA). The signal broadly tracks the polymerase-bearing segment of polyproteins or standalone RdRps, with recurrent local suppression at the invariant catalytic Asp residues; non‑polymerase replication enzymes (e.g., capping/MTase, protease) show little activation.
Activation pattern: Long, domain-level activation over hundreds of residues. In polyproteins, activation often turns on sharply at the cleavage that releases the RdRp and remains high across the entire RdRp chain (sometimes extending into a helicase–polymerase fragment). In large/standalone polymerases, activation is strongest across the N‑terminal/fingers and polymerase‑proximal regions and commonly shows local troughs (often zero) at catalytic Asp residues (motifs A/C). Activation is minimal in distant capping/methyltransferase or protease domains and is sparse in non‑viral proteins.
Exemplars: - dsRNA virus VP1 RdRp: strong, continuous activation across an extended N‑terminal region preceding the annotated catalytic palm; reduced signal through the core catalytic domain.
- Mononegavirales L polymerase (Paramyxoviridae): high activation across the N‑terminal–mid L region preceding the RdRp catalytic core; zero at Mg2+-binding Asp residues; weak/none over downstream PRNTase and 2′‑O‑methyltransferase modules.
- Picornaviridae 3Dpol: strong activation across the N‑terminal half (including disordered and NLS‑containing segments); sharp troughs at the catalytic Asp residues; reduced in the C‑terminal catalytic palm.
- Plant-virus Pro–Pol polyprotein (VPg–protease–polymerase): activation rises at the VPg/Pro–Pol junction and stays high throughout the released RdRp chain, including the catalytic domain; negligible over upstream protease/N‑terminal proteins.
- Positive‑strand plant‑virus replicase module with helicase–polymerase fragment: high activation across the helicase‑containing cleavage product that encompasses the RdRp catalytic domain; little signal on upstream methyltransferase/OTU peptidase/other accessory domains.
- Probable RdRp (unclassified plant/fungal/invertebrate RNA viruses): contiguous high activation across a large C‑terminal region corresponding to the polymerase domain, spanning disordered‑to‑structured transitions; N‑terminal regions remain low.

7942.label: Nucleotide-handling catalytic modules
7942.summary: Catalytic-module regions of viral nucleotide-polymerizing enzymes, predominantly RNA-directed RNA polymerases, with activation spread broadly across the replicase block and adjacent structured elements rather than confined to the catalytic core; the feature also extends to structurally related or degenerate nucleotide-binding modules (GUK-like) and compositionally similar flexible regulatory regions.
7942.description:
Summary: Catalytic-module regions of viral nucleotide-polymerizing enzymes, predominantly RNA-directed RNA polymerases, with activation spread broadly across the replicase block and adjacent structured elements rather than confined to the catalytic core; the feature also extends to structurally related or degenerate nucleotide-binding modules (GUK-like) and compositionally similar flexible regulatory regions.
Activation pattern: Broad regional activation over polymerase modules, with residue-level peaks falling preferentially in hydrophobic/aromatic-rich helices and strands C-terminal to the annotated catalytic palm domain. In viral polyproteins, activation concentrates in C-terminal replicase blocks.
Exemplars: - Viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerases/replicases (including Mononegavirales L proteins, narnavirus RdRps, bacteriophage RNA replicases): broad activation across the polymerase module with strong peaks in the C-terminal half of the catalytic block.
- Reverse transcriptases (eukaryotic telomerase and retroelement/bacterial RTs): activation on the RT catalytic domain and surrounding regions.
- DNA-dependent DNA polymerases (e.g., family B): activation on the palm domain and neighboring regions involved in nucleotide addition.
- cGAS-like nucleotidyltransferases: activation across the NTase core.
- CRISPR-Cas9 nucleases: activation within the HNH and RuvC nuclease regions.
- MAGUK guanylate kinase-like domains (e.g., in CARD11): activation at the N-terminus of the GUK-like fold, consistent with recognition of a nucleotide-handling module even when catalytically inactive.
- Cytosolic phospholipase A2 gamma: activation over a disordered C-terminal region required for lipid-droplet localization and at a phosphoserine, reflecting the feature's tendency to score flexible, acidic/basic-rich regulatory segments akin to linkers around phosphate-chemistry active sites.

9008.label: Polymerase palm DxD motif
9008.summary: Catalytic palm active-site di-aspartate (DxD) segment of nucleic acid polymerases—especially the YMDD/GDD-type motif that coordinates Mg2+/Mn2+—in reverse transcriptases, RNA-dependent RNA polymerases, telomerase RTs, and (more weakly) some DNA polymerases; the feature captures the short β‑strand environment surrounding the metal-binding Asp pair.
9008.description:
Summary: Catalytic palm active-site di-aspartate (DxD) segment of nucleic acid polymerases—especially the YMDD/GDD-type motif that coordinates Mg2+/Mn2+—in reverse transcriptases, RNA-dependent RNA polymerases, telomerase RTs, and (more weakly) some DNA polymerases; the feature captures the short β‑strand environment surrounding the metal-binding Asp pair.
Activation pattern: Residue-level peaks concentrated in a short window (≈8–15 residues) within the polymerase palm, maximized on the consecutive catalytic Asp residues and tapering across adjacent β‑strand residues; occasional secondary peaks at other conserved acidic residues in the same RT/RdRp palm but minimal activation elsewhere (e.g., no signal in RNase H or priming/terminal protein regions).
Exemplars: - Hepadnavirus reverse transcriptase: strong, localized peak over the YMDD motif and its β‑strand context in the RT palm; silent in terminal protein and RNase H domains.
- Retroviral reverse transcriptase (e.g., HIV-1 Pol): sharp peak centered on the di‑Asp of the YxDD/YMDD region that binds Mg2+.
- Telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT): highest activation at the catalytic double‑Asp in motif C (e.g., HDD/ADD), with a smaller peak at an upstream palm acidic site; little outside the RT domain.
- RNA-dependent RNA polymerases of positive-, negative-sense, and dsRNA viruses (including Mononegavirales L): activation at the palm motif C (typically GDD or close variants) and flanking β‑strand residues.
- Group II intron maturase and bacterial retron reverse transcriptases: activation on the RT palm YxDD-like catalytic segment.
- DNA-dependent DNA polymerases: weaker activation on the palm acidic catalytic motif.

10777.label: RT/RdRp pre-catalytic region
10777.summary: Active-site–proximal segment of RNA-dependent polymerases (reverse transcriptases and RdRps): the conserved pre‑catalytic region immediately N‑terminal to the metal-binding Asp residues (“DD/GDD” motif C) within the RT/RdRp module, typically encompassing the motif B/primer‑grip loop and adjacent helix that engage the template/incoming NTP and help close the palm domain; shared across viral RdRps and reverse transcriptases, including telomerase and retrons.
10777.description:
Summary: Active-site–proximal segment of RNA-dependent polymerases (reverse transcriptases and RdRps): the conserved pre‑catalytic region immediately N‑terminal to the metal-binding Asp residues (“DD/GDD” motif C) within the RT/RdRp module, typically encompassing the motif B/primer‑grip loop and adjacent helix that engage the template/incoming NTP and help close the palm domain; shared across viral RdRps and reverse transcriptases, including telomerase and retrons.
Activation pattern: Regional activation in internal 40–90 aa windows within RT/RdRp domains, with sharp residue-level peaks on flexible loop/coil–helix elements enriched for small (G, S/T) and acidic (D/E) residues. The signal usually terminates right before the annotated Mg2+-binding Asp(s) of the catalytic site, or lies immediately upstream of the annotated start of the RdRp catalytic domain; long polymerases may show multiple such windows around the polymerase module.
Exemplars: - Bacterial retron reverse transcriptases: disordered loop within the RT domain that ends immediately before the Mg2+-binding Asp of the catalytic “DD” region.
- Telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT): short disordered loop followed by a helix in the N-terminal RT core, with activation dropping to baseline at the catalytic Asp; weak secondary signal within RT beta-sheets.
- Hepadnavirus P protein (reverse transcriptase): long loop with a short helix in the RT domain, ceasing just before a beta-strand bearing the Mg2+-coordinating Asp residues.
- Mononegavirales L polymerases (RdRp within L): helical/coil segment directly upstream of the annotated RdRp catalytic core, with activation dropping upon entry into the catalytic domain.
- Positive-sense ssRNA replicase polyproteins (RdRp chain): coil flanked by helices immediately N-terminal to the RdRp catalytic domain boundary.
- RNA virus RdRp catalytic subunits (e.g., fungal/yeast RNA viruses, narnaviruses): promoter/template-binding helix and adjacent loop at the N-terminus of the catalytic core, spanning into the start of the RdRp palm.

13567.label: Viral replication accessory regions
13567.summary: Non-catalytic, polymerase-adjacent accessory regions of viral genome-replication enzymes (RdRPs, reverse transcriptases/hepadnaviral P, and viral primases), typically flexible/low-complexity and helical modules used for replication-complex assembly or regulation rather than the catalytic core
13567.description:
Summary: Non-catalytic, polymerase-adjacent accessory regions of viral genome-replication enzymes (RdRPs, reverse transcriptases/hepadnaviral P, and viral primases), typically flexible/low-complexity and helical modules used for replication-complex assembly or regulation rather than the catalytic core
Activation pattern: Long, contiguous regional activation blocks that preferentially cover N‑terminal or mid‑protein accessory segments enriched in G/D/K/S/T and mixed disorder-to-helix content; the signal avoids canonical catalytic motifs and metal-binding sites (e.g., RdRP palm/fingers, primase acidic residues, zinc fingers) and often drops to zero over the catalytic domains
Exemplars: - RNA-directed RNA polymerases (dsRNA, +ssRNA, −ssRNA): activation over N‑terminal leader/accessory regions; off over the promoter-binding site and polymerase catalytic domain.
- Mononegavirales L polymerases: activation in the non-catalytic capping/methyltransferase/linker modules rather than the RdRP core.
- Reverse-transcribing polymerases (hepadnaviral polymerase P/RT-like): activation in terminal protein/spacer and other non-catalytic segments, not the RT/RNase H active sites.
- Bacteriophage RNA replicases: activation in non-catalytic N‑terminal regions.
- Viral DNA primases: activation in a mid‑protein helical/coil accessory subdomain; absent at the catalytic acidic residues and zinc-finger module.
- Other replication-associated viral enzymes (e.g., capping or MTase components): activation on accessory stretches outside enzyme active sites.

13590.label: Viral RdRp palm catalytic core
13590.summary: Core nucleotidyl-transferase/polymerase catalytic module (right-hand/palm active site) — most prominently the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp/NIb) catalytic domain of viral replicases; occasionally cross-reacts with homologous palm-based nucleotidyl transferases (e.g., some family B DNA polymerases and CRISPR Cas10/Csm1 cyclase/palm domains), but strongest and most consistent for viral RdRps

Summary: Core nucleotidyl-transferase/polymerase catalytic module (right-hand/palm active site) — most prominently the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp/NIb) catalytic domain of viral replicases; occasionally cross-reacts with homologous palm-based nucleotidyl transferases (e.g., some family B DNA polymerases and CRISPR Cas10/Csm1 cyclase/palm domains), but strongest and most consistent for viral RdRps
Activation pattern: Domain-level, long contiguous activation that turns on at the polymerase module (often at the C-terminus of large replicase polyproteins) and spans the catalytic core and adjacent subdomains; strongest over the palm/catalytic region containing conserved polymerase motifs (A–C, including GDD) and nearby structural elements (e.g., TPR2/Palm2/Thumb), sometimes extending into the immediate disordered C-terminal tail; minimal or absent over non-polymerase accessory regions (protease, methyltransferase, helicase, capping, capsid); non-RdRp palm NTases show variable or weak activation
Exemplars:
- Viral RdRp/NIb (positive-sense RNA viruses such as norovirus and potyviruses): activation across the C-terminal RdRp catalytic domain and into short disordered tails
- Alphavirus-like and related replicase polyproteins: activation exclusively on the C-terminal RdRp domain, not on upstream methyltransferase, protease, helicase, or capping modules
- Negative-/dsRNA polymerases (e.g., PB1/VP1/λ3/L-like): activation on the conserved polymerase core
- Some family B DNA polymerases (especially primer-independent PolB): activation over TPR2, Palm2, and Thumb; others (e.g., terminal-protein-primed phi29 PolB) may be weak or inactive
- CRISPR-associated Cas10/Csm1: activation on the C-terminal Palm-like cyclic oligonucleotide synthase domain

- Alphavirus-like and related replicase polyproteins: activation exclusively on the C-terminal RdRp domain, not on upstream methyltransferase, protease, helicase, or capping modules
- Negative-/dsRNA polymerases (e.g., PB1/VP1/λ3/L-like): activation on the conserved polymerase core
- Some family B DNA polymerases (especially primer-independent PolB): activation over TPR2, Palm2, and Thumb; others (e.g., terminal-protein-primed phi29 PolB) may be weak or inactive
- CRISPR-associated Cas10/Csm1: activation on the C-terminal Palm-like cyclic oligonucleotide synthase domain

14359.label: Polymerase palm catalytic motif
14359.summary: Conserved catalytic palm subdomain of right-hand nucleotidyl-transferase polymerases, strongest for RNA-directed enzymes (RNA-dependent RNA polymerases and reverse transcriptases, including telomerase), centered on motif A of the palm around a conserved catalytic Asp and Mg2+-binding site.
14359.description:
Summary: Conserved catalytic palm subdomain of right-hand nucleotidyl-transferase polymerases, strongest for RNA-directed enzymes (RNA-dependent RNA polymerases and reverse transcriptases, including telomerase), centered on motif A of the palm around a conserved catalytic Asp and Mg2+-binding site.
Activation pattern: Regional activation over a contiguous stretch (tens of residues) within the polymerase module, with pronounced peaks on motif A containing a conserved Asp adjacent to a Mg2+ ligand; minimal signal in non-polymerase domains (e.g., protease, RNase H, zinc-finger). Enriched for acidic (D/E) and glycine residues; peaks typically sit just adjacent to the catalytic Asp rather than exactly on it.
Exemplars: - Retroviral/retrotransposon Pol polyproteins: activation confined to the Reverse Transcriptase core, absent over the protease and RNase H domains.
- Plant +ssRNA virus RdRPs (e.g., NIb from potyviruses and other plant viruses): strong activation over the palm catalytic motif.
- Negative-sense RNA virus L proteins (Mononegavirales and related): activation over the RdRp palm catalytic region around the Mg2+-binding Asp.
- dsRNA virus polymerases (e.g., reoviral λ3/rotaviral VP1): activation in the catalytic palm.
- Group II intron maturase RTs: activation over the RT-like palm active site.
- Bacterial retron reverse transcriptases: activation centered on the RT palm catalytic motif.
- Telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT): activation within the RT-like palm subdomain.
- Endogenous retroelements (e.g., LINE-1 ORF2p and other retroelement RTs): activation over the RT core palm.
- DNA polymerases (A/B families): weaker but detectable activation over the homologous palm active-site region due to shared fold.

2689.label: Exposed helical binding surfaces
2689.summary: Solvent-exposed alpha-helical interaction surfaces (often including coiled-coils) that mediate binding to nucleic acids and/or partner proteins; highlights helical scaffolds rather than catalytic cores
2689.description:
Summary: Solvent-exposed alpha-helical interaction surfaces (often including coiled-coils) that mediate binding to nucleic acids and/or partner proteins; highlights helical scaffolds rather than catalytic cores
Activation pattern: Regional activation across long alpha-helices and helical linkers (frequently coiled-coil–like), with residue-level peaks biased to hydrophobic residues (I/V/L/A/M/F) along the helical face with intermittent K/E peaks; depleted on beta-strands and enzymatic active-site residues; can span large portions of helical-rich domains
Exemplars: CRISPR-Cas13a endoribonucleases: activation tracks crRNA-binding and linker helices adjacent to HEPN domains while sparing catalytic H/R; Viral fusion/assembly and capsid-fiber families (e.g., hemagglutinin/fusion stalks, adenovirus fiber, coiled-coil capsid scaffolds): activation on long heptad-repeat helices mediating trimerization and virion exposure; Type III secretion and Legionella effectors: activation on helical segments and coiled-coil motifs used for secretion-chaperone binding and host-target engagement; Nucleic acid–binding replication/packaging proteins (nucleoproteins, helicase/loader and genome-packaging factors): activation on helical patches that contact RNA/DNA; Eukaryotic cytoskeletal/mitotic scaffolds (HEAT/ARM and coiled-coil repeat proteins): activation across extended alpha-solenoid/coiled-coil regions; Apicomplexan adhesins/secreted host-interaction proteins: activation on coiled-coil stems and helical repeats exposed to the extracellular milieu

6403.label: Basic disordered NLS/NA-binding patches
6403.summary: Positively charged, lysine/arginine‑rich intrinsically disordered segments (often at the N‑terminus) that serve as generic nucleic‑acid/chromatin‑binding patches and/or classical nuclear localization signals, frequently flanked by serine/threonine sites for phosphoregulation; prevalent in nuclear and DNA/RNA‑associated proteins, including many nuclear DNA viruses.
6403.description:
Summary: Positively charged, lysine/arginine‑rich intrinsically disordered segments (often at the N‑terminus) that serve as generic nucleic‑acid/chromatin‑binding patches and/or classical nuclear localization signals, frequently flanked by serine/threonine sites for phosphoregulation; prevalent in nuclear and DNA/RNA‑associated proteins, including many nuclear DNA viruses.
Activation pattern: Residue‑level peaks centered on Lys/Arg (with secondary peaks on nearby Ser/Thr) within low‑pLDDT/disordered regions; often concentrated at very N‑terminal positions; patchy across long nuclear proteins; little to no activation in folded catalytic domains.
Exemplars: - Epstein–Barr virus nuclear antigen (EBNA3): sharp activation on a KRKR motif in the disordered N‑terminus; minor activation in another disordered segment.
- Herpesvirus capsid‑associated protein VP80: peaks on K/R clusters within disordered C‑terminal tail consistent with genome/transport interaction patches.
- Multi‑domain enzyme with a structured Mg‑binding catalytic C‑terminus: activation confined to disordered, basic N‑terminal segments (putative NLS/nucleic‑acid‑binding tail), absent over the catalytic domain.
- U3 small nucleolar RNP factor: N‑terminal disordered basic residues (R/K) adjacent to multiple S/T phosphosites in a nucleolar RNA‑processing protein.
- Yeast chromatin regulator Spt21: isolated peaks on R/K within low‑confidence helices/coils, consistent with basic IDRs used for chromatin association.
- RNA chaperones (e.g., La/SSB): activation on basic low‑complexity regions that mediate RNA binding and nuclear localization.

7111.label: Polar IDR PTM hotspots
7111.summary: Low-complexity, intrinsically disordered regulatory regions in nuclear gene-regulatory/chromatin proteins—especially in fungi—enriched in polar/acidic residues (S/T/Q/N, often with D/E, P/G), serving as activation/interaction modules and PTM hotspots (notably phosphorylation and SUMO), while avoiding folded DNA-binding and catalytic cores.
7111.description:
Summary: Low-complexity, intrinsically disordered regulatory regions in nuclear gene-regulatory/chromatin proteins—especially in fungi—enriched in polar/acidic residues (S/T/Q/N, often with D/E, P/G), serving as activation/interaction modules and PTM hotspots (notably phosphorylation and SUMO), while avoiding folded DNA-binding and catalytic cores.
Activation pattern: Predominantly long, contiguous regional activation across N-/C-terminal IDRs and polar linkers; residue-level peaks concentrate within clusters of S/T/Q/N (often with D/E) and frequently coincide with annotated phosphosites or SUMO-acceptor lysines. Activation is minimal over high-confidence structured catalytic and DNA-binding domains.
Exemplars: - Fungal transcription factors: strong activation on acidic/QN-rich activation domains and disordered terminal tails, with little signal on structured DNA-binding cores (as in EUC1).
- Histone-modification enzymes (writers/erasers: HATs, HMTs, HDACs, demethylases): activation on long regulatory IDRs flanking catalytic domains, often harboring phospho/SUMO sites.
- Telomere-associated and sequence-specific DNA-binding proteins: activation on low-complexity N-/C-terminal arms used for recruiting chromatin factors; little on the structured DNA-binding core.
- DNA repair/checkpoint proteins: activation on disordered S/TQ-rich regions targeted by checkpoint kinases; weak on folded domains.
- SUMO/ubiquitin E3 ligases linked to chromatin: activation on acidic/polar regulatory IDRs adjacent to core ligase domains, consistent with PTM-rich control segments.

7304.label: Viral helical functional regions
7304.summary: Regional feature firing on medium-to-long contiguous stretches within viral and phage accessory/structural proteins, often overlapping functionally important segments such as RNA-binding regions, zinc-binding motifs, and structured helical cores.
7304.description:
Summary: Regional feature firing on medium-to-long contiguous stretches within viral and phage accessory/structural proteins, often overlapping functionally important segments such as RNA-binding regions, zinc-binding motifs, and structured helical cores.
Activation pattern: Broad regional activation across large portions of the protein, with peaks falling on mixed hydrophobic/polar residues within structured helices or within annotated functional motifs (e.g., HCCH zinc-binding motif, RNA-binding region); peaks tend to cluster in short contiguous windows of 5-10 residues but the overall active region spans much larger fractions of the chain.
Exemplars:
- HIV-1/HIV-2 virion infectivity factor (Vif): activation across the central region overlapping the RNA-binding region and the HCCH zinc-binding motif.
- Ebola virus membrane-associated protein VP24: activation on multiple structured helices and a C-terminal hydrophobic segment.
- Bacteriophage P1 DarA (anti-restriction protein): activation in an internal segment adjacent to a coiled-coil region.

7645.label: Patchy structural-region peaks
7645.summary: A broad, sequence-context feature that fires in scattered patches across many diverse proteins, with peaks often falling in folded chain regions and at local structural boundaries rather than being restricted to any single fold class
7645.description:
Summary: A broad, sequence-context feature that fires in scattered patches across many diverse proteins, with peaks often falling in folded chain regions and at local structural boundaries rather than being restricted to any single fold class
Activation pattern: Mixed regional activation with multiple residue-level peaks distributed along the protein; long proteins typically show several activated patches (~10–20% of residues), while short proteins can show one compact peak; peaks include positions inside structured domains (β-strands, short helices, C-terminal folded subdomains) as well as some disordered segments
Exemplars:
- Viral antigens with disordered C-terminal regions (e.g., HDV small delta antigen): peaks in disordered Ser/Gly/Lys-containing stretches
- Viral capsid proteins (e.g., rotavirus VP6): peaks at short N-terminal helical segments
- Bacterial/plant metabolic enzymes (PEPCK, ACCase β subunit): peaks within the folded catalytic chain, away from active-site motifs
- RNA polymerase α-like subunits: peaks within the C-terminal domain (alpha-CTD)
- Bacterial type III effectors (e.g., HopW1-1) and anti-restriction phage proteins (DarA): scattered patches distributed along the chain
- Small secreted toxins (e.g., heat-stable enterotoxin II): compact peak inside a disulfide-stabilized β-strand
- Short viral immune-evasion proteins (e.g., HSV ICP47): peak within the functional/active domain region

9001.label: Aromatic-hydrophobic core motifs
9001.summary: Hydrophobic/aromatic-rich core segments of domains that either (i) scaffold catalytic nucleophile/His (or Ntn) pockets in enzymes or (ii) form non-enzymatic recognition cores (e.g., XPC/Rad4 DNA-damage wedges) and cofactor-binding pockets (FAD/ATP); activation is selective to members with extended hydrophobic/aromatic runs in mid-to-late domain regions, typically organized around an aromatic-hydrophobic motif (e.g., HxWNxV / AWNxV-like) flanking the catalytic residue.
9001.description:
Summary: Hydrophobic/aromatic-rich core segments of domains that either (i) scaffold catalytic nucleophile/His (or Ntn) pockets in enzymes or (ii) form non-enzymatic recognition cores (e.g., XPC/Rad4 DNA-damage wedges) and cofactor-binding pockets (FAD/ATP); activation is selective to members with extended hydrophobic/aromatic runs in mid-to-late domain regions, typically organized around an aromatic-hydrophobic motif (e.g., HxWNxV / AWNxV-like) flanking the catalytic residue.
Activation pattern: Focal activation on short aromatic/hydrophobic motifs embedded within mid/core stretches of larger domains; activation occurs in subfamilies that contain expanded aromatic/hydrophobic inserts around catalytic or recognition sites rather than uniformly across all homologs.
Exemplars: - Peptide:N-glycanase and transglutaminase-like cysteine hydrolases: activation across the fold around the Cys–His–Asp triad and oxyanion hole (subset with extended hydrophobic loops).
- Calpain/papain-like cysteine proteases: activation over the protease core (subset with enlarged hydrophobic substrate-binding regions).
- Deamidases/amidohydrolases (non-PNGase): activation over cysteine-centered pockets with hydrophobic surrounds (subset-specific).
- Homing inteins/HINT endonucleases: activation on the nucleophile-containing HINT fold.
- Gamma-glutamyltransferase (GGT; Ntn hydrolase): activation around the N-terminal nucleophile in hydrophobic cores.
- Peptide methionine sulfoxide reductases (MsrA/MsrB): activation on thiol-based active sites when accompanied by extended aromatic/hydrophobic neighborhoods.
- Cryptochrome/photolyase family: activation when the long Trp-chain/FAD-pocket extension is present; not universal across all photolyases.
- FAD:protein FMN transferase (ApbE): activation on the FAD-binding/catalytic core.
- Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases: occasional activation across the ATP/aa-binding core; not universal.
- DNA-damage recognition proteins (XPC/Rad4): activation on the aromatic beta-hairpin/propeller core that wedges distorted DNA.
- C2 domain-containing and centrosomal/cytoskeletal/flagellar proteins: activation on aromatic/hydrophobic motifs outside the canonical C2 module, in accessory hydrophobic segments of the larger protein.
- Note: ATP-dependent ligases (e.g., GlnA3) and sulfurtransferases (rhodanese) generally remain inactive unless they harbor such extended aromatic/hydrophobic inserts.

9576.label: Catalytic cysteine loop-helix motif
9576.summary: Active-site nucleophilic cysteine motif: a short loop→helix segment that positions the catalytic Cys of a Cys–His (±Asp/Asn) dyad/triad, typically in a local Cys–Gly/glycine-rich context, shared across cysteine-dependent enzymes including cysteine proteases/deubiquitinases (OTU/ULP/USP/UCH/Josephin), NlpC/P60 peptidoglycan amidases/endolysins, Cif-family protein-glutamine deamidases, CLN5-type acyl-thioester intermediate hydrolases/transferases, viral cysteine proteases, and YopJ-family acyltransferases.
9576.description:
Summary: Active-site nucleophilic cysteine motif: a short loop→helix segment that positions the catalytic Cys of a Cys–His (±Asp/Asn) dyad/triad, typically in a local Cys–Gly/glycine-rich context, shared across cysteine-dependent enzymes including cysteine proteases/deubiquitinases (OTU/ULP/USP/UCH/Josephin), NlpC/P60 peptidoglycan amidases/endolysins, Cif-family protein-glutamine deamidases, CLN5-type acyl-thioester intermediate hydrolases/transferases, viral cysteine proteases, and YopJ-family acyltransferases.
Activation pattern: Residue-level peaks centered on the catalytic cysteine within a compact 10–30 aa cluster spanning the preceding loop and the N-terminus of an alpha-helix; secondary peaks on residues immediately flanking the catalytic Cys (e.g., the adjacent Gly of a Cys–Gly motif) and occasionally nearby substrate-binding or processing residues (e.g., Gly-Gly autolysis sites); typically high structural confidence; rare weaker activation on structurally analogous helix/coil patches in non-catalytic binding domains.
Exemplars: - OTU deubiquitinases: peak on the Cys-loop catalytic Cys with spread into the adjacent helix; minor signal on nearby acidic/variable-loop residues.
- SUMO/ULP proteases (including viral ULP-like proteases): peak at the nucleophilic Cys at a helix N-terminus; secondary peak at the catalytic His; extension to a substrate-binding residue.
- Legionella SdeA deubiquitinase: sharp peak at the catalytic Cys in the N-terminal DUB domain; minor activation near the His of the active site.
- NlpC/P60-type peptidoglycan amidases (e.g., Tse1): strong peak at the nucleophilic Cys in a short helix.
- Cif-family protein-glutamine deamidases (e.g., CHBP, Cif): sharp peak at the catalytic Cys at the N-terminus of an alpha-helix, with spread along the helix.
- CLN5 BMP synthases: peak at the nucleophile Cys forming the acyl-thioester intermediate, with spread into the surrounding loop/helix.
- Viral cysteine proteases (e.g., adenovirus protease): peak at the catalytic Cys in a helix; minor peak at an autolysis Gly-Gly site.
- YopJ-family Nε‑fatty acyltransferases (e.g., IcsB): peak at the catalytic Cys at a loop→helix junction.
- Calponin-homology binding domain (MICAL): weak activation on a conserved helix/coil segment that mimics the geometry of the targeted motif despite lacking a catalytic cysteine.

9802.label: Cysteine adjacent oxyanion helix
9802.summary: Active-site nucleophile-adjacent alpha helix/oxyanion-hole segment immediately C-terminal to the catalytic cysteine in cysteine-dependent proteases and isopeptidases. The feature captures the short helix and preceding loop that position/stabilize the catalytic thiolate and transition state (Cys–Gly–(Ser) neighborhood with transition-state–stabilizing residues such as Gln/Asn/Ser, sometimes nearby Trp), while consistently excluding the cysteine itself. It unifies papain-like endopeptidases and diverse deubiquitinase/Ubl isopeptidase folds across bacteria, eukaryotes, and viruses.
9802.description:
Summary: Active-site nucleophile-adjacent alpha helix/oxyanion-hole segment immediately C-terminal to the catalytic cysteine in cysteine-dependent proteases and isopeptidases. The feature captures the short helix and preceding loop that position/stabilize the catalytic thiolate and transition state (Cys–Gly–(Ser) neighborhood with transition-state–stabilizing residues such as Gln/Asn/Ser, sometimes nearby Trp), while consistently excluding the cysteine itself. It unifies papain-like endopeptidases and diverse deubiquitinase/Ubl isopeptidase folds across bacteria, eukaryotes, and viruses.
Activation pattern: Strong, localized regional activation over a contiguous 10–30 residue stretch within the catalytic domain, rising sharply immediately after the nucleophilic cysteine and peaking in the adjacent alpha helix; the catalytic cysteine itself is deactivated (near-zero). Activation may include the preceding “regulatory” loop and residues forming the oxyanion hole; little to no signal in propeptides or noncatalytic domains. The pattern holds across well-ordered helices and also in lower-confidence helical/coil segments in viral proteases.
Exemplars: - OTU deubiquitinases: helix directly after the catalytic Cys within the catalytic core/regulatory loop is maximally highlighted (e.g., regulatory-loop helix following Cys; nearby stabilizing His in the helix is emphasized while the Cys is not).
- UCH deubiquitinases: the N-terminal catalytic helix containing the nucleophile is activated around it (transition-state Gln highlighted), with the nucleophilic Cys de-emphasized and distal catalytic His not highlighted.
- ZUFSP/ZUP1 deubiquitinases: a well-structured helix immediately C-terminal to the catalytic Cys shows peak activation (Q/S residues in the helix emphasized).
- Josephin/MJD deubiquitinases: short N-terminal helix beginning at the catalytic Cys is strongly activated while the Cys itself and distal catalytic His are not.
- Calpains: helical residues just downstream of the catalytic Cys within the peptidase core peak in activation; other active-site residues (His/Asn) are lower.
- ATG4 autophagy proteases: a high-confidence helix immediately following the nucleophilic Cys is highlighted; other catalytic residues (His/Asp) are inactive.
- Bacterial virulence cysteine proteases (e.g., Ig-targeting proteases): a central alpha helix starting at the nucleophile Cys shows the strongest activation, with flanking beta/coil regions weak.
- Viral papain-like proteases (arterivirus Nsp1α/Nsp2): short segments directly C-terminal to the catalytic Cys within the peptidase domains are highlighted, even when predicted structure is partially disordered.

- ZUFSP/ZUP1 deubiquitinases: a well-structured helix immediately C-terminal to the catalytic Cys shows peak activation (Q/S residues in the helix emphasized).
- Josephin/MJD deubiquitinases: short N-terminal helix beginning at the catalytic Cys is strongly activated while the Cys itself and distal catalytic His are not.
- Calpains: helical residues just downstream of the catalytic Cys within the peptidase core peak in activation; other active-site residues (His/Asn) are lower.
- ATG4 autophagy proteases: a high-confidence helix immediately following the nucleophilic Cys is highlighted; other catalytic residues (His/Asp) are inactive.
- Bacterial virulence cysteine proteases (e.g., Ig-targeting proteases): a central alpha helix starting at the nucleophile Cys shows the strongest activation, with flanking beta/coil regions weak.
- Viral papain-like proteases (arterivirus Nsp1α/Nsp2): short segments directly C-terminal to the catalytic Cys within the peptidase domains are highlighted, even when predicted structure is partially disordered.

10498.label: Cysteine-centered catalytic loop-strand
10498.summary: Active-site neighborhood of thiol-dependent amide/isopeptide–bond enzymes—most prominently cysteine-centered deamidases, transamidases, and peptidases (e.g., PNGase/Transglutaminase-like and OTU DUB families)—capturing the short loop/helix and adjacent strand that position the catalytic Cys with a nearby His and acidic residue (often with local Cys/Gly enrichment and, in some cases, Zn2+ coordination); secondarily, the feature also marks structurally similar Cys/Gly-enriched loop–strand modules in non-cognate proteins, including some DNA damage-recognition factors (e.g., RAD4/XPC), and weakly marks analogous catalytic-core segments of other amide-chemistry enzymes (e.g., glutamine synthetase) and viral RdRp cores.
10498.description:
Summary: Active-site neighborhood of thiol-dependent amide/isopeptide–bond enzymes—most prominently cysteine-centered deamidases, transamidases, and peptidases (e.g., PNGase/Transglutaminase-like and OTU DUB families)—capturing the short loop/helix and adjacent strand that position the catalytic Cys with a nearby His and acidic residue (often with local Cys/Gly enrichment and, in some cases, Zn2+ coordination); secondarily, the feature also marks structurally similar Cys/Gly-enriched loop–strand modules in non-cognate proteins, including some DNA damage-recognition factors (e.g., RAD4/XPC), and weakly marks analogous catalytic-core segments of other amide-chemistry enzymes (e.g., glutamine synthetase) and viral RdRp cores.
Activation pattern: Predominantly a single, contiguous regional activation within catalytic domains (tens to ~100 residues), with residue-level peaks at or near cysteine- and glycine-containing loops or loop–helix boundaries; often coincident with variable loops that shape a pocket or with nearby metal-binding elements (Zn2+/Mg2+). In non-cognate proteins (e.g., RAD4/XPC, viral RdRp), activation contracts to short 8–15 residue motifs inside conserved cores or DNA-binding loops.
Exemplars:
- Peptide:N-glycanase (PNGase; transglutaminase-like superfamily): activation spans the Cys-rich region and adjoining mixed secondary structure in the catalytic core, peaking on a short helix/loop immediately C-terminal to the first Zn-binding Cys.
- Transglutaminase (TG2): activation on the catalytic-core loop/helix that positions the catalytic Cys-His-Asp triad.
- OTU deubiquitinase (cysteine protease): activation on the catalytic OTU domain’s variable loop that abuts the catalytic Cys and shapes the S1 pocket.
- DNA repair RAD4/XPC: activation on a short beta-strand/loop module used for lesion recognition, reflecting the same Cys/Gly-enriched loop–strand topology without a thiol catalytic site.
- Glutamine synthetase (amide ligase): activation on a short helix within the catalytic domain adjacent to Mg2+-ligating residues.
- Viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase: a localized 8–15-residue activation within the conserved catalytic core.
- Type VI secretion system spike (VgrG): moderate activation on a conserved beta-strand and flexible loop segment with peaks at Cys/Gly, indicating recognition of a short structural motif.

10693.label: Transglutaminase-like Cys hydrophobic motif
10693.summary: A conserved hydrophobic sequence patch characteristic of the transglutaminase-like domain found in cytokinesis/septation proteins, LIM–transglutaminase proteins (Hillarin/ltd-1), Kyphoscoliosis peptidase, and Dynein regulatory complex subunit 7 (CCDC135/lobo). The motif typically takes the form "LFKxLCSxAGL" or "LLxSMLIGAG" and surrounds a catalytic or structurally analogous cysteine where one is present.
10693.description:
Summary: A conserved hydrophobic sequence patch characteristic of the transglutaminase-like domain found in cytokinesis/septation proteins, LIM–transglutaminase proteins (Hillarin/ltd-1), Kyphoscoliosis peptidase, and Dynein regulatory complex subunit 7 (CCDC135/lobo). The motif typically takes the form "LFKxLCSxAGL" or "LLxSMLIGAG" and surrounds a catalytic or structurally analogous cysteine where one is present.

Activation pattern: Residue-level peaks within a short local window (≈5–15 aa) covering a hydrophobic stretch of large aliphatic/aromatic residues (L/F/M/V/I) often flanking a Cys, with Gly residues at the C-terminal edge. Activation lies outside coiled-coil and disordered regions, on the conserved transglutaminase-like core.

Exemplars:
- Kyphoscoliosis peptidase and its homologs (e.g., ltd-1): activation on the catalytic Cys loop of the transglutaminase-like domain.
- Hillarin (LIM and transglutaminase domain protein): activation on the conserved LFKRLCSYAGL patch.
- Fungal cytokinesis protein 3 (S. pombe and S. cerevisiae Cyk3): activation on the equivalent hydrophobic patch within the transglutaminase-like region.
- Dynein regulatory complex subunit 7 / CCDC135 / lobo (Drosophila, mouse, bovine, Xenopus): activation on the analogous LLxSMLIGAG hydrophobic motif.
- N-malonyltransferase FDB2: activation near the acyl-thioester catalytic Cys in an analogous hydrophobic local context.

10816.label: Terminal low-complexity interaction tails
10816.summary: Terminal low‑complexity interaction tails (predominantly C‑terminal) that are disordered‑to‑helical segments enriched in polar/charged residues with interspersed hydrophobics, carrying short linear motifs or key residues used for partner docking (protein or nucleic acid), oligomerization, or proximity to regulatory redox sites
10816.description:
Summary: Terminal low‑complexity interaction tails (predominantly C‑terminal) that are disordered‑to‑helical segments enriched in polar/charged residues with interspersed hydrophobics, carrying short linear motifs or key residues used for partner docking (protein or nucleic acid), oligomerization, or proximity to regulatory redox sites
Activation pattern: Long, contiguous regional activation over mid‑to‑C‑terminal stretches, often reaching the extreme terminus; residue‑level peaks at short linear motifs or critical residues (e.g., RGD, catalytic/modified Ser, regulatory Cys, leucine‑rich oligomerization positions). Usually low‑pLDDT (IDR/coil) but can include a terminal amphipathic α‑helix with high pLDDT; in some small viral proteins, activation can also occur at the N‑terminus.
Exemplars: - Arenavirus nucleoproteins: strong activation on the C‑terminal tail mediating host DAXX binding and homomultimerization, with leucine/isoleucine hotspots in a disordered helix/coil segment.
- ERO1‑like oxidoreductases: activation on the C‑terminal regulatory loop and terminal α‑helix adjacent to the redox‑active cysteine pair.
- Bacteriophage terminal/primer proteins: activation on the C‑terminal priming domain containing the covalent primer serine and an RGD motif for DNA polymerase docking.
- Gram‑negative T3SS/T4SS effectors/components: activation on long acidic/proline‑rich terminal regions used for chaperone/host interaction and secretion‑linked partner binding.
- Viral structural/replication proteins (capsid/tegument/envelope tails, polymerase cofactors): activation on low‑complexity terminal tails that mediate assembly and host interactions.
- CRISPR/anti‑restriction and other DNA‑defense proteins: activation on flexible terminal segments presenting SLiMs for complex assembly or DNA/protein contacts.
- Archaeal methyl‑coenzyme M reductase subunits: activation on extended terminal tails/flexible linkers implicated in multi‑subunit assembly.

10826.label: Polybasic low-complexity IDRs
10826.summary: Compositionally biased low-complexity segments enriched in polar/charged residues (often Lys/Arg‑rich) — typically intrinsically disordered polybasic patches and repeats, with occasional short basic helices — a general sequence/structural property common in viral proteins and DNA‑associated factors rather than a specific motif.
10826.description:
Summary: Compositionally biased low-complexity segments enriched in polar/charged residues (often Lys/Arg‑rich) — typically intrinsically disordered polybasic patches and repeats, with occasional short basic helices — a general sequence/structural property common in viral proteins and DNA‑associated factors rather than a specific motif.
Activation pattern: Regional activation across extended low‑complexity stretches (frequently at N/C termini or linkers) with broad, distributed signal over many residues; minimal signal in well‑folded globular cores; can reappear on isolated short basic helices adjacent to or outside the disordered regions.
Exemplars: - Viral nucleocapsid/core and protamine-/histone-like proteins: strong activation across Lys/Arg‑rich, low‑complexity RNA/DNA‑binding regions used for genome packaging.
- Viral replication proteins (RNA‑dependent RNA polymerases, helicases, methyltransferases/capping enzymes): activation on basic, compositionally biased N/C‑terminal tails and interdomain linkers.
- Viral ubiquitin-system E3 ligases: activation on flexible, charged low‑complexity segments implicated in adaptor/substrate engagement.
- Viral and eukaryotic serine/threonine kinases (especially from large DNA viruses): activation on disordered, basic terminal extensions and insertions.
- DNA-associated nuclear proteins: activation on polybasic, low‑complexity patches (including NLS‑like regions) and other compositionally biased stretches.
- Holocytochrome c‑type synthase: activation over the disordered, compositionally biased N‑terminus containing heme‑regulatory motif repeats and the N‑myristoylation context, silence across the structured core, and re‑activation on a distal basic C‑terminal helix.

10903.label: Secondary structure boundary capping motifs
10903.summary: Secondary-structure boundary elements—especially alpha-helix capping/transition segments and short helices at domain junctions—with occasional overlap to small metal-binding inserts (e.g., cysteine-rich Zn-binding loops)
10903.description:
Summary: Secondary-structure boundary elements—especially alpha-helix capping/transition segments and short helices at domain junctions—with occasional overlap to small metal-binding inserts (e.g., cysteine-rich Zn-binding loops)
Activation pattern: Primarily localized regional activation over short stretches (∼5–30 aa) centered on helix–coil or helix–strand junctions; peaks often extend a few residues into the helix and/or adjacent coil; sporadic single-residue spikes occur exactly at boundaries or in low-confidence loop segments; in some cases, a broader continuous region across an inter-domain insert containing multiple such junctions and conserved cysteines
Exemplars: - C2-domain proteins: activation on a short beta–coil boundary immediately C-terminal to the C2 domain.
- Peptide:N-glycan amidases (PNGase/deglycosylases): activation across the inter-domain region between thioredoxin-like and PAW domains, peaking over a cysteine-rich Zn-binding insert and neighboring helix/strand segments.
- RAD4/XPC DNA-damage recognition proteins: activation at the end of a long helix transitioning into coil and a short beta element within the lesion-recognition core.
- Bacterial peptidyl‑tRNA hydrolase: activation on the N-terminal alpha-helix and the preceding coil (first beta–alpha unit).
- MaoC-like 3‑hydroxyacyl‑ACP dehydratase: activation at the start of the MaoC domain, spanning a coil-to-helix transition and the first helix.

11213.label: Nuclear phospho-regulated Ser/Thr-rich IDRs
11213.summary: Ser/Thr-rich, low-complexity intrinsically disordered regulatory regions (typically N- or C-terminal tails) of nuclear DNA replication/repair and chromatin-associated proteins, enriched for acidic/basic compositional tracts and phosphorylation sites (often S/T–P motifs) that mediate phospho-regulated interactions.

Summary: Ser/Thr-rich, low-complexity intrinsically disordered regulatory regions (typically N- or C-terminal tails) of nuclear DNA replication/repair and chromatin-associated proteins, enriched for acidic/basic compositional tracts and phosphorylation sites (often S/T–P motifs) that mediate phospho-regulated interactions.
Activation pattern: Predominantly long regional activation over IDRs (often at termini), with little to no signal in folded catalytic cores; residue-level peaks concentrate on clusters of serine/threonine (including known phosphosites) within compositionally biased acidic/basic segments.
Exemplars: - DNA repair helicase Mph1/FANCM family: activation on disordered N- and C-terminal tails; no activation on the structured helicase ATPase core.
- NuA4 histone acetyltransferase complex subunit Eaf7: strong activation across the disordered C-terminal half, peaking at annotated phosphoserines.
- ISWI chromatin-remodeling subunit Ioc4: dominant activation on a long C-terminal IDR containing alternating acidic/basic tracts and phosphoserines; minimal signal in structured regions.
- Replication initiation/ORC–MCM regulators: activation on S/T-rich disordered terminal regions that harbor cell-cycle phospho-sites.
- Kinetochore/centromere and chromosome passenger complex components: activation on acidic/basic low-complexity tails used for regulated protein–protein docking.
- Telomere maintenance factors: activation on disordered regulatory segments flanking DNA/RNA-binding cores.
- Nuclear pore complex subunits: activation on low-complexity disordered repeats within flexible FG-/charged regions.
- SUMO/ubiquitin E3 ligases and viral chromatin-interacting regulators: activation on proline- and S/T-rich disordered activation domains targeted by phosphorylation.

11651.label: Ser/Thr-Pro-rich acidic IDRs
11651.summary: Long, intrinsically disordered, low‑complexity tracts enriched in Ser/Thr with interspersed Pro and often acidic residues (E/D)—i.e., S/T‑P‑rich IDRs—capturing mucin‑like O‑glycosylation‑prone repeats in secreted proteins and acidic/proline‑rich activation/interaction regions in nuclear/viral regulators.

Summary: Long, intrinsically disordered, low‑complexity tracts enriched in Ser/Thr with interspersed Pro and often acidic residues (E/D)—i.e., S/T‑P‑rich IDRs—capturing mucin‑like O‑glycosylation‑prone repeats in secreted proteins and acidic/proline‑rich activation/interaction regions in nuclear/viral regulators.
Activation pattern: Strong regional activation across extended low‑complexity/disordered segments; highest over S/T runs with P and acidic residues but tolerant of other small/polar residues (A/Q/G/V); depleted in structured elements (signal peptides, helices/folded domains, transmembranes) and C‑terminal GPI‑anchor/propeptides; does not target specific short motifs or N‑glycosylation sequons.
Exemplars: - Herpesviral nuclear antigens/transactivators (e.g., EBNA family): activation on long central proline‑/acidic‑rich disordered blocks that serve as activation/interaction regions; low signal over adjacent structured helical islands.
- Fungal GPI‑anchored cell‑surface adhesins (e.g., Fig2p/Flo/Als families): activation on extracellular Ser/Thr‑rich mucin‑like repeats immediately after the signal peptide; absent on the signal peptide and on the C‑terminal GPI‑anchor/propeptide; no specific boost at N‑glycosylation sequons.
- Broadly across eukaryotic regulatory proteins and viral regulatory/accessory proteins: activation on Ser/Thr/Pro‑rich, acidic low‑complexity IDRs used for flexible interactions and post‑translational modification.

11676.label: Disordered Ser/Thr phosphorylation sites
11676.summary: Short linear motifs centered on serine/threonine within intrinsically disordered regions that correspond to eukaryotic Ser/Thr phosphorylation sites (often SP/TP or basic R/K-flanked motifs), used for regulatory control across diverse proteins including viral proteins
11676.description:
Summary: Short linear motifs centered on serine/threonine within intrinsically disordered regions that correspond to eukaryotic Ser/Thr phosphorylation sites (often SP/TP or basic R/K-flanked motifs), used for regulatory control across diverse proteins including viral proteins
Activation pattern: Residue-level peaks on single S/T or 1–3 aa motifs, punctate and distributed across proteins; strongly enriched in low-pLDDT coils and low-complexity segments; depleted in folded domains and transmembrane helices; occasional peaks at edges of low-confidence helices; context frequently includes nearby proline and/or basic residues
Exemplars: - PH plus RapGAP scaffold proteins: activation on S/T residues in disordered linkers; minimal signal in folded PH and GAP domains
- Chromatin regulator Spt21: multiple peaks in disordered C-terminal regions; includes a known phosphoserine site
- TORC1 subunit Tco89: peaks at/near an annotated phosphothreonine and other disordered segments
- Large transmembrane receptor with long cytosolic tail (stum): activation confined to disordered cytosolic regions; none in transmembrane helices
- Developmental cytoskeletal regulator (bottleneck): clusters on S/T within low-complexity, basic-enriched disordered C-terminus
- Small GTPase regulators (e.g., RhoGAPs, RasGEFs, ARF GEFs) and protein kinases: signal found in regulatory low-complexity regions and termini rather than catalytic cores, consistent with phosphorylation-prone SLiMs

12332.label: Hydrophobic MoRF hotspots in IDRs
12332.summary: Hydrophobic/aromatic hotspots within intrinsically disordered, low‑complexity regions (IDRs)—especially long linkers and terminal tails—marking short linear interaction–prone elements (MoRF/SLiM-like) rather than folded domains.

Summary: Hydrophobic/aromatic hotspots within intrinsically disordered, low‑complexity regions (IDRs)—especially long linkers and terminal tails—marking short linear interaction–prone elements (MoRF/SLiM-like) rather than folded domains.

- Yeast regulatory proteins (e.g., stress/transport suppressors): scattered hydrophobic residues highlighted within disordered segments across the sequence.

13801.label: Alpha-helical residue detector
13801.summary: Residue-level detector of alpha-helical secondary structure, with a bias toward amphipathic/charged helices and helical bundles/repeats, independent of specific function or taxonomy.
13801.description:
Summary: Residue-level detector of alpha-helical secondary structure, with a bias toward amphipathic/charged helices and helical bundles/repeats, independent of specific function or taxonomy.
Activation pattern: Sparse, discrete residue-level peaks concentrated within DSSP H helices across long stretches of proteins; largely absent from disordered tails; insensitive to local pLDDT (appears in both low- and high-confidence helices); occasionally touches transmembrane helices but does not uniformly mark them.
Exemplars: - CRISPR-associated endoribonuclease Cas13a: peaks in the helical linker and HEPN helical elements, including residues near crRNA-binding and catalytic helices.
- Viral capsid-associated protein (VP80): scattered single-residue peaks confined to alpha-helices across the capsid protein.
- Arenavirus nucleoprotein: sharp peaks in the helical core; little/no signal in the disordered C-terminal tail.
- Type III secretion effector (HopM1): numerous peaks across predicted alpha-helical segments spanning the effector.
- Apicomplexan rhoptry protein (high-molecular-weight rhoptry protein): multiple activated alpha-helical segments, with moderate signal in a predicted transmembrane helix and in disulfide-bearing helices.
- Eukaryotic ER oxidase (ERO1-like): activation on helices within the helical bundle, not on redox-active cysteines or specific FAD-binding motifs.
- Fungal spore wall protein: sparse peaks in helical regions of the mature chain, absent from the signal peptide.

15352.label: Acidic IDR linear motifs
15352.summary: Short low-complexity intrinsically disordered linear motifs used for protein–protein interactions—including acidic D/E-rich tracts as well as other short linear motifs (e.g., PIP boxes, viral late-domain motifs, and the conserved acidic C-terminal tail of ribosomal P-stalk proteins, …GFGLFD-like)

Activation pattern: Regional activation with sharp residue-level peaks confined to short (≈10–30 aa) windows in IDRs/low-complexity regions; frequently terminus-biased (especially extreme C-termini for P-stalk tails and PIP boxes); peaks fall in clustered acidic patches or in short hydrophobic/aromatic-anchored linear motifs (e.g., LxLxL-like, GFGLFD, QxxLxF-type PIP cores); minimal signal in structured cores but can show multiple peaks across extended low-complexity regions

15430.label: Extended hydrophobic helical tracts
15430.summary: Extended low‑polarity, hydrophobic cluster–rich segments (enriched in L/V/I/F/Y/W/A/M with frequent G/P breaks) with alpha‑helical propensity; these regions often appear as long, flexible/low‑confidence tracts in viral structural and polymerase proteins but also comprise stable helical cores in soluble secretory enzymes (composition‑driven rather than motif‑specific, and not specifically transmembrane)

Activation pattern: Regional activation across long contiguous stretches, with multiple peaks on aliphatic/aromatic residues; repeats across several segments per protein; commonly overlaps low‑pLDDT/IDR regions in viral proteins yet also marks well‑ordered alpha‑helical domains; avoids sharp, short motifs (e.g., NLS, disulfide/catalytic cysteine loops, signal peptides)
Exemplars: - Negative‑sense RNA virus nucleoproteins: long predicted helical segments with low pLDDT (flexible, assembly‑prone amphipathic helices).
- Papillomavirus major capsid protein (L1): intrinsically disordered coil/loop regions spanning many residues, enriched in hydrophobic residues within flexible surface tracts.
- Influenza A polymerase PB2: multiple low‑confidence segments (helical, strand, and coil) marked by extended hydrophobic composition.
- ER oxidoreductase ERO1‑alpha: stable, multi‑helix FAD‑binding core rich in hydrophobic residues; low activation in the signal peptide and cysteine‑rich regulatory loop.

15785.label: Exposed protein termini detector
15785.summary: A positional/structural detector of protein chain ends, strongest at the extreme C-terminus and weakly at the extreme N-terminus. It marks short terminal tail segments (typically the last 4–8 residues), usually unstructured/low-confidence and sometimes including the final turn of a helix, with signal rising toward and peaking on the terminal residue. The concept is the presence of an exposed chain terminus rather than a specific sequence motif.

The concept is the presence of an exposed chain terminus rather than a specific sequence motif.
Activation pattern: Residue-level peaks concentrated at the very C-terminus (short contiguous runs with a monotonic ramp to the last residue); interiors largely silent even in disordered regions; occasional small N-terminal blips (often at M1–L3); frequently located immediately after the last helix.
Exemplars: - Protein phosphatase 1 regulatory subunit (PPP1R35): silent internally; activation confined to the C-terminal helix-to-coil end segment, peaking on the terminal residue.
- APC membrane recruitment protein family (AMER/APC membrane recruitment protein 3): sharp hotspot on the final unstructured hexapeptide; no activation in numerous internal disordered/structured regions.
- Enhancer of split bHLH transcriptional repressor (E(spl)-M2): activation over the last 6 residues of a C-terminal coil immediately following the final helix, maximal at the terminal cysteine.
- Photoreceptor scaffolding/low-complexity protein (PIP82): weak N-terminal start signal (M1–Q6) and a strong C-terminal run culminating at the last residue; interior (including annotated motifs and helices) remains inactive.

15805.label: S/T-rich low-complexity IDRs
15805.summary: Intrinsically disordered, low‑complexity, serine/threonine- and charge‑rich segments (flexible linkers, targeting regions, and cytosolic/luminal tails), often containing P/G and K/R/E/D, and frequently forming transient/low‑confidence helices; largely absent from well‑folded domain cores and transmembrane helices

Activation pattern: Regional activation across extended IDRs with many residue‑level peaks on S/T and adjacent polar/charged residues; sparse or absent over structured globular domains, coiled‑coils of high confidence, and transmembrane spans; occasional activation on low‑pLDDT helical segments embedded within disordered regions and juxtamembrane basic clusters
Exemplars: - Eisosome/cortical membrane protein (yeast Sle1 family): activation on disordered, polar eisosome‑targeting region and other low‑complexity coils, with strongest peaks in long IDRs.
- 12‑TM solute carrier–type sodium transporter: activation confined to disordered N‑terminal tail and large extramembranous loops; silent across all transmembrane helices.
- ArfGAP regulator with PH and ankyrin repeats (AGAP family): activation on long disordered linkers between domains and basic low‑complexity blocks after the PH domain; off in GLD/PH cores, C4 zinc‑finger catalytic region, and ankyrin repeats.
- TORC1 scaffold subunit (Tco89‑like): strong hotspots in low‑complexity, disordered basic/acidic segments with sporadic peaks at helix edges; does not uniformly track annotated phosphosites.
- Inner nuclear membrane SUN‑domain protein: activation on low‑confidence helical stretches and basic clusters in the post‑TM luminal tail and juxtamembrane region; absent in the coiled‑coil, transmembrane helix, and structured SUN domain.

271.label: Hydrophobic beta-strand core
271.summary: Structural signal for hydrophobic/aromatic residues that build the beta-strand cores of folded beta-sheet domains—most prominently C2 beta-sandwich and WW modules, but also other beta-rich interaction domains (SH2/SH3/PH/PTB/PDZ/GRAM) and, in some cases, alpha/beta enzyme folds with central beta-sheets (e.g., GNAT N-terminal acetyltransferases); it marks the scaffold rather than Ca2+-binding or catalytic sites.

Activation pattern: Residue-level sparse peaks confined to folded beta-sheet domains, concentrated on hydrophobic/aromatic positions within DSSP E strands (often showing an alternating pattern on one face of a sheet). Domain-level restriction to these beta-sheet regions; minimal or absent in Ca2+-binding loops, disordered linkers, transmembranes, and most helices. In multidomain proteins, the pattern repeats across each such module.
Exemplars:
- Synaptotagmins (tandem C2 Ca2+-lipid sensors): peaks on hydrophobic beta-strands of both C2 domains, not on Ca2+-binding loops.
- DOC2 family (double C2-like proteins): alternating hydrophobic residues in beta-strands across both C2 domains.
- Plant and animal C2-domain proteins: localized peaks on beta-strands within the C2 domain adjacent to Ca2+-binding motifs; no signal in transmembrane or disordered regions.
- Rab11-family interacting proteins (C2-mediated membrane targeting): sparse, high-confidence peaks on beta-strands in the N-terminal C2; negligible in the RBD and disordered tails.
- NEDD4/NEDD4L/SMURF HECT E3 ligases with C2 and WW modules: strong peaks on beta-strands in the C2 domain and on the two strands of each WW domain; only weak, scattered signal in the helical HECT region.
- N-terminal acetyltransferases (NatA/NatC; GNAT fold): sparse peaks on hydrophobic residues within the central beta-sheet core; weak/absent in surrounding helices.

2805.label: E2/UEV core and backside mimetics
2805.summary: E2/UBC–UEV (E2‑variant) core: the feature captures the ubiquitin‑conjugating enzyme fold and its noncatalytic UEV homologs, focusing on the HPN loop/active‑site region (including the catalytic cysteine when present) and adjacent hydrophobic/Trp‑rich interaction surfaces; it extends to convergent E2/UEV‑backside‑like docking patches embedded in diverse trafficking, ligase/transferase, kinase, and regulatory scaffolds.
2805.description:
Summary: E2/UBC–UEV (E2‑variant) core: the feature captures the ubiquitin‑conjugating enzyme fold and its noncatalytic UEV homologs, focusing on the HPN loop/active‑site region (including the catalytic cysteine when present) and adjacent hydrophobic/Trp‑rich interaction surfaces; it extends to convergent E2/UEV‑backside‑like docking patches embedded in diverse trafficking, ligase/transferase, kinase, and regulatory scaffolds.
Activation pattern: Domain-level activation across a single contiguous 40–150 aa segment corresponding to the UBC/UEV core (β‑sheet with flanking helices) around the HPN loop, or an analogous hydrophobic/Trp‑rich partner‑docking patch without the full E2 fold; in true E2s it often includes the catalytic Cys; in large multidomain proteins, multiple disjoint activated blocks map to repeated or separate E2‑/UEV‑like modules or mimetic docking regions.
Exemplars:
- Ubiquitin E2s (UBE2/UBC family): activation spans the catalytic Cys–HPN loop and surrounding UBC core, including the backside/Trp-containing interaction surface
- Ubiquitin‑like E2s (SUMO Ubc9, NEDD8 Ubc12, UFM1/ISG15 E2s; autophagy E2‑like Atg3/Atg10): same E2 fold region around the active‑site loop
- ESCRT‑I UEV subunits (TSG101/VPS23): activation over the UEV domain (E2‑fold without catalytic Cys), including the PTAP‑binding pocket
- E2‑like proteins across bacteria/viruses: activation on their E2/UEV‑like cores that mediate thioester transfer or peptide docking
- COPII coat components (Sec23/Sec24): activation on an E2‑/UEV‑like interaction subdomain within the coat scaffold
- Phosphoinositide kinases (PI3/4/5 kinases, PIP5Ks): activation on an embedded E2‑/UEV‑mimetic hydrophobic patch used for partner docking
- Tubulin‑tyrosine ligase‑like enzymes (TTLL/TTL): activation on an internal E2‑like hydrophobic/Trp‑rich patch within the catalytic domain
- Lipoxygenases: activation on the N‑terminal interaction module (PLAT/C2‑like) whose hydrophobic/Trp surface mimics the E2/UEV interaction patch
- cGAS‑like nucleotidyltransferases (MB21/cGLR family): activation on a localized subdomain that recapitulates the E2/UEV‑like interaction surface
- Mediator complex subunits: activation on small UBL/E2‑like or mimetic interaction modules within subunits
- Rap GTPase-activating proteins (SIPA1L family): activation on a short coiled‑coil/HEAT‑like docking segment adjacent to the RapGAP region that presents a Trp‑/hydrophobic E2‑backside‑like surface

3150.label: Short conserved loop/turn motifs
3150.summary: Short conserved loop/turn motifs in diverse viral, bacterial, and eukaryotic proteins. The feature highlights compact β-turn or loop segments often following a "DGxx" or similar small-residue prelude, in disordered cytoplasmic tails, exposed loops, or surface-accessible segments of larger folded domains.
3150.description:
Summary: Short conserved loop/turn motifs in diverse viral, bacterial, and eukaryotic proteins. The feature highlights compact β-turn or loop segments often following a "DGxx" or similar small-residue prelude, in disordered cytoplasmic tails, exposed loops, or surface-accessible segments of larger folded domains.

Activation pattern: Short regional activation with sharp residue-level peaks spanning 2–6 residues centered on small/hydrophobic residues (A, G, I, V, T, C) and occasionally P/Y/R, often in a "DGxxxxIG"-style local context. Activations are typically embedded in cytoplasmic, disordered, or exposed loop regions.

Exemplars:
- EPEC/EHEC translocated intimin receptor Tir – sharp activation on a conserved cytoplasmic "DGxxAAIG" segment around residue ~120, with secondary peaks in an extracellular IPSGE-containing region.
- Adenoviral pre-histone-like nucleoprotein (pVII) – activation on the C-terminal Pro/Arg-rich segment overlapping the nuclear localization signal (RVPVRTRP).
- Vaccinia 39 kDa core protein A4 – activation on a Cys/Thr/Pro-rich stretch within a disordered region (CTTPTV…TVCTT).
- Potyviral helper component proteinase polyprotein – activation on internal loop segments within the P1 protease and HC-Pro domains.
- Haemophilus hemoglobin-binding TBDR – activation on exposed loop residues within the TBDR β-barrel domain.
- Microsporidian polar tube protein 3 – activation on internal short hydrophobic loop motifs.

4898.label: Cytosolic helical repeat scaffolds
4898.summary: Nucleo/cytoplasmic regulatory scaffolds in medium‑to‑very‑large eukaryotic proteins: extended helical‑repeat and low‑complexity S/T/P‑rich segments with alternating acidic/basic tracts, commonly spanning long linkers and cytosolic loops of multi‑pass membrane proteins as well as extended repeat regions of soluble regulators; signal largely avoids transmembrane helices and compact enzymatic/catalytic cores.
4898.description:
Summary: Nucleo/cytoplasmic regulatory scaffolds in medium‑to‑very‑large eukaryotic proteins: extended helical‑repeat and low‑complexity S/T/P‑rich segments with alternating acidic/basic tracts, commonly spanning long linkers and cytosolic loops of multi‑pass membrane proteins as well as extended repeat regions of soluble regulators; signal largely avoids transmembrane helices and compact enzymatic/catalytic cores.
Activation pattern: Broad, band‑like activation over hundreds of residues in cytosolic or nucleoplasmic regions, strongest on continuous helix‑rich stretches and adjacent low‑complexity S/T/P‑rich blocks; peaks track acidic/basic clusters. Activation is sharply reduced across transmembrane helices and most globular catalytic cores, with occasional spillover at membrane‑proximal helices.
Exemplars: - Rab/Arf small‑GTPase regulators (DENN‑domain GEFs; TBC/ArfGAP; TSC2/RhebGAP): activation over long coiled‑coil/linker scaffolds flanking catalytic modules.
- TRPM cation channels: strong activation across large cytosolic domains preceding the transmembrane array and adjacent Ser/Thr‑rich disordered blocks; near‑absent over the transmembrane core and distal enzymatic domains (e.g., alpha‑kinase in TRPM6/7 or NUDT9‑H in TRPM2).
- Glucan synthases (plant callose synthases/GSL and fungal FKS1): maximal activation in central cytosolic regulatory loops with spillover into adjacent membrane‑proximal helices.
- PIKK family DNA‑damage kinases (ATR/MEC1): activation across N‑terminal HEAT/ARM repeat scaffolds; low on C‑terminal kinase domains.
- mRNA surveillance factors (SMG5/SMG7): activation on acidic/basic low‑complexity tracts flanking inactive PIN‑like domains.
- cGAS‑like receptors (cGLR/cGAS): activation on basic/acidic flanking segments outside the catalytic nucleotidyltransferase core.
