14410.label: RBR ligase helical extensions
14410.summary: A feature specific to RBR-family E3 ubiquitin ligases, marking helical/coiled-coil segments of the TRIAD supradomain and its C-terminal extensions (Ariadne/LDD-like regions) rather than core catalytic Cys/His positions
14410.description:
Summary: A feature specific to RBR-family E3 ubiquitin ligases, marking helical/coiled-coil segments of the TRIAD supradomain and its C-terminal extensions (Ariadne/LDD-like regions) rather than core catalytic Cys/His positions
Activation pattern: Broad regional activation spanning the TRIAD supradomain and adjacent C-terminal helical regions, with the sharpest residue-level peaks on hydrophobic/aromatic and charged residues in coiled-coil or helix segments downstream of the RING2 domain; activation is dense across the domain but does not concentrate on Zn-coordinating residues
Exemplars: - RNF216 (mouse and human): peak activation in the C-terminal coiled-coil/helical segment immediately downstream of the RING2/TRIAD.
- RNF31/HOIP (mouse and human): peak activation throughout the LDD domain C-terminal to the TRIAD supradomain.
- ANKIB1 (zebrafish and mouse): peak activation in a coiled-coil region C-terminal to the TRIAD.
- Ariadne-family E3 ligases (Arabidopsis ARI1/ARI15/ARI16, Dictyostelium rbrA): peak activation on conserved helical residues within/adjacent to the Ariadne C-terminal region.

13960.label: Charged helical disordered linkers
13960.summary: Charge-rich, low-complexity α-helical/coiled-coil–prone intrinsically disordered regions that flank or link to structured domains; most frequent in DNA/chromatin/replication factors but also present in other scaffolding/signaling proteins; the feature favors long basic/acidic runs with local helical propensity and avoids the folded catalytic, DNA-binding, or other globular cores when present.

8496.label: Disordered low-complexity pre/propeptides
8496.summary: Low-complexity / disordered-prone protein segments, including small uncharacterized proteins, micropeptides, precursor pro-regions, secreted peptide hormone/toxin precursors, viral structural/glycoprotein precursors, and proline-rich linker/tail regions
8496.description:
Summary: Low-complexity / disordered-prone protein segments, including small uncharacterized proteins, micropeptides, precursor pro-regions, secreted peptide hormone/toxin precursors, viral structural/glycoprotein precursors, and proline-rich linker/tail regions
Activation pattern: Predominantly broad, regional activation that often spans most or all of short proteins and extends across entire propeptide or chain regions; superimposed residue-level peaks frequently on S/T/P and short repeats (SP/TP, PP, GP) but also on adjacent residues within the same low-complexity stretch
Exemplars: - Polyomavirus agnoproteins: widespread activation across fully disordered, P/S/T- and proline-rich microproteins
- Peroxisomal biogenesis factors (PEX membrane proteins): activation on low-pLDDT cytosolic loops/tails
- Glycoside hydrolases (e.g., intracellular arabinofuranosidases): strong activation on long C-terminal disordered, low-complexity tails annotated as compositional bias
- Viral envelope glycoprotein precursors: activation across signal peptide and adjacent chain regions
- Secreted peptide hormones/toxin precursors: broad activation across pre/propeptide stretches (e.g., neurotrophin and kininogen precursors)
- Small proteins and micropeptides: broad activation across extended low-complexity segments

10196.label: Nuclear interdomain hydrophobic stretches
10196.summary: Internal hydrophobic-rich segments within large, multidomain nuclear proteins—particularly transposon-derived zinc finger / BED-domain proteins, GTF2I-like transcription factors, and other transcription/regulatory factors—located in the middle-to-C-terminal portion of the protein, outside the annotated zinc finger or repeat domains.
10196.description:
Summary: Internal hydrophobic-rich segments within large, multidomain nuclear proteins—particularly transposon-derived zinc finger / BED-domain proteins, GTF2I-like transcription factors, and other transcription/regulatory factors—located in the middle-to-C-terminal portion of the protein, outside the annotated zinc finger or repeat domains.
Activation pattern: Predominantly long, contiguous regional activation across a hydrophobic stretch and its flanking residues; per-residue peaks land on aliphatic/aromatic residues (I, V, L, F, Y, M, A) embedded in sequences such as IxNxISExV, MDVVVD, FTVVRVI, or VLKKNVYAML; activation is broadly distributed across many residues of the protein (often >100 active positions) and does not coincide with annotated catalytic, metal-binding, or modification sites.
Exemplars: Transposon-derived zinc finger proteins (ZNF618, ZNF862): activation across a mid-protein segment well outside the C2H2/TTF-type zinc finger domains; BED-type zinc finger proteins (ZBED39, FAM200C/ZBED8): activation on a central hydrophobic stretch downstream of the BED domain; GTF2I repeat domain-containing proteins (GTF2IRD2, GTF2IRD2B): activation on a conserved MDVVVD-containing segment C-terminal to the GTF2I-like repeats; EPM2A-interacting protein 1 (laforin-interacting protein): activation on a central IINTISEW segment; KIAA1586 E3 SUMO ligase: activation on a mid-protein hydrophobic stretch outside the N-terminal SUMO-interaction region; p52rIPK (PRKRIR): activation on a central GVSVALGTI segment downstream of the THAP zinc finger.

13651.label: Active-site pocket-lining loops
13651.summary: Active-site “lid/cap” and pocket‑lining segments within catalytic core domains—typically flexible loops and their flanking short helices/β‑strands that shape or gate substrate/cofactor‑binding sites—often enriched in glycine and aromatic residues; most prominently the photolyase/cryptochrome α/β domain region around the antenna (MTHF) pocket, with analogous substrate‑binding loops highlighted in diverse enzymes (TIM‑barrel and other α/β cores, lysozyme‑like and metallo‑enzymes).
13651.description:
Summary: Active-site “lid/cap” and pocket‑lining segments within catalytic core domains—typically flexible loops and their flanking short helices/β‑strands that shape or gate substrate/cofactor‑binding sites—often enriched in glycine and aromatic residues; most prominently the photolyase/cryptochrome α/β domain region around the antenna (MTHF) pocket, with analogous substrate‑binding loops highlighted in diverse enzymes (TIM‑barrel and other α/β cores, lysozyme‑like and metallo‑enzymes).
Activation pattern: Domain-level, dense regional activation across a long stretch of the photolyase/cryptochrome α/β core; in other families, localized mid‑sequence segments within the catalytic domain, with residue‑level peaks on glycine, proline, and aromatic residues in loops (often lower pLDDT) and adjacent short helices/strands that line the binding cleft; typically adjacent to, or partially overlapping, substrate/cofactor‑binding determinants rather than metal/ATP ligands themselves.
Exemplars: - Photolyase/cryptochrome family: broad activation across the α/β core including the antenna cofactor (MTHF) binding region (e.g., around E193), with weaker signal on FAD‑binding motifs.
- Class I aminoacyl‑tRNA synthetase (glutamyl‑tRNA ligase): a flexible inter‑helical loop in the N‑terminal catalytic Rossmann‑like domain.
- Type‑3 copper oxidase (tyrosinase): central domain loops/turns (glycine‑rich) and nearby secondary structure, touching some copper‑ligating histidines at the edge.
- Carbohydrate‑active enzymes:
  • GH1/β‑glucosidase: active‑site β‑strand/coil carrying glycon‑binding N203 and catalytic proton donor E204, plus a disulfide‑stabilized loop (C223–C230).
  • GH84/O‑GlcNAcase: patches within the catalytic barrel including substrate‑binding Y335 and a pocket‑shaping coil between β‑strands (around P368).
  • GH13/1,4‑α‑glucan branching enzyme: extended active‑site loop and adjacent core elements containing the transition‑state stabilizer Y236, substrate‑binding R265/G282, and essential W274.
- GH25 lysozyme: C‑terminal β/coil region within the lysozyme domain away from the annotated catalytic residues, consistent with a cap/pocket‑lining segment.
- Ferrochelatase: middle α/β region (including a helical segment) adjacent to the porphyrin‑binding surface (near Y131), not on the Fe2+‑binding residues.
- CRISPR Cas1 endonuclease: a long core α‑helix with peaks at G98/E104 and minor signal in the preceding loop, consistent with a surface shaping the DNA‑binding/active site cleft rather than the metal‑ligand triad.
- Glutamate‑cysteine ligase: contiguous mid‑core helices/coil/β that form the catalytic pocket without specific annotated ligand atoms, matching a gating/pocket‑lining role.

3204.label: Inteins and terminal IDRs
3204.summary: Intervening/peripheral non-core polypeptide segments—especially self-splicing inteins embedded within host proteins and long, low-complexity intrinsically disordered termini (signal peptides/propeptides and C-terminal tails)—that are absent from or peripheral to the stable folded extein/catalytic core
3204.description:
Summary: Intervening/peripheral non-core polypeptide segments—especially self-splicing inteins embedded within host proteins and long, low-complexity intrinsically disordered termini (signal peptides/propeptides and C-terminal tails)—that are absent from or peripheral to the stable folded extein/catalytic core
Activation pattern: Regional/domain-level activation over long, contiguous stretches. In intein-bearing proteins, activation typically begins immediately after the N-terminal splice junction and often extends through much or all of the intein (sometimes strongest near the intein N-terminus) while exteins remain low; in secretory/precursor proteins, activation covers the N-terminal signal/propeptide; in many eukaryotic proteins, activation spans extended C-terminal IDRs/isoform-specific segments. Structured catalytic cores show little or no activation.
Exemplars: - DNA replication factor C small subunit with dual inteins: activation on the N-terminal regions of each intein; exteins and the intein C-termini/homing-endonuclease portions are weak.
- Glutamine–fructose-6-phosphate aminotransferase with a large intein: continuous activation across the entire intein (including HTH and homing endonuclease subdomains); exteins are not activated.
- Plant polygalacturonase precursor: activation on the N-terminal signal peptide/propeptide and a disordered C-terminal tail; the catalytic core is weak.
- FAD-dependent monooxygenase: activation confined to a long disordered C-terminal tail; the FAD-binding/catalytic core is not activated.
- Mediator complex subunit 26A (RNA Pol II mediator): activation across a long C-terminal intrinsically disordered region that is missing in an alternative isoform; the structured N-terminal domain is unactivated.

7460.label: FAR1/FRS transcription factor marker
7460.summary: A FAR1/FRS plant transcription factor family marker; the feature fires broadly across these proteins, including their FAR1 DNA-binding modules, central MULE domains, SWIM-type zinc-finger regions, coiled-coil tails, and intervening regions.
7460.description:
Summary: A FAR1/FRS plant transcription factor family marker; the feature fires broadly across these proteins, including their FAR1 DNA-binding modules, central MULE domains, SWIM-type zinc-finger regions, coiled-coil tails, and intervening regions.
Activation pattern: Dense, near-whole-protein activation across FAR1/FRS family members, with the strongest residue-level peaks landing on charged/polar positions (E, D, R, K, S) in helical or loop contexts within and between the annotated FAR1, MULE, and SWIM domains.
Exemplars: - FAR1/FRS plant transcription factors (FAR1, FRS1–11 and related): dense activation along the full protein, with peaks both in and around the FAR1 DNA-binding module and in central regions between the FAR1, MULE, and SWIM-type Zn-finger domains
- B3-domain auxin response factors: strong activation across the B3 DNA-binding domain, peaking on beta-strand segments
- RGS (Regulator of G-protein signaling) proteins: sharp single-residue peaks at a helix N-cap loop within the RGS domain
- Multi-pass transporters (e.g., P4-ATPase flippases) and TMC channels: extended activation across hydrophobic transmembrane helices, often enriched in the C-terminal half
- Plant immune NLR/TIR and S-domain receptor-like kinases/lectins: activation along leucine-rich repeat cores and adjoining transmembrane segments
- Cell-wall polysaccharide enzymes and lectins: activation on structured hydrophobic cores of carbohydrate-binding/catalytic modules
- DNA/RNA-binding and replication/repair factors: activation on well-folded nucleic-acid-binding domain cores

5865.label: Short solvent-exposed patches
5865.summary: Short, solvent-exposed patches (≈10–25 aa) in loops, helix-caps, or disordered tails at domain edges or near active-site rims, with mixed composition that sometimes includes Lys/Arg/Pro/Gly enrichment and sometimes aromatic or Cys-containing context. The feature recurs across diverse protein families.
5865.description:
Summary: Short, solvent-exposed patches (≈10–25 aa) in loops, helix-caps, or disordered tails at domain edges or near active-site rims, with mixed composition that sometimes includes Lys/Arg/Pro/Gly enrichment and sometimes aromatic or Cys-containing context. The feature recurs across diverse protein families.
Activation pattern: Regional activation on short contiguous segments with sharp residue-level peaks; typically in coil/loop, short helices, or disordered tails at domain boundaries or surface-exposed motifs; multiple discrete patches when small domains repeat; non-transmembrane.
Exemplars:
- Methyl-CpG-binding domain proteins (e.g., MBD8, SETDB2): activation at the C-terminal end of the MBD domain in a coil/loop segment that contacts DNA; a weaker signal also appears in a SET-domain SAM/active-site loop in SETDB2.
- UbiD-like/phenolic acid decarboxylases: activation on a surface segment within the catalytic chain, in an aromatic/hydrophobic loop region.
- Histidine biosynthesis enzymes (PRA-CH/hisIE/his7): activation across the PRA-CH signature region (mixed secondary structure) that binds ribose-phosphate/carboxylate moieties.
- Chalcone isomerase-like/AtFAP family: activation on the C-terminal helix/coil at the active-site rim that forms a charged/gating patch contacting the ligand headgroup.
- Chemokines (CC, CXC, CX3C, XC) and viral chemokine mimics: activation on basic GAG/heparin-binding loops or C-terminal tails.
- Kazal-type serine protease inhibitors: activation on a disulfide-stabilized loop near the C-terminal end of the Kazal-like domain.
- Organellar ribosomal proteins (mitochondrial/chloroplast): activation on Lys-rich, often disordered tails/loops that contact rRNA.
- Splicing/EJC/snRNP-associated proteins: activation on short RGG/basic RNA-binding segments.

15462.label: Polymerase/nuclease catalytic cores
15462.summary: Core catalytic machinery and nucleic‑acid–binding channels of phosphodiester‑processing enzymes (polymerases and related nucleases), characterized by acidic Asp/Glu metal‑binding motifs (e.g., DxD/GDD/DFDGD, DDH, HNH/RuvC) and adjacent glycine‑rich and basic loops that contact RNA/DNA
15462.description:
Summary: Core catalytic machinery and nucleic‑acid–binding channels of phosphodiester‑processing enzymes (polymerases and related nucleases), characterized by acidic Asp/Glu metal‑binding motifs (e.g., DxD/GDD/DFDGD, DDH, HNH/RuvC) and adjacent glycine‑rich and basic loops that contact RNA/DNA
Activation pattern: Predominantly domain‑level activation across the catalytic core and nucleic‑acid channel with residue‑level peaks on conserved acidic clusters (metal‑binding Asp/Glu motifs) and glycine‑rich loops; in very large subunits (e.g., RNAP) activation extends over long contiguous regions, and also appears on basic patches of polymerase‑associated/elongation factors that line the nucleic‑acid path
Exemplars: - Multi‑subunit DNA‑dependent RNA polymerases (bacterial/archaeal core β′/β; eukaryotic RNAP I/II/III and plant RNAP IV/V): activation on the double‑psi β‑barrel active site (e.g., NADFDGD) and surrounding funnel/clamp residues that bind the RNA–DNA hybrid.
- Viral RNA‑dependent RNA polymerases: activation on the palm domain (motif A DxD and motif C GDD) and the template/product channel.
- Reverse transcriptases and telomerase TERT: activation on the RT‑like palm (e.g., YxDD/H–ADD motifs) and RNA/DNA binding groove.
- DNA polymerases (families A/B/C): activation on palm DxD/DxE metal‑binding residues, nearby glycine‑rich loops, and basic O‑helix/channel residues; often also on the proofreading exonuclease DEDh motif.
- Argonaute/PIWI proteins: activation on the PIWI catalytic DDH tetrad and the basic guide–target duplex channel (MID/PAZ–PIWI interface).
- CRISPR Class 2 endonucleases (e.g., Cas9, Cas12; sometimes Cas13): activation on RuvC (DDE/DDD) and HNH catalytic motifs (or charged HEPN active sites) and the nucleic‑acid binding cleft.
- RNase H–like and RNA processing/cleavage factors (RNase H/RNase III; TFIIS/GreA): activation on acidic hairpins that coordinate metals and on basic RNA‑contacting surfaces.
- Polymerase‑associated subunits and elongation factors (e.g., Spt5/DSIF, TFIIF/Nus factors): activation on basic patches that track the nucleic‑acid path or reach into the RNAP active center.

15704.label: Anion-binding mixed-charge IDRs
15704.summary: Extended mixed‑charge, aromatic/glycine‑enriched low‑complexity segments (often intrinsically disordered) that form polyelectrostatic and cation–pi interaction patches used to engage anionic ligands (DNA/RNA backbones, phosphate headgroups) or carbohydrate surfaces, typically as long N/C‑terminal tails or solvent‑exposed loops flanking catalytic/reader cores
15704.description:
Summary: Extended mixed‑charge, aromatic/glycine‑enriched low‑complexity segments (often intrinsically disordered) that form polyelectrostatic and cation–pi interaction patches used to engage anionic ligands (DNA/RNA backbones, phosphate headgroups) or carbohydrate surfaces, typically as long N/C‑terminal tails or solvent‑exposed loops flanking catalytic/reader cores
Activation pattern: Regional activation over long contiguous stretches of low‑complexity sequence; strongest in basic/acidic mixed segments with interspersed aromatics and glycines. In enzymes, activation concentrates in flexible loops or terminal extensions near nucleic‑acid/phosphate/carbohydrate‑binding surfaces; in chaperones/scaffolds, often a single charged patch (e.g., C‑terminal region).
Exemplars: - Meiotic recombination endonuclease SPO11/TopoVI‑A: activation on basic/disordered termini and acidic TOPRIM‑adjacent loops that contact DNA.
- Viral DNA primases (AEP/DnaG‑like): activation on Lys/Arg‑rich ssDNA‑binding segments and adjacent acidic metal‑binding motifs.
- Chromatin reader/modifier complexes (e.g., PHD/bromodomain/Tudor‑containing scaffolds): activation on low‑complexity acidic/basic tails with aromatic clusters used for chromatin engagement and multivalent interactions.
- SEC14/CRAL‑TRIO lipid‑binding proteins: activation on cationic/aromatic gating loops and charged flexible regions that recognize phosphate headgroups.
- Bacterial trigger factor (Tig) chaperone: a single activating site in the acidic, highly charged C‑terminal cradle.
- cGAS/cGLR innate immune nucleotide cyclases: activation on the basic, disordered N‑terminal DNA/membrane‑binding extension.
- Nuclear cap‑binding protein subunit 1 (CBP80): activation on long charged IDRs flanking HEAT repeats that scaffold cap‑binding/RNA processing factors.
- Plant glycohydrolases (beta‑amylases, alpha‑mannosidases): activation on aromatic/charged carbohydrate‑binding loops or appended CBMs and flexible linkers.
- Alkaline phosphatases (PhoA and orthologs): activation on mixed‑charge, aromatic surface loops near the metal/phosphate‑binding site or flexible terminal regions.

12915.label: Downstream Gly/Pro patch activation
12915.summary: Short microdomains in proteins that often contain Zn-binding ribbons or related Cys/His motifs, but the activation itself falls on Gly/Pro-rich and basic/acidic patches located downstream of the metal-binding region, not on the ligating residues.
12915.description:
Summary: Short microdomains in proteins that often contain Zn-binding ribbons or related Cys/His motifs, but the activation itself falls on Gly/Pro-rich and basic/acidic patches located downstream of the metal-binding region, not on the ligating residues.
Activation pattern: Short regional activation with residue-level peaks concentrated on coil/turn or β-strand segments enriched in Gly, Pro, and basic residues; signal typically spares the Zn-coordinating Cys/His residues themselves and is offset from the structural Zn-binding core.
Exemplars:
- Mitochondrial bL32m (human, bovine, mouse, yeast): activation on a conserved Gly/Pro-rich patch (GGPF(K/R)AP or analogous basic/acidic stretch) downstream of the Cys4 Zn ribbon.
- TFIIE/TFE family: in TFEα, activation on a short patch following the HTH domain.
- Papillomavirus E7: Cys/His-rich C-terminal Zn-binding module.
- RING-type E3 ligases (including RING-CH/MARCH): Cys/His Zn-finger knuckle region.
- Small ribosomal proteins: Zn-binding variants (e.g., eS27, L31/L36) or short basic patches (e.g., eS26).
- USPs: ZnF-UBP when present (e.g., USP5/USP13) or short basic loops/insertions in catalytic/UBL regions (e.g., USP4).
- HypA and RAD50: His/Cys-rich metal-binding loops/Zn-hook.
- MsrB: Cys4 Zn-binding tail in many bacterial/archaeal MsrBs.
- Plant VIN3-like proteins: PHD-type Cys/His Zn-binding fingers.

13570.label: Folded viral protein cores
13570.summary: Domain/chain-level signal active across large, well-folded viral and nucleic-acid-binding proteins, with strong activation on adenovirus DNA-binding and shutoff proteins, herpesvirus tegument/UL95 proteins, Ebola VP40 matrix protein, and rhabdovirus nucleoproteins, and moderate activation on DDE/RNase H–like DNA transposase catalytic cores.
13570.description:
Summary: Domain/chain-level signal active across large, well-folded viral and nucleic-acid-binding proteins, with strong activation on adenovirus DNA-binding and shutoff proteins, herpesvirus tegument/UL95 proteins, Ebola VP40 matrix protein, and rhabdovirus nucleoproteins, and moderate activation on DDE/RNase H–like DNA transposase catalytic cores.
Activation pattern: Broad activation across extended structured blocks; often begins after N-terminal accessory/low-complexity or disordered segments and covers most of the folded portion of the chain.
Exemplars:
- DNA transposases (THAP9/P-element, DDE/RNase H–like): activation on the mid-to-C-terminal catalytic α/β core; absent on N-terminal THAP zinc finger.
- Adenovirus shutoff (p100K) proteins: activation through the EIF4G-binding region and RRM domain, absent in N- and C-terminal disordered regions.
- Adenovirus DNA-binding protein, HHV-8 UL95 homolog, bovine herpesvirus UL47, Ebola VP40, and rhabdovirus nucleoprotein: strong, broadly distributed activation over the folded body of the protein.

346.label: Alpha-solenoid helical scaffolds
346.summary: Long all-alpha helical scaffold domains—primarily alpha-solenoids/HEAT-like repeats (including MIF4G/ACE1) and related helical-rod bundles—that mediate protein-protein interactions in large eukaryotic assemblies
346.description:
Summary: Long all-alpha helical scaffold domains—primarily alpha-solenoids/HEAT-like repeats (including MIF4G/ACE1) and related helical-rod bundles—that mediate protein-protein interactions in large eukaryotic assemblies

Exemplars: - Y-complex nucleoporins (e.g., Nup85): activation on the central ACE1 alpha-solenoid scaffold region
- Gamma-tubulin ring complex components (GCP3): activation across the C-terminal helical scaffold domain
- Formins (FH2-containing): strong activation spanning the FH2 all-alpha helical bundle
- Cap-binding/translation factor scaffolds (CBP80/NCBP1): peak activation within the MIF4G (HEAT-repeat) domain with moderate activation across downstream helical segments

8623.label: Broad disordered linker activation
8623.summary: Broad, distributed feature that activates across large fractions of long, often disordered or low-complexity proteins, with prominent activity in zinc finger/transposase-derived DNA-binding proteins and other large nuclear/regulatory proteins. Activation frequently covers disordered regions and extends into structured DNA-binding regions, while well-folded zinc-finger arrays and RING domains themselves are often skipped.
8623.description:
Summary: Broad, distributed feature that activates across large fractions of long, often disordered or low-complexity proteins, with prominent activity in zinc finger/transposase-derived DNA-binding proteins and other large nuclear/regulatory proteins. Activation frequently covers disordered regions and extends into structured DNA-binding regions, while well-folded zinc-finger arrays and RING domains themselves are often skipped.

Activation pattern: Long, contiguous activation blocks that often span 50-99% of the chain; peaks tend to fall on disordered or low-complexity stretches and on KR/ED/STP-rich segments, with notable peaks also on DNA-binding regions such as the RAG1 NBD; classical structured zinc finger and RING domains within the same proteins are typically silent.

Exemplars:
- Zinc finger/THAP/BED DNA-binding proteins and transposase-derived factors (ZMYM5, ZBTB10, ZNF862, ZBED5, SCAND3): broad activation across the chain with peaks in disordered/linker regions; the canonical zinc-finger arrays themselves are largely inactive.
- V(D)J recombination-activating protein 1 (RAG1): strongest peaks within the NBD DNA-binding region (~residues 390-457), with the RING-type and RAG1-type zinc fingers silent.
- E3 SUMO-protein ligase KIAA1586: near-complete coverage of the chain, with peaks in the disordered N-terminal SUMO-interaction region.
- 52 kDa repressor of the inhibitor of the protein kinase (p52rIPK): broad activation with peaks in a central disordered acidic stretch.
- Ubiquitin system enzymes (E3 ligases, DUBs): activation often spans the chain rather than being confined to catalytic cores.

5351.label: Cys/His-rich DNA-binding cores
5351.summary: DNA- and nucleic-acid–binding/regulatory domain cores of transcription factors and nucleic-acid enzymes, with a strong bias toward Cys/His-rich, often zinc-coordinating motifs; the feature preferentially recognizes specific DNA-binding folds (e.g., FLYWCH, GCM, FAR1/FRS, WRKY/BED) and also non–zinc-dependent DNA-binding cores (e.g., HSF winged-helix) or nuclease cores, and can fire on related Cys/His-rich metal-binding modules (e.g., PARP Zn fingers, BIR, CHORD) across diverse taxa including eukaryotes and DNA viruses.
5351.description:
Summary: DNA- and nucleic-acid–binding/regulatory domain cores of transcription factors and nucleic-acid enzymes, with a strong bias toward Cys/His-rich, often zinc-coordinating motifs; the feature preferentially recognizes specific DNA-binding folds (e.g., FLYWCH, GCM, FAR1/FRS, WRKY/BED) and also non–zinc-dependent DNA-binding cores (e.g., HSF winged-helix) or nuclease cores, and can fire on related Cys/His-rich metal-binding modules (e.g., PARP Zn fingers, BIR, CHORD) across diverse taxa including eukaryotes and DNA viruses.
Activation pattern: Primarily domain-level contiguous blocks confined to annotated DNA/RNA-interaction regions (DNA-binding domains and nuclease cores), with residue-level peaks on histidines and some cysteines and spillover into immediately adjacent beta/coil/helix elements; frequently N-terminal in TFs. Signal strength varies by family: strong on C2H2-like fingers (e.g., FLYWCH) and GCM-type metal-coordinated folds, and on the FAR1 DNA-binding core; often minimal on unrelated domains in the same protein (e.g., SWIM in FRS). In enzymes, signal can localize to nucleic-acid–interacting catalytic cores (e.g., AP endonuclease, RNA exonucleases). Block length ranges from short Zn-finger motifs to larger (~70–100 aa) domain cores.
Exemplars:
- FLYWCH-type zinc-finger transcription factors: activation across the FLYWCH finger core and its immediate C-terminal extension, with strong peaks on His residues.
- FAR1/FRS transposase-derived transcription regulators: strong block over the N-terminal FAR1 DNA-binding domain; little to no signal on the downstream MULE region or the C-terminal SWIM zinc finger.
- GCM family transcription factors: activation within the GCM DNA-binding domain, including its Cys/His metal-coordination cluster and contiguous beta/helix elements.
- WRKY transcription factors: activation on the WRKY DNA-binding domain encompassing the C2H2/C2HC zinc-finger segment.
- BED-type transposon-derived regulators: activation over the BED zinc-finger DNA-binding module.
- PARP family DNA repair proteins: activation on DNA-binding regulatory modules (zinc fingers where present) or alternative DNA-interaction elements (e.g., PARP2/3).
- IAP BIR-repeat proteins: activation on the zinc-binding BIR domain.
- CHORD-domain co-chaperones: activation on the Cys/His-rich CHORD domain.
- Viral DNA-binding/replication regulators: activation on Cys/His-rich, metal-coordinating DNA-binding segments.
- Heat shock factor (HSF) transcription factors: activation on the N-terminal winged-helix DNA-binding domain.
- AP endonucleases and RNA exonucleases: activation on nuclease cores at nucleic-acid–interacting surfaces.

5021.label: Polybasic intrinsically disordered regions
5021.summary: Low-complexity, often intrinsically disordered regions in short proteins, precursors, and microproteins across taxa, including viral accessory proteins, neuropeptide/hormone precursors, sperm nuclear proteins, flexible enzyme tails/inserts, and antisense-derived/uncharacterized microproteins. Activation is biased toward, but not restricted to, basic (Lys/Arg) clusters, with frequent peaks also at Pro/Ser/Gly residues in disordered context.
5021.description:
Summary: Low-complexity, often intrinsically disordered regions in short proteins, precursors, and microproteins across taxa, including viral accessory proteins, neuropeptide/hormone precursors, sperm nuclear proteins, flexible enzyme tails/inserts, and antisense-derived/uncharacterized microproteins. Activation is biased toward, but not restricted to, basic (Lys/Arg) clusters, with frequent peaks also at Pro/Ser/Gly residues in disordered context.
Activation pattern: Regional activation spanning extended low-pLDDT/disordered segments with numerous modest residue-level peaks, occurring at N-termini, internal flexible inserts, or C-terminal tails; polybasic clusters (KR/RR) often coincide with the strongest peaks, but activation also appears at non-basic residues within these regions.
Exemplars: - Retroviral integrase: strong activation in the annotated disordered central linker.
- Type II toxin–antitoxin antitoxins (TacA family): activation on the N-terminal IDR and a flexible low-confidence helix; structured C-terminus largely inactive.
- Viral tegument/accessory microproteins: diffuse activation across basic, disordered bodies, including polybasic NLS-like motifs.
- Neuropeptide/hormone prohormone precursors: broad activation in KR/RR-rich propeptide regions used for convertase processing.
- Sperm nuclear proteins (protamines/transition proteins): pervasive activation across Lys/Arg-rich disordered sequences.
- ATP synthase ε subunit: activation on flexible/basic tails or segments of the small subunit.
- RNA/tRNA modification enzymes: activation on low-complexity basic tails/loops implicated in RNA binding.
- Cysteine-rich venom/toxin precursors: activation across precursor sequences including signal peptide and mature toxin segments.
- Eukaryotic microproteins/antisense-derived short proteins: widespread activation across their largely disordered sequences.

16345.label: Phosphate-binding charged β/α junctions
16345.summary: Charged structural interfaces that engage phosphate-rich ligands and support phosphoryl-transfer chemistry—most often β→turn→α junctions within α/β catalytic cores (polymerase-like, PTP/SAC-like, TTL/TTLL folds) and, by extension, extended charged scaffolding surfaces in large cytosolic/nuclear complexes (e.g., cullin/APC)—seen across nucleic acid/nucleotide-associated enzymes and scaffolds
16345.description:
Summary: Charged structural interfaces that engage phosphate-rich ligands and support phosphoryl-transfer chemistry—most often β→turn→α junctions within α/β catalytic cores (polymerase-like, PTP/SAC-like, TTL/TTLL folds) and, by extension, extended charged scaffolding surfaces in large cytosolic/nuclear complexes (e.g., cullin/APC)—seen across nucleic acid/nucleotide-associated enzymes and scaffolds
Activation pattern: Primarily regional/domain-level activation across catalytic cores or long, charged interaction surfaces in large proteins, with occasional sharp residue-level peaks at β→turn→α secondary-structure transitions; often spans long stretches or multiple regions within multi-domain proteins
Exemplars: - Telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT): activation across the reverse-transcriptase core, especially palm/fingers β/α junctions enriched in acidic/basic residues that coordinate NTPs and nucleic acids.
- Viral DNA replication proteins (e.g., viral DNA/RNA polymerases and processing factors): activation over polymerase catalytic cores and adjacent charged surfaces that bind DNA/RNA and metal-cofactor–stabilized phosphates.
- Y-family DNA polymerases and Rev1: activation on the polymerase palm and surrounding charged loops used for lesion bypass and dNTP handling.
- Phosphoinositide SAC-domain phosphatases: activation on the PTP-like catalytic loop (e.g., HCX5R region) and neighboring basic patches that engage anionic phosphoinositide headgroups.
- Tubulin-tyrosine ligase-like (TTLL/TTL) enzymes: activation over the ATP-dependent catalytic domain and basic grooves that interact with acidic tubulin C-terminal tails during glutamylation/glycylation or tyrosination.
- Cullin family scaffolds and APC subunit 2 (cullin-like): activation along extended, highly charged α-helical scaffolding surfaces (including the neddylation/E2–RING engagement region) that organize ubiquitin ligase complexes.
- mRNA cap-binding protein eIF4E (eIF4E3): localized, low-level activation at a β→turn→α junction in the ordered core, consistent with the feature’s preference for charged β/α structural transitions rather than disordered segments or specific cap-contact residues.

2366.label: Extended hydrophobic segment detector
2366.summary: Detector of extended hydrophobic/Leu-rich segments: activates on long patches enriched in bulky hydrophobic and aromatic residues (Leu, Ile, Val, Phe, Tyr, Trp; often Cys), independent of secondary structure, marking generic hydrophobic surfaces/cores, membrane-associating stretches, and leucine-rich interaction motifs (e.g., NES) across diverse proteins, especially viral structural proteins
2366.description:
Summary: Detector of extended hydrophobic/Leu-rich segments: activates on long patches enriched in bulky hydrophobic and aromatic residues (Leu, Ile, Val, Phe, Tyr, Trp; often Cys), independent of secondary structure, marking generic hydrophobic surfaces/cores, membrane-associating stretches, and leucine-rich interaction motifs (e.g., NES) across diverse proteins, especially viral structural proteins
Activation pattern: Predominantly regional activation over long sequence stretches with superimposed residue-level peaks at L/I/V/F/Y/W/C; occurs in helices, strands, and coils; common in low-pLDDT/disordered regions as well as structured domains; not tied to a specific fold or compartment
Exemplars: - Viral nucleoproteins (e.g., rabies virus N): widespread activation on L/I/V across the RNA cap-binding region and adjacent segments, reflecting hydrophobic packing patches
- Viral matrix proteins (e.g., RSV M): strong activation on leucine-rich segments within importin-binding regions and the leucine-rich nuclear export signal
- Innate immune adaptor STING: activation on hydrophobic residues in helices and β-strands, including an aromatic residue in the cGAMP-binding pocket, with peaks in additional hydrophobic helical stretches
- Viral envelope/membrane proteins (general class): activation on hydrophobic/aromatic and cysteine-containing segments consistent with transmembrane/packing patches
- Diverse enzymes and nucleic-acid–processing proteins (general class): activation on extended hydrophobic cores/surfaces without motif specificity

924.label: Proline cysteine low complexity repeats
924.summary: Selective for short proline-rich low-complexity repeat tracts, especially C-C-X-P–type cysteine/proline repeats in keratin-associated and matrix structural proteins, and P-P-S-P / S-P-P-S-P tracts in hydroxyproline-rich secreted peptide precursors.
924.description:
Summary: Selective for short proline-rich low-complexity repeat tracts, especially C-C-X-P–type cysteine/proline repeats in keratin-associated and matrix structural proteins, and P-P-S-P / S-P-P-S-P tracts in hydroxyproline-rich secreted peptide precursors.
Activation pattern: Sparse residue-level peaks within tandem 4-residue Pro/Cys-containing repeats in low-complexity/disordered segments; peaks typically land on Cys or Pro at recurring repeat positions, or on Pro/Ser within PPPSP-like motifs. Little to no activation in flanking signal peptides or non-repetitive linker regions.
Exemplars:
- Keratin-associated proteins (KRTAP5 family): strong activation across each of the C-C-X-P tandem repeats spanning the central repeat region, with peaks on the cysteines of the repeat.
- Shell matrix proteins (e.g., Prismalin-14): activation across P-I-Y-R / P-F-S-Y type 4-residue tandem repeats in the mature chain.
- Hydroxyproline-rich systemin precursors (HypSys A/B): activation on the PPPSP / SPPSP proline-rich motifs within the mature peptide and surrounding disordered region, often coinciding with 4-hydroxyproline / O-glycosylation sites; no activation in the signal peptide.

11061.label: Helical MoRF/SLiM motifs
11061.summary: Short, flexible helical or helix–coil boundary motifs (MoRF/SLiM-like) used for partner, nucleic‑acid, and targeting interactions; compositionally biased toward small hydrophobic/flexible residues (G, A, L, V, S, T, P), common in viral proteins, secretion effectors, and trafficking/assembly factors, and typically adjacent to but not coincident with catalytic residues.
11061.description:
Summary: Short, flexible helical or helix–coil boundary motifs (MoRF/SLiM-like) used for partner, nucleic‑acid, and targeting interactions; compositionally biased toward small hydrophobic/flexible residues (G, A, L, V, S, T, P), common in viral proteins, secretion effectors, and trafficking/assembly factors, and typically adjacent to but not coincident with catalytic residues.
Activation pattern: Residue-level peaks scattered across long proteins, enriched in low‑to‑moderate confidence regions (low pLDDT) and at secondary-structure boundaries in helices and coils; broad domain coverage with punctate hotspots, often near binding/targeting sites rather than on core catalytic residues; coverage varies widely between proteins.
Exemplars: - CRISPR-associated RNases (Cas13a): peaks in the Helical-1 domain around the pre-crRNA processing site (e.g., near R438/K441/I442) and at boundaries across helical/HEPN regions, but not on the HEPN catalytic tetrads.
- Type III secretion effectors (e.g., Shigella IpaA): sparse peaks in low-confidence α-helical segments within disordered regions typical of host-interaction SLiMs.
- Paramyxovirus nucleoproteins (e.g., Nipah N): disordered helices and helix–coil transitions near RNA-binding surfaces.
- Pneumovirus phosphoproteins (RSV P): MoRF-like boundary segments in an overall disordered protein, including the onset of an NLS and flexible turns.
- Apicomplexan ookinete/surface proteins (e.g., PIMMS43): low/moderate-pLDDT ectodomain helices/coils away from signal peptide and transmembrane segments, consistent with linear epitope/interaction motifs.
- Herpesviridae tegument and DNA-packaging/capsid accessory proteins; Adenoviridae structural/replication proteins; Poxvirus proteins: many short peaks across low-complexity regions used for assembly and host interactions.
- Peroxisome biogenesis/targeting proteins: flexible tail/IDR motifs (e.g., NLS/PTS-like targeting signals) in otherwise variable contexts.
- Secreted peptide hormone/neuropeptide precursors: disordered propeptide segments carrying short processing/interaction motifs (excluding signal peptides).
- Bacterial type III/IV secretion effectors and host-manipulating enzymes (ubiquitin/ADP-ribosylation-related): SLiM-bearing disordered helices used for host targeting and binding.
